text: {r:I}[ay] – men, kamina. Bu o’rinda siz o’zingizni {p:ay}lana ichida tasavvur qilishingiz mumkin. Yanada yaxshiroq esda qolishi uchun bu holatga siz bo’rttirishlar, qandaydir ranglar va qo’shimchalar qo’shishingiz mumkin. Siz tasavvur qilgan holat qanchalik absurd, be’mani yoki bo’rttirilgan bo’lsa u shunchalik esda qolarli bo’ladi. Masalan bu vaziyatda siz o’zingizni pushti sochda tasavvur qilishingiz yoki aylanaga qandaydir rang berishingiz mumkin.
examples: {r:I am tired.} - Men charchadim.
{r:I am late.} - Men kech qoldim.
{r:I am cold.} - Men sovqotyapman.
{r:I am your friend.} - Men sening do'stingman.

text: {r:You}[yu] – sen, siz. "Kavkaz asirasi" filmidagi {p:Yu}ri Nikulinni yaxshi eslasangiz kerak. Yuri sherigiga "Pulni aslida sen yashirding, {h:SEN}" demoqda mana bu rasmda.
examples: {r:You are my friend.} - Sen mening do'stimsan.
{r:You are tall.} - Sen uzunsan.
{r:You are cold.} - Sen sovqotyapsan.
{r:You are late.} - Sen kech qolding.

text: {r:He}[hi] – u (erkak jinsi uchun). Tasavvur qiling Amerikada o’g’il bolalar {p:XI-XI-XI} deya, qizlar esa SHI-SHI-SHI deya kular ekan.
examples: {r:He is my father.} - U mening otam.
{r:He is tall.} - U uzun.
{r:He is tired.} - U charchagan.
{r:He is late.} - U kech qoldi.

text: {r:She}[ʃi] – u (xotin-qizlar uchun). Tasavvur qiling Amerikada o’g’il bolalar XI-XI-XI deya, qizlar esa {p:SHI-SHI-SHI} deya kular ekan.
examples: {r:She is my mother.} - U mening onam.
{r:She is my friend.} - U mening do'stim.
{r:She is tired.} - U charchagan.
{r:She is late.} - U kech qoldi.

text: {r:It}[ɪt] – u (jonsiz predmet yoki hayvonlarga nisbatan). Ingliz tilida hayvonlarga ham, jonsiz predmetlarga ham bitta u olmoshi (ya’ni it) ishlatilishini eshitgan itimiz Bobik (sizning itingiz Reks bo’lsa aynan uni tasavvur qilishingiz mumkin) ozgina xafa bo’libdi va bo’rilardek uvillabdi. U U U U U U U U U
examples: {r:It is cold.} - Havo sovuq.
{r:It is blue.} - U ko'k.
{r:It is my favorite color.} - U mening sevimli rangim.
{r:It is late.} - Kech bo'ldi.

text: {r:We}[wi] – biz. Multfilmdagi ayiqcha {p:Vi}nni Puhni eslasangiz kerak. Vinni bir – biridan arazlab yurgan do’stlarini yig’ib ‘’Haqiqiy kuchimiz ahilligimiz va oqibatimizda. {h:Biz} bir – birimizni har doim shod etaylik’’ debdi.
examples: {r:We are friends.} - Biz do'stmiz.
{r:We are tired.} - Biz charchadik.
{r:We are late.} - Biz kech qoldik.
{r:We are cold.} - Biz sovqotyapmiz.

text: {r:They}[ðeɪ] – ular. {p:Zay}niddin erishgan yutuqlari uchun faqat {h:ular}dan, ya’ni ota-onasi, ustoz va do’stlaridan minnatdor. Agar Zaynidinni tanimasingiz Zaynobiddinni yo Ozarbayjon qo’shiqchisi Uzeirni tasavvur qilishingiz mumkin.
examples: {r:They are my father and mother.} - Ular mening otam va onam.
{r:They are tall.} - Ular uzun.
{r:They are tired.} - Ular charchagan.
{r:They are late.} - Ular kech qoldi.

text: {r:My}[maɪ] – mening. Bu o’rinda Mening Yurtim ya’ni My5 kanalini eslashingiz mumkin. Bugun My5 da may haqida ko’rsatuv.
examples: {r:My name is Ali.} - Mening ismim Ali.
{r:My father is tall.} - Mening otam uzun.
{r:My favorite color is blue.} - Mening sevimli rangim ko'k.
{r:My friend is tired.} - Mening do'stim charchagan.

text: {r:Name}[neɪm] – ism, ot. Futbolda Ronaldo va Messidan keying eng nomdor {h:ism} qaysi? Ko’pchilik {p:Neym}ar deb javob beradi.
examples: {r:My name is Ali.} - Mening ismim Ali.
{r:Your name is Sara.} - Sening isming Sara.
{r:His name is John.} - Uning ismi John.
{r:Her name is Mary.} - Uning ismi Mary.

text: {r:Father}[ˈfɑːðər] – ota, dada. Bu so’z o’zbek tilida ham bor va siz ham ko’p marotaba eshitgansiz '{h:padar}' so’zini. Tasavvur qiling padari buzrukvoringiz {p:fazogir} va u fazoga raketada chiqqan birinchi o’zbek.
examples: {r:My father is tall.} - Mening otam uzun.
{r:Your father is late.} - Sening otang kech qoldi.
{r:His father is tired.} - Uning otasi charchagan.
{r:Their father is cold.} - Ularning otasi sovqotyapti.

text: {r:Mother}[ˈmʌðər] – ona, oyi. Tasavvur qiling sizning {h:ona}ngiz {p:MOTOR} sotish bilan shug'ullanadi.
examples: {r:My mother is kind.} - Mening onam mehribon.
{r:Your mother is tall.} - Sening onang uzun.
{r:Her mother is tired.} - Uning onasi charchagan.
{r:Their mother is late.} - Ularning onasi kech qoldi.

text:
{r:Favorite}[ˈfeɪ.vər.ɪt] – sevimli. 
Davron Kabulov va Ozodbek Nazarbekov futbol jamoamizda kimlar o’ynashi kerakligini muhokama qilyapti. 
Davron Kabulov: Darvozaga kimni qo’yamiz? 
Ozodbek Nazarbekov: Alisher {p:FAY}z {p:VART}aga. Chunki u mening {h:sevimli} shogirdim.
examples: {r:Davron is my favorite friend.} – Davron mening sevimli do'stim.
{r:Yellow is your favorite color.} – Sariq sizning sevimli rangingiz.
{r:Julia is my favorite name.} - Julia men uchun sevimli ism.
{r:It is my favorite game.} - Bu mening sevimli o'yinim.

text: {r:Color}[ˈkʌlər] – Rang. Har xil bo’yoq ranglarni yoppasiga sotib oladiganlar gruppasi aniqlandi. Bullar {p:kallar}, sochi yo’qlar. Sochi bordek ko’rinishi uchun har xil {h:rang}lardan sotib olib bo’yab olishar ekan.
examples: {r:Blue is a color.} - Ko'k - bu rang.
{r:My favorite color is blue.} - Mening sevimli rangim ko'k.
{r:What is your favorite color?} - Sening sevimli ranging nima?
{r:My table's color is blue.} - Mening stolim rangi ko'k.

text: {r:Blue}[blu] – ko'k, moviy. Garchi {p:bulu}t oq rangda bo’lsada, atrofi {h:ko’k} rangda.
examples: {r:My favorite color is blue.} - Mening sevimli rangim ko'k.
{r:The book is blue.} - Kitob ko'k.
{r:The car is blue.} - Mashina ko'k.
{r:Your shirt is blue.} - Sening ko'ylaging ko'k.

text: {r:Cold}[koʊld] – sovuq; shamollash. Mana bu rasmdagi menman. Ko'lda baliq tutyapman, havo sovuqligidan ko’l muzlab qolgan. Muzlagan, {h:sovuq} {p:KO'LD}a baliq tutyapman.
examples: {r:It is cold today.} - Bugun havo sovuq.
{r:I am cold.} - Men sovqotyapman.
{r:You are cold.} - Sen sovqotyapsan.
{r:We are cold.} - Biz sovqotyapmiz.

text: {r:Your}[jʊr] – sening / sizning. Rasmdagi {h:sening} {p:yo’r}gaging bolajon.
examples: {r:Your book is on the table.} - Sening kitobing stol ustida.
{r:Is this your phone?} - Bu sizning telefoningizmi?
{r:Your father is tall.} - Sizning dadangiz uzun.
{r:Is your mother kind?} - Onangiz mehribonmi?

text: {r:Tall}[tɔːl] – uzun. Bo'yingiz {h:uzun} bo'lishini xohlasangiz bolaligingizdan {p:TOLL} shoxlariga osilib sakrab katta bo'lishingiz kerak.
examples: {r:My father is tall.} - Mening otam uzun.
{r:Your friend is tall.} - Sening do'sting uzun.
{r:He is tall.} - U uzun.
{r:They are tall.} - Ular uzun.

text:
{r:Late}[leɪt] – kechikmoq. [b]to be[/b] late ya'ni [b]am/is/are[/b] late shaklida qo'llaniladi. 
Armiyada intizom juda muhim. Lekin mana bu {p:leyt}enant har doim ishga {h:kechikib keladi} va boshlig’idan gap eshitadi.
examples: {r:I am late.} - Men kech qoldim.
{r:You are late.} - Sen kech qolding.
{r:He is late.} - U kech qoldi.
{r:They are late.} - Ular kech qoldi.

text: {r:Friend}[frend] – do’st. Ota-onalarning eng yaqin {h:do'st}i - {p:farzand}i
examples: {r:You are my friend.} - Sen mening do'stimsan.
{r:She is my friend.} - U mening do'stim.
{r:My friend is tired.} - Mening do'stim charchagan.
{r:My friend is tall.} - Mening do'stim uzun.

text: {r:Tired}[ˈtaɪərd] – charchagan. Tasavvur qiling bir kuni kriket o’ynashga qaror qildingiz. Lekin sizda kriket tayog’i va to’pi yo’q. Hovlingizagi {p:TAY}oq va daladan olib kelingan {p:RED}iskani kriket o’ynash uchun ishlatdingiz. Lekin TAYoq bilan urilganda REDiska yorilib ketaverardi va dalaga yugurib borib yangi rediskalarni terib kelardingiz va oxiri qattiq {h:charchab} qoldingiz.
examples: {r:I am tired.} - Men charchadim.
{r:You are tired.} - Sen charchading.
{r:He is tired.} - U charchagan.
{r:They are tired.} - Ular charchagan.

text: {r:Brother} [ˈbrʌðər] – aka, uka. Qiziqarlisi xuddi shu so’z, o’zbek tilida ham mavjud. O’zbekchada u so’z {p:‘’BIRODAR’’} tarzda yangraydi.
examples: {r:My brother is at home.} - Mening akam uyda.
{r:Is your brother afraid of dogs?} - Akang itlardan qo'rqadimi?
{r:My brother is not hungry.} - Mening akam och emas.
{r:That is my brother’s key.} - Bu mening akamning kaliti.

text: {r:Sister} [ˈsɪstər] – singil yoki opa. Mening {h:singlim} har kuni ertalab sut sog’adi va mana bu {p:SISTER}naga tashiydi.
examples: {r:My sister is kind.} - Mening singlim mehribon.
{r:Is your sister at home?} - Singling uydami?
{r:My sister is not interested in dogs.} - Mening singlim itlarga qiziqmaydi.
{r:This is my sister’s table.} - Bu mening singlimning stoli.

text:
{r:Afraid} [əˈfreɪd] – qo’rqqan. Bu so'z sifat so'z turkumiga oid va asosan to be fe'li bilan ya'ni [b]am/is/are afraid[/b] shaklida qo'llaniladi. 
Bir kuni afandi men dunyodagi yagona afandiman deya o’zini o’zi xursand qilib o’tirsa, televizordan yangilik eshitib qolibdi. Aytishlaricha bir uy to’la {p:AF}andilarga {p:REYD} o’tkazilibdi va hozir ular so’roq qilinyapti ekan. Afandi ham keyin cho’chib {h:qo’rqib} qolibdi.
examples: {r:I am not afraid of dogs.} - Men itlardan qo'rqmayman.
{r:Is your brother afraid?} - Akang qo'rqadimi?
{r:She is afraid of the dark.} - U qorong'ulikdan qo'rqadi.
{r:They are not afraid of the sun.} - Ular quyoshdan qo'rqmaydi.

text: {r:Dog} [dɔg] – it. Hot {p:DOG} yeyapsiz va birdaniga sherigingiz aslida bu "issiq {h:it}" degani tarjima qilsak deb qoldi va sizning ishtahangiz yo'qoldi.
examples: {r:This dog is kind.} - Bu it mehribon.
{r:Is that your dog?} - Bu sening itingmi?
{r:My dog is not hungry.} - Mening itim och emas.
{r:This dog is afraid of people.} - Bu it odamlardan qo'rqadi.

text: {r:O'Clock} [oʊˈklɑk] – soat. Faraz qiling sizning uyingizda juda katta soat bor. Bir kuni strelkasi buzilib qolgan edi siz o’sha zahoti {p:O'QLOV}ni strelka o'rniga qo'yib qo'ydingiz. Hozir O'QLOV {h:soat} necha bo'lgani ko'rsatyapti strelka emas.
examples: {r:It is 7 o’clock now.} - Hozir soat 7.
{r:Is it 5 o’clock?} - Soat 5mi?
{r:They are not here at 8 o’clock.} - Ular soat 8da bu yerda emas.
{r:My father is usually tired at 10:00 o’clock.} - Otam odatda soat 10:00 da charchagan bo'ladi.

text: {r:Now} [naʊ] – hozir. Qadimda xonlarimizning {p:nav}karlari bo’lgan, {h:hozirgi} militsiya xodimlari va soldatlarga to’g’ri keladi.
examples: {r:I am at home now.} - Men hozir uydaman.
{r:Is your sister here now?} - Singling hozir uydami?
{r:My mother is not hungry now.} - Onam hozir och emas.
[center][b]right now - hoziroq, hozirda.[/b][/center]
{r:Read this book right now.} - Bu kitobni hoziroq o'qi.
{r:Come home right now.} - Hoziroq uyga kel.

text: {r:Hungry} [ˈhʌŋgri] – och. Eshshak aytdi “Hozir {h:och}man lekin qanday qilib qornimni to’yg’azishni bilaman. Hozir bir qattiq {p:HANGRIY} egam menga bir to’p pichan olib keladi”
examples: {r:I am hungry.} - Men ochman.
{r:Is your brother hungry?} - Akang ochmi?
{r:The dog is not hungry now.} - It hozir och emas.
{r:They are hungry at 12 o’clock.} - Ular soat 12 da och bo'lishadi.

text: {r:Interest} [ˈɪntrəst] – qiziqish. Aynan rus va o'zbek tillarida ham [b]interest[/b] bu qiziqish. Lekin bu so'zning asosan [b]am/is/are[/b] interested shakli qo'llaniladi va kimdir nimagadir qiziqishini bildiradi.
examples: {r:I am interested in books.} - Men kitoblarga qiziqaman.
{r:Is she interested in dogs?} - U itlarga qiziqadimi?
{r:My brother is not interested.} - Mening akam qiziqmayapti.
{r:They are interested in colors.} - Ular rangalarga qiziqadi.

text: {r:Home} [hoʊm] – uy. Baribir o'zbekligimga boramanda domda(ko'p qavatli uyda) yashashni xohlamayman, hovli joyni xohlayman. Mening {h:uyim} {p:HOVLIM} bo'lishi kerak.
examples: {r:I am at home now.} - Men hozir uydaman.
{r:Is your sister at home?} - Singling uydami?
{r:The dog is not at home.} - It uyda emas.
{r:They are at home at 6 o’clock.} - Ular soat 6da uyda.

text: {r:People} [ˈpiːpəl] – odamlar. Mana bu {p:PI}stoletim {p:PL}astmassadan yasalgan. Lekin shundan ham {h:odamlar} ko'rsa titrashadi.
examples: {r:The people are kind.} - Odamlar mehribon.
{r:Are the people hungry?} - Odamlar ochmi?
{r:These people are not afraid.} - Bu odamlar qo'rqmaydi.
{r:The people are at home now.} - Odamlar hozir uyda.

text: {r:Sun} [sʌn] – quyosh. Tasavvur qiling, uyingizdagi {p:SAN}diqda {h:quyosh} rasmi bor.
examples: {r:The sun is late today.} - Bugun quyosh kechikyapti.
{r:Is the sun yellow now?} - Quyosh hozir sariqmi?
{r:My mother is afraid of the sun.} - Mening onam quyoshdan qo'rqadi.
{r:They are interested in the sun.} - Ular quyoshga qiziqadi.

text: {r:Yellow} [ˈjɛloʊ] – sariq. Mana bu {p:YILOV}iq bola yig'lasa rangi {h:sarg'ayib} ketadi.
examples: {r:The sun is yellow.} - Quyosh sariq.
{r:Is the table yellow?} - Stol sariqmi?
{r:The dog is not yellow.} - It sariq emas.
{r:My friend's favourite color is yellow.} - Do'stimning sevimli rangi sariq.

text: {r:Kind} [kaɪnd] – mehribon. Rus yigiti o’zbek oilaga kuyov bo’libdi va qaynota –qaynonasi haqida so’ralganda shunday deydi: ‘’Kaynanamni bilmadim, lekin {p:kaynat}am juda {h:mehribon}’’.
examples: {r:My sister is kind.} - Mening singlim mehribon.
{r:Is your brother kind?} - Akang mehribonmi?
{r:The dog is not kind.} - It mehribon emas.
{r:They are kind people.} - Ular mehribon odamlar.

text: {r:That} [ðæt] – o’sha, anavi. Iz{p:zat} burchakda ivirsib yotgan {h:o’sha} musorni supurib oldi. {p:Zat}o onasini ham xursand qildi.
examples: {r:That is my friend.} - O'sha mening do'stim.
{r:Is that your dog?} - O'sha sening itingmi?
{r:That table is not warm.} - Bu stol issiq emas.
{r:They are interested in that.} - Ular o'shanga qiziqadi.

text: {r:This} [ðɪs] – bu, shu. Yoshlar uchun {p:DIS}koteka – bu ko’ngilochar maskan, yoshi kattalar uchun {h:bu} yoshlar buzilib ketadigan joy.
examples: {r:This is my key.} - Bu mening kalitim.
{r:Is this your sister?} - Bu sening singlingmi?
{r:This dog is not hungry.} - Bu it och emas.
{r:They like this sun.} - Ular bu quyoshni yoqtiradi.

text: {r:Key} [kiː] – kalit. Men {h:kalitlarimni} yo’qotmaslik va har doim menga ko’rinib turishi uchun {p:KIY}imimga hammasini taqib olaman.
examples: {r:This is my key.} - Bu mening kalitim.
{r:Is that your key?} - Bu sening kalitingmi?
{r:The key is not on the table.} - Kalit stol ustida emas.
{r:They are looking for the key.} - Ular kalitni qidirayapti.

text: {r:Today} [təˈdeɪ] – bugun. Raj Kapurning tugun ko’targan daydi obrazini eslaysizmi? {p:TU}gunchali {p:DAY}di faqat {h:buguni} uchun yashaydi, ertasini o’ylamaydi.
examples: {r:Today is warm.} - Bugun issiq.
{r:Is your brother at home today?} - Akang bugun uydami?
{r:The sun is not yellow today, it is reddish.} - Bugun quyosh sariq emas, u qizg'ishroq.
{r:They are hungry today.} - Ular bugun och.

text: {r:Warm} [wɔrm] – iliq. Toshkentda qahraton qishda Yoshlar Forumi Mustaqillik maydonida o‘tkazildi. Hamma qalin kurtkalar kiyib kelgan edi, chunki havo juda sovuq edi. Lekin forum boshlanishi bilan quyosh chiqib, qorlar erib ketdi. Birdan havo shunchalik {h:iliq} bo‘lib ketdiki {p:FORUM}da, barchamiz kurtkalarimizni yechib tashladik.
examples: {r:It is warm today.} - Bugun iliq.
{r:Is the water warm?} - Suv iliqmi?
{r:That coffee is warm.} - O'sha kofe iliq.
{r:They like warm weather.} - Ular iliq ob-havoni yoqtiradi.

text: {r:Table} [ˈteɪbəl] – stol. Aptekachining uyida shunchalik tabletkalari ko'p ekanki bir kuni farzandining dars qilishi uchun haqiqiy stol sotib olish o'rniga uyidagi {p:table}tkalardan {h:stol} yasab tashlabdi.
examples: {r:This table is yellow.} - Bu stol sariq.
{r:Is that your table?} - Bu sening stolingmi?
{r:The key is not on the table.} - Kalit stol ustida emas.
{r:My friend's favourite table is blue.} - Do'stimning sevimli stoli ko'k rangda.

text: {r:Again} [əˈɡeɪn] – yana. Men fokuschiman va hozir sizlarga fokus ko'rsataman. Mana bu 100 dollarni pasga bir {p:egayin} {h:yana} bitta 100 dollarlik qo'limda paydo bo'ladi.
examples: {r:It is cold today again.} - Bugun yana sovuq.
{r:Is your brother hungry again?} - Akang yana ochmi?
{r:The dog is not afraid again.} - It yana qo'rqmaydi.
{r:They are at home again.} - Ular yana uyda.

text:
{r:Eat}[ˈiːt] – yemoq. 
O'tgan zamon shakllari - ate, eaten. 
Tasavvur qiling siz {p:IT}aliya bayrog'ini {h:yeb} qo'ydingiz.
examples: {r:I am eating right now.} - Men hozirda ovqatlanyapman.
{r:My friend is eating. He is hungry now.} - Mening do'stim ovqatlanyapti. U hozir och.
{r:They are not eating.} - Ular hech narsa yemayapti.
{r:The child ate an apple.} - Bola olma yedi.

text:
{r:Read}[ˈriːd] - o'qimoq, mutolaa qilmoq. 
O'tgan zamon shakllari - read, read. Bu so'zning hozirgi va o'tgan zamon shakllarining barchasi bir xil [b]read[/b] shaklida yoziladi. Lekin hozirgi zamon shakli [i]rid[/i] deya talaffuz qilinsa o'tgan zamon shakllari [i]red[/i] deya talaffuq qilinadi.
examples: {r:I am reading a book.} - Men kitob o'qiyapman.
{r:My brother is interested in reading.} - Mening akam o'qishga qiziqadi.
{r:They are not reading.} - Ular o'qimayapti.
{r:The child is reading a letter.} - Bola xat o'qiyapti.

text: {r:Rain}[ˈreɪn] - yomg'ir; yomg'ir yog'moq. Faraz qiling bugun O'zbekiston bo'yicha bitta sizning {p:RAYON}ingizda {h:yomg'ir} yog'yapti. Yoqqanda ham oddiy yomg'ir emas balki qurbaqali yomg'ir.Qiziqarli tarafi okean bo'yida joylashgan davlatlarda ummondagi to'lqinlar natijasida ba'zan haqiqatdanda baliqli yoki qurbaqali yomg'irlar bo'lib turadi.
examples: {r:It is raining now.} - Hozir yomg'ir yog'yapti.
{r:Is it raining?} - Yomg'ir yog'yaptimi?
{r:They are not walking in the rain.} - Ular yomg'irda yurmayapti.
{r:My father is interested in rain.} - Mening otam yomg'irga qiziqadi.

text:
{r:Shine}[ˈʃaɪn] – yarqiramoq, nur sochmoq; yarq etib ajralib turmoq. 
O'tgan zamon shakllari - shone, shined. 
Qozoqlar o’tovida mehmon bo’ldim va meni rosa mehmon qilishdi. Ketayotgan paytim esa qozoq buvimiz “Balam {p:SHAYN}i ich, ichseng qara emes aq jigit bo’lib nur {h:sachesen}” dedi. Haqiqatdan ularning mo’jizaviy choyini ichib bug’doyrangdan oq yigitga aylandim.
examples: {r:The sun is shining.} - Quyosh porlayapti.
{r:You are shining today.} - Bugun yarqirayapsan.
{r:They are not playing because the sun is shining.} - Ular o'ynamayapti, chunki quyosh porlayapti.
{r:The weather is warm, and the sun is shining.} - Ob-havo issiq va quyosh porlayapti.

text:
{r:Run}[ˈrʌn] – yugurmoq. 
O'tgan zamon shakllari - ran, ran. 
4 yoshli jiyanimga 'mana shu randa bilan seni sunnat qilib qo'yaman' deb hazillashgan edim. Shundan beri {p:ran}dani ko’rsa {h:yugurib} qochib ketadigan bo’ldi.
examples: {r:I am running right now.} - Men hozirda yuguryapman.
{r:Is he running?} - U yuguryaptimi?
{r:They are not running.} - Ular yugurmayapti.
{r:The child ran in the park.} - Bola parkda yugurdi.

text: {r:Walk}[ˈwɔːk] – yurmoq. Viloyatimga bilet olib qo’ydim. Lekin Vokzalga yetib borish uchun pulim qolmadi va men {p:vok}zalgacha piyoda {h:yurib} bordim.
examples: {r:I am walking to the park.} - Men parkka piyoda borayapman.
{r:I am walking with my friends again.} - Men yana do'stlarim bilan yuribman.
{r:They are not walking.} - Ular piyoda yurmayapti.
{r:The child is walking with his dog.} - Bola iti bilan piyoda yuryapti.

text: {r:Work}[ˈwɜːrk] – ish; ishlamoq. Yigit va qiz suhbati. Qiz: Nima ish qilasiz. Yigit: {p:VOR}larning {p:K}rugidaman. O’g’irlik, talonchilik, kontrabanda qilaman. {h:‘Ishim’} shu.
examples: {r:My sister is working now.} - Singlim hozir ishlayapti.
{r:Is she working?} - U ishlayaptimi?
{r:I am working with my friends again.} - Men yana do'stlarim bilan ishlayapman.
{r:The child is not working, he is playing.} - Bola ishlamayapti, u o'ynayapti.

text:
{r:Write}[ˈraɪt] – yozmoq. 
O'tgan zamon shakllari - wrote, written. 
Rayhon plastik mahsulotlarni toksik zaharli hisoblaydi, shuning uchun har doim {p:Ray}hon {p:t}emir ruchkada {h:yozadi}.
examples: {r:Are you writing a letter now?} - Sen hozir xat yozyapsanmi?
{r:Your father is writing a book again.} - Otangiz yana kitob yozyapti.
{r:We are writing a letter to the president.} - Biz prezidentga xat yozyapmiz.
{r:The child wrote his name.} - Bola ismini yozdi.

text:
{r:Do}[duː] – qilmoq. 
O'tgan zamon shakllari - did, done. 
{p:Du}radgor nafaqat mebel tayyorlaydi, balki {p:du}tor ham {h:qiladi}.
examples: {r:I am doing my homework.} - Men uy vazifamni qilyapman.
{r:What are you doing?} - Nima qilyapsan?
{r:They are not doing anything.} - Ular hech narsa qilmayapti.
{r:I did my work.} - Men o'z ishimni qildim.

text: {r:Listen}[ˈlɪsən] – eshitmoq. Mana bu {p:listn}i olib o’qib beraman, bu yerda ingliz tilini qanday o’rganish kerakligi yozilgan. Siz meni {h:eshiting} diqqat bilan.
examples: {r:I am listening to music.} - Men musiqani tinglayapman.
{r:Is she listening?} - U tinglayaptimi?
{r:They are not listening to me.} - Ular meni tinglamayapti.
{r:Your friend is listening to a story.} - Do'sting hikoya tinglayapti.

text: {r:Child}[ˈtʃaɪld] – bola. Ko’plab mashhur odamlar {h:bolalig}ida kambag’al bo’lgani va hatto uyi bo’lmasdan {p:chaylad}a yashagani haqida aytishadi. Chayla bu kichkina qilib qurilgan vaqtinchalik uy.
examples: {r:The child is playing.} - Bola o'ynayapti.
{r:Is the child eating?} - Bola ovqatlanyaptimi?
{r:They are not playing with the child.} - Ular bola bilan o'ynamayapti.
{r:The child is wearing a hat.} - Bola shlyapa kiyayapti.

text:
{r:Wear}[ˈwɛr] - kiymoq. 
O'tgan zamon shakllari - wore, worn. 
Hozir suvni asrash uchun paxta dalalarini yo'q qilishimiz kerak deyishyapti. O'ylab qolaman agar paxta dalalarini {p:VAYR}on qilishsa, mato ishlab chiqarilmasa, nima {h:kiyamiz} keyin?
examples: {r:I am wearing a hat.} - Men shlyapa kiyayapman.
{r:Is she wearing a bag?} - U sumka taqiyaptimi?
{r:They are not wearing hats.} - Ular shlyapa kiygan emas.
{r:Your friend wore warm clothes.} - Do'stingiz issiq kiyimlar kiydi.

text: {r:Hat}[ˈhæt] - shlyapa, bosh kiyim. Tasavvur qiling bir kuni eski xat topib oldingiz. Bolalikdagi qog'ozdan har xil narsalar yasaganligingiz esingizga tushib ketdida {p:XAT}ni qayirib undan {h:shlyapa} yasab kiyib oldingiz.
examples: {r:I am wearing a blue hat.} - Men ko'k shlyapa kiyganman.
{r:I am interested in Uzbek hats.} - Men o'zbek shlyapalariga qiziqaman.
{r:They are not wearing hats.} - Ular shlyapa kiymayapti.
{r:Your hat is shining.} - Sening shlyapang yarqirayapti.

text: {r:Play}[ˈpleɪ] – o’ynamoq. O’zbek tilida tez-tez ishlatiladigan {p:play}store yoki {p:play}station so’zlari aynan mana shu play so’zidan olingan. Bu o’rinda pleystordan o’yin yuklab olishingiz yoki pleysteyshnda futbol {h:o’ynayotganingizni} tasavvur qiling.
examples: {r:I am playing with my dog.} - Men itim bilan o'ynayapman.
{r:Is she playing football?} - U futbol o'ynayaptimi?
{r:They are not playing.} - Ular o'ynamayapti.
{r:My friends are playing in the park again.} - Do'stlarim yana parkda o'ynayapti.

text: {r:Watch}[ˈwɑːtʃ] – ko’rmoq, tomosha qilmoq. Omar ismli qo'shiqchining {p:VACH}acha nomli qo'shig'i shunchalik mashhur bo'ldiki hozir 7 yoshdan 70 yoshgacha tomoshabinlar televizorda faqat shuni {h:ko'ryapti}.
examples: {r:I am watching TV.} - Men televizor ko'rayapman.
{r:Is he watching a movie?} - U kino ko'rayaptimi?
{r:They are not watching TV.} - Ular televizor ko'rmayapti.
{r:My brother is watching football again.} - Mening akam yana futbol ko'ryapti.

text: {r:Please}[ˈpliːz] – iltimos; marhamat. Tasavvur qiling kompyuter o'yinlarini yaxshi ko'ruvchi og'lingiz '{h:Iltimos}, {p:Pleys}teyshn olib bering' deya iltimos qilyapti.
examples: {r:Please, listen to me.} - Iltimos, meni tingla.
{r:Is he saying please?} - U "iltimos" deyaptimi?
{r:Please, walk with me today.} - Iltimos, men bilan yur bugun.
{r:Please, eat your plov now.} - Iltimos, oshingni hozir ye.

text: {r:Be}[biː] - bo'lmoq.
examples: {r:I am being careful.} - Men ehtiyotkor bo'lyapman.
{r:Is he being kind?} - U mehribon bo'lyaptimi?
{r:They are not being kind.} - Ular mehribon bo'lmayapti.
{r:Be kind and warm.} - Mehribon va iliq bo'l.

text: {r:Look}[ˈlʊk] – qaramoq. - Lug’atga {h:qara} piyoz nima ekan rus tilida. - {p:Luk} ekan.
examples: {r:I am looking at the sun.} - Men quyoshga qarayapman.(at bu yerda -ga qo'shimchasini beradi)
{r:Is she looking at the dog?} - U itga qarayaptimi?
{r:Yes, she is.} - Ha shunday.
{r:They are not looking at the table.} - Ular stolga qaramayapti.

text: {r:Weather}[ˈwɛðər] – ob-havo. Pokiston {p:vazir}i Shahboz Sharif Londonga majlisga keldi va o’sha payti ‘{h:ob-havo}’ o’zgarib, kuchli yomg’ir boshlandi. {p:VAZIR} kutilmaganda majlislar zalining ayol xodimidan soyabonni tortib oldi va o’zini yomg’irdan himoya qildi. Vazirning ob-havo bilan muammosi borga o’xshaydi.
examples: {r:The weather is warm.} - Ob-havo issiq.
{r:The weather is fantastic today?} - Ob-havo bugun fantastik(a'lo darajada).
{r:They are not going out because the weather is bad.} - Ular tashqariga chiqmayapti, chunki ob-havo yomon.
{r:The weather is not cold.} - Ob-havo sovuq emas.

text: {r:Letter}[ˈlɛtər] – xat;harf. Qadimda qanday xat jo’natishganini bilasizmi? Odatda xatni {p:letr}ovkaning bo’sh idishiga solib dengizga oqizishgan, lekin {h:xat} ko’pincha boshqa insonlar qo’liga tushgan.(Letrovka – 1 litrlik aroq)
examples: {r:I am writing a letter to my friend.} - Men xat yozyapman do'stimga.
{r:Is she reading a letter?} - U xat o'qiyaptimi?
{r:No she is not.} - Yo'q unday emas.
{r:I am interested in letters.} - Men harflarga qiziqaman.

text:
{r:Go}[ɡoʊ] - bormoq. 
O'tgan zamon shakllari - went, gone
examples: {r:I am going to the park.} - Men parkka borayapman.
{r:Is he going to the hotel?} - U mehmonxonaga borayaptimi?
{r:They are not going.} - Ular bormayapti.
{r:My friend is going with his mother.} - Do'stim onasi bilan borayapti.
{r:I went to the school.} - Men maktabga bordim.

text:
{r:Feel}[ˈfiːl] – his qilmoq. 
O'tgan zamon shakllari - felt, felt. 
Dambo multfilmini eslang. {p:Fil}ni uchganini ko’rib odamlar hayrat va taajublanish {h:his etyapti}.
examples: {r:I am feeling fine.} - Men o'zimni yaxshi his qilyapman.
{r:Is she feeling good?} - U o'zini yaxshi his qilyaptimi?
{r:They felt tired.} - Ular o'zlarini charchagan his qilishdi.
{r:The man is feeling funny.} - Erkak kishi o'zini kulgili his qilyapti.

text: {r:Fine}[ˈfaɪn] - yaxshi, zo'r. Xotinni egovlaydigani emas balki MAYIN bo'lgani {p:FAYIN}({h:yaxshi}).
examples: {r:I am feeling fine.} - Men o'zimni yaxshi his qilyapman.
{r:Is the weather fine?} - Ob-havo yaxshimi?
{r:They are not feeling fine.} - Ular o'zlarini yaxshi his qilmayapti.
{r:My brother is fine.} - Akam yaxshi.

text:
{r:Take}[ˈteɪk] – olmoq;olib bormoq. 
O'tgan zamon shakllari - took, taken. 
Sotuvchi amaki: odamlar har doim qimmat sotasan deydi. Ular faqat {p:tekin} bo’lsa {h:oladi}.
examples: {r:I am taking an umbrella.} - Men soyabon olayapman.
{r:Is she taking her bag?} - U sumkasini olayaptimi?
{r:They are taking me to a restaurant.} - Ular meni restoranga olib borishyapti.
{r:This man took two letters.} - Bu kishi ikkita xat oldi.

text: {r:Umbrella}[ʌmˈbrɛlə] - soyabon. Mani dadam zo'r usta bo'ganla. {p:OMBURLA}dan {h:soyabon} yasab tashaganla. (Yaxshi mnemonik misol uchun Toshkent shevasida yozishga to'g'ri keldi)
examples: {r:I am taking an umbrella.} - Men soyabon olayapman.
{r:Is he taking an umbrella?} - U soyabon olayaptimi?
{r:They are not taking umbrellas.} - Ular soyabon olmayapti.
{r:My umbrella is yellow.} - Mening soyabonim sariq rangli.

text: {r:Close}[ˈkloʊz] – yopmoq. Tasavvur qiling siz semizsiz, vazningiz baland, {p:kiloyiz} ko’pligidan restoran yoki do’konlarga kirishda eshikka sig'maysiz va ko'plab do’kon egalari siz kirayotganingizda 'biz bugun {h:yopildik} boshqa joyga boring' deyishadi.
examples: {r:I am closing the door.} - Men eshikni yopayapman.
{r:Are they closing the hotel?} - Ular mehmonxonani yopishyaptimi?
{r:They are not closing the door.} - Ular eshikni yopmayapti.
{r:The man is closing his umbrella.} - Erkak kishi soyabonini yopayapti.

text: {r:Good}[ɡʊd] – yaxshi. Turmush o’rtog’ingiz zaryadkasi bilan muammosi bor Iphone ishlatadi. Unga telefon qildingiz va {p:GUD}ok ketdi ‘’Ha {h:‘yaxshi’} telefoni o’chib qolmabdi’’ dedingiz.
examples: {r:I am feeling good.} - Men o'zimni yaxshi his qilyapman.
{r:Is the weather good?} - Ob-havo yaxshimi?
{r:They are not feeling good.} - Ular o'zlarini yaxshi his qilmayapti.
{r:The child is good.} - Bola yaxshi.

text: {r:What}[ˈwʌt] – nima. {p:Vat}a {h:nima} buni bilmaydiganlar bor. Agar bilmasangiz biz sizga rasmini taqdim etamiz.
examples: {r:What are you doing?} - Siz nima qilyapsiz?
{r:What is she taking?} - U nima olayapti?
{r:What is your name?} - Ismingiz nima?
{r:What is that man doing?} - Erkak kishi nima qilyapti?

text: {r:Where}[ˈwɛr] - qayer, qayerga, qayerda.
examples: {r:Where are you going?} - Siz qayerga borayapsiz?
{r:Where is she staying?} - U qayerda turibdi?
{r:Where are they taking the umbrella?} - Ular soyabonni qayerga olib borayapti?
{r:Where is the child?} - Bola qayerda?

text: {r:Stay}[ˈsteɪ] - qolmoq, turmoq. Chet davlatga sayohatga borib mehmonxonasida turmoqchi bo'lsam hammasi kir va isqirt ekan. Nihoyat {p:SUTDAY} oq va toza mehmonxona topdim va o'sha yerda {h:turdim}.
examples: {r:I am staying at the hotel.} - Men mehmonxonada qolayapman.
{r:Where are they staying?} - Ular qayerda qolishyapti?
{r:They are not staying here.} - Ular qolmayapti bu yerda.
{r:The child is staying with his mother.} - Bola onasi bilan qolayapti.

text: {r:Hotel}[hoʊˈtɛl] - otel, mehmonxona. O'zbek va rus tillarida ham 'hotel' ning talaffuz bo'yicha biroz farq qiluvchi shakli 'otel' qo'llaniladi.
examples: {r:I am staying at the hotel.} - Men mehmonxonada qolayapman.
{r:Is she staying at the hotel?} - U mehmonxonada qolayaptimi?
{r:They are closing the hotel.} - Ular mehmonxonani yopishyapti.
{r:The man is going to the hotel.} - Erkak kishi mehmonxonaga borayapti.

text: {r:Funny}[ˈfʌni] – kulgili. Menimcha dunyodagi eng {h:kulgili} predmet mana bu bo’lsa kerak. {p:FAN}ar {p:IY}ak shaklida, haqiqatdan ajoyib.
examples: {r:I am feeling funny.} - Men o'zimni kulgili his qilyapman.
{r:This movie is funny.} - Bu film kulgili.
{r:They are not feeling funny.} - Ular o'zlarini kulgili his qilmayapti.
{r:The child is funny.} - Bola kulgili.

text: {r:Cry}[ˈkraɪ] – yig’lamoq. Bolaligimda Simba multfilmi kinoteatrlarda qo’yilgan payti, men juda ham kinoteatrga tushishni xohlaganman. Lekin pulim bo’lmagan. ‘’Oyi men ham {p:kiray}’’ deb {h:yig’lab} qolaverganman.
examples: {r:I am not crying.} - Men yig'lamayapman.
{r:Is she crying?} - U yig'layaptimi?
{r:They are not crying.} - Ular yig'lamayapti.
{r:The child is crying.} - Bola yig'layapti.

text: {r:Hand}[ˈhænd] – qo’l. {p:Hand}alak bu kichkina qovun. Hajmi {h:qo’l} panjasidek.
examples: {r:I am taking her hand.} - Men uning qo'lini ushlayapman.
{r:Why are your hands blue?} - Nimaga sizning qo'llaringiz ko'k?
{r:They are not holding hands.} - Ular qo'llarini ushlamayapti.
{r:The child is holding his mother’s hand.} - Bola onasining qo'lini ushlayapti.

text: {r:Single}[ˈsɪŋɡəl] – yolg’iz(turmush o’rtog’i yoq inson uchun ishlatiladi);yagona. Ota onamiz hammamizni oilali qildi. Uyda faqat {p:singl}im qoldi {h:yolg’iz} turmush qurmagan.
examples: {r:I am single.} - Men bo'ydoqman.
{r:Is your sister single?} - Singling yolg'izmi?
{r:They are not single.} - Ular bo'ydoq emas.
{r:This man is single.} - Bu kishi bo'ydoq.

text: {r:How}[ˈhaʊ] – qanday. {p:Hav}as guruhi {h:qanday} qilib hind qo’shiqlarini mohirona ijro etishi meni hayron qoldiradi.
examples: {r:How are you feeling?} - O'zingizni qanday his qilyapsiz?
{r:How is the weather?} - Ob-havo qanday?
{r:How are you?} - Qalaysiz?
{r:How is the child?} - Bola qanday?

text: {r:Time}[ˈtaɪm] - vaqt; marta.
examples: {r:What time is it?} - Soat nechi?
{r:Is it time to go?} - Ketish vaqti bo'ldimi?
{r:They are not staying for a long time.} - Ular uzoq vaqt qolmayapti.
{r:The child is playing all the time.} - Bola hamma vaqt o'ynayapti.

text:
{r:Man}[ˈmæn] – erkak. Ko'plik shakli men - erkaklar. 
Bu yerda {p:men} – erkaakk man deb ko’krak kerib yuradigan yigitlarimizni va {h:erkaklarni} tasavvur qilishingiz mumkin.
examples: {r:The man is going to the hotel.} - Erkak kishi mehmonxonaga borayapti.
{r:Is that man feeling good?} - O'sha kishi o'zini yaxshi his qilyaptimi?
{r:This man is interested in movies.} - Bu kishi kinolarga qiziqadi.
{r:I am seeing two men here.} - Men bu yerda ikkita erkakni ko'ryapman.
{r:Three men are running in the stadium.} - Uchta erkak stadionda yuguryapti.

text: {r:Wife}[ˈwaɪf] – xotin. Tasavvur qiling Bluetooth {p:WAYF}ayni {h:xotinlikka} olibdi
examples: {r:This man is with his wife.} - Bu kishi xotini bilan.
{r:Is Barno his wife?} - Barno uning xotinimi?
{r:They are not staying with their wives.} - Ular xotinlari bilan qolmayapti.
{r:My wife is taking the keys.} - Xotinim kalitlarni olayapti.

text: {r:Why}[ˈwaɪ] – nima uchun. Televizorda Jasur Umirovni qo’shig’i yangrayapti. {p:Vay}-vay-vay {h:nega} yerga urding mani osmondagi oy.
examples: {r:Why are you crying?} - Nega yig'layapsiz?
{r:Why is she going?} - U nega ketayapti?
{r:Why are they not staying?} - Ular nega qolmayapti?
{r:Why are you late?} - Nimaga kech qolding?
{r:I come to the park every day.} - Men har kuni parkka kelaman.
{r:Does she come here often?} - U bu yerga tez-tez keladimi?
{r:They do not come to the shop.} - Ular do'konga kelmaydi.
{r:Come home right now.} - Hoziroq uyga kel.
{r:I came yesterday.} - Men kecha keldim.

text: {r:angry}[ˈæŋɡri] – jahli chiqqan, asabiylashgan. Tasavvur qiling bolangizni ko’rish uchun maktabiga bordingiz. Bolangiz sinfdoshlari ichida eng betartib, {p:ENG KIRI.} Rosa {h:jahlingiz} chiqdi va vaziyatni to’g’rilash uchun majlis o’tkazdingiz.
examples: {r:I am not angry.} - Men jahli chiqmaganman.
{r:Is he angry?} - U jahli chiqqanmi?
{r:They are never angry.} - Ularni hech qachon jahli chiqmaydi.
{r:My parents are sometimes angry.} - Ota-onamni ba'zan jahli chiqadi.

text: {r:book}[bʊk] – kitob. Qadimda bir bukri aqlli inson yashab o'tgan ekan. Odamlar uning bukri yelkasiga tikilib turishini bilgan {p:BUK}ri yelkasiga {h:kitob} yopishtirib olib odamlarning hech bo'lmasa bir-ikki bet kitob o'qishiga sababchi bo'lar ekan.
examples: {r:I like this book.} - Menga bu kitob yoqadi.
{r:Does she read books every day?} - U har kuni kitob o'qiydimi?
{r:They do not have this book.} - Ularda bu kitob yo'q.
{r:I am reading interesting books right now.} - Hozirda qiziqarli kitoblar o'qiyapman.

text: {r:Like}[laɪk] - yoqtirmoq, yaxshi ko'rmoq. Instagramda rasmlarga har safar {p:LAYK} bosganingida uni {h:yoqtirganingizni} ko'rsatasiz.
examples: {r:I like the park.} - Menga park yoqadi.
{r:Does she like the shop?} - U do'konni yoqtiradimi?
{r:They do not like dinner.} - Ular kechki ovqatni yoqtirmaydi.
{r:My parents like big houses.} - Ota-onam katta uylarni yoqtiradi.

text: {r:live}[lɪv] – yashamoq. Tasavvur qiling siz {p:Liv}erpul shahrida {h:yashaysiz.} Qo'shningiz esa Muhammad Saloh.
examples: {r:I live in a big house.} - Men katta uyda yashayman.
{r:Does she live here?} - U bu yerda yashaydimi?
{r:They do not live in the city.} - Ular shaharda yashamaydi.
{r:My parents live with me.} - Ota-onam men bilan yashaydi.

text: {r:shop}[ʃɒp] – do’kon. Tasavvur qiling, siz xuddi Aktivistga o’xshab do’konlarga reyd qilyabsiz. Muddati o’tgan mahsulotlar bo’lsa {h:‘’do’kon’’} egasiga {p:SHAP}aloq tortib yuboryapsiz.
examples: {r:I go to the shop every week.} - Men har hafta do'konga boraman.
{r:Does she like the shop?} - U do'konni yoqtiradimi?
{r:They do not come to the shop.} - Ular do'konga kelmaydi.
{r:My parents often shop here.} - Ota-onam tez-tez bu yerda xarid qiladi.

text: {r:parents}[ˈperənts] - ota-ona. Tasavvur qiling sizning {h:ota-onangiz} {p:PLINTUS} sotish bilan shug'ullanadi.
examples: {r:My parents live with me.} - Ota-onam men bilan yashaydi.
{r:Do your parents come here?} - Sizning ota-onangiz bu yerga keladimi?
{r:They do not have parents.} - Ularning ota-onasi yo'q.
{r:My parents are always kind.} - Ota-onam doim mehribon.

text:
{r:Have}[hæv] – bor. 
O'tgan zamon shakllari - had, had. 
Toshkentda havo juda yaxshi. Hamma joyda quyoshning nurlari va {p:hav}o {h:bor}.
examples: {r:I have a big house.} - Mening katta uyim bor.
{r:Does she have a book?} - Unda kitob bormi?
{r:They do not have dinner here.} - Ular bu yerda kechki ovqat yemaydi.
{r:My parents had a shop.} - Ota-onamning do'koni bor edi.

text: {r:dinner}[ˈdɪnər] - kechki ovqat. Ishxonamizda {p:DINOR}a ismli mehribon qiz bor. U har kuni {h:kechki ovqat} tayyorlab ishxonadagilarga tarqatadi.
examples: {r:I have dinner every day.} - Men har kuni kechki ovqat yeyman.
{r:Does she like dinner?} - U kechki ovqatni yoqtiradimi?
{r:They do not have dinner at home.} - Ular uyda kechki ovqat yemaydi.
{r:My parents always have dinner together.} - Ota-onam doim birga kechki ovqat yeydi.

text: {r:Every}[ˈevri] – har. {p:Ever}est cho’qqisini bilsangiz kerak, dunyodagi eng baland cho’qqi. Deyarli {h:har bir} mamlakat vakillari ushbu cho’qqini zabt etishgan.
examples: {r:I come here every day.} - Men har kuni bu yerga kelaman.
{r:Does she go to the shop every week?} - U har hafta do'konga boradimi?
{r:They do not visit every month.} - Ular har oy tashrif buyurmaydi.
{r:My parents travel every year.} - Ota-onam har yili sayohat qiladi.

text: {r:Day}[deɪ] – kun. Mana bu Charli Chaplin ijrosidagi {p:DAY}di bugun qaysi {h:kun} ekanligini ham bilmayman deydi.
examples: {r:I read a book every day.} - Men har kuni kitob o'qiman.
{r:Is it raining here every day?} - Bu yerda har kuni yomg'ir yog'yaptimi?
{r:Today is a different day.} - Bugun boshqacha kun.
{r:Today is my working day again.} - Bugun yana ishlaydigan kunim.

text: {r:week}[wiːk] – hafta. 'Boriga Baraka' ko’plab tomoshabinlarga ega har {h:hafta} efirga uzatiluvchi {p:vik}torina.
examples: {r:I go to the shop every week.} - Men har hafta do'konga boraman.
{r:Are you at home?} - Bu hafta uydamisan?
{r:They do not come this week.} - Ular bu hafta kelmaydi.
{r:The weather is cold this week.} - Ob-havo bu hafta sovuq.

text: {r:Month}[mʌnθ] – oy. Oldin juda ham ko'p energetik ichimlik ichardim va sog'liqqa ham cho'ntakka ham zarar qilardim. Shundan so'ng xotinim menga energetik ichishni taqiqlab qo'ydi. Lekin hozir uning ruxsati bilan bir {h:oy}da bir marta {p:MONS}ter energetik ichimligidan ichib turaman.
examples: {r:January is my father's favorite month.} - Yanvar dadamning sevimli oyi.
{r:I wear boots in cold months.} - Sovuq oylarda men etik kiyaman.
{r:Next month is April.} - Keyingi oy aprel.
{r:Where is your sister going this month?} – Singlingiz bu oy qayerga boryapti?

text: {r:Year}[jɪər] – yil. Tasavvur qiling bu yil bizda '{p:YER} {h:YILI}'!
examples: {r:I come here every year.} - Men har yili bu yerga kelaman.
{r:My favorite color is blue this year.} - Bu yil mening sevimli rangim ko'k.
{r:I am reading funny books this year.} - Men bu yil kulgili kitoblar o'qiyapman.
{r:My parents are not celebrating Nawruz every year.} - Ota-onam har yili ham Navro'zni nishonlamaydi.

text: {r:big}[bɪɡ] – katta. Men tez tayyor bo’ladigan lapshalardan {p:BIG} Bonni afzal ko’raman. Chunki Rollton, Hot Lunchlardan ancha {h:‘’katta’’} va to’yimli.
examples: {r:I have a big house.} - Mening katta uyim bor.
{r:Does she like big shops?} - U katta do'konlarni yoqtiradimi?
{r:They do not have a big car.} - Ularda katta mashina yo'q.
{r:My parents live in a big city.} - Ota-onam katta shaharda yashaydi.

text: {r:different}[ˈdɪfrənt] – farqli. Maktabimiz direktori hammadan {h:farqli}, gapirganda ham, kiyinishda ham, xarakeri bilan ham hammadan ajralib turadi. {p:Di}rektorimiz {p:frans}uz, balki sababi shudir.
examples: {r:I like different books.} - Menga turli kitoblar yoqadi.
{r:Does she have different shops?} - Unda turli do'konlar bormi?
{r:They do not live in different cities.} - Ular turli shaharlarda yashamaydi.
{r:My parents visit different places every year.} - Ota-onam har yili turli joylarga tashrif buyuradi.

text: {r:always}[ˈɔːlweɪz] - har doim.
examples: {r:I always come here.} - Men doim bu yerga kelaman.
{r:Does she always read books?} - U doim kitob o'qiydimi?
{r:They do not always have dinner at home.} - Ular doim uyda kechki ovqat yemaydi.
{r:My parents always help me.} - Ota-onam doim menga yordam beradi.

text: {r:never}[ˈnevər] – hech qachon. Uzoq yashash uchun nevropotolog {p:nerv}larni asrab {h:hech qachon} asabiylashmaslikni tavsiya qiladi.
examples: {r:I never go to the shop.} - Men hech qachon do'konga bormayman.
{r:She never comes here.} - U hech qachon bu yerga kelmaydi.
{r:They never have dinner late.} - Ular hech qachon kechki ovqatni kech yemaydi.
{r:My parents never get angry.} - Ota-onam hech qachon jahli chiqmaydi.

text: {r:often}[ˈɒfn] – tez-tez. {p:Oft}ob {p:n}uri ostida {h:tez-tez} badanni chiniqtirish, inson suyaklarini juda mustahkam qiladi.
examples: {r:I often read books.} - Men tez-tez kitob o'qiman.
{r:Jahongir often comes here.} - Jahongir tez-tez bu yerga keladi.
{r:They do not often go to the park.} - Ular tez-tez parkka bormaydi.
{r:My parents often visit me.} - Ota-onam tez-tez meni ko'rishga keladi.

text: {r:sometimes}[ˈsʌmtaɪmz] – ba’zan. Garchi Samandar kam ovqat yesada, {h:ba’zan} ochofatga aylanib '{p:Sam}andar {p:to’ymas}' bo’lib ketadi.
examples: {r:I sometimes feel angry.} - Men ba'zan jahlim chiqadi.
{r:Does she sometimes read books?} - U ba'zan kitob o'qiydimi?
{r:They do not sometimes have dinner at home.} - Ular ba'zan uyda kechki ovqat yemaydi.
{r:My friends sometimes travel.} - Do'stlarim ba'zan sayohat qiladi.

text: {r:usually}[ˈjuːʒuəli] - odatda. {p:YUZLI} dollar kupyurasi {h:odatda} eng ko'p tarqalgan pul kupyurasi ekan.
examples: {r:I usually come here.} - Men odatda bu yerga kelib turaman.
{r:Does she usually read books?} - U odatda kitob o'qiydimi?
{r:It usually rains here in January.} - Yanvarda odatda bu yerda yomg'ir yog'adi.
{r:My parents usually help me.} - Ota-onam odatda menga yordam beradi.

text: {r:job}[dʒɒb] – ish. Amakimning taklifiga ko’ra ish qidirib shaharga keldim. Chunki 'ish topib bera olasizmi o’zi' deganimda, amakim bitta gap aytdilar. '{p:Jovop} {h:ish} bor' dedilar.
examples: {r:Aziza has a good job.} - Azizaning yaxshi ishi bor.
{r:Does John like his job?} - Jon o'z ishini yoqtiradimi?
{r:My friend works at a new job.} - Mening do'stim yangi ishda ishlaydi.
{r:Botir and I don’t have jobs.} - Botir va menda ish yo'q.

text:
{r:drink}[drɪŋk] – ichmoq. 
O'tgan zamon shakllari - drank, drunk. 
Tasavvur qiling, sizning qo'shningiz Bodring. Issiq yoz kunlarida siz 0.5 litr suv ichsangiz, Bo{p:dring} bodringligiga borib 20 litr suv {h:ichib} qo'yadi bir kunda.
examples: {r:Botir drinks tea.} - Botir choy ichadi.
{r:Does Aziza drink water?} - Aziza suv ichadimi?
{r:We drank coffee.} - Biz kofe ichdik.
{r:My friend drinks tea every evening.} - Mening do'stim har oqshom choy ichadi.

text: {r:water}[ˈwɔːtər] - suv;sug'ormoq. Tasavvur qiling do'stingiz {p:BOTIR} {h:suv} tashish bilan shug'ullanadi.
examples: {r:John drinks water.} - Jon suv ichadi.
{r:Does your friend like water?} - Sening do'sting suvni yoqtiradimi?
{r:They have clean water.} - Ularda toza suv bor.
{r:Aziza always drinks water.} - Aziza doim suv ichadi.

text: {r:hard}[hɑːrd] – qiyin. Vatikanni {p:xarit}adan topish juda {h:qiyin}, chunki u eng kichik davlat.
examples: {r:I don’t work hard.} - Men qattiq ishlamayman.
{r:Does Aziza study hard?} - Aziza qattiq o‘qiydimi?
{r:John works very hard.} - Jon juda qattiq ishlaydi.
{r:My friend doesn’t play hard.} - Mening do'stim qattiq o'ynamaydi.

text: {r:tea}[tiː] – choy. Tasavvur qiling sizda sehrli choynak bor. Agar eski {p:TI}yin tangalarni solsangiz ichiga shu zahoti qaynoq {h:choy} paydo bo’lib qoladi. Choynakni changini artib turing balki ichidan jin ham chiqib qolar.
examples: {r:I drink tea in the evening.} - Men kechqurun choy ichaman.
{r:Does John like tea?} - Jon choyni yoqtiradimi?
{r:Aziza drinks tea every day.} - Aziza har kuni choy ichadi.
{r:My friend doesn’t have tea now.} - Mening do'stimda hozir choy yo'q.

text: {r:Very}[ˈveri] – juda. {p:Ver}gul gapda ma’noni ajratuvchi, sanash ohangini bildiruvchi {h:juda} juda muhim belgi.
examples: {r:This tea is very good.} - Bu choy juda yaxshi.
{r:Does she work very hard?} - U juda qattiq ishlaydimi?
{r:They are very kind.} - Ular juda mehribon.
{r:My friend runs very fast.} - Mening do'stim juda tez yuguradi.

text:
{r:Know}[noʊ] – bilmoq. 
O'tgan zamon shakllari - knew, known. 
{p:Nov}vot har kun yeydigan inson aqliy salohiyati yaxshilanib, {h:bilimi} oshadi.
examples: {r:I knew Aziza.} - Men Azizani bilardim.
{r:Does John know this key?} - Jon bu kalitni biladimi?
{r:My brother knows English.} - Mening akam inglizcha biladi.
{r:They don’t know this job.} - Ular bu ishni bilmaydi.

text: {r:Many}[ˈmeni] – ko’p. Hayolparast yigit tushida {h:‘Ko’p} qizlar tanlaydi {p:meni, meni, meni},’ deyayotgan ekan.
examples: {r:Aziza has many books.} - Azizada ko'p kitob bor.
{r:Does John have many friends?} - Jonning ko‘p do‘stlari bormi?
{r:My mother does not have many dogs.} - Onamning italari ko'p emas.
{r:You have many good books.} - Sening yaxshi kitoblaring ko'p.

text: {r:Her}[hər] – ayol va qizlar uchu uni, unga, uning. Aziza {p:xo’r} jamoasida ishlaydi. Unga bu ish juda yoqadi, kasbdoshlari esa {h:uning} oila a’zolaridek.
examples: {r:I don’t help her.} - Men unga yordam bermayman.
{r:Does she know her job well?} - U ishini yaxshi biladimi?
{r:They don’t come to John's.} - Ular Jonning uyiga kelishmaydi.
{r:I am afraid to talk to her.} - Men unga gapirishga qo'rqaman.(to bu yerda ikkita fe'lni bog'lovchi vosita)

text: {r:His}[hɪz] – uning o’g’il bolaga nisbatan, uniki. {p:His}obchimiz bor ishxonamizda. Oyliklarni hisoblab tarqatish {h:uning} vazifasi
examples: {r:I don’t know his friend.} - Men uning do'stini bilmayman.
{r:He is not interested in his job.} - U ishiga qiziqmaydi.(Ingliz tilida bunday gaplarda egalik olmoshlari(his,my) ko'rsatilishi kerak)
{r:They don’t play with his brother.} - Ular uning akasi bilan o'ynamaydi.
{r:My parents always believe his talent.} - Ota-onam doim uning qobiliyatiga ishonadi.

text:
{r:speak}[spiːk] – gapirmoq. 
O'tgan zamon shakllari - spoke, spoken. 
Tasavvur qiling aroq ichdingiz zakiskasi bilan, ya’ni {p:spi}rt va {p:ik}ra yedingiz. Ana endi ularni ta’sirida rosa {h:gapiryapsiz}.
examples: {r:I don’t speak Spanish.} - Men ispan tilida gapirmayman.
{r:Does she speak English?} - U ingliz tilida gapiradimi?
{r:They don’t speak very often.} - Ular juda tez-tez gapirmaydi.
{r:My friend spoke very fast.} - Mening do'stim juda tez gapirdi.

text: {r:shower}[ˈʃaʊər] – dush. Tasavvur qiling {h:dushga} tushdingiz va ustingizdan suv tushishi uchun jo’mrakni buradingiz. Suv o’rniga bir quchoq {p:SHAVR}ma tushib kelyapti.
examples: {r:I don’t take a shower at night.} - Men kechasi dush qabul qilmayman.
{r:Does she take a shower every day?} - U har kuni dush qiladimi?
{r:They don’t like cold showers.} - Ular sovuq dushni yoqtirmaydi.
{r:My brother takes a shower every week.} - Mening akam har hafta dush qabul qiladi.

text: {r:heavy}[ˈhevi] - og'ir. Bu vaziyatda semirib {h:og'ir}lashib ketgan {p:XAVI}ni tasavvur qilishingiz mumkin.
examples: {r:Shahzod is very heavy.} - Shahzod juda og'ir.
{r:Does she have a heavy bag?} - Unda og'ir sumka bormi?
{r:They don’t like heavy rain.} - Ular kuchli yomg'irni yoqtirmaydi.
{r:My brother carries heavy things.} - Mening akam og'ir narsalarni ko'taradi.

text: {r:bag}[bæɡ] - sumka. Bu vaziyatda {h:sumka} taqib olgan {p:BEG}emotni tasavvur qiling.
examples: {r:I don’t have a big bag.} - Mening katta sumkam yo'q.
{r:Does she carry a new bag?} - U yangi sumka ko'taradimi?
{r:They don’t like my bag.} - Ular mening sumkamni yoqtirmaydi.
{r:My father buys new bags.} - Mening otam yangi sumkalar sotib oladi.

text: {r:New}[nuː] – yangi. Klipmeykr {p:NU}rimonning {h:‘’yangi’’} klipi NYU Yorkda olinishi ma’lum bo’ldi. Xonanda esa kim ekanligi hozircha aniq emas.
examples: {r:I don’t like new things.} - Menga yangi narsalar yoqmaydi.
{r:Are you buying a new house?} - Yangi uy olyapsizmi?
{r:They don’t want new jobs.} - Ular yangi ish istamaydi.
{r:Why are you buying a new hat and an umbrella?} - Nimaga yangi shlyapa va soyabon sotib olyapsan.

text:
{r:cost}[kɒst] – narx. 
O'tgan zamon shakllari - cost, cost. 
Kuyovimizga kiyim qildik. Kiyimlari orasida eng {h:narxi} balandi – bu uning {p:kast}umi bo’ldi.
examples: {r:I don’t know its cost.} - Men uning narxini bilmayman.
{r:Does she know the cost?} - U narxini biladimi?
{r:What is the cost of your house?} - Uyingizning narxi qancha.
{r:My parents don’t like things that cost a lot.} - Ota-onam juda qimmat narsalarni yoqtirmaydi.

text: {r:money}[ˈmʌni] - pul.
examples: {r:Where is my money?} - Pulim qani?
{r:How much money do you have?} - Qancha puling bor?
{r:They don’t spend much money.} - Ular ko'p pul sarflamaydi.
{r:My parents always save money.} - Ota-onam doim pul yig'adi.

text: {r:believe}[bɪˈliːv] – ishonmoq. {p:Be}gzod {p:liv}ak qilaman agar buxgalter bo’lib ishga kirsam deb {h:ishonardi.} Uning livaklari oxiri uning qamalishi bilan yakunlandi.
examples: {r:I don’t believe him.} - Men unga ishonmayman.
{r:Does she believe me?} - U menga ishonadimi?
{r:My parents don’t believe that story.} - Ota-onam bu hikoyaga ishonmaydi.
{r:I always believe my friend.} - Men har doim do'stimga ishonaman.

text: {r:But}[bʌt] – ammo. Televizor ko’rishni xohlayman. {h:Ammo} yangi {p:bat}areya sotib olishim kerak pult uchun.
examples: {r:I don’t like tea, but I drink coffee.} - Men choyni yoqtirmayman, ammo kofe ichaman.
{r:The table is yellow but I don't like that color.} - Stol sariq rangda ammo bu rang menga yoqmaydi.
{r:They don’t have much money, but they are happy.} - Ularning ko'p puli yo'q, ammo ular baxtli.
{r:My friend is poor, but very kind.} - Mening do'stim kambag'al, ammo juda mehribon.

text: {r:Because}[bɪˈkɒz] – chunki. {p:Bee}line {p:Kaz}axstan – bu eng zo’r aloqa provayderi. {h:Chunki} 5 dollarga cheksiz internetga ega bo’lasiz.
examples: {r:I don’t drink tea because I don’t like it.} - Men choy ichmayman, chunki u menga yoqmaydi.
{r:I walk because i don't have a car.} - Men piyoda yuraman chunki mashinam yo'q.
{r:They don’t come often because they are always working.} - Ular tez-tez kelib turmaydi chunki har doim ishlashadi.
{r:My parents save money because things cost a lot.} - Ota-onam pul yig'adi, chunki narsalar qimmat turadi.

text: {r:Who}[huː] – kim. {p:Xu}rshidni bugun sinfdoshlari sinfkom etib saylashdi. Hayajonlangan Xurshid esa ‘’Xurshid, ki-ki-{h:kim} edi?” deya hammaning kulgisiga sababchi bo’ldi.
examples: {r:Who is she?} - U kim?
{r:Who do you talk to?} - Siz kim bilan gaplashasiz?
{r:Who teaches at the school?} - Maktabda kim o'qituvchilik qiladi?
{r:Who buys these shoes?} - Bu poyabzallarni kim sotib oladi?

text: {r:Which}[wɪtʃ] - qaysi.
examples: {r:Which book do you like?} - Qaysi kitobni yoqtiradasiz?
{r:Which room is yours?} - Qaysi xona sizniki?
{r:Which woman is your mother?} - Qaysi ayol sizning onangiz?
{r:Which shoes do you want?} - Qaysi poyabzallarni xohlaysiz?

text: {r:Talk}[tɔːk] – gapirmoq. Aytishlaricha {p:tok} urishi hatto kamgap insonni ham soatlab {h:sayraydigan} qilib qo’yarkan.
examples: {r:You talk to my parents every day.} - Sen har kuni ota-onam bilan gaplashasan.
{r:Does your friend talk to her friends?} - Sening do'sting do'stlari bilan gaplashadimi?
{r:We don’t talk much.} - Biz ko'p gaplashmaymiz.
{r:My brother talks to the teacher.} - Mening akam o'qituvchi bilan gaplashadi.

text: {r:Much}[mʌtʃ] – ko’p. Hayit bayrami kunlari {p:mach}it eng {h:ko’p} odam to’planadigan hududdir.
examples: {r:Ali doesn’t have much money.} - Alining ko'p puli yo'q.
{r:Does your mother drink much water?} - Sening onang ko'p suv ichadimi?
{r:We don’t talk much.} - Biz ko'p gaplashmaymiz.
{r:Their friends don’t spend much money.} - Ularning do'stlari ko'p pul sarflamaydi.

text: {r:End}[end] - tugash, nihoya; tugamoq. Amerika kinolarining tugash qismini eslaysizmi? Oxirida ekranda THE {p:END} degan yozuv chiqadi. {h:Tugadi} degani.
examples: {r:This movie ends at 9 o’clock.} - Bu film soat 9da tugaydi.
{r:Does his class end soon?} - Uning darsi tez orada tugaydimi?
{r:We don’t stay until the end.} - Biz oxirigacha qolmaymiz.
{r:Her parents always stay until the end.} - Uning ota-onasi doim oxirigacha qoladi.

text: {r:Their}[ðeər] – ularning. Mnemonik assotsatsiya sifatida {p:Zoyir} ismini yoki U{p:zeyr} qo'shiqchini o'ylashingiz mumkin.
examples: {r:Their house is small.} - Ularning uyi kichik.
{r:Do your friends like their jobs?} - Do'stlaring o'z ishlarini yoqtiradimi?
{r:We don’t visit their parents often.} - Biz ularning ota-onasinikiga tez-tez bormaymiz.
{r:Her father knows their friends.} - Uning otasi ularning do'stlarini biladi.

text: {r:Our}[aʊər] – bizning. {h:Bizning} qizimizni ozgina koyisak ham yig’lab yuboradi. Keyin uni soatlab {p:avr}aymiz.
examples: {r:Our school is big.} - Bizning maktabimiz katta.
{r:Do your parents like our room?} - Sening ota-onang bizning xonamizni yoqtiradimi?
{r:They don’t visit our house often.} - Ular bizning uyimizga tez-tez kelmaydi.
{r:Her family always helps our family.} - Uning oilasi doim bizning oilamizga yordam beradi.

text: {r:Breakfast}[ˈbrekfəst] – nonushta. Taniqli aktyor Burak O’zchivit O’zbekistondagi madaniyat festivaliga tashrif buyurdi. Ertalab {h:nonushta} qilishga ulgurmagan {p:BURAK FEST}ivalda tayyorlangan oshni tezroq suzishlarini talab qilib turib oldi.
examples: {r:You eat breakfast every morning.} - Sen har kuni ertalab nonushta qilasan.
{r:Does your sister have breakfast at home?} - Sening opang uyda nonushta qiladimi?
{r:We don’t eat breakfast together.} - Biz birga nonushta qilmaymiz.
{r:Ali and I always have breakfast early.} - Ali va men doim erta nonushta qilamiz.

text:
{r:Say}[seɪ] – aytmoq, demoq. 
O'tgan zamon shakllari - said, said. 
{p:Say}lovda qatnashayotgan {p:Say}yora, mumkin bo’lmasada kimga ovoz berganini saylov uchastkasida hammaga {h:aytib} chiqdi.
examples: {r:I said hello to my friends.} - Men do'stlarimga salom dedim.
{r:Does she say thank you?} - U rahmat deydimi?
{r:They don’t say much.} - Ular ko'p gapirmaydi.
{r:My parents always say good things.} - Ota-onam doim yaxshi narsalar deydi.

text: {r:Wash}[wɒʃ] – yuvmoq, cho’miltirmoq. Itingizni {h:cho’miltirmoqchimisiz?} Unda unga qarab “yu{p:VOSH}, yuvosh” desangiz itingiz haqiqatdan yuvoshlashib sizga qarshilik ko’rsatmaydi.
examples: {r:I wash my hair every day.} - Men har kuni sochlarimni yuvaman.
{r:Does she wash her shoes?} - U poyabzallarni yuvadimi?
{r:They don’t wash their car often.} - Ular mashinalarini tez-tez yuvmaydi.
{r:My parents always wash their hands before eating.} - Ota-onam doim ovqatdan oldin qo'llarini yuvadi.

text: {r:Hair}[heər] – soch. {p:Hayr}iddin sinfimizda eng {h:sochi} uzun bola.
examples: {r:My wife has long hair.} - Xotinimning uzun sochlari bor.
{r:Does she wash her hair every day?} - U har kuni sochlarini yuvadimi?
{r:We don’t cut our hair often.} - Biz sochlarimizni tez-tez qirqmaymiz.
{r:My friends like my hair.} - Do'stlarim sochimni yoqtiradi.

text: {r:Nurse}[nɜːrs] – hamshira. Tumanimiz hamshiralari svet tez-tez o’chishidan shikoyat qilishyapti. {h:Hamshiralar} {p:NURS}izlikda va qorong’ilikda ishlamoqchi emas.
examples: {r:The nurse is kind and she is interested in football.} - Hamshira mehribon va u futbolga qiziqadi.
{r:Does the nurse work at the school?} - Hamshira maktabda ishlaydimi?
{r:They don’t know the nurse because they don't see her often.} - Ular hamshirani tanimaydi chunki uni tez-tez ko'rmaydilar.
{r:Which nurse do you want to talk to?} - Qaysi hamshira bilan gaplashmoqsisiz?

text: {r:Shoe}[ʃuː] – oyoq-kiyim. Sovet kinosining asosoiy qahramonlaridan biri Shurikni eslasangiz kerak. {p:SHU}rik ‘’Ivan Vasilevich o’z kasbini o’zgartiradi’’ filmida jigarrang ‘’oyoq-kiyim’’ kiygan va tez orada shunday {h:tuflilar} Sovet Ittifoqida mashhur bo’lib ketgan.
examples: {r:Her father buys new shoes every year.} - Uning otasi har yili yangi poyabzal sotib oladi.
{r:Does she wash her shoes often?} - U poyabzallarni tez-tez yuvadimi?
{r:My friends don’t like these shoes.} - Mening do'stlarim bu poyabzallarni yoqtirmaydi.
{r:When do you usually buy new shoes?} - Odatda qachon yangi poyabzal sotib olasiz?

text:
{r:Buy}[baɪ] – sotib olmoq. 
O'tgan zamon shakllari -bought, bought. 
Chet elga ketishdan oldin, O’zbekiston {p:bay}rog’ini {h:sotib oldim} va har bir vatandoshimiz shunday qilishi kerak.
examples: {r:I bought many new books.} - Men ko'p yangi kitoblar sotib oldim.
{r:Do you buy blue tables again?} - Yana ko'k stollar sotib olasizmi?
{r:Sometimes I buy different books in English.} - Ba'zan ingliz tilidagi turfa xil kitoblar sotib olaman.
{r:Why does he buy a new umbrella every year?} - Nega u har yili yangi soyabon sotib oladi?
{r:I buy shampoo and take a shower on weekends.} - Men hafta oxirida shampun sotib olaman va dush qabul qilaman.

text:
{r:Teach}[tiːtʃ] – o’rgatmoq, o’qitmoq. 
O'tgan zamon shakllari - taught, taught. 
Aqlli insonlar farzandlariga {p:tinch} dunyoni shunday asrashni {h:o’rgatadilar}, ba’zilar esa avlodlariga hasadgo’ylik, nafrat va adovat hissini meros qoldiradi.
examples: {r:I taught English.} - Men ingliz tilidan dars berganman.
{r:Does she teach at the school?} - U maktabda o'qituvchilik qiladimi?
{r:They don’t teach math.} - Ular matematikadan dars bermaydi.
{r:My parents teach me many things.} - Ota-onam menga ko'p narsalarni o'rgatadi.

text: {r:School}[skuːl] – maktab. Tasavvur qiling, siz muskullaringiz bilan maqtanyapsiz. Mu{p:skul}laringizda esa mikroblar {h:maktab} qurib qanday qilib dunyo egallash strategiyasi bo’yicha dars o’tyapti.
examples: {r:I go to school every day.} - Men har kuni maktabga boraman.
{r:Do they like their school?} - Ular o'z maktabini yoqtiradimi?
{r:They don’t study at this school this year.} - Ular bu maktabda bu yil o'qimaydi.
{r:My sister likes her school because she plays with her friends here.} - Mening singlim maktabini yaxshi ko'radi chunki u yerda do'stlari bilan o'ynaydi.

text: {r:Room}[ruːm] – xona. Aroq ichadigan {p:rum}kalarni alohida {h:xona}da saqlayman, farzandlarim ko’rmasin, ba’zan ichishimni ham bilmasin deyman.
examples: {r:I clean my room every week.} - Men har hafta xonamni tozalayman.
{r:Does she like her room?} - U o'z xonasini yoqtiradimi?
{r:They don’t use this room often.} - Ular bu xonani tez-tez ishlatmaydi.
{r:My parents always help me clean my room.} - Ota-onam doim xonamni tozalashda menga yordam beradi.

text:
{r:Woman}[ˈwʊmən] – ayol. Ko'plik shakli women - ayollar. 
 Otilgan {p:vu}lqon {p:min}oraga jiddiy zarar yetkazmadi va minora ichidagi {h:ayollarga} zarar yetmadi
examples: {r:This woman is kind and warm.} - Bu ayol mehribon va iliq.
{r:Does this woman work here?} - Bu ayol shu yerda ishlaydimi?
{r:That woman has different books because she is very interested in books.} - Bu ayolning turli kitoblari bor chunki u juda kitoblarga qiziqadi.
{r:Single women read books much.} - Yolg'iz ayollar ko'p kitob o'qiydi.
{r:Three women are listening to me.} - Uchta ayol meni tinglayapti.

text: {r:Small}[smɔːl] – kichik. Tasavvur qiling siz taniydigan I{p:smoil} tanishlaringiz orasida eng gavdasi {h:kichigi}.
examples: {r:This bag is small but it costs much money.} - Bu sumka kichkina lekin ancha pul turadi.(Kelasiz darslarimizda much va a lot of ni solishtiramiz va farqlarini ko'rib chiqamiz)
{r:Does she like small houses?} - U kichik uylarni yoqtiradimi?
{r:They don’t live in a small city.} - Ular kichik shaharda yashamaydi.
{r:Laziz has a small shop and a big hotel.} - Lazizning kichkina do'koni va katta mehmonxonasi bor.

text: {r:These}[ðiːz] - bular, shular. This ning ko'plik shakli.
examples: {r:I like these shoes.} - Menga bu poyabzallar yoqadi.
{r:I never like these people.} - Bu odamlarni hech qachon yoqtirmayman.
{r:They don’t buy these things.} - Ular bu narsalarni sotib olmaydi.
{r:My parents always choose these gifts.} - Ota-onam doim bu sovg'alarni tanlaydi.

text: {r:Short}[ʃɔːrt] – kalta, past. Yozda qaysi {h:kalta} kiyamiz? – Albatta {p:short}ik.
examples: {r:I feel very short because my friends are tall.} - Men o'zimni kalta his qilaman chunki do'stlarim uzun.
{r:It is not fine to wear short dress in Uzbekistan.} - O'zbekistonda kalta kiyim kiyish yaxshi emas.
{r:A short man is coming to run in the stadium.} - Kalta bo'yli kishi stadionda yugurish uchun kelyapti.
{r:My parents have a short walk every evening.} - Ota-onam har kecha qisqa sayr qiladi.

text: {r:Black}[blæk] - qora.
examples: {r:I have got a black umbrella.} - Mening qora soyaboni bor.
{r:Does she have black tables?} - Unda qora stollari bormi?
{r:They don’t have black cars.} - Ularda qora mashinalar yo'q.
{r:My parents have a black bicycle.} - Ota-onamning qora velosipedi bor.

text: {r:Guy}[ɡaɪ] – yigit. Germaniyada {p:gay}ka klyuchlari {h:yigit} kishi ko'rinishida ishlab chiqilar ekan.
examples: {r:I know that guy. He wants to drink water.} - Men bu yigitni taniman. U suv ichishni xohlaydi.
{r:Does she like that guy?} - U o'sha yigitni yoqtiradimi?
{r:This guy is very tired because he is working so hard today.} - Bu yigit juda charchagan chunki bugun juda qattiq ishlayapti.
{r:Why is that guy still single?} - Nega bu yigit hali ham yolg'iz?

text: {r:Girl}[ɡɜːrl] – qiz. Qizcha dengizda girdobda cho'kib ketayotgan edi, xayriyatki uzoqdan bir laylak kelib qoldi va {h:qizchani} {p:gir}dobdan {p:l}aylak qutqarib qoldi.
examples: {r:This girl is very angry with her parents.} - Bu qiz ota-onasidan jahli chiqqan.
{r:This girl is hungry. Why doesn't she eat something now?} - Bu qiz och. U nega nimadir yeb olmaydi?
{r:They don't play with that girl.} - Ular o'sha qiz bilan o'ynamaydi.
{r:This girl is crying because she is single.} - Bu qiz yig'layapti chunki u yolg'iz.

text: {r:Want}[wɒnt] - xohlamoq. Onasi o'g'liga 'kim bo'lishni xohlaysan katta bo'lsang' debdi. O'g'li esa {p:Vand}am dek karatist bo'lishni {h:xohlashini} aytdi.
examples: {r:I want to read many books.} - Men juda ko'p yangi kitoblar o'qishni xohlayman.
{r:What do you want to eat?} - Nima yeyishni xohlaysiz?
{r:Why does Sherzod want to go to America?} - Nega Sherzod Amerikaga borishni xohlaydi?
{r:Your friends want to buy a new house.} - Do'stlaringiz yangi uy sotib olmoqchi.

text: {r:Eye}[aɪ] – ko'z. Qiziqarli fakt, {p:ay}iq {h:ko'z}larining oq qismi bo'lmaydi, u faqat qorachiq.
examples: {r:I have got blue eyes.} - Mening ko'k ko'zlarim bor.
{r:Has she got beautiful eyes?} - Unda chiroyli ko'zlar bormi?
{r:They don't have green eyes.} - Ularda yashil ko'zlar yo'q.
{r:My parents have brown eyes.} - Ota-onamning jigarrang ko'zlari bor.

text: {r:Door}[dɔːr] - eshik. Tasavvur qiling do'stingiz {p:DO'VR}on Imzoda {h:eshik} yasovchi bo'lib ishlaydi.
examples: {r:I have a yellow door.} - Mening sariq eshigim bor.
{r:Which door do you want to buy? Black, yellow or blue?} - Qaysi eshikni sotib olishni xohlaysiz? Qora, sariq yoki ko'kini?
{r:They don't have a big door, only small doors.} - Ularda katta eshik yo'q, faqat kichiklari bor.
{r:My house has got a beautiful door.} - Uyimning eshigi chiroyli.

text: {r:Animal}[ˈænɪməl] - hayvon. Bu yil {p:anomal} sovuq va issiq bo'ldi. {h:Hayvonlardek} bo'kirib yubordik.
examples: {r:I have a cat; it is my favorite animal.} - Mening mushugim bor; u mening sevimli hayvonim.
{r:Why don't you like animals?} - Nimaga hayvonlarni yoqtirmaysiz?
{r:They don't have any animals.} - Ularda hech qanday hayvon yo'q.
{r:Have you got many animals?} - Sizning ko'p hayvonlaringiz bormi?

text: {r:Horse}[hɔːrs] – ot. Sunnat to'yim bo'lganda ot sovg'a qilgan tog'alarim va dadamning do'stlari. Biz esa qarzlarni to'lash uchun to'ydan keyin ikkita otni ham sotib yuborganmiz. Oshanda {h:ot} uchun {p:xo'rs}inishni his qilganman.
examples: {r:I want to ride a horse.} - Men ot minmoqchiman.
{r:Does she have a horse?} - Unda ot bormi?
{r:They don't like horses.} - Ular otlarni yoqtirmaydi.
{r:Their horses are very tired and hungry.} - Ularning otlari charchagan va och.

text: {r:Knife}[naɪf] – pichoq. Bilasizmi qaysi joy eng ko'p pichoq ishlatadi. Menimcha bu {p:NAY F}abrikalari chunki nayni tekislash va unga teshiklar ochish uchun ko'plab {h:pichoq} ishlatiladi.
examples: {r:I have a sharp knife.} - Mening o'tkir pichog'im bor.
{r:I am buying a new knife at this shop.} - Men bu do'konda yangi pichoq sotib olyapman.
{r:Our English friend likes Uzbek knifes.} - Bizning ingliz do'stimiz o'zbek pichoqlarini yaxshi ko'radi.
{r:My parents always keep the knife in the kitchen.} - Ota-onam doim pichoqni oshxonada saqlaydi.

text: {r:Cat}[kæt] – mushuk. Bu vaziyatda Abdullajonning {p:KET}monida uchayotgan {h:mushuk}ni tasavvur qiling.
examples: {r:I have got a yellow cat.} - Mening sariq mushugim bor.
{r:This cat feels good in my new house.} - Bu mushuk mening yangi uyimda o'zini yaxshi his qilyapti.
{r:Have you got a beautiful cat?} - Chiroyli mushugingiz bormi?
{r:My parents have a cat too.} - Ota-onamning ham mushugi bor.

text: {r:Children}[ˈtʃɪldrən] - bolalar. Irimchilarning aytishicha agar yoshlikdan {p:chiltir} kalla bo'lib yursangiz {h:bolalar}ingiz ko'p bo'lar ekan.
examples: {r:They have two children.} - Ularning ikki farzandi bor.
{r:Does she teach children?} - U bolalarga dars beradimi?
{r:These children live in this small room.} - Bu bolalar mana shu kichik xonada yashaydi.
{r:My parents love their children.} - Ota-onam farzandlarini yaxshi ko'radi.

text: {r:House}[haʊs] – uy. Doktor {p:Haus} serialini eslasangiz kerak. Bosh qahramon doktoring familiyasi {h:uy} degan ma'noni bildiradi.
examples: {r:I have a big house.} - Mening katta uyim bor.
{r:Why are you buying a new house?} - Nega yangi uy sotib olyapsiz?
{r:They don't have a house.} - Ularda uy yo'q.
{r:My parents have a beautiful house.} - Ota-onamning chiroyli uyi bor.

text: {r:Beautiful}[ˈbjuːtɪfəl] - chiroyli, go'zal. Moda ixlosmandlarining aytishicha dunyodagi eng {h:chiroyli} tufli bu {p:BUY}rak shaklidagi {p:TUFL}i ekan.
examples: {r:I have a beautiful garden.} - Mening chiroyli bog'im bor.
{r:Does she have beautiful eyes?} - Unda chiroyli ko'zlar bormi?
{r:They don't have a beautiful house.} - Ularda chiroyli uy yo'q.
{r:My parents have a beautiful cat.} - Ota-onamning chiroyli mushugi bor.

text: {r:Garden}[ˈɡɑːrdn] - bog'. Tasavvur qiling siz uzoq vaqt cho'milmagansiz va mikroblar {p:GARDAN}ingizda {h:bog'} qurib tashlashgan.
examples: {r:That woman has a small garden.} - Bu ayolning kichik bog'i bor.
{r:Does she like the garden?} - U bog'ni yoqtiradimi?
{r:Their garden is big, our garden is small.} - Ularning bog'i katta, bizning bog' kichkina.
{r:My parents always work in the garden.} - Ota-onam doim bog'da ishlaydi.

text: {r:Bicycle}[ˈbaɪsɪkl] - mototsikl, velosiped.
examples: {r:I never ride a bicycle.} - Mening hech qachon velosiped haydamayman.
{r:Does she ride a bicycle?} - U velosiped haydaydimi?
{r:I usually ride a bicycle after taking a shower.} - Men odatda dushdan keyin velosiped minaman.
{r:My brother is never interested in bicycles.} - Mening akam/ukam hech qachon velosipedga qiziqmagan.

text: {r:Long}[lɒŋ] – uzoq, uzun. Tasavvur qiling {p:Lon}donda {h:uzoq} muddat qolib ketdingiz, shahar sizga yoqdi. Lekin baribir Vatanni sog'inyapsiz.
examples: {r:I have got long hair.} - Mening uzun sochlarim bor.
{r:Has she got a long dress?} - Unda uzun ko'ylak bormi?
{r:He always works long hours.} - U har doim ko'p soatlar ishlaydi.
{r:My parents have a long walk every evening.} - Ota-onam har kecha uzun(uzoq) sayr qiladi.

text: {r:Something}[ˈsʌmθɪŋ] – nimadir. Bu usta yigitning ismi {p:Sam}andar {p:sin}gan {h:nimadir} narsalarni tuzatdi.
examples: {r:I want something to eat.} - Men nimadir yeyishni xohlayman.
{r:Please take something to eat at school.} - Iltimos maktabda yeyish uchun nimadir ol.
{r:She wants to say something to you.} - U senga nimadir deyishni xohlaydi.
{r:Aziza often writes something to her friend.} - Aziza do'stiga tez-tez nimadir yozib turadi.

text: {r:Street}[striːt] - ko'cha.
examples: {r:I live on a quiet street.} - Men tinch ko'chada yashayman.
{r:Does she walk on this street?} - U bu ko'chada yuradimi?
{r:This is not a good street to live.} - Bu yashash uchun yaxshi ko'cha emas.
{r:My sisters often clean the street.} - Opalarim tez-tez ko'chani tozalaydi.

text: {r:Those}[ðoʊz] - anavilar, o'shalar. Bilasizmi ovqatni quruq o'zini yeyolmayman. Piyoz, salat yoki nimadir qo'shishim kerak. Hech bo'lmaganda rasmdagi {h:anavi} {p:sous}lardan bo'lishi kerak. Shunda taom men uchn yeyishli bo'ladi.
examples: {r:I like those shoes.} - Menga bu poyabzallar yoqadi.
{r:Does she want those books?} - U bu kitoblarni xohlaydimi?
{r:I don't like those angry guys.} - Men anavi jahldor yigitlarni yoqtirmayman.
{r:What are those nurses doing here?} - Anavi hamshiralar bu yerda nima qilyapti.

text: {r:Night}[naɪt] – tun. {p:Nayk} kompaniyasi {h:tunda} yorug'lik tarqatuvchi krossovkalarni ishlab chiqaryapti.
examples: {r:I was at home last night.} - Kecha kechqurun uyda edim.
{r:Were you at the park at night?} - Kechqurun parkda edingizmi?
{r:They weren't at the party last night.} - Ular kecha kechqurun bazmda emas edi.
{r:My brothers are usually tired at night.} - Akalarim odatda kechqurun charchab qolishadi.

text: {r:Last}[læst] – oxirgi, o'tgan. Orol dengizi qurib boryapti. Ko'plab baliqlarni esa yo qirilib ketishdi yo ovlandi. Kecha baliqchilar {h:oxirgi} {p:las}osni ovlashdi.
examples: {r:I was at the shop last week.} - Men o'tgan hafta do'konda edim.
{r:They weren't here last year.} - Ular o'tgan yili bu yerda emas edi.
{r:My parents were happy last holiday.} - Ota-onam o'tgan ta'tilda baxtli edi.
{r:This is my last bicycle.} - Bu mening eng oxirgi velosipedim.
{r:Today is his last day in Uzbekistan.} - Bugun uning O'zbekistondagi oxirgi kuni.

text: {r:Yesterday}[ˈjestərdeɪ] – kechagi kun. Bu dunyoda hech narsa {p:yostig'day} {h:kechagi} kunni eslatib turmaydi. Yostig'da kecha nechta soch to'kilgani, charchaginingizdan uyqu payti so'lak oqqani, hammasi ko'rinib turadi.
examples: {r:I was at the park yesterday.} - Men kecha parkda edim.
{r:Were you at home yesterday?} - Siz kecha uyda edingizmi?
{r:They weren't at the party yesterday.} - Ular kecha bazmda emas edi.
{r:My parents were busy yesterday.} - Ota-onam kecha band edi.

text: {r:After}[ˈæftər] – keyin. Go'zal aktrisaga ko'plar havas bilan boqardi. Lekin bir uning {p:aft}ini makiyajdan {h:keyingi} holatini ko'rdim va taniy olmadim.
examples: {r:I was at the shop after school.} - Men maktabdan keyin do'konda edim.
{r:Was she at home after work?} - U ishdan keyin uyda edimi?
{r:They weren't here after the party.} - Ular bazmdan keyin bu yerda emas edi.
{r:My parents were tired after the journey.} - Ota-onam sayohatdan keyin charchagan edi.

text: {r:Journey}[ˈdʒɜːrni] – sayohat. '200 dollar bilan Dubayga sayohat qiling' degan e'lonni ko'rib qoldim va bu turistik agent bilan Telegramda gaplashdik. Ular tezroq to'lov qilishim kerakligini yo'qsa joy to'lib qolishini aytib mendan 200 dollar olishdi. To'lov qilganimdan so'ng Telegramda meni CHORNIYga tiqib izsiz g'oyib bo'ldi. {h:Sayohat} va'da qilganlar {p:CHORNIY}ga tiqishdi.
examples: {r:I was on a long journey last week.} - Men o'tgan hafta uzoq safarda edim.
{r:Was she tired after the journey?} - U safardan keyin charchagan edimi?
{r:They weren't happy with the journey.} - Ular safardan mamnun emas edi.
{r:My parents were excited about the journey.} - Ota-onam safardan xursand edi.

text: {r:Before}[bɪˈfɔːr] – oldin. Forsaj 9 filmi dunyo bo'yicha olamshumul mashhurlikka erishdi. Tomoshabinlar kinoteatrlarga yopirilib borishmoqda. {p:Bi}letni {p:for}sajga {h:oldinroq} olib qo'yish kerak.
examples: {r:I was at the shop before dinner.} - Men kechki ovqatdan oldin do'konda edim.
{r:Was she at home before the party?} - U bazmdan oldin uyda edimi?
{r:They weren't here before the journey.} - Ular safardan oldin bu yerda emas edi.
{r:My parents were happy before the holiday.} - Ota-onam ta'tildan oldin baxtli edi.

text: {r:Holiday}[ˈhɒlədeɪ] – bayram; ta'til. Bugun men shaharda MuradBuildings ning eng baland etajidan uy oldim. Ya'ni yangi uyim binoning tomida, juda keng va shinam. Hech ham ko'p qavatli uyda yashayotgandek his qilmayman, xuddi HOVLIDAY. Bayram kunlari yig'ilib shashlik pishirishga zo'r joy. Bu {p:HOVLIDAY} joyda mening har kunim {h:bayram}.
examples: {r:I was on holiday last month.} - Men o'tgan oy ta'tilda edim.
{r:Was she happy during the holiday?} - U ta'til paytida baxtli edimi?
{r:They weren't at home during the holiday.} - Ular ta'til paytida uyda emas edi.
{r:My parents were relaxed after the holiday.} - Ota-onam ta'tildan keyin xotirjam edi.

text: {r:Expensive}[ɪkˈspensɪv] – qimmat. 2100 yilda bundan bir asr oldingi eksponatlar ko'rgazmasi bo'lyapti. Eng {h:qimmat} {p:EKSPON}at {p:SV}itofor bu yerda. Chunki texnologiyalar rivojlanishi bilan 2035 – yildan so'ng svitoforlar yo'q bo'lib ketgan.
examples: {r:The hotel was expensive.} - Mehmonxona qimmat edi.
{r:Was the journey expensive?} - Safar qimmatga tushdimi?
{r:They weren't happy with the expensive gift.} - Ular qimmat sovg'aga mamnun emas edi.
{r:This hotel is expensive for us.} - Bu mehmonxona biz uchun qimmat.

text: {r:Morning}[ˈmɔːrnɪŋ] – ertalab. Alkash odam ichib olib uyining kalitini yo'qotib qo'yibdi va {h:ertalab} {p:mo'ri} orqali uyiga kiribdi.
examples: {r:I was at the park yesterday morning.} - Men kecha ertalab parkda edim.
{r:Was she at home this morning?} - U bugun ertalab uyda edimi?
{r:They weren't at school this morning.} - Ular bugun ertalab maktabda emas edi.
{r:My parents were busy this morning.} - Ota-onam bugun ertalab band edi.

text: {r:Happy}[ˈhæpi] - baxtli, xursand.
examples: {r:I was happy yesterday.} - Men kecha baxtli edim.
{r:Was she happy after the party?} - U bazmdan keyin baxtli edimi?
{r:They weren't happy with the result.} - Ular natijadan mamnun emas edi.
{r:My parents were happy during the holiday.} - Ota-onam ta'til paytida baxtli edi.

text: {r:There}[ðeər] - u yerda, u yerga. Siz rasmda ko'rsatilgan anavi yerga borishingiz kerak. Chunki {h:u yerda} sizni do'stingiz {p:ZOYIR} kutib turibdi.
examples: {r:I was there last night.} - Men kecha kechqurun u yerda edim.
{r:Was Anvar there yesterday?} - Anvar kecha u yerda edimi?
{r:They weren't there after the journey.} - Ular safardan keyin u yerda emas edi.
{r:His parents were there before the party.} - Uning ota onasi bazmdan oldin u yerda edi.

text: {r:Here}[hɪər] – bu yerda. Onasi {p:Hi}lolaga {p:YER} chopishni buyurdi. U esa {h:'bu yerda'} 8 ta erkak yashashini va nimaga erkaklar ishini qiz bola qilishi kerakligini ta'kidladi.
examples: {r:I was here yesterday.} - Men kecha bu yerda edim.
{r:Was she here two days ago?} - U ikki kun oldin bu yerda edimi?
{r:They weren't here this morning.} - Ular bugun ertalab bu yerda emas edi.
{r:My sister was here after the journey.} - Singlim safardan keyin bu yerda edi.

text: {r:Bad}[bæd] – yomon. Aslida bu so'z o'zbek tilida ham 'yomon' degan ma'noni anglatadi. Amakim badminton o'ynayotib qattiq yiqilib tushgan, shuning uchun {p:bad}minton uning uchun eng {h:yomon} sport turi.
examples: {r:The weather was bad yesterday.} - Kecha ob-havo yomon edi.
{r:Was the result bad?} - Natija yomon edimi?
{r:They weren't happy with the bad news.} - Ular yomon xabardan mamnun emas edi.
{r:My parents were upset by the bad result.} - Ota-onam yomon natijadan xafa bo'ldi.

text: {r:Difficult}[ˈdɪfɪkəlt] – qiyin. Institutda {p:din fakultet}ida o'qish {h:qiyin.} Imtihonlari ham oson emas.
examples: {r:The journey was difficult.} - Safar qiyin edi.
{r:Was the test difficult?} - Test qiyin edimi?
{r:They weren't prepared for the difficult task.} - Ular qiyin vazifa uchun tayyor emas edi.
{r:My parents were tired after the difficult day.} - Ota-onam qiyin kundan keyin charchagan edi.

text: {r:Result}[rɪˈzʌlt] - natija, rezultat. Bu so'z o'zbek tilida ham keng qo'llaniladi.
examples: {r:The result was good.} - Natija yaxshi edi.
{r:Are you happy with he result?} - Natijadan xursandmisan?
{r:They weren't happy with the result.} - Ular natija bilan mamnun emas edi.
{r:What was your result there?} - U yerda sening natijang qanaqa edi?

text: {r:Easy}[ˈiːzi] – oson. O'g'ri honamdan televizorni olib ketibdi. Uni topish {h:oson}, chunki eshikni ochib kirgan, eshikda esa uning barmoq {p:izi} qolgan. Shu izdan foydalanib men uni topib olaman.
examples: {r:The test was easy.} - Test oson edi.
{r:Was the journey easy?} - Safar osonmidi?
{r:They weren't prepared for the easy task.} - Ular oson vazifa uchun tayyor emas edi.
{r:My parents were happy with the easy result.} - Ota-onam oson natijadan mamnun edi.

text: {r:Thank}[θæŋk] – minnatdorchilik bildirmoq. Ota o'g'liga qarab ''Mana katta uy soldik, to'y qildik. Hammasi yaxshi bo'ldi. O'g'lim bu yutuqlar {p:senik}i, men sendan {h:minnatdorman}'' dedi.
examples: {r:Thank you!} - Rahmat sizga!
{r:Thanks! You helped me.} - Rahmat! Menga yordam berdingiz.
{r:They did not thank for the help.} - Ular yordam uchun minnatdorchilik bildirmadi.
{r:My sister thanked me for the support.} - Opam qo'llab-quvvatlash uchun mendan minnatdor edi.

text: {r:Window}[ˈwɪndoʊ] – deraza. Bizni shaharchada dovul tez-tez bo'lib turadi va odamlarni vahimaga soladi. Bu yerliklar ichishadi {p:vino dov}ul payti, shunda dovul bo'lib {h:derazalar} sinib ketsa ham vahimaga tushmaydi.
examples: {r:The window was open yesterday.} - Kecha deraza ochiq edi.
{r:Was the window broken?} - Deraza singan edimi?
{r:They weren't happy with the dirty window.} - Ular iflos derazadan xursand emas edi.
{r:My brother was surprised by this yellow window.} - Mening akam mana bu sariq derazadan hayratda edi.

text: {r:Afternoon}[ˌæftərˈnuːn] - peshin, obed.
examples: {r:I was at the park yesterday afternoon.} - Men kecha tushdan keyin parkda edim.
{r:Was she at home this afternoon?} - U bugun tushdan keyin uyda edimi?
{r:They weren't at school this afternoon.} - Ular bugun tushdan keyin maktabda emas edi.
{r:His parents took a shower this afternoon.} - Uning ota-onasi peshinda dush qabul qilishdi.

text: {r:Some} – ba’zi, bir nechta. {p:Sam}andar {p:Sam}arqanddagi {h:bir necha} tarixiy obidalarni sayr etdi.
examples: {r:I was with some friends last night.} - Men kecha kechqurun ba'zi do'stlarim bilan edim.
{r:Was she with some colleagues yesterday?} - U kecha ba'zi hamkasblari bilan edimi?
{r:Some girls were beautiful, some were not.} - Ba'zi qizlar juda chiroyli edi, ba'zilari esa yo'q.
{r:Some guys are tall, some are short here.} - Bu yerda ba'zi yigitlar uzun, ba'zilari esa past.

text:
{r:become} – bo’lmoq. 
O'tgan zamon shakllari - became, become. 
Konsertga bilet sotib oldim, {p:bi}let {p:Kom}ilovlar konsertiga. Tarixda birinchi marta ota-o’g’il konserti {h:bo’lyapti}.
examples: {r:I was happy, but later I became tired.} - Men baxtli edim, lekin keyinroq charchadim.
{r:I want to become happy.} - Men baxtli bo'lishni xohlayman.
{r:The weather is becoming warm after May.} - Maydan keyin havo issiq bo'lyapti.
{r:Javohir became my friend.} - Javohir mening do'stimga aylandi.

text:
{p:Eslatma: Bugungi darsimiz barcha darslar ichida eng kattasi va shuning uchun ikki yoki uchga bo'lib o'rganing.} 
{r:Sleep}[sliːp] - uyqu; uxlamoq. 
O'tgan zamon shakllari - slept, slept. 
Uyqungiz kelmayaptimi? Unda borib {p:SIYIP} keling. Bir zumda {h:uxlab} qolasiz keyin.
examples: {r:I slept well last night.} - Men kecha yaxshi uxladim.
{r:Did she sleep late yesterday?} - U kecha kech uxladimi?
{r:They didn't sleep much during the journey.} - Ular safar paytida ko'p uxlamadi.
{r:Children slept early last night.} - Bolalar kecha erta uxladilar.

text: {r:Ago}[əˈɡoʊ] – avval. Er xotiniga 10 yil {h:oldin} sevib uylangan edi, hozir esa afsusda. Chunki ayoli uni har kuni {p:ego}vlaydi.
examples: {r:I arrived here two days ago.} - Men ikki kun oldin bu yerga keldim.
{r:Did Laura start her job a week ago?} - Laura bir hafta oldin ishini boshladimi?
{r:They didn't visit us a month ago.} - Ular bir oy oldin bizga tashrif buyurmadi.
