{r:They visited the hospital two days ago.} - Ular ikki kun oldin kasalxonaga kelishdi.

text: {r:Language}[ˈlæŋɡwɪdʒ] - til. Mana bu sehrli {p:sendvich.} Agar uning ichiga Amerika yoki Angliya bayrog'ini solib yuborsangiz ingliz {h:tilini} birdaniga o'rganib qolasiz.
examples: {r:How long have you been learning the language?} - Tilni qancha vaqtdan beri o'rganyapsiz?
{r:I have been learning the English language for three years with my friends.} - Men uch yildan beri do'stlarim bilan ingliz tilini o'rganyapman.
{r:She has been studying Uzbek with her husband since last year.} - U o'tgan yildan beri eri bilan o'zbek tilini o'rganyapti.
{r:English is an easy language.} - Inglizcha oson til.

text: {r:Finish}[ˈfɪnɪʃ] - tugatmoq, yakunlamoq; yakun, marra. Yugurganda marra so'zini bildiruvchi {p:finishni} eslang.
examples: {r:How long have you been trying to finish the work?} - Ishni tugatishga qancha vaqtdan beri harakat qilyapsiz?
{r:I have been trying to finish the work for two hours.} - Men ikki soatdan beri ishni tugatishga harakat qilyapman.
{r:It is easy to finish the work in a quiet office.} - Sokin ofisda ishni tugatish oson.
{r:They have finished the project a month ago.} - Ular loyihani bir oy avval tugatdi.
{r:Finish the job and take a seat here.} - Ishingni tugat va bu yerga o'tir.

text: {r:Danger}[ˈdeɪndʒə] – xavf. {p:DEN}giz {p:JIR}afasini ko’rdingizmi qoching. Bu katta {h:xavf} degani chunki ularning yo’lbarsdek o’tkir tishlari bor va kutilmaganda hamla qilishlari mumkin.
examples: {r:How long have you been in danger?} - Xavf ostida qancha vaqtdan berisiz?
{r:I have been in danger for a few minutes.} - Men bir necha daqiqadan beri xavf ostidaman.
{r:She does not like this kind of dangers.} - U bunday turdagi xavflarni yoqtirmaydi.
{r:They haven’t had any danger yet.} - Ular hali hech qanday xavfga duch kelmadi.

text: {r:Free}[friː] - ozod;tekin; ozod qilmoq. Mana bu rasmdagi kartoshka {p:FRI}lar mutlaqo {h:tekin}.
examples: {r:I have been free for 8 months. I was in prison before.} - Men 8 oydan beri ozodman. Oldin qamoqda edim.
{r:These bags are free. They don't cost any money.} - Bu sumkalar tekin. Ular hech qancha pul turmaydi.
{r:They haven't freed the bird yet.} – Ular hali qushni bo‘shatmadi.
{r:When are you free today?} - Bugun qachon bo'shsiz?

text: {r:Luxury}[ˈlʌkʃəri] - hashamat. Amir Temurning {p:LASHKARI} agar unga 10 yildan ortiq xizmat qilsa {h:hashamatli} uy-joy sovg'a qilingan.
examples: {r:Have you ever stayed in a luxury hotel?} – Siz hech hashamatli mehmonxonada qolganmisiz?
{r:She's just bought a luxury car.} – U hozirgina yangi hashamatli mashina sotib oldi.
{r:We haven't seen such luxury before.} – Biz ilgari bunday hashamatni ko'rmaganmiz.
{r:They've been living in luxury for years.} – Ular yillardan beri hashamatda yashaydi.

text: {r:Territory}[ˈterɪtəri] - territoriya, hudud. Bir xil so'zlar.
examples: {r:Have you ever visited this territory?} – Siz hech bu hududga borganmisiz?
{r:The army has just arrived at this territory.} – Armiya hozirgina bu hududga yetib keldi.
{r:Why don't you clean your territory?} - Nega hududingni tozalab yurmaysan?
{r:We've been studying this territory's history since April.} – Biz bu hudud tarixini Apreldan beri o‘rganayapmiz.

text: {r:Music}[ˈmjuːzɪk] - musiqa.
examples: {r:How long have you been listening to music?} – Siz qancha vaqtdan beri musiqa eshityapsiz?
{r:He has been listening to music for 12 hours.} - U 12 soatdan beri musiqa eshityapti.
{r:She hasn't listened to this music before.} – U ilgari bu musiqani eshitmagan.
{r:They've been making music together for months.} – Ular oylardan beri birga musiqa yaratishadi.

text: {r:Arrival}[əˈraɪvl] - tashrif, kelish. Arrive(yetib kelmoq) so'zidan yasalgan.
examples: {r:Have you announced your arrival?} – Kelishingiz haqida e'lon qildingizmi?
{r:The train's arrival has been delayed.} – Poyezning kelishi kechikdi.
{r:His arrival was a surprise for us.} – Uning kelishi biz uchun syurpriz edi.
{r:We've been waiting for your arrival since morning.} – Biz ertalabdan beri kelishingizni kutayapmiz.

text: {r:Sleepy}[ˈsliːpi] - uyquchan, mudroq. Sleep(uxlamoq) so'zidan yasalgan.
examples: {r:Have you been feeling sleepy all day?} – Siz kun bo‘yi uyqusirayapsizmi?
{r:I've been sleepy since morning.} – Men ertalabdan beri uyqusirayman.
{r:Sunny weather makes us sleepy} - Quyoshli ob-havo bizni mudroq qiladi.
{r:I am feeling sleepy now after a long journey.} - Uzoq sayohatdan so'ng men hozir uyquchan his qilyapman.

text:
{r:Stand}[stænd] – turmoq, tik turmoq. 
O'tgan zamon shakllari - stood, stood. 
‘’Yuragiga stent qo’ydiryapti ekan’’ degan gapni ko’p eshitgan bo’lsangiz kerak. Stent ham biz o’rganayotgan mana shu so’zdan olingan. Chunki {p:stent} o’sha joyda {h:turadi}, joylashadi va qon aylanishini yaxshilaydi.
examples: {r:I am standing near the door since morning.} - Men eshik yonida ertalabdan beri turibman.
{r:The helicopter stood near my shop} - Vertolyot do'konim oldida turdi.
{r:She stands in front of the class.} - U sinf oldida tik turadi.
{r:The seat is dirty. I prefer to stand.} - O'rindiq kir ekan. Men tik turishni afzal ko'raman.

text: {r:Cool}[kuːl] – salqin. Qadimgi qabilalar havo isib jazirama bo’lganda osmonga {p:kul} sepishgan ekan. Bu marosim havoning {h:salqin}lashishiga olib kelishiga ishonishgan.
examples: {r:The weather is cool today.} – Bugun havo salqin.
{r:I don't like cool days.} – Men salqin kunlarni yoqtirmayman.
{r:Your kitchen is coool.} - Oshxonangiz salqin ekan
{r:We want to keep the room cool.} – Xonani salqin saqlashni xohlaymiz.

text: {r:Dancer}[ˈdɑːnsə] - raqqos, tansor. Dance(raqs) so'zidan yasalgan.
examples: {r:Have you ever been a professional dancer?} – Siz hech professional raqqos bo‘lganmisiz?
{r:I am a dancer and we don't make much money.} - Men raqqosman va biz ko'p pul topmaymiz.
{r:They haven't invited the main dancer yet.} – Ular hali bosh raqqosni taklif qilmadi.
{r:We've been watching this dancer for years.} – Biz yillardan beri bu raqqosni tomosha qilamiz.

text: {r:Bed}[bed] - kravat, ko'rpa-yostiq. Men kecha nafaqat o’zimga, balki {p:bed}anamga ham chiroyli {h:kravat} sotib oldim.
examples: {r:I sleep in my bed.} - Men o‘z kravatimda uxlayman.
{r:Is this your bed?} - Bu sening kravatingmi?
{r:That bed is not soft.} - O'sha kravat yumshoq emas.
[center][b]go to bed - uxlashga yotmoq[/b][/center]
{r:I go to bed at 10 p.m.} – Men soat 10 da uxlashga yotaman.
{r:We went to bed after watching a movie} – Biz film tomosha qilgandan keyin yotdik.

text: {r:Only}[ˈoʊn.li] – faqat, yolg'iz. Qon bosimini yaxshi saqlash uchun yaxshi dori bor. {h:Faqatgina} hafta davomida {p:o’n li}mon ichsangiz hammasi yaxshi bo’ladi.
examples: {r:I only have one brother.} - Mening faqat bir akam bor.
{r:She talks only about the school.} - U faqat maktab haqida gapiradi.
{r:This room is only for nurses.} - Bu xona faqat hamshiralar uchun.
{r:We only speak English here.} - Biz bu yerda faqat inglizcha gaplashamiz.

text: {r:Cake}[keɪk] – tort. Bugun farzandingizni tug’ilgan kuni va sizning pulingiz yo’q tort sotib olgani. Shuning uchun arzon {p:KEYK}s sotib oldingizda uni ustiga krem surtib yasama {h:tort} tayyorladingiz. Bolangiz esa yasama tortingizni haqiqiy va mazzali tort deb o’yladi.
examples: {r:She baked a chocolate cake yesterday} - U kecha shokoladli tort pishirdi (Past).
{r:I have never decorated a cake} - Men hech qachon tort bezatmaganman (Pr. Perfect).
{r:They ate the whole cake last night} - Ular kechqurun butun tortni yeb qo'yishdi (Past).
{r:We have just ordered a birthday cake} - Biz hozirgina tug'ilgan kun torti buyurtma qildik (Pr. Perfect).

text:
{r:Throw}[θroʊ] – otmoq, uloqtirmoq. 
O'tgan zamon shakllari - threw, thrown. 
Kecha bir nechta yosh yigitlar {p:so’rov}noma qog’ozi tarqatishdi. Men esa olganimdan so’ng musor chelakka {h:otib yubordim}.
examples: {r:He threw the ball to me an hour ago} - U bir soat oldin menga to'p otgan (Past).
{r:She has thrown away all old clothes} - U barcha eski kiyimlarni tashlab yuborgan (Pr. Perfect).
{r:They threw paper planes in class} - Ular darsda qog'oz samolyotlar otishgan (Past).
{r:I have never thrown a stone to your windows.} - Men hech qachon derazangizga tosh otmaganman. (Pr. Perfect).

text:
{r:Hurt}[hɜːt] - og'ritmoq, og'rimoq. 
O'tgan zamon shakllari - hurt, hurt. 
Har safar mosh {p:XO'RD}a yeganimdan so'ng sochlarim {h:og'rib} qoladi.
examples: {r:My back hurt after the exercises} - Mashqlardan keyin orqam og'ridi (Past).
{r:He has hurt his knee twice this year} - U bu yil tizzasini ikki marta jarohatlab oldi (Pr. Perfect).
{r:The dog bit and hurt me last week} - Kuchuk o'tgan hafta meni tishlab jarohatlagan edi (Past).
{r:She has never hurt anyone} - U hech kimni ranjitmagan(ko'nglini og'ritmagan). (Pr. Perfect).
{r:My eyes are hurting now.} - Hozir ko'zlarim og'riyapti.

text: {r:Middle}[ˈmɪdəl] - o'rta, o'rtancha. Shaxmat bo'yicha musobaqada yutganimdan so'ng menga oltin medal berishdi. Lekin hech qachon bunday g'alati medalni ko'rmaganman. {p:MEDAL}ning {h:o'rtasi} teshik.
examples: {r:We met in the middle of the bridge} - Biz ko‘prikning o‘rtasida uchrashgan edik (Past).
{r:The teacher has always stood in the middle} - O‘qituvchi doim o‘rtada turgan (Pr. Perfect).
{r:They sat in the middle row at the cinema} - Ular kinoda o‘rta qatorda o‘tirishgan (Past).
{r:My level is middle} - Darajam o'rtacha.

text: {r:Jump}[dʒʌmp] – sakramoq. Siz bu o’rinda {p:Jamb}ul yoki Jamshid ismli tanishingizni {h:sakrayotganini} tasavvur qiling.
examples: {r:The cat jumped to the table yesterday} - Mushuk kecha stolga sakragan edi (Past).
{r:She has jumped with a parachute three times} - U parashyut bilan uch marta sakragan (Pr. Perfect).
{r:Children jumped again and again yesterday.} - Bolalar kecha qayta-qayta sakrashdi. (Past).
{r:Children have just jumped from the table.} - Bolalar hozirgina stoldan sakrashdi.(Pr. Perfect).

text: {r:Other}[ˈʌðər] - boshqa. 'Suyunchi' filmini eslasangiz kerak. {p:ANZR}at buvi film oxirida nevaralarining kelajakdagi {h:boshqa} oyna sindirishlariga ham Shermat amakiga pul to'lab ketadi.
examples: {r:My dog does not play with other dogs.} - Mening itim boshqa itlar bilan o'ynamaydi.
{r:Others don't study here.} - Boshqalar bu yerda o'qimaydi.
{r:Another woman called and told me about you.} - Boshqa ayol qo'ng'iroq qildi va sen haqingda aytdi.(another bu a artiklining other ga qo'shilgan shakli grammatika bo'limida batafsil tushuntiraman.)
{r:I have invited you to the wedding but not others.} - Men seni to'yga taklif qilganman lekin boshqalarni emas.

text: {r:Side}[saɪd] – taraf, tomon. Tasavvur qiling ikkita Said ismli o’rtog’ingiz bor. Ikkalasi ham sizga juda yaqin. Qayerga borsangiz ham o’ng {h:tarafingizda} ham {p:Said}, chap tarafingizda ham Said.
examples: {r:I sat on the other side of the table.} - Men stolning boshqa tomonida o'tirdim.
{r:She has never been on this side before.} - U ilgari bu tomonda hech bo'lmagan.
{r:They haven’t moved to the other side yet.} - Ular hali boshqa tomonga ko'chmadi.
{r:The other side is cool.} - Boshqa tomon salqinroq.

text: {r:Call}[kɔːl] – qo’ng’iroq qilmoq:chaqirmoq. Hayvonot olamining biz bilmagan sirlari ko’p. Masalan {p:ko’l}makdagi qurbaqalar bir-birlariga {h:telefon qilib} soatlab g’iybatlashar ekan.
examples: {r:My mother called me for dinner} - Onam kechki ovqatga chaqirgan edi (Past).
{r:I have never called this number} - Men bu raqamga hech qo‘ng‘iroq qilmaganman (Pr. Perfect).
{r:They called a doctor yesterday} - Ular kecha shifokor chaqirishgan (Past).
{r:She has just called a taxi} - U hozirgina taksi chaqirdi (Pr. Perfect).
{r:Call me before I go to bed.} - Uxlashga yotishimdan oldin qo'ng'iroq qil.

text:
{r:Blow}[bloʊ] – esmoq; puflamoq. 
O'tgan zamon shakllari - blew, blown. 
Tasavvur qiling agar Toshkentda 2017 – yili tayyorlangan 8 tonnalik {p:PALOV} shamolning kuchli {h:esishi} tufayli uchib ketganida butun shahar guruchga to’lib ketgan bo’lardi.
examples: {r:The wind is blowing hard now.} - Hozir shamol qattiq esayapti.
{r:She has never blown a balloon.} - U hech qachon sharni puflamagan.
{r:They haven’t blown the dust yet.} - Ular hali changni puflashmadi.
{r:The wind blew so hard yesterday.} - Shamol kecha juda qattiq esdi.

text: {r:Cause}[kɔːz] – sabab. Maktabda odatda nima gap bo’lsa ham ustozga yetkazuvchi bolalar bo’ladi. Ko’pincha boshqa bolalar ularni maza qilib yurishlariga to’siq boluvchi sabab hisoblashadi va bu {h:sababni} '{p:kaz}yol' deyishadi.
examples: {r:The storm caused damage} - Bo‘ron zarar yetkazgan edi (Past).
{r:Smoking has caused many health problems} - Chekish ko‘plab sog‘liq muammolariga sabab bo‘lgan (Pr. Perfect).
{r:He caused an accident} - U baxtsiz hodisaga sabab bo‘lgan edi (Past).
{r:This has never caused issues before} - Bu ilgari hech qachon muammo tug‘dirmagan (Pr. Perfect).

text: {r:Explain}[ɪkˈspleɪn] - tushuntirmoq.
examples: {r:The teacher explained the rule} - O‘qituvchi qoidani tushuntirgan edi (Past).
{r:You have never explained this to me} - Siz buni menga hech tushuntirmagansiz (Pr. Perfect).
{r:They explained their decision} - Ular qarorlarini tushuntirishgan (Past).
{r:I have just explained everything} - Men hozirgina hamma narsani tushuntirdim (Pr. Perfect).

text: {r:Cleaner}[ˈkliːnər] - tozalovchi, farrosh. Clean(tozalamoq) so'zidan yasalgan.
examples: {r:She hired a cleaner last month} - U o‘tgan oy tozalovchi yollagan edi. (Past).
{r:She has already hired a  cleaner} - U allaqachon tozalovchi yolladi. (Pr. Perfect).
{r:They bought a new cleaner} - Ular yangi tozalovchi sotib olishgan (jihozga nisbatan. Past tense).
{r:My wife has just finished cleaning} - Xotinim hozirgina tozalashni tugatdi (Pr. Perfect).

text: {r:Beginner}[bɪˈɡɪnər] - boshlang'ich, yangi boshlagan, novichok. Begin(boshlamoq) so'zidan yasalgan.
examples: {r:He started as a beginner} - U boshlang‘ich sifatida ish boshlagan edi (Past).
{r:She has never taught beginners} - U boshlang‘ichlarga hech dars bermagan (Pr. Perfect).
{r:They joined the beginner’s class} - Ular boshlang‘ichlar sinfiga qo‘shilishgan (Past).
{r:I have just completed the beginner course} - Men hozirgina boshlang‘ich kursni tugatdim (Pr. Perfect).

text: {r:Payment}[ˈpeɪmənt] - to'lov. Pay(to'lamoq) so'zidan yasalgan.
examples: {r:We made the payment yesterday} - Biz kecha to‘lov qilgan edik (Past).
{r:They have never missed a payment} - Ular hech qachon to‘lovni o‘tkazib yubormagan (Pr. Perfect).
{r:She received the payment} - U to‘lovni olgan edi (Past).
{r:The system has just finished your payment} - Tizim hozirgina to‘lovingizni tugatdi (Pr. Perfect).

text: {r:Transport}[ˈtrænspɔːt] - transport; tashimoq.
examples: {r:They used public transport} - Ular jamoat transportidan foydalanishgan (Past).
{r:I have never used transport} - Men hech qachon transportdan foydalanmaganman (Pr. Perfect).
{r:We transported wood from the forest to the city.} - Biz o'rmondan shaharga yog'och tashiganmiz. (Past).
{r:The products have just arrived by transport} - Tovarlar hozirgina transport orqali yetib keldi (Pr. Perfect).

text: {r:Orange}[ˈɔːrɪndʒ] - apelsin; apelsinrang. Aranjoviy(apelsinrang) so'zi shu so'zdan yasalgan.
examples: {r:She peeled an orange} - U apelsin archiladi (Past).
{r:We have never grown oranges} - Biz hech qachon apelsin o‘stirmaganmiz (Pr. Perfect).
{r:They bought orange yesterday} - Ular kecha apelsin sotib olishgan (Past).
{r:I have just eaten two oranges} - Men hozirgina ikkita apelsin yedim (Pr. Perfect).

text: {r:Yes}[jɛs] - ha.
examples: {r:He said yes to the offer} - U taklifga ha deb javob bergan edi (Past).
{r:They have never answered yes} - Ular hech qachon ha deb javob bermagan (Pr. Perfect).
{r:We heard yes from the manager} - Biz menejerdan ha javobini eshitdik. (Past).
{r:She has just <nodded> yes} - U hozirgina ha deb <bosh chayqadi> (Pr. Perfect).

text: {r:Me}[miː] – meni, menga. Men Mi telefonini ishlataman qiziqarlisi men Mi smartfonini emas balki, Mi meni tanlagan. Agar mi telefonini bilmasangiz Milan jamoasi, Mirabbos yoki Mirolimni tasavvur qilishingiz mumkin.
examples: {r:They called me} - Ular meni chaqirishgan edi (Past).
{r:You have never visited me} - Siz menga hech kelmagansiz (Pr. Perfect).
{r:She helped me} - U menga yordam berdi (Past).
{r:You have already invited me to your wedding.} - To'yingga meni allaqachon taklif qilgansan (Pr. Perfect).

text: {r:Use}[juːz] – foydalanmoq. {p:Yuz} dollar eng sevimli va ko’p {h:foydalaniladigan} kupyura. Unda Benjamin Franklin yuzi tasvirlangan.
examples: {r:We used this method last year} - Biz o'tgan yili bu usuldan foydalangan edik (Past).
{r:She has never used a computer} - U hech qachon kompyuterdan foydalanmagan (Pr. Perfect).
{r:They used all the materials} - Ular barcha materiallardan foydalanishgan (Past).
{r:I have just used the last one} - Men hozirgina oxirgisidan foydalandim (Pr. Perfect).

text:
{r:Injury}[ˈɪndʒəri] – jarohat. to be injured - jarohatlanmoq.
 Tasavvur qiling {p:anjir} yesangiz oyoqlaringizga {h:yara} toshyapti, qancha ko’p yesangiz shuncha ko’p paydo bo’lyapti.
examples: {r:I don't play football because of my injury.} - Jarohatim sabab futbol o'ynamayman.
{r:The player was injured during the game.} - O'yinchi o'yin paytida jarohat oldi.
{r:The dog was injured yesterday.} - It kecha jarohat oldi.
{r:They were not injured in the accident.} - Ular baxtsiz hodisada jarohat olishmadi.
{r:My parents were injured in the accident.} - Ota-onam baxtsiz hodisada jarohatlandi.

text: {r:Butter}[ˈbʌtər] – sariyog’. Siz bu vaziyatda do’stingiz {p:BOTIR}ni yuziga {h:sariyog’} surtib olganini tasavvur qilishingiz mumkin.
examples: {r:This butter is produced by my sister.} - Bu sariyog' singlim tomonidan ishlab chiqariladi.
{r:The butter was used in the kitchen.} - Sariyog' oshxonada ishlatildi.
{r:They didn’t buy the butter 2 days ago.} - Ular 2 kun oldin sariyog' sotib olishmadi.
{r:The butter was sold last week.} - Sariyog' o‘tgan hafta sotildi.

text: {r:Milk}[mɪlk] – sut. Siz sutni shunchalik yaxshi ko’rasizki tishingiz va {p:MILK}ingizdan {h:sutni} xidi kelib turadi.
examples: {r:The milk is transported to the city in the mornings.} - Sut ertalablari shaharga tashiladi.
{r:The milk was boiled in the morning.} - Sut ertalab qaynatildi.
{r:They didn’t drink the milk.} - Ular sut ichishmadi.
{r:The milk was boiled yesterday.} - Sut kecha qaynatilgan.

text: {r:Loud}[laʊd] – baland, qattiq, shovqinli(ovoz, tovush, musiqa). Ovozingiz {h:balandroq} bo’lishini xohlaysizmi? Yechimi juda oddiy. {p:LAV}lagi {p:T}erisini yuvmasdan loyi bilan yeb yuboring. Tez orada foydasini sezasiz.
examples: {r:The music was too loud.} - Musiqa juda baland edi.
{r:The noise is reduced after 10 PM.} - Shovqin kechki soat 10 dan keyin kamaytiriladi.
{r:Loud songs must be banned in schools.} - Baland qo'shiqlar maktablarda taqiqlanishi kerak.
{r:A loud noise was made by the children.} - Baland shovqin bolalar tomonidan qilindi.

text: {r:Noise}[nɔɪz] – shovqin. Tasavvur qiling kimdir sizni kechqurun shovqin qilib chaqiradi. 'U kim ekan' deya yugurib chiqsangiz {h:shovqin} qilgan odam {p:NOIZ} yo’qolib qoladi.
examples: {r:The noise is heard from the street.} - Ko'chadan shovqin eshitiladi.
{r:The noise was stopped by the teacher.} - Shovqin o'qituvchi tomonidan to‘xtatildi.
{r:I thought Akfa windows block the noise from the road.} - Men Akfa derazalari yo'ldan kelayotgan shovqinni bloklaydi deb o'ylagan edim.
{r:The question about the noise must be answered.} - Shovqin haqidagi savolga javob berilishi kerak.

text:
{r:Bite}[baɪt] – tishlamoq. 
O'tgan zamon shakllari - bit, bitten. 
Mening chiroyli qora baytal otim bor. U nafaqat chiroyli balki shaddodhamdir. Mahallaning itlari baytalni tishlamaydi balki mening {p:BAYT}alim ularni {h:tishlab} oladi agar yoqtirmasa.
examples: {r:The apple was bitten by the child.} - Olma bola tomonidan tishlandi.
{r:The child is biting apples once and throwing.} - Bola olmalarni bitta tishlab keyin tashlab yuboryapti.
{r:They were bitten by the dog yesterday.} - Ular kecha it tomonidan tishlandi.
{r:Why was this orange bitten? It was mine.} - Nimaga bu apelsin tishlangan? Bu meniki edi.

text: {r:Sand}[sænd] – qum. Tasavvur qiling juda qadimiy {p:SAND}iq topib oldingiz. Ichida oltinlar bo’lsa kerak deb shoshilib ochdingiz. Lekin afsuski sandiqni ichida to’la {h:qum} bor ekan.
examples: {r:The shoes are filled with sand in desert.} - Poyabzal qum bilan to'lib ketadi cho'lda.
{r:These sands are transported to the city.} - Bu qumlar shaharga tashiladi.
{r:They didn’t clean the sand.} - Ular qumni tozalashmadi.
{r:Sand was found in the box.} - Qum sandiqdan topildi.
{r:Why is this sand so cool?} - Nega bu qum juda salqin?

text: {r:Stamp}[stæmp] - muhr, shtamp;muhrlamoq. O'zbek tilida ham stamp ning talaffuz jihatdan biroz farqlanuvchi shakli ya'ni 'shtamp' so'zi keng qo'llaniladi.
examples: {r:The letter is usually stamped by our boss.} - Xat odatda boshlig'imiz tomonidan muhrlanadi.
{r:The passport was stamped at the airport.} - Pasport aeroportda muhrlandi.
{r:No, it was not stamped.} - Yo‘q, u muhrlanmadi.
{r:We are given new stamps every year.} - Bizga har yili yangi muhrlar beriladi.

text: {r:Pronounce}[prəˈnaʊns] - talaffuz qilmoq. Aytishlaricha agar {p:PRAN}ik {p:UNS}iz qilinsa faqatgina suv, jelatin va kremdan siz r harfini {h:talaffuz} qila olmay qolar ekansiz agar shunday pranikni yesangiz.
examples: {r:The word was pronounced correctly.} - So'z to'g'ri talaffuz qilindi.
{r:How is that word pronounced?} - O'sha so'z qanday talaffuz qilinadi?
{r:They didn’t pronounce it well.} - Ular uni yaxshi talaffuz qilishmadi.
{r:The word 'newspaper' was pronounced incorrectly.} - 'Gazeta' so'zi noto'g'ri talaffuz qilindi.

text:
{r:Steal}[stiːl] – o’g’irlamoq. 
O'tgan zamon shakllari - stole, stolen. 
Tasavvur qiling siz juda {p:stil}niy kiyinasiz va shuning uchun ham qizlarni(yigitlarni) yuragini {h:o’g’irlaysiz}.
examples: {r:The money was stolen from the bag.} - Pul sumkadan o'g'irlangan edi.
{r:Davron is a good guy! He does not steal anything.} - Davron yaxshi yigit. U hech nima o'g'irlamaydi.
{r:The money was stolen in the hospital.} - Kasalxonada pul o'g‘irlab ketilgan.
{r:The phones were stolen by those guys.} - Telefonlar o‘sha yigitlar tomonidan o‘g‘irlangan.

text: {r:Bridge}[brɪdʒ] – ko’prik. Mana bu dunyodagi eng antiqa {h:ko’prik.} Yuzlab o{p:BRICH}lardan yasalgan.
examples: {r:The old bridge was built in 1960.} – Eski ko‘prik 1960-yilda qurilgan.
{r:When was the new bridge completed?} – Yangi ko‘prik qachon tugallandi?
{r:The damaged part of the bridge was repaired.} – Ko'prikning zarar ko‘rgan qismi ta’mirlandi.
{r:Modern materials are used for bridge construction.} – Ko'prik qurilishida zamonaviy materiallar ishlatiladi.

text:
{r:Send}[sɛnd] - jo'natmoq. 
O'tgan zamon shakllari - sent, sent. 
Har oy mening dadam 10 000 {p:SENT} jo'natadi menga Rossiyadan. Bu 100 dollar {h:jo'natadi} degani.
examples: {r:The package was sent yesterday.} – Posilka kecha jo‘natilgan.
{r:Why weren’t the documents sent earlier?} – Hujjatlar nega oldinroq jo‘natilmadi?
{r:The letter was not sent.} – Xat jo‘natilmadi.
{r:Important messages are sent <through> email.} – Muhim xabarlar elektron pochta <orqali> yuboriladi

text: {r:Repair}[rɪˈpeər] – ta’mirlamoq, tuzatmoq. {p:REPER}lar jamiyat uchun biror foydali ish bilan shug’ullanmayotganligi uchun ularni biror foydali ishga majburlashimiz kerak. Masalan majburan uylarni {h:ta’mirlash} ishlariga jalb qilish yaxshi g’oya.
examples: {r:My phone was repaired quickly.} – Telefonim tezda ta’mirlandi.
{r:Where are cars usually repaired here?} – Mashinalar odatda qayerda ta’mirlanadi?
{r:The watch was repaired properly.} – Soat to‘g‘ri tuzatildi.
{r:Old houses are repaired every year.} – Eski uylar har yili ta'mirlanadi.

text: {r:Damage}[ˈdæmɪdʒ] - zarar; zararlamoq, shikastlamoq. Mening dadam yanglishib 800 000 so'mga {p:CHO'MICH} sotib olibdi va onamning fikricha oilaviy byudjetimizga katta {h:zarar} keltiribdi.
examples: {r:The roof was damaged in the storm.} – Tom bo‘ron paytida shikastlangan.
{r:How much was your car damaged?} – Mashinangiz qanchalik shikastlangan?
{r:This damage was caused by a fire.} - Bu zarar yong'indan kelib chiqqan.
{r:A few damages were done by animals.} - Ba’zi zararlar hayvonlar tomonidan qilindi.

text: {r:Surprise}[sərˈpraɪz] - hayratlantirmoq; hayrat, syurpriz. 'Syurpriz' so'zi aynan shu so'zdan kelib chiqqan.
examples: {r:Everyone was surprised by the news.} – Hammasi yangilikdan hayratda qoldi.
{r:Your arrival was a big surprise.} - Sizning kelishingiz syurpriz edi.
{r:Nobody was surprised by your late arrival.} - Hech kim sizning kech tashrifingizdan hayratlanmadi.
{r:People were surprised by the decorations.} – Odamlar bezaklardan hayratda qolishdi.

text:
{r:Show}[ʃoʊ] – ko’rsatmoq. 
O'tgan zamon shakllari - showed, shown. 
Chet ellik do’stim mehmon bo’lib keldi va unga ovqat tayyorladim. Ovqat {p:sho’v}la edi va uni do’stimga {h:ko’rsatdim}, u esa bu ovqatni osh deb o’yladi.
examples: {r:The exhibition is shown worldwide.} – Ko‘rgazma butun dunyoga namoyish etilmoqda.
{r:When was the results shown?} – Natijalar qachon ko‘rsatildi?
{r:You showed good results.} - Sen yaxshi natijalar ko'rsatding.
{r:When do you show me your home?} - Qachon menga uyingni ko'rsatasan?

text: {r:Wedding}[ˈwɛdɪŋ] – to’y. Tasavvur qiling sizning do’stingizning {h:to’yiga} bir {p:VET}erinar {p:DIN}amit ko’tarib kelibdi “Aslida bu qiz bilan men ahdu-paymon qilgandi” deya.
examples: {r:Their wedding was celebrated beautifully.} – Ularining to‘yi chiroyli nishonlandi.
{r:Weddings are important in my country.} - To'ylar juda muhim bizning davlatda.
{r:When is his wedding?} - Uning to'yi qachon?
{r:Today is my brother's wedding day.} - Bugun mening akamning to'yi.

text: {r:Wood}[wʊd] – yog’och. Mana bu ‘Golli{p:VUD}’ degan yozuvni O’zbekiston poytaxti Toshkentda ham yozishibdi faqat ammo {h:yog’och}dan.
examples: {r:This furniture was made from wood.} - Bu mebel yog'ochdan qilingan.
{r:Trees are cut and wood is made.} - Daraxtlar kesiladi va yog'och qilinadi.
{r:We are big buyers of wood.} - Biz yog'ochning katta xaridorlarimiz.
{r:I need wood to build house.} - Uy qurishim uchun yog'och kerak

text: {r:Fire}[faɪər] – yoqmoq, o’t. Sevgan qizi bilan ajralishgandan so’ng, {p:Fay}oz {p:R}asmlarni hammasini {h:yoqib yubordi}, birga tushganlarini ham, qizning o’zinikini ham.
examples: {r:The building was destroyed by fire.} – Bino yong‘inda vayron bo‘lgan.
{r:We set fire to the old house.} - Biz eski uyga o't qo'ydik.
{r:The fire was caused by carelessness.} - Yong'in ehtiyotsizlikdan kelib chiqqan
{r:We don't need fire now.} - Bizga hozir olov kerak emas.

text: {r:Try}[traɪ] – harakat qilmoq;sinab ko'rmoq, ta'tib ko'rmoq. {h:Harakat qilishda} gap ko’p. Kecha bir voqea meni hayratlantirdi, {p:tra}ktorni {p:ay}iq haydab ketyapti ekan, qoyil.
examples: {r:He has tried hard to get rich.} - U boyib ketishga qattiq harakat qildi.
{r:Her husband is trying to learn a new language.} - Uning eri yangi til o'rganishga harakat qilyapti.
{r:Workers tried to solve the problem yesterday.} - Ishchilar kecha muammoni hal qilishga urindi.
{r:John tried Palov just once.} - John oshni faqat bir marta ta'tib ko'rgan.

text: {r:Opposite}[ˈɒpəzɪt] – qarama-qarshi, teskari, ro’para. Siz yo’ldan o’tmoqchisiz {h:qarama-qarshi} tarafga. Lekin u yerda katta {p:OPPO IT}ni ko’rib qo’rqdingiz va orqaga qaytdingiz.
examples: {r:The house was built opposite the park.} - Uy bog'ning qarshisida qurilgan edi.
{r:Has the shop been opened opposite the school?} - Do'kon maktab qarshisida ochilganmi?
{r:They haven’t seen the opposite side yet.} - Ular hali qarama-qarshi tomonni ko'rishmadi.
{r:My teachers have already visited the opposite building.} - O'qituvchilarim qarama-qarshi binoga tashrif buyurdi.
{r:My father is tall and my mother is the opposite.} - Otam uzun onam esa teskarisi.

text: {r:Grass}[ɡræs] – o’t. Bugun mashhur shaxmat {p:GRASS}meystri hamyurtimiz Nodirbek Abdusattorov {h:o’t} ustida shaxmat qiroli Magnus Karlsen bilan ikki partiya shaxmat o’ynab qora donalarda Magnusni yengishga muvaffaq bo’ldi.
examples: {r:The grass was cut by the gardener.} - O't bog'bon tomonidan kesildi.
{r:Has the grass been watered yet?} - O't sug'orilganmi?
{r:Yes, the grass has been watered already.} - Ha o't allaqachon sug'orilgan.
{r:This grass has just been painted.} - Bu o'tlar hozirgina bo'yaldi.
{r:You can have a seat on the grass.} - O't ustiga o'tirishing mumkin

text: {r:Iron}[ˈaɪərn] – dazmol; dazmollamoq. Tasavvur sizning {h:dazmol}ingizga {p:ERON} bayrog'i tushirilgan.
examples: {r:The shirt has just been ironed for the meeting.} - Ko'ylak yig'ilish uchun endigina dazmollangan.
{r:Are your clothes being ironed now?} - Kiyimlaringiz hozir dazmollanmoqdami?
{r:The old iron has been replaced with a new one.} - Eski dazmol yangisi bilan almashtirildi.
{r:This dress is being ironed carefully by my mother.} - Bu ko'ylak onam tomonidan ehtiyotkorlik bilan dazmollanmoqda.

text: {r:Roof}[ruːf] – tom. Bu vaziyatda siz o’zingiz tanigan xohlagan {p:Ruf}at ismli insonni {h:tom} tagida tasavvur qilishingiz mumkin.
examples: {r:The roof has been repaired after the storm.} - Tom bo'rondan keyin ta'mirlandi.
{r:Is the roof being cleaned today?} - Tom bugun tozalanmoqdami?
{r:Our old house's roof has never been painted.} - Eski uyimizning tomi hech qachon bo'yalmagan.
{r:New materials are being used for the roof now.} - Tom uchun endi yangi materiallar ishlatilmoqda.

text: {r:Knock}[nɒk] – taqillatmoq. Tasavvur qiling eshingiz {h:taqillyapti}. Borib ochsangiz bolalaringiz eshikka qarab {p:nok} otyapti ekan qanchalik dursillar ekan deb.
examples: {r:The door has been knocked on many times.} - Eshik ko'p marta taqillatilgan.
{r:Is the door being knocked on now?} - Eshik hozir taqillatilmoqdami?
{r:The sound has been heard from the window.} - Tovush derazadan eshitilgan.
{r:I knock on the door to call children for breakfast.} - Bolalarni nonushtaga chaqirish uchun eshikni taqillataman.

text: {r:Flower}[ˈflaʊər] - gul. O'zbekistonda kundan-kunga mashhurlikka erishayotgan {p:FLAV}is ichimligining endi {h:gul}dan qilingan turi ham sotuvga chiqarilmoqda.
examples: {r:These flowers have been grown in our garden.} - Bu gullar bog'imizda o'stirilgan.
{r:Are the flowers being watered now?} - Gullar hozir sug'orilmoqdami?
{r:A beautiful blue flower has been found by my friend.} - Do'stim tomonidan chiroyli ko'k gul topildi.
{r:I am a beginner with flowers.} - Gullar bo'yicha men boshlang'ichman(novichok).

text: {r:Storm}[stɔːm] – to’fon, bo’ron. Qadimgi zamonda baliqchilar to’riga ulkan sazan tushib qolsa ularni qo’yib yuborishgan. Chunki ulkan sazanni tutib olish bo’ronni olib keladi deya hisoblashgan. Menda ham kecha {p:S}azan {p:TO’RIM}ga tushib qolibdi. {h:Bo’ron} bo’lib ketmasin deb qo’yib yubordim.
examples: {r:The big trees have been broken by the storm.} - Katta daraxtlar bo'ron tomonidan sindirildi.
{r:Is a new storm being formed now?} - Hozir yangi bo'ron shakllanmoqdami?
{r:Yes, a new storm is now being formed.} - Ha yangi bo'ron shakllanmoqda.
{r:Sardor is watching news about the storm.} - Sardor bo'ron haqidagi yangiliklarni tomosha qilyapti.

text: {r:Battery}[ˈbætəri] - batareya. Bir xil so'zlar!
examples: {r:The car battery has been charged fully.} - Avtomobil akkumulyatori to'liq zaryadlangan.
{r:Is the phone battery being replaced today?} - Telefon batareyasi bugun almashtirilmoqdami?
{r:A new battery has been bought for this toy.} - Bu o'yinchoq uchun yangi batareya sotib olindi.
{r:Extra batteries are being kept in the bag.} - Qo'shimcha batareyalar sumkada saqlanmoqda.

text: {r:Machine}[məˈʃiːn] - mashina(avtomobil emas), uskuna, jihoz, qurilma. Bir xil so'zlar.
examples: {r:This old machine has been used for many years.} - Bu eski mashina ko'p yillar davomida ishlatilgan.
{r:The big machine is being repaired now.} - Katta mashina hozir ta'mirlanmoqda.
{r:The new washing machine has been delivered to my home.} - Yangi kir yuvish mashinasi uyimga yetkazildi.
{r:All the necessary parts are being bought for the machine.} - Mashina uchun barcha kerakli qismlar sotib olinmoqda.

text: {r:Pass}[pæs] – uzatmoq, o’tmoq. Futbol o’ynayotgandik, qanot o’yinchisiga {p:pass} ber desam, paslik qilib topni {h:uzatmadi}.
examples: {r:The ball has been passed to your friend.} - To'p do'stingizga uzatilgan.
{r:Is the key being passed from hand to hand?} - Kalit qo'ldan-qo'lga o'tmoqdami?
{r:Our class has never passed this difficult test.} - Bizning sinfimiz bu qiyin testdan hech qachon o'tmagan.
{r:My sister has passed her exams.} - Mening singlim imtihonlardan o'tdi.

text: {r:For}[fɔː] – fura. Pushti rangdagi {p:fur}a faqat ayol haydovchilar {h:uchun}.
examples: {r:This gift has been bought for your mother.} - Bu sovg'a onangiz uchun sotib olingan.
{r:Is this song being played for us?} - Bu qo'shiq biz uchun ijro etilmoqdami?
{r:Yes, this song is being played for us.} - Ha bu qo'shiq biz uchun ijro etilmoqda.
{r:Delicious dinner is being prepared for our guests.} - Mehmonlarimiz uchun mazali kechki ovqat tayyorlanmoqda.

text: {r:Round}[raʊnd] - dumaloq. Bu vaziyatda {h:dumaloq} shakldagi {p:RAND}ani tasavvur qilishingiz mumkin.
examples: {r:The big table has been made round.} - Katta stol dumaloq qilingan.
{r:Are new round plates being bought for the party?} - Ziyofat uchun yangi dumaloq likopchalar sotib olinmoqdami?
{r:This ball has always been round.} - Bu to'p har doim yumaloq bo'lgan.
{r:Many things are being built in a round shape now.} - Hozir ko'plab narsalar dumaloq shaklda qurilmoqda.

text: {r:Early}[ˈɜːli] - erta. Tasavvur qiling turli sayyoralar o'rtasidagi majlisga {p:YERLI}lar har doim {h:erta} kelishar ekan.
examples: {r:Breakfast has been served early today.} - Bugun nonushta erta tayyorlandi.
{r:Is the new show being started early?} - Yangi shou erta boshlanmoqdami?
{r:The work has been finished surprisingly early.} - Ish ajablanarli darajada erta tugatildi.
{r:New classes are being offered early in the morning.} - Har ertalab yangi darslar taklif qilinmoqda.

text: {r:Complete}[kəmˈpliːt] - tugatmoq, bitirmoq; to'liq, butunlay. Bizning 90 yoshli qo'shnimiz haykaltarosh {p:KAMPIR IT} haykali loyihasini 1 yilda {h:bitirdi}.
examples: {r:The homework has been completed by my brother.} - Uy vazifasi akam tomonidan tugatildi.
{r:All tasks have been completed on time.} - Barcha vazifalar o'z vaqtida bajarildi.
{r:New houses are being completed every month.} - Har oy yangi uylar qurib bitkazilmoqda.
{r:This is a complete list of necessary things.} - Bu kerakli narsalarning to'liq ro'yxati.
{r:My father is complete opposite of my mother.} - Dadam (xarakteri bo'yicha) onamning g'irt teskarisi.

text: {r:Sentence}[ˈsɛntəns] – gap, jumla. Mashhur tennischi juftlik har kuni ko’proq shug’ullanib yanada yaxshiroq natijalarga erishish uchun bir-biriga “{p:SEN TENIS}, men tenis, bolalarimiz ham tenis” degan {h:gap} aytar ekan.
examples: {r:A new sentence has been written in this book.} - Bu kitobda yangi gap yozilgan.
{r:Are all the sentences being read now?} - Barcha gaplar hozir o'qilmoqdami?
{r:Many different sentences have been learned today.} - Bugun ko'plab turli gaplar o'rganildi.
{r:Difficult sentences are being explained by the teacher.} - Qiyin gaplar o'qituvchi tomonidan tushuntirilmoqda.

text: {r:About}[əˈbaʊt] – haqida. {p:Ab}dullajon {p:out}dan to’pni o’yinga kiritayapti. U futbol {h:haqida} ko'p narsa biladi. Xo’sh siz ham qiziqasizmi? Bu ilovada futbolga tegishli shaxslarni va atamalarni ham qo’shishimiz mumkin.
examples: {r:Many stories have been told about this old house.} - Bu eski uy haqida ko'p hikoyalar aytilgan.
{r:Are we being told the truth about this?} - Bizga bu haqida haqiqat aytilmoqdami?
{r:Everything has been said about this shower.} - Bu dush haqida hamma narsa aytilgan.
{r:Interesting facts are being written about our country.} - Mamlakatimiz haqida qiziqarli faktlar yozilmoqda.

text: {r:Fruit}[fruːt] – meva. {p:FR}ansuz {p:UT}yuglari juda ajoyib ko’rinishda bo’ladi. Ularning shakli {h:mevalar} ko’rinishida yasaladi. Masalan bananli utyug, qulupnayli utyug.
examples: {r:Fresh fruit has been bought from the shop.} - Do'kondan yangi meva sotib olindi.
{r:We usually eat this fruit after dinner.} - Odatda bu mevalarni kechki ovqatdan so'ng yeymiz.
{r:This big yellow fruit has been eaten by the child.} - Bu katta sariq meva bola tomonidan yeyilgan.
{r:Different fruits are being sold in the market now.} - Bozorda endi turli mevalar sotilmoqda.

text: {r:Winner}[ˈwɪnər] - g'olib. Win(yutmoq) so'zidan yasalgan.
examples: {r:The winner has been announced on TV.} - G'olib televizorda e'lon qilindi.
{r:Is the prize being given to the winner now?} - Sovrin g'olibga hozir berilmoqdami?
{r:Our team has become the winner many times.} - Bizning jamoamiz ko'p marta g'olib bo'lgan.
{r:New winners are celebrating today.} - Bugun yangi g'oliblar nishonlashmoqda.

text: {r:Countryman}[ˈkʌntrɪmən] - vatandosh. Country(davlat) va man(kishi) so'zlarining birlashuvidan yasalgan.
examples: {r:Many countrymen have been invited to our city.} - Shahrimizga ko'plab vatandoshlar taklif qilindi.
{r:Is the old countryman's story being told again?} - Eski vatandoshning hikoyasi yana aytilmoqdami?
{r:His name has been known by many countrymen.} - Uning ismi ko'plab vatandoshlar tomonidan tanilgan.(known bu yerda mashhur degani)
{r:Local traditions are being learned by our countrymen.} - Mahalliy an'analar yosh vatandoshlarimiz tomonidan o'rganilmoqda.

text: {r:Mountainous}[ˈmaʊntɪnəs] - tog'li. Mountain(tog') so'zidan yasalgan.
examples: {r:The new road has been built <through> a mountainous area.} - Yangi yo'l tog'li hudud <orqali> qurilgan.
{r:Is this big mountainous region being explored for tourism?} - Bu katta tog'li hudud turizm uchun o'rganilmoqdami?
{r:Many stories have been created about the mountainous places.} - Tog'li joylar haqida ko'plab hikoyalar yaratilgan.
{r:New roads are being built in the mountainous regions.} - Tog'li hududlarda yangi yo'llar qurilmoqda.

text: {r:True}[truː] – to’gri, haqiqat. Oldinlari institutga kirish uchun imtihonlarda bunkerlar bo’lar edi. Bunkerdagilarning vazifasi pul evaziga imtihonda o’tirgan talabaning qo’ng'iroqlariga javob berib imtihondan o’tishga yordamlashish edi. {p:TRU}bkani ko’tarasan va {h:to’g'ri} javobni aytasan. Lekin bu tizim tufayli ko’pchilik haqiqatdanda tayyorlangan abityurentlar imtihonlardan o’ta olishmadi.
examples: {r:I used to believe that story was true.} - Men bu hikoyani haqiqat deb ishonardim.
{r:Did your friend use to think this news was true?} - Do'stingiz bu yangilikni haqiqat deb o'ylarmidi?
{r:It didn't use to be true that he was tired.} - U charchaganligi rost emas edi.
{r:My parents used to know what was true.} - Ota-onam nima haqiqat ekanligini bilar edi.

text: {r:Happen}[ˈhæpən] - sodir bo'lmoq. Biror ishni boshlashdan oldin ko'p o'ylanmaslik kerak va '{p:HAPPA}' deya boshlash kerak, shunda u amalda {h:sodir bo'lish}i mumkin.
examples: {r:What used to happen when you were late?} - Kechikganingizda nima sodir bo'lar edi?
{r:Ali used to wonder why this happened.} - Ali nima uchun bu sodir bo'lganligiga hayron qolar edi.
{r:That kind of thing didn't use to happen often.} - Bunday narsalar tez-tez sodir bo'lmas edi.
{r:Many big things used to happen in this city.} - Bu shaharda ko'plab katta narsalar sodir bo'lar edi.

text: {r:Waiter}[ˈweɪtər] - ofitsiant
examples: {r:My brother used to work as a waiter.} - Akam ofitsiant bo'lib ishlar edi.
{r:Did you use to give the waiter money?} - Siz ofitsiantga pul berarmidingiz?
{r:That waiter didn't use to be kind.} - O'sha ofitsiant mehribon emas edi.
{r:They used to know every waiter in this hotel.} - Ular bu mehmonxonadagi har bir ofitsiantni tanir edi.

text: {r:Barber}[ˈbɑːbər] - sartarosh. Mana bu 'Menga {p:BARIBIR}' nomli sartaroshxona. Bu yerdagi {h:sartaroshlarga} haqiqatdan bari bir. Eng xunuk soch fasonlarini shu yerda topasiz, kirsangiz sizni ham qo'ykalla qilib qo'yishadi.
examples: {r:I used to visit the barber every month.} - Men har oy sartaroshga borar edim.
{r:This barber has been single for a long time.} - Bu sartarosh ancha vaqtdan beri yolg'iz.
{r:She didn't use to like this barber's style.} - U bu sartaroshning uslubini yoqtirmas edi.
{r:Our old barber used to tell funny stories.} - Bizning eski sartaroshimiz kulgili hikoyalar aytar edi.

text: {r:Move}[muːv] – ko’chmoq. Madagaskar multfilmini eslang Aleks va uning do’stlari Madagaskarga {h:ko’chgan}dan so’ng. 'Ay layk {p:muv} it' qo’shig’ini aytishni boshlaydi.
examples: {r:We used to move to different houses every year.} - Biz har yili turli uylarga ko'char edik.
{r:Did your family use to move a lot?} - Oilangiz ko'p ko'chib yurarmidi?
{r:They didn't use to move often.} - Ular tez-tez ko'chmas edi.
{r:This big old table used to move easily.} - Bu katta eski stol osonlikcha siljir edi.

text: {r:Normally}[ˈnɔːməli] - odatda; normalniy, odatdagidek. Agar bu so'z gap boshida kelsa odatda ma'nosini bildiradi. Agar gapning o'rtasi yoki oxirida kelsa normalniy, odatdagidek ma'nolarini bildiradi.
examples: {r:I used to wake up normally at 7 o'clock.} - Men odatda soat 7da uyg'onar edim.
{r:Our team normally used to start working at 9 o'clock.} - Bizning jamoamiz odatda 9 da ish boshlar edi.
{r:The dog didn't use to play normally when it was cold.} - Sovuq bo'lganida kuchuk odatdagidek o'ynamas edi.
{r:My brother used to eat normally every day.} - Akam har kuni odatdagidek ovqatlanar edi.

text: {r:Fit}[fɪt] – sog’lom, baquvvat, tetik; mos kelmoq, yarashmoq. Shu kunlarda keng qo’llaniladigan {p:fit}ness so’zi mana shu so’zdan olingan. So’zning ikkinchi ma'nosini esda saqlash uchun adabiyot darsligida o’tiladigan shoir Fitratni eslang. Kitobdagi rasmida bosh kiyimi ham va u {p:Fit}ratga juda {h:yarashib} turibdi.
examples: {r:These old clothes used to fit me.} - Bu eski kiyimlar menga mos kelar edi.
{r:Did this hat use to fit your head?} - Bu shlyapa boshingizga mos kelarmidi?
{r:His new shoes didn't use to fit him well.} - Uning yangi poyabzallari unga yaxshi mos kelmas edi.
{r:That job used to fit his skills.} - O'sha ish uning ko'nikmalariga juda mos kelar edi.

text: {r:Young}[jʌŋ] – yosh. {p:Yang}i avlod kim? Bu {h:yosh} avlod, bizda yosh avlod qadrlanadi, ularni erkalaymiz, tarbiya beramiz va yangi telefon, yangi kiyimlar olib beramiz.
examples: {r:When I was young, I used to play on the street.} - Yoshligimda men ko'chada o'ynar edim.
{r:Did your mother use to travel a lot when she was young?} - Onangiz yoshligida ko'p sayohat qilarmidi?
{r:They didn't use to work very hard when they were young.} - Ular yoshligida juda qattiq ishlashmas edi.
{r:Ali used to read many books when he was young.} - Ali yoshligida ko'plab kitoblarni o'qir edi.

text: {r:Clothes}[kloʊðz] – kiyimlar. Tasavvur qiling sizni {p:KILOYIZ} ko’payib endi eski {h:kiyimlaringiz} sig’mayapti, Shrek bo’lib ketyapsiz. Ehtiyot bo’ling Shrekdek yashillashib ham ketmang.
examples: {r:I used to wear colorful clothes.} - Men rangli kiyimlar kiyar edim.
{r:Did you use to buy new clothes often?} - Siz tez-tez yangi kiyimlar sotib olarmidingiz?
{r:They didn't use to have many clothes.} - Ularda ko'p kiyimlar bo'lmas edi.
{r:My sister used to make her own clothes.} - Singlim o'zining kiyimlarini o'zi tikar edi.

text: {r:Party}[ˈpɑːti] – kecha, vecherinka. Ekologik {p:partiy}a a'zolari karantin payti {h:vecherinka} uyushtirishibdi, qo’shimchasiga juda ko’p shashliklar pishirib havoga ham zarar yetkazishdi. Xullas ular ekologiyani asrash o'rniga bazm uyushtirish ekologiyani buzishibdi.
examples: {r:We used to go to parties every week.} - Biz har hafta ziyofatlarga borar edik.
{r:Did she use to like big parties?} - U katta ziyofatlarni yoqtirarmidi?
{r:They didn't use to invite many people to their parties.} - Ular ziyofatlariga ko'p odamlarni taklif qilishmas edi.
{r:Our friend used to organize the best parties.} - Do'stimiz eng yaxshi ziyofatlarni uyushtirar edi.

text: {r:Petrol}[ˈpɛtrəl] – benzin, kerosin. Mana bu {p:PIT}larning {p:ROL}igi. {h:Benzin} bilan yuradi faqat.
examples: {r:This old car used to use a lot of petrol.} - Bu eski mashina ko'p benzin ishlatar edi.
{r:Did your father use to check the petrol level?} - Otangiz benzin darajasini tekshirarmidi?
{r:We didn't use to buy much petrol.} - Biz ko'p benzin sotib olmasdik.
{r:The price of petrol used to be very cheap.} - Benzin narxi juda arzon bo'lar edi.

text: {r:Bath}[bæθ] – cho’milish, yuvinish. Cho’milish uchun uyda yetarli sharoitim yo’q. Shuning uchun har safar{p:BAS}ketbol savatchasiga shlankani osib qo’yib suvni tomchilatib {h:yuvinaman}.
examples: {r:I used to take a cold bath in summer.} - Men yozda sovuq vanna qabul qilar edim.(take ning ma'nolari ko'p bu yerda qabul qilmoq ma'nosida kelyapti)
{r:Did your child use to play in the bath?} - Farzandingiz vannada o'ynarmidi?
{r:They didn't use to have a big bath in their new home because it was still being built.} - Ularning yangi uyida katta vanna bo'lmas edi chunki uy hali ham qurilayotgan edi.
{r:Taking a bath used to be a weekly event for us.} - Cho'milish biz uchun haftalik tadbir(ish, odat) bo'lar edi.

text: {r:Same}[seɪm] - bir xil, ayni. Haykaltaroshlikda odamning ko'rinishini eng yaxshi chiqarib beroladigan va {h:bir xil} qiyofani ko'rsatib beroladigan xomashyo bu {p:SEYM}ent bo'lsa kerak.
examples: {r:My friend and I used to wear the same clothes.} - Do'stim ikkalamiz bir xil kiyimlar kiyar edik.
{r:Did they use to always say the same thing?} - Ular doim bir xil gapni aytisharmidi?
{r:This problem didn't use to be <the same as before>.} - Bu muammo <avvalgidek bir xil> emas edi.
{r:We used to come home at the same time every day.} - Biz har kuni bir xil vaqtda uyga kelar edik.

text: {r:Movie}[ˈmuːvi] – film. Kecha ajoyib bir kino ko’rdim. Film Nobel mukofotini olgan olim haqida. {p:MU}kofot {p:VI}rusga davo topganligi uchun berilgan bu {h:kinoda}.
examples: {r:We used to watch a movie every weekend.} - Biz har dam olish kunlari film ko'rar edik.
{r:Did you use to like horror movies?} - Siz qo'rqinchli filmlarni yoqtirarmidingiz?
{r:That old cinema didn't use to show many new movies.} - O'sha eski kinoteatr ko'p yangi filmlarni ko'rsatmas edi.
{r:My favorite movie used to be 'Star Wars'.} - Mening sevimli filmim 'Yulduzlar jangi' edi.

text: {r:Horror}[ˈhɒrər] – qo’rquv, dahshat. Men itning akillashidan {h:qo’rquvga} tushaman. Shuning uchun menga “It {p:HURAR}, karvon o’tar” demang. Karvon o’tsa o’taversin lekin itning hurishi meni dahshatga soladi.
examples: {r:My sister used to love horror stories.} - Singlim qo'rqinchli hikoyalarni juda yoqtirar edi.
{r:Did you use to be afraid of horror movies?} - Siz qo'rqinchli filmlardan qo'rqarmidingiz?
{r:That old house didn't use to give me horror.} - O'sha eski uy menga qo'rquv bermas edi.
{r:Many children used to read horror books.} - Ko'plab bolalar qo'rqinchli kitoblarni o'qir edi.

text:
{r:Ride}[raɪd] – minmoq, haydamoq. 
O'tgan zamon shakllari - rode, ridden. 
Tasavvur qiling mashhur {p:Ray}hon {p:D}amas {h:haydayapti}.
examples: {r:I used to ride my bicycle to school.} - Men maktabga velosipedda minib borar edim.
{r:Did your friend use to ride a horse?} - Do'stingiz ot minarmidi?
{r:They didn't use to ride the bus often.} - Ular avtobusda tez-tez minmas edilar.
{r:Children used to ride their bikes in the park.} - Bolalar bog'da o'z velosipedlarida minar edilar.

text: {r:Train}[treɪn] – poyezd. Bu o’rinda mashhur futbol {p:treyn}erlarini {h:poyezd} ishchilari sifatida tasavvur qiling. Agar bu mavzudan yiroq bo’lsangiz, o’zingiz tanigan maktab yoki universitet sport trenerlarini ham tasavvur qilishingiz mumkin.
examples: {r:We used to take the train to the city.} - Biz shaharga poyezdda borar edik.
{r:The fast train used to be expensive and clean.} - Tezkor poyezd qimmat va toza bo'lar edi.
{r:This old train didn't use to run very fast.} - Bu eski poyezd juda tez yurmas edi.
{r:What is the exact arrival time for this train?} - Bu poyezdning aniq kelish vaqti qachon?

text: {r:Cinema}[ˈsɪnəmə] - kinoteatr. Toshkentda yaqinda 'Ha {p:SENIMI}' nomli {h:kinoteatr} ochildi.
examples: {r:This old building used to be a cinema.} - Bu eski bino kinoteatr bo'lgan edi.
{r:Did you use to go to the cinema every week?} - Siz har hafta kinoteatrga borarmidingiz?
{r:There didn't use to be many cinemas here.} - Bu yerda ko'p kinoteatrlar bo'lmas edi.
{r:My friends and I used to meet at the cinema.} - Do'stlarim va men kinoteatrda uchrashar edik.

text: {r:Boring}[ˈbɔːrɪŋ] – zerikarli. Agar hayotingiz {h:zerikarli} tuyulsa kinoteatrga {p:BORING}, bo’lmasa teatrga boring, yo’qsa sayohatga BORING, yo’qsa zooparkka boring. Xullas qayergadir BORING zeriksangiz.
examples: {r:This book used to be very boring.} - Bu kitob juda zerikarli edi.
{r:Did your job use to be boring?} - Ishingiz zerikarli edimi?
{r:The lessons didn't use to be so boring.} - Darslar bunchalik zerikarli emas edi.
{r:I used to think learning English was boring.} - Ingliz tilini o'rganishni zerikarli deb o'ylar edim.

text: {r:Person}[ˈpɜːsən] - shaxs, odam. O'zbek tilida ham qo'llaniladigan {p:person}al va {p:person}aj so'zlari aynan mana shu so'zdan yasalgan.
examples: {r:He used to be a very kind person.} - U juda mehribon odam edi.
{r:Did your teacher use to be a tall person?} - O'qituvchingiz baland bo'yli odam edimi?
{r:I didn't use to know that person.} - Men u odamni tanimas edim.
{r:That person used to live in this old house.} - Bu eski uyda o'sha kishi yashar edi.

text: {r:Twice}[twaɪs] – ikki marta. Tualetga kirsam g’aroyib voqeani guvohi bo’ldim. {p:Tva}letda {p:ays}bergni ko’rdim, bitta emas {h:ikkita} aysberg.
examples: {r:I'm going to visit the park twice this week.} - Men bu hafta bog'ga ikki marta bormoqchiman.
{r:Are you going to call your friend twice today?} - Bugun do'stingizga ikki marta qo'ng'iroq qilmoqchimisiz?
{r:They aren't going to eat outside twice in one day.} - Ular bir kunda ikki marta tashqarida ovqatlanmoqchi emas.
{r:My brother is going to clean his room twice this weekend.} - Akam bu dam olish kunlari o'z xonasini ikki marta tozalamoqchi.

text: {r:Needy}[ˈniːdi] - muhtoj, zarur bo'lgan. Need(kerak, lozim) so'zining sifat shakli va asosan odamlarga nisbatan ishlatiladi. Mnemonik namuna uchun 9 - darsdagi need ga qarang.
examples: {r:We're going to help the needy people in our city.} - Biz shahrimizdagi muhtoj odamlarga yordam bermoqchimiz.
{r:Is she going to donate money to the needy?} - U muhtojlarga pul xayriya qilmoqchimi?
{r:Ali isn't going to ignore the needy this time.} - Ali bu safar muhtojlarni e'tiborsiz qoldirmoqchi emas.
{r:Her parents are going to support a needy family.} - Uning ota-onasi bir muhtoj oilani qo'llab-quvvatlamoqchi.

text: {r:Exactly}[ɪɡˈzæktli] - aniq, tiniq, tochno. Olimlarning aytishicha {p:EGIZAKLI} juftliklar bir-biriga {h:aniq} mos keluvchi juftliklar ekan. Bir-biriga mosligidan egizak farzand ko'rib yuborishar ekan.
examples: {r:I'm going to explain it exactly how it happened.} - Men bu qanday sodir bo'lganini aniq tushuntirmoqchiman.
{r:Is she going to follow the instructions exactly?} - U ko'rsatmalarni aniq bajarmoqchimi?
{r:What exactly are you going to eat for breakfast? Butter or eggs?} - Nonushtaga aniq nima yemoqchisiz? Saryog'mi yoki tuxum?
{r:The scientist is going to measure the amount exactly.} - Olim miqdorni aniq o'lchamoqchi.

text: {r:Driver}[ˈdraɪvər] - haydovchi. Drive(haydamoq) so'zidan yasalgan.
examples: {r:I'm going to call the taxi driver now.} - Men hozir taksi haydovchisini chaqirmoqchiman.
{r:Is your father going to thank the bus driver?} - Otangiz avtobus haydovchisiga minnatdorchilik bildirmoqchimi?
{r:They aren't going to hire a new driver for their company.} - Ular o'z kompaniyasi uchun yangi haydovchi yollamoqchi emas.
{r:My friend is going to talk to the truck driver.} - Do'stim yuk mashinasi haydovchisi bilan gaplashmoqchi.

text: {r:Central}[ˈsɛntrəl] - markaziy, sentral. Bir xil so'zlar!
examples: {r:We're going to visit the central market today.} - Biz bugun markaziy bozorga bormoqchimiz.
{r:Is the new shop going to be in the central area?} - Yangi do'kon markaziy hududda bo'ladimi?
{r:They aren't going to leave the central station yet.} - Ular hali markaziy stansiyani tark etmoqchi emas.
{r:Tourists are going to explore the central part of the city.} - Sayyohlar shaharning markaziy qismini o'rganmoqchi.

text: {r:Decision}[dɪˈsɪʒən] - qaror. Decide(qaror qilmoq) so'zidan olingan. Mnemonik namuna uchun 13 - darsdagi decide ga qarang.
examples: {r:I'm going to make a big decision soon.} - Men tez orada katta qaror qilmoqchiman.
{r:Nobody is going to explain this decision to us.} - Hech kim bizga bu qarorni tushuntirmoqchi emas.
{r:They aren't going to change their decision now.} - Ular hozir qarorini o'zgartirmoqchi emas.
{r:My parents are going to support my decision <no matter what>.} - Ota-onam mening qarorimni <nima bo'lsa ham> qo'llab-quvvatlamoqchi.

text: {r:Invitation}[ˌɪnvɪˈteɪʃən] - taklifnoma. Invite(taklif qilmoq) so'zidan yasalgan. Mnemonik namuna uchun 13 - darsdagi invite ga qarang.
examples: {r:We're going to send the invitations next week.} - Biz keyingi hafta taklifnomalarni yubormoqchimiz.
{r:Is he going to accept the invitation to the party?} - U ziyofatga taklifnomani qabul qilmoqchimi?
{r:They aren't going to ignore the invitation to the wedding.} - Ular to'y taklifnomasini e'tiborsiz qoldirmoqchi emas.
{r:My sister is going to prepare many invitations.} - Singlim ko'plab taklifnomalarni tayyorlamoqchi.

text: {r:Future}[ˈfjuːtʃər] – kelajak. O’zbek futbolining {h:kelajagi} yo’q. Bizda {p:fu}tbol {p:chir}igan.(Namuna uchun berildi. hech kimni shaxsiyatiga dahl qilmoqchi emasmiz!)
examples: {r:I'm going to plan for my future career.} - Men kelajakdagi karyeramni rejalashtirmoqchiman.
{r:Is she going to think about the future of the company?} - U kompaniyaning kelajagi haqida o'ylamoqchimi?
{r:They aren't going to worry about the future too much.} - Ular kelajak haqida juda ko'p tashvishlanmoqchi emas.
{r:Our parents are going to save money for our future.} - Ota-onamiz bizning kelajagimiz uchun pul yig'moqchi.

text: {r:Intend}[ɪnˈtɛnd] – niyat qilmoq, rejalashtirmoq. Ot so'z turkumiga xos shakli intention(niyat, reja). Odamlar katta uylar qurish uchun tenderlar uyushtirishadi. Sichqonlar {p:in}lar qurish uchun {p:tend}erlar qilishar ekan. Ular odamlarning har bir uy proyektining ichida o’zlarining inlarini qurishni {h:niyat qilishgan}.
examples: {r:They intend to open a new shop.} - Ular yangi do'kon ochishni niyat qilishmoqda.
{r:The company intends to hire new workers.} - Kompaniya yangi ishchilar yollashni rejalashtiryapti.
{r:I'm going to explain my intention clearly.} - Men o'z niyatimni aniq tushuntirmoqchiman.
{r:Is she going to change her intention to study abroad?} - U chet elda o'qish niyatini o'zgartirmoqchimi?

text: {r:Sure}[ʃʊər] – aniq, ishonchi komil bo’lgan, albatta. {p:Shur}ik Ninani o’g’rilardan qutqarishga {h:ishonchi komil}.
examples: {r:I'm going to <make sure> everything is ready for the party.} - Men ziyofatga hamma narsa tayyorligiga <ishonch hosil qilmoqchiman>.
{r:Is she going to be sure about her plan?} - U o'z rejasi haqida ishonch hosil qilmoqchimi?
{r:Sure. She is going to be sure about her plan.} - Albatta. U o'z rejasi haqida ishonch hosil qilmoqchi.
{r:We're going to check everything to be sure.} - Biz ishonch hosil qilish uchun hamma narsani tekshirmoqchimiz.

text: {r:Sky}[skaɪ] - osmon.
examples: {r:The sky is going to be clear tonight.} - Bu kecha osmon ochiq bo'ladi.
{r:Are you going to watch the sky for stars?} - Yulduzlarni ko'rish uchun osmonni kuzatmoqchimisiz?
{r:It's not going to rain; the sky is blue.} - Yomg'ir yog'moqchi emas; osmon ko'k.
{r:We're going to enjoy the beautiful sky this evening.} - Biz bu oqshom chiroyli osmondan zavqlanmoqchimiz.

text:
{r:Clear}[klɪər] – aniq, tiniq, tushunarli.
 - Amaki shaharga davolanishga ketayotgan bo’lsangiz nega pul olmadingiz.
 - {p:Kli}nika {p:Ir}odaniki, jiyanim bo’ladi. Tushunarlimi?
 - Tushunarli.
examples: {r:The sky is going to be clear tomorrow.} - Osmon ertaga ochiq bo‘ladi.
{r:The instructions were clear to everyone.} - Ko‘rsatmalar hammaga tushunarli edi.
{r:The road is clear for us.} - Biz uchun yo‘l ochiq.
{r:Her intentions are clear.} - Uning niyatlari aniq.

text: {r:Cloud}[klaʊd] – bulut. Bu holatda Jan {p:KLOD} vandamning {h:bulutlar} orasida uchib yurganini tasavvur qilishingiz mumkin.
examples: {r:That big cloud is going to bring heavy rain.} - Bu katta bulut kuchli yomg'ir olib kelmoqchi.
{r:Are we going to see many clouds tomorrow?} - Ertaga ko'p bulutlarni ko'ramizmi?
{r:The sky isn't going to stay cloudy all day.} - Osmon butun kun bulutli bo'lib turmaydi.
{r:She's going to take photos of the interesting clouds.} - U qiziqarli bulutlarning suratini olmoqchi.

text: {r:Dear}[dɪər] – qadrli, qadrdon. Tasavvur qiling sizning uchun hayotda eng {h:qadrli} inson bu {p:DIYOR}.
examples: {r:I'm going to write a letter to my dear grandmother.} - Men qadrli buvimga xat yozmoqchiman.
{r:Are you going to call your dear mother today?} - Bugun qadrli onangizga telefon qilmoqchimisiz?
{r:He isn't going to forget his dear friends.} - U qadrli do'stlarini unutmoqchi emas.
{r:We're going to visit our dear buyers next week.} - Biz kelasi hafta qadrli xaridorlarimiznikiga tashrif buyurmoqchimiz.

text: {r:Ready}[ˈrɛdi] – tayyor. - Ekinlardan qaysi biri birinchi tayyor bo’ladi? Har doim {p:redi}ska birinchi {h:tayyor} bo’ladi
examples: {r:The food is going to be ready for dinner soon.} - Ovqat tushlik uchun tez orada tayyor bo'ladi.
{r:Are you going to be ready on time for the party?} - Ziyofatga vaqtida tayyor bo'lasizmi?
{r:Nobody is ready to sleep.} - Hech kim uxlashga tayyor emas.
{r:We're going to get ready for the trip quickly.} - Biz safarga tez tayyor bo'lmoqchimiz.

text: {r:Shelf}[ʃɛlf] – polka, javon. Bizning {p:SHEF} povarni o’zining maxsus {h:polkasi} bor. Bitta polkada idishlar, boshqasida pichoqlar, boshqasida qoshiq va sanchqi turadi. Juda tartibli odam lekin menga yoqmaydigan tarafi sochini yashilga bo’yab olgan. Ba'zan o’sha yashil sochlari polkasiga ham tushib ishtahamni bug’adi.
examples: {r:I'm going to repair this old shelf tomorrow.} - Men bu eski javonni ertaga tuzatmoqchiman.
{r:Is he going to build new shelves for his books?} - U kitoblari uchun yangi javonlar yasamoqchimimi?
{r:The new books aren't going to fit in this small shelf.} - Yangi kitoblar bu kichik javonga sig'maydi.
{r:They're going to organize the yellow shelf first.} - Ular birinchi bo'lib sariq javonni tartibga solmoqchi.

text: {r:Unique}[juˈniːk] - nodir, noyob, unikal.
examples: {r:This gift is going to be unique and special.} - Bu sovg'a noyob va maxsus bo'ladi.
{r:Does this guy have a unique name?} - Bu yigitning noyob ismi bormi?
{r:Her new style isn't going to be unique.} - Uning yangi uslubi endi noyob bo'lmaydi.
{r:This girl's hair is very unique.} - Bu qizning sochi juda noyob.

text: {r:Defect}[ˈdiːfɛkt] - defekt, kamchilik. Rus tilidan o'zlashtirilgan defekt so'zi o'zbek tilida ham keng qo'llaniladi.
examples: {r:They're going to check the product for any defects.} - Ular mahsulotni har qanday nuqsonlar uchun tekshirmoqchi.
{r:Is the factory going to fix these defects quickly?} - Zavod bu nuqsonlarni tezda tuzatmoqchimi?
{r:This new phone isn't going to have any defects.} - Bu yangi telefonda hech qanday nuqson bo'lmoqchi emas.
{r:We're going to report the defect to the manager.} - Biz nuqson haqida menejerga xabar bermoqchimiz.

text: {r:Arrange}[əˈreɪndʒ] - tashkillashtirmoq, uyushtirmoq. Mening {p:ER}im {p:RENJ} Roverda {h:tashkillashtirgan} Merrimi marosimini.
examples: {r:The meeting has already been arranged.} - Uchrashuv allaqachon tashkil qilingan.
{r:Who is going to arrange the cake for the wedding?} - To'y uchun to'rtni kim tashkillashtirmoqchi?
{r:They aren't going to arrange transportation for everyone.} - Ular hamma uchun transportni tashkil qilmoqchi emas.
{r:We're going to arrange everything nicely for the guests.} - Biz mehmonlar uchun hamma narsani chiroyli tartibga solmoqchimiz.

text: {r:Appointment}[əˈpɔɪntmənt] - uchrashuv. Appoint(belgilamoq, tayinlamoq) so'zidan yasalgan.
examples: {r:She's going to make a doctor's appointment tomorrow.} - U ertaga shifokor bilan uchrashuv belgilamoqchi.
{r:Are they going to have an appointment with the lawyer?} - Ularning advokat bilan uchrashuvi bormi?
{r:He isn't going to miss his important appointment.} - U muhim uchrashuvini o'tkazib yubormoqchi emas.
{r:We're going to confirm the appointment by phone.} - Biz uchrashuvni telefon orqali tasdiqlamoqchimiz.

text: {r:Meat}[miːt] – go’sht. Instagramda taniqli blogger {p:MIT}ti har xil mahsulotlarning reklamasi orqali pul topadi. Uning oxirgi reklamasi {h:go’sht} haqida edi.
examples: {r:I will cook meat for dinner tomorrow.} - Ertaga kechki ovqat uchun go'sht pishiraman.
{r:My sister will buy fresh meat from the market.} - Singlim bozordan yangi go'sht sotib oladi.
{r:The chef will prepare delicious meat for the guests.} - Oshpaz mehmonlar uchun mazali go'sht tayyorlaydi.
{r:Your family will enjoy the meat at the party.} - Oilangiz ziyofatda go'shtdan bahramand bo'ladi.

text: {r:Lamp}[læmp] - lampochka. Bir xil so'zlar!
examples: {r:I will buy a new lamp for my table.} - Men stolim uchun yangi chiroq sotib olaman.
{r:My friend will <turn on> the lamp in the evening.} - Do'stim kechqurun chiroqni <yoqadi>.
{r:The electrician will fix the broken lamp today.} - Elektrik singan chiroqni bugun ta'mirlaydi.
{r:Our parents will replace the old lamp with a new one.} - Ota-onamiz eski chiroqni yangisi bilan almashtiradi.

text: {r:Jeans}[dʒiːnz] - jinsi shim. Bir xil so'zlar!
examples: {r:I will wear my new jeans to the party.} - Men ziyofatga yangi jinsimni kiyaman.
{r:My sister will wash her favorite jeans tonight.} - Singlim sevimli jinsisini kechqurun yuvadi.
{r:Ali will buy blue jeans from that shop.} - Ali o'sha do'kondan ko'k jinsi shim sotib oladi.
{r:Your brother will find comfortable jeans for the trip.} - Akangiz sayohat uchun qulay jinsi shim topadi.

text: {r:Arrangement}[əˈreɪndʒmənt] - tashkil etish; rejalar. Arrange(tashkil etmoq) so'zidan yasalgan. Mnemonik namuna uchun 22 - darsdagi arrange ga qarang.
examples: {r:I will make the arrangement for the meeting.} - Men uchrashuvni tashkillashtiraman.
{r:My team will check the arrangement before the event.} - Jamoam tadbirdan oldin tashkillashtirishni tekshiradi.
{r:The manager will approve the new arrangement.} - Menejer yangi tashkillashtirishni tasdiqlaydi.
{r:We shall finalize the arrangement for the trip next week.} - Biz keyingi hafta sayohat uchun tashkillashtirishni yakunlaymiz.

text: {r:Old}[oʊld] – qari. Ronaldo {p:old} tarafdan {h:qari}, yondan esa juda yosh ko’rinadi.
examples: {r:I will visit my old grandmother this weekend.} - Men bu dam olish kunlari qari buvimni ziyorat qilaman.
{r:Your friend will tell us about the old times.} - Do'stingiz bizga eski kunlar haqida aytadi.
{r:This tree will grow very old here.} - Bu daraxt bu yerda o'sib qariydi.
{r:My parents will share old photos with us.} - Ota-onamiz biz bilan eski fotosuratlarni bo'lishadi.

text: {r:Bread}[brɛd] – non. Siz bu vaziyatda mashhur aktyor {p:Bred} Pittning {h:non} yeyotganini tasavvur qilishingiz mumkin.
examples: {r:I will buy fresh bread from the bakery.} - Men novvoyxonadan yangi non sotib olaman.
{r:Your mother will bake delicious bread for breakfast.} - Onang nonushta uchun mazali non pishiradi.
{r:The children will eat all the bread quickly.} - Bolalar barcha nonni tezda yeyishadi.
{r:We shall share our bread with those in need.} - Biz nonimizni muhtojlar bilan bo'lishamiz.

text: {r:Probably}[ˈprɒbəbli] – ehtimol, balki. Bu {p:pro}fessor {p:bibl}iyadan dars berar ekanlar. {h:Balki} u xristyan missioneridir.
examples: {r:I will probably go to the concert next month.} - Ehtimol keyingi oy konsertga boraman.
{r:She will probably finish her work by evening.} - U balki kechgacha ishini tugatar.
{r:Your family will probably visit us next summer.} - Oilangiz ehtimol, kelasi yozda biznikiga tashrif buyurar.
{r:It will probably rain later today.} - Bugun keyinroq ehtimol, yomg'ir yog'adi.

text: {r:Trip}[trɪp] - sayohat. Mening oshxonamda yashovchi tarakanlar o'zlarining keyingi sayohat marshruti bo'yicha bosh qotirishmoqda. Oila boshlig'i keyingi {h:sayohat} {p:TRUB}a bo'ylab bo'lishi kerakligini aytyapti.
examples: {r:I will plan a short trip for the holidays.} - Men ta'tillar uchun qisqa sayohatni rejalashtiraman.
{r:My friends will join us on this trip.} - Do'stlarim bu sayohatda bizga qo'shiladi.
{r:The children will remember this trip forever.} - Bolalar bu sayohatni abadiy eslaydilar.
{r:We shall enjoy every moment of our trip.} - Biz sayohatimizning har bir lahzasidan zavqlanamiz.

text: {r:Game}[ɡeɪm] - o'yin.
examples: {r:I will watch the football game <tonight>.} - Men <bugun kechqurun> futbol o'yinini ko'raman.
{r:My brother will play a new video game.} - Akam yangi video o'yin o'ynaydi.
{r:The children will enjoy the game together.} - Bolalar o'yindan birgalikda zavqlanishadi.
{r:Our team will win the next game.} - Jamoamiz keyingi o'yinni yutadi.

text:
{r:Lend}[lɛnd] – qarz bermoq, nimadir berib turmoq. 
O'tgan zamon shakllari - lent, lent. 
Xullas og’aynilar sochim qizlarnikidek o’sib ketdi. Endi menga {h:qarz berib} turinglar bitta {p:LENT}a sotib olay.
examples: {r:I will lend you my umbrella if it rains.} - Agar yomg'ir yog'sa, men sizga soyabonimni berib turaman.
{r:My neighbor will lend me his ladder.} - Qo'shnim menga narvonini beradi.
{r:The bank will lend money to reliable customers.} - Bank ishonchli mijozlarga pul beradi.
{r:She will lend her favorite book to her friend.} - U sevimli kitobini do'stiga beradi.

text: {r:Rich}[rɪtʃ] – boy. Xorvatiya juda kichik mamlakat bo’lishiga qaramasdan, futbol u yerda rivojlangan. Davlatning eng {h:boy} odami ham futbolchi, hammamiz tanigan mashhur Real Madrid futbolchisi Mod{p:rich}.
examples: {r:She will become rich and successful in her career.} - U o'z karyerasida boy va muvaffaqiyatli bo'ladi.
{r:This new business will make him rich.} - Bu yangi biznes uni boy qiladi.
{r:I will not compare the rich and poor people.} - Boy va kambag'al odamlarni solishtirmayman.
{r:Your hard work will bring rich rewards.} - Mehnatlaringiz boy mukofotlar olib keladi.

text: {r:Weekend}[ˌwiːkˈɛnd] - hafta oxiri, otdix kunlari. Week(hafta) va end(tugash) so'zlarining birlashuvidan yasalgan.
examples: {r:I will relax at home this weekend.} - Men bu dam olish kunlari uyda dam olaman.
{r:My family will go to the park on the weekend.} - Oilam dam olish kunlari bog'ga boradi.
{r:The weather will be sunny all weekend.} - Ob-havo butun dam olish kunlari quyoshli bo'ladi.
{r:We shall finish our homework by the weekend.} - Biz uy vazifalarimizni dam olish kunlarigacha tugatamiz.

text:
{r:Mean}[miːn] – anglatmoq. 
O'tgan zamon shakllari - meant, meant. 
Prezidentimiz BMT {p:MIN}barida o’zbek tilida birinchi marta so’zladilar va bu ko’p narsa {h:anglatadi.} Demak rivojlanyapmiz, bizni tanishyapti, bizni jahon sahnasida o’z tilimizda eshitishyapti.
examples: {r:This word will mean something important to him.} - Bu so'z unga muhim narsani anglatadi.
{r:Your silence means that you agree.} - Sukut saqlashingiz rozi ekanligingizni anglatadi.
{r:What do you mean by that?} - Bu bilan nima demoqchisiz?
{r:Her smile will mean she is happy.} - Uning tabassumi uning baxtli ekanligini anglatadi.

text: {r:Science}[ˈsaɪəns] - ilm, fan. Noodatiylikni yaxshi ko'raman. Men ilm-fan ning ham noodatiy yo'nalishi bilan shug'ullanaman. Soyalarni o'rganaman. Sizning {p:SOYANIZ}zi o'rganish mening uchun {h:ilm-fan}.
examples: {r:Science will help humanity.} - Fan insoniyatga yordam beradi.
{r:My son will study computer science at university.} - O'g'lim universitetda kompyuter ilmini o'rganadi.
{r:This discovery will change the future of science.} - Bu kashfiyot ilm-fanning kelajagini o'zgartiradi.
{r:Science is very important for independent Uzbekistan.} - Ilm-fan mustaqil O'zbekiston uchun muhim.

text: {r:Famous}[ˈfeɪməs] – mashhur. Alisher Fayz qo’shiq aytishni tashlab endi mis savdosi bilan shug’ullanyapti ekan. O’zining savdo shirkatini ‘’{p:Fayz mis}’’ deb atabdi va bu narsa xalq orasida {h:mashhur} voqeaga aylanib ketibdi.
examples: {r:You will become famous for your artwork.} - Siz san'at asaringiz bilan mashhur bo'lasiz.
{r:This song will become famous worldwide.} - Bu qo'shiq butun dunyoda mashhur bo'ladi.
{r:His new movie will be famous very soon.} - Uning yangi filmi juda tez orada mashhur bo'ladi.
{r:The city will be famous for its history.} - Shahar o'z tarixi bilan mashhur bo'ladi.

text: {r:Right}[raɪt] – o’ng. Ko’chada ketayotganimda {p:Rayi}mni ko’rdim. Pushti tog’orani {h:o’ng} qo’lida ko’tarib ketayotgan ekan.
examples: {r:Turn right at the corner.} - Burchakda o'ngga buriling.
{r:Is this the right side?} - Bu o'ng tarafmi?
{r:My right hand is stronger.} - Mening o'ng qo'lim kuchliroq.
{r:The door is on the right.} - Eshik o'ng tomonda.

text: {r:Thirst}[θɜːst] - chanqoq. Mnemonik namuna uchun o'tgan darsdagi thirsty ga qarang.
examples: {r:The long walk will cause thirst.} - Uzoq yurish chanqoqni keltirib chiqaradi.
{r:Clean water will satisfy everyone's thirst.} - Toza suv hamma chanqog'ini qondiradi.
{r:I shall bring water for your thirst.} - Men chanqog'ingiz uchun suv olib kelaman.
{r:The travelers will feel big thirst in the desert.} - Sayohatchilar cho'lda juda katta chanqoqni his qilishdi.

text: {r:Hunger}[ˈhʌŋɡər] - ochlik. Hungry(och) so'zidan yasalgan.
examples: {r:The poor children will suffer from hunger.} - Kambag'al bolalar ochlikdan aziyat chekishadi.
{r:These needy people are always hungry.} - Bu muhtoj insonlar har doim och.
{r:He is not rich. Hunger is his big friend.} - U boy emas. Ochlik uning katta do'sti.
{r:This newspaper is about hunger in these regions.} - Bu gazeta bu hududlardagi ochlik haqida.

text: {r:Traveler}[ˈtrævələr] - sayyoh. Travel(sayohat qilmoq) so'zidan yasalgan.
examples: {r:The young traveler will explore new cultures.} - Yosh sayohatchi yangi madaniyatlarni o'rganadi.
{r:My friend will meet the traveler at the airport.} - Do'stim sayyoh bilan aeroportda uchrashadi.
{r:Every traveler will find something interesting here.} - Har bir sayohatchi bu yerda nimadir qiziqarli narsalarni topadi.
{r:This map will help any traveler on their journey.} - Bu xarita har qanday sayohatchiga safarida yordam beradi.

text: {r:Dirt}[dɜːt] - kir(ot). Mnemonik namuna uchun dirty(kir sifat) ga qarang.
examples: {r:The rain will wash away the dirt from the streets.} - Yomg'ir ko'chalardagi iflosliklarni yuvib tashlaydi.
{r:Children will play in the dirt with their toys.} - Bolalar o'z o'yinchoqlari bilan loyqada(kirlikda) o'ynashadi.
{r:We shall clean all the dirt from the car.} - Biz mashinadan barcha iflosliklarni tozalaymiz.
{r:Proper cleaning will remove all the dirt.} - To'g'ri tozalash barcha ifloslikni olib tashlaydi.

text: {r:Tomorrow}[təˈmɒroʊ] – ertaga. Mening otam ham ajoyib ovchi bo’lgan va omadli tumor taqqan ov payti. Men ham {h:ertaga} dadamning {p:TUMOR}ini {p:OV} payti taqib olaman.
examples: {r:Tomorrow will be a busy day.} - Ertaga band kun bo'ladi.
{r:It will snow tomorrow evening.} - Ertaga kechki payt qor yog'adi.
{r:I will meet you tomorrow morning at the cafe.} - Men sizni ertaga ertalab kafeda ko'raman.
{r:They will announce the winners tomorrow.} - Ular g'oliblarni ertaga e'lon qilishadi.

text: {r:Poor}[pʊr] – kambag'al, nochor. {p:Por}axo’rlik mamlakatda faqat {h:kambag’allarni} ko’paytiradi.
examples: {r:I will help the poor.} - Men kambag'allarga yordam beraman.
{r:Will he become poor?} - U kambag'al bo'ladimi?
{r:My sister will not be poor.} - Mening singlim kambag'al bo'lmaydi.
{r:They will support poor families.} - Ular nochor oilalarni qo‘llab-quvvatlaydi.

text: {r:Offer}[ˈɒfər] – taklif, taklif qilmoq. Hamkorlarimiz shunchalik ajoyib taklif aytdiki, men '{p:ofar}in {h:taklif}izga' deb yuboribman.
examples: {r:I will not accept that offer.} - Men bu taklifni qabul qilmayman.
{r:Will your friend offer a good price?} - Do'stingiz yaxshi narx taklif qiladimi?

text: {r:Box}[bɒks] – quti. Mashhur {p:boks} sport turning asl ma’nosi '{h:quti}' degani. Chunki boks ringi qutiga o’xshaydi.

text: {r:Exercise}[ˈɛksərsaɪz] – mashq; mashq qilmoq. Mening bobom 'yoshligimda {p:eks}kavatorchilar {p:soyuz}ining boshlig’i bo’lganman, o'zim ham {h:mashq} qilardim, qo'l ostimdagilarni ham mashq qildirardim.' deydilar.
examples: {r:What kind of exercises do you know for headache?} - Bosh og'rig'i uchun qanday mashqlarni bilasiz?

{r:Will the teacher give us more exercises?} - O'qituvchi bizga ko'proq mashq beradimi?

text: {r:Wind}[wɪnd] - shamol. Uy qursangiz oddiygina bolt va VINTlar ishlatmang. Iloji bo'lsa mustahkam mixlar bilan uyingizni quring. Kichkinagina {p:VINT}lar bilan uy qursangiz uyingizni {h:shamol} uchirib ketadi.
examples: {r:I will not go outside in this strong wind.} - Men bu kuchli shamolda tashqariga chiqmayman.

{r:The children will not play outside in this cold wind.} - Bolalar bu sovuq shamolda tashqarida o'ynashmaydi.
{r:Will the wind break the old house?} - Shamol eski uyni qo'porib tashlaydimi?

text: {r:Deficit}[ˈdɛfɪsɪt] - kamchilik, taqchillik, defitsit. Bir xil so'zlar!
examples: {r:The government will not ignore the <budget deficit>.} - Hukumat <byudjet taqchilligini> e'tiborsiz qoldirmaydi.

{r:Will the experts explain the cause of the deficit?} - Ekspertlar taqchillikning sababini tushuntiradimi?

text: {r:Logic}[ˈlɒdʒɪk] - logika, mantiq. Bir xil so'zlar.

{r:Will everyone understand the logic of this system?} - Bu tizimning mantiqini hamma tushunadimi?

text: {r:Own}[oʊn] – o’z, o’ziniki;egalik qilmoq. Qonunga muvofiq {p:ovn}i faqatgina {h:o’z} nomingizga olingan miltiq bilan amalga oshirish mumkin.
examples: {r:I do not own a house right now.} - Men hozirda uyga egalik qilmayman.

{r:This is my own house.} - Bu mening o'z uyim.
{r:Where is your own key?} - O'z kaliting qani?

text: {r:Liar}[ˈlaɪər] - yolg'onchi. Lie(yolg'on gapirmoq) so'zidan yasalgan. Mnemonik namuna uchun 16 - darsga qarang.
examples: {r:I will not trust a liar.} - Men yolg'onchiga ishonmayman.
{r:Will you forgive the liar?} - Yolg'onchini kechirasizmi?
{r:My brother will not believe the liar's story.} - Akam yolg'onchining hikoyasiga ishonmaydi.
{r:This is my shirt. You are a liar.} - Bu mening ko'ylagim. Sen yolg'onchisan.

text: {r:Learner}[ˈlɜːrnər] - o'rganuvchi. Learn(o'rganmoq) so'zidan yasalgan.
examples: {r:I will not stop being a good learner.} - Men yaxshi o'rganuvchi bo'lishni to'xtatmayman.
{r:Will you help the new learner?} - Yangi o'rganuvchiga yordam berasizmi?
{r:The teacher will not ignore the learner's questions.} - O'qituvchi o'rganuvchining savollarini e'tiborsiz qoldirmaydi.
{r:Will the young learner understand the lesson?} - Yosh o'rganuvchi darsni tushunadimi?

text: {r:Comparison}[kəmˈpærɪsən] - taqqoslash, qiyoslash. Compare(taqqoslamoq) so'zidan olingan. Mnemonik namuna uchun 17 - darsdagi compare ga qarang.
examples: {r:I will not make a quick comparison.} - Men tez taqqoslash qilmayman.
{r:The comparison between these two planes is important.} - Bu ikki samolyotni taqqoslash juda muhim.
{r:This report is about a comparison in human mood in sunny and cloudy weather.} - Hisobot quyoshli va bulutli ob-havoda inson kayfiyati taqqosi haqida.
{r:Is this news about price comparisons?} - Bu yangilik narx tafovutlari haqidami?

text: {r:Independence}[ˌɪndɪˈpɛndəns] - mustaqillik. Independent(mustaqil) so'zidan yasalgan.
examples: {r:I will not give up my independence.} - Men mustaqilligimdan voz kechmayman.
{r:Will your country celebrate its independence?} - Mamlakatingiz mustaqillik kunini nishonlaydimi?
{r:The people will not lose their independence.} - Odamlar o'z mustaqilligini yo'qotmaydi.
{r:Will the new law protect our independence?} - Yangi qonun mustaqilligimizni himoya qiladimi?

text: {r:Freely}[ˈfriːli] - erkin. Free(erkin) so'zining ravish shakli.
examples: {r:I will not speak freely in front of everyone.} - Men hamma oldida erkin gapirmayman.

{r:Will the birds fly freely in the sky?} - Qushlar osmonda erkin uchadimi?

text: {r:Accomplish}[əˈkʌmplɪʃ] – muvaffaqiyatli tugatmoq, amalga oshirmoq, bajarmoq. {p:AKAM PLASH}ini kiysa Jeyms Bond bo’lib ketadi go’yoki va davlat tomonidan qo’yilgan barcha vazifalarni muvaffaqiyatli {h:bajarib}, jinoyatchilarni panjara ortiga tiqadi.
examples: {r:I will not <give up> until I accomplish my goal.} - Men maqsadimga erishgunimcha <taslim> bo'lmayman.

{r:How do you accomplish your plans quickly?} - Qanday qilib rejalaringni tez amalga oshirasan?
{r:Will she accomplish her dream?} - U o'z orzusini amalga oshiradimi?

text: {r:Absorb}[əbˈsɔːb] – shimmoq, yutmoq, o'zlashtirmoq. {p:Abz}al {p:orb}it {h:shimib} yuradi doimo, chunki u og’zidan qandaydir hid kelib turishini xohlamaydi.
examples: {r:I will not absorb negative energy.} - Men salbiy energiyani o'zlashtirmayman.
{r:Will you absorb the information quickly?} - Ma'lumotni tez o'zlashtirasizmi?
{r:The soil will not absorb the water.} - Tuproq suvni shimib olmaydi.
{r:Will the new student absorb the lesson quickly?} - Yangi o'quvchi darsni tezda o'zlashtiradimi?

text: {r:Close}[kloʊs] – yaqin. Tasavvur qiling {p:GILOS}ga {h:yaqin} tursangiz qizarib ketasiz.
examples: {r:I will not stay close to the fire.} - Men olovga yaqin turmayman.
{r:Will she be close to the house?} - U uyga yaqin bo‘ladimi?
{r:My brother will not sit close to the window.} - Mening akam derazaga yaqin o'tirmaydi.
{r:Will they move close to the park?} - Ular parkga yaqin ko‘chishadimi?

text: {r:Please}[pliːz] - xursand qilmoq, ko'nglini olmoq. Mening qarindoshim Qizilqum cho'llarida yashaydi va uyi har doim chang bo'ladi. Menimcha uni {h:ko'nglini olishim} uchun {p:PLIS}os sovg'a qilishim kerak.
examples: {r:I will not please everyone with my decision.} - Men qarorim bilan hammani xursand qilmayman.
{r:Will you please your parents by studying?} - O'qish orqali ota-onangizni xursand qilasizmi?
{r:Sure. I will please my parents.} - Albatta. Ota-onamni xursand qilaman.
{r:This beautiful skirt will please my sister.} - Bu chiroyli yubka singlimni xursand qiladi.

text: {r:Break}[breɪk] - tanaffus. Agar ishingizdan bezor bo'lgan bo'lsangiz {h:tanaffus} oling va ko'nglingizni ochuvchi {p:BREYK}dens bilan shug'ullaning.
examples: {r:I will not take a break now.} - Men hozir tanaffus olmayman.
{r:Will you take a break during the meeting?} - Yig'ilish paytida tanaffus olasizmi?
{r:I need a long break from the job.} - Ishdan uzoq tanaffus olishim kerak.
{r:She will take a long break from the job.} - U ishidan katta tanaffus oladi.

text: {r:Present}[ˈprɛzənt] - sovg'a, hadya. Men tog'amga sovg'a jo'natdim. Amerikaga ketish uchun bir necha yildan beri harakat qilayotganligi uchun men unga {p:PREZidENT} Trampning haykalchasini {h:sovg'a qildim}.
examples: {r:I will not open the present yet.} - Men hali sovg'ani ochmayman.
{r:Will you buy a present for your friend?} - Siz do'stingiz uchun sovg'a sotib olasizmi?
{r:My friend will not bring a present.} - Do'stim sovg'a olib kelmaydi.
{r:A new present is being bought for our dear teacher.} - Qadrli o'qituvchimiz uchun yangi sovg'a olinyapti.

text: {r:Little}[ˈlɪt.əl] – kichik, kam, ozgina. Styuart Litlni eslasangiz kerak. U odamlar tarafidan asrab olingan sichqoncha. U boshqalardan {h:kichkina} bo’lganligi uchun ham {p:Littl} deb laqab berilgan.
examples: {r:The dancer has a little time.} – Raqqosning kamgina vaqti bor.

{r:There is little time left.} – Ozgina vaqt qoldi.
{r:The traveler drank a little water.} – Sayohatchi ozgina suv ichdi.
