text: {r:Voice}[vɔɪs] – ovoz, nutq. Tasavvur qiling, sigiringiz bir kuni qo’shiq aytvordi. Siz esa ‘’{p:Voy s}igirimizni yaxshigina {h:ovozi} bor ekan, artist qilsak bo’lar ekan’’ dedingiz.
examples: {r:Her voice is very soft.} – Uning ovozi juda yumshoq.
{r:I lost my voice after the concert.} – Konsertdan keyin ovozim yo‘qoldi.
{r:I heard a strange voice, perhaps it was John.} – Men g‘alati ovoz eshitdim, balki bu Jon bo‘lgandir.
{r:My little brother is asleep now. Don't raise your voice.} - Ukam hozir uyquda. Ovozingni ko'tarma.

text: {r:Earth}[ɜːθ] – yer sayyorasi. Siz bu vaziyatda {p:ERS}iz ayollarning {h:yer} shari globusini ko’tarib olganini tasavvur qiling.
examples: {r:How much knowledge do you have about the Earth?} - Yer haqida qancha biliming bor?
{r:His wife might visit the Earth Science museum.} - Uning rafiqasi Yer haqidagi fanlar muzeyiga tashrif buyurishi mumkin.
{r:Our children may not understand the importance of Earth.} - Bolalarimiz Yerning ahamiyatini tushunmasligi mumkin.
{r:Their family might plant more trees to help the Earth.} - Ularning oilasi Yerga yordam berish uchun ko'proq daraxt ekishi mumkin.

text: {r:Repetition}[ˌrɛpəˈtɪʃən] - takrorlash. Bir xil so'zlar!
examples: {r:I may need repetition to understand this lesson.} - Men bu darsni tushunish uchun takrorlashim kerak bo'lishi mumkin.
{r:She doesn't want repetition in words in her letter to her lawyer.} - U advokatiga yozayotgan xatida bir xil so'zlar takrorlanishini xohlamaydi.
{r:Their buyer may not like the repetition in the design.} - Ularning xaridori dizayndagi takrorlanishni yoqtirmasligi mumkin.
{r:His parents might explain the importance of repetition.} - Uning ota-onasi takrorlashning ahamiyatini tushuntirishi mumkin.

text: {r:Symbol}[ˈsɪmbəl] - ramz, simvol. Bir xil so'zlar.
examples: {r:This may be a symbol of peace.} - Bu tinchlik ramzi bo'lishi mumkin.
{r:Her husband might recognize the symbol.} - Uning eri ramzni tanib olishi mumkin.
{r:Their lawyer may not understand what this symbol means.} - Ularning advokati ramzning ma'nosini tushunmasligi mumkin.
{r:My teachers might teach us about different symbols.} - O'qituvchilarim bizga turli ramzlar haqida o'rgatishi mumkin.

text: {r:Singer}[ˈsɪŋər] – qo’shiqchi. {p:SING}limning {p:ER}i 35 yoshida o’zining kuchli vokal qobiliyatlari borligini sezib qolibdi va tez orada mashhur {h:qo’shiqchi} bo’lib ketdi. Lekin xarakteri o’zgarib hozir salomimizga alik olmayapti.
examples: {r:I may become a famous singer one day.} - Men bir kuni mashhur qo'shiqchi bo'lishim mumkin.
{r:Her sister might perform at the local concert.} - Uning singlisi mahalliy kontsertda chiqish qilishi mumkin.
{r:Their dog may not like the singer’s loud voice.} - Ularning iti qo'shiqchining baland ovozini yoqtirmasligi mumkin.
{r:Your parents might support your dream of being a singer in the future.} - Ota-onangiz kelajakda qo'shiqchi bo'lish orzuingizni qo'llab-quvvatlashi mumkin.

text: {r:Winter}[ˈwɪntər] – qish. Agar {h:qishda} traktorning motori muzlab qolsa, eng yaxshisi {p:vino tr}aktorga quyish kerak, keyin yurib ketadi.
examples: {r:It may snow this winter.} - Bu qishda qor yog'ishi mumkin.
{r:Her family might buy a new coat for winter.} - Uning oilasi qish uchun yangi palto sotib olishi mumkin.
{r:The bus driver might not drive here in winter.} - Avtobus haydovchisi qishda bu yerga kelishni xohlamasligi mumkin.
{r:May I travel this time in winter?} - Bu safar qishda sayohat qilsam maylimi?

text:
{r:Depend}[dɪˈpɛnd] – bog’liq bo’lmoq, tayanmoq.
 Hozir hamma institutlarga kira olyapti, institutlar ari inidan ham ko’p. {p:DIP}lom {p:END}i kelajak garovi emas. Hamma narsa harakating va qobiliyatingga {h:bog'liq}.
examples: {r:I may depend on your help for this task.} - Men bu vazifa uchun sizning yordamingizga tayanishim mumkin.
{r:His wife might not depend on others for money.} - Uning rafiqasi pul uchun boshqalarga tayanmasligi mumkin.
{r:Our success may depend on the weather tomorrow.} - Muvaffaqiyatimiz ertaga ob-havoga bog'liq bo'lishi mumkin.
{r:Your future depends on the law.} - Kelajagingiz qonunga bog'liq.
{r:You may depend on me for help.} - Siz yordam uchun menga tayanishingiz mumkin.

text: {r:Food}[fuːd] - ovqat, taom, yegulik.
examples: {r:I may try new food at the restaurant.} - Men restoranda yangi taomlarni tatib ko'rishim mumkin.
{r:May I eat this food?} - Bu ovqatni yesam maylimi?
{r:Our dog may not like this kind of food.} - Itimizga bu turdagi ovqat yoqmasligi mumkin.
{r:Their parents might order food for the party.} - Ularning ota-onasi ziyofat uchun ovqat buyurtma qilishi mumkin.

text: {r:Prefer}[prɪˈfɜː] – afzal ko’rmoq. Amerika prezidenti Tramp oxirgi paytlarda qishloq xo’jaligiga ko’p e’tibor qaratyapti. BBC ning yozishicha {p:PRE}zident {p:FER}malarda chorvachilikni dehqonchilikdan {h:afzal} deb biladi. Chunki dehqonchilik katta suv resurslarini talab qiladi.
examples: {r:I prefer tea over coffee today.} - Men bugun kofedan choyni afzal ko'raman.
{r:Her sister might prefer reading books to watching movies.} - Uning singlisi filmlarni tomosha qilishdan ko'ra kitob o'qishni afzal ko'rishi mumkin.
{r:Our buyer may not prefer cold weather for the trip.} - Bizning xaridorimiz sayohat uchun sovuq ob-havoni afzal ko'rmasligi mumkin.
{r:Their parents might prefer staying at home on the weekend.} - Ularning ota-onasi dam olish kunlari uyda qolishni afzal ko'rishi mumkin.

text:
{r:Understand}[ˌʌndərˈstænd] - tushunmoq. 
O'tgan zamon shakllari - understood, understood. 
Mashhur futbolchilar Parkentdagi bizning mahallamizga kelib {p:ADIR}likda {p:TEN}nis o'ynashardi. Men umuman {h:tushun}mas edim. Oxiri bilsam oyoqni baquvvat qilar ekan bu narsa.
examples: {r:I may not understand Spanish.} - Men ispanchani tushunmasligim mumkin.
{r:Shahzoda might not understand how to paint eggs.} - Shahzoda tuxumlarni qanday bo'yashni tushunmasligi mumkin.
{r:Their lawyer may not understand the full report.} - Ularning advokati to'liq hisobotni tushunmasligi mumkin.
{r:I understood your problem.} - Men sening muammoyingni tushundim.

text: {r:Excuse}[ɪkˈskjuːz] - uzur, kechirim; bahona. Texnik jihozlari olami vakili ekskavator juda dangasa ekan. Qishda sovuq, bahorda yomg'irli, yozda issiq deya ishlamas ekan. Lekin {p:EKS}kavatorning {p:KUZ}ga {h:bahonasi} o'tmas ekan.
examples: {r:Excuse me. May I come in?} - Kechirasiz! Kirish mumkinmi?
{r:His wife might not accept my weak excuse.} - Uning rafiqasi mening zaif uzrimni qabul qilmasligi mumkin.
{r:I have no excuse for what i did.} - Qilgan ishimga bahonam yo'q.
{r:Our manager might give us a valid excuse for the delay.} - Menejerimiz kechikish uchun asosli uzr topishi mumkin.

text: {r:Coat}[koʊt] – palto. Karantin payti sizni {p:KOVID}dan himoya qiluvchi {h:palto} ishlab chiqarildi lekin har kimning bu paltoni sotib olishga qurbi yetmaydi.
examples: {r:It may rain, so take your coat.} - Yomg'ir yog'ishi mumkin, shuning uchun paltoningizni oling.(so ning ma'nolari ko'p. Bu yerda shuning uchun degani)
{r:Her sister might buy a new winter coat.} - Uning singlisi yangi qishki palto sotib olishi mumkin.
{r:May I wear your coat today?} - Paltoyingizni bugun kiyib tursam maylimi?
{r:Her husband might forget his coat at work.} - Uning eri paltosini ishda unutishi mumkin.

text: {r:More}[mɔː] – ko’proq. Agar qorbobo {p:mo’ri}dan tushsa {h:ko’proq} sovg’a beradi deb ishonadi bolalar.
examples: {r:We may need more time for this project.} - Bizga bu loyiha uchun ko'proq vaqt kerak bo'lishi mumkin.
{r:May I ask for more food?} - Ko'proq ovqat so'rasam maylimi?
{r:I may have more questions after the lesson.} - Darsdan keyin menda ko'proq savollar bo'lishi mumkin.
{r:Your teacher might give us more exercise.} - O'qituvchingiz bizga ko'proq mashq berishi mumkin.

text: {r:Slow}[sloʊ] – sekin. Bir kuni matematika, adabiyot va slovar kitoblari yo’lga chiqishibdi va ular orasida eng {h:sekin} yurgani {p:SLOV}ar bo’libdi.
examples: {r:The traffic may be slow this evening.} - Bugun kechqurun transport sekin harakatlanishi mumkin.
{r:Your dog might be slow because of injured leg.} - Itingiz oyog'idagi jarohati tufayli bugun sekin bo'lishi mumkin.
{r:The old computer may work very slow today.} - Eski kompyuter bugun juda sekin ishlashi mumkin.
{r:His car might come slow because of the snow.} - Uning mashinasi qor tufayli sekin kelishi mumkin.

text: {r:Wrong}[rɒŋ] – noto’g’ri. Bizning xalq o’ng tarafni yaxshi ko’radi, o’ng qo’lni, nimaiki o’ng narsa bo’lsa shu to’g’ri deydi. Lekin {p:VR}ach {p:O'NG} taraf bilan harakatlanish, ish boshlashni {h:noto’g’ri} hisoblaydi. Chunki qon tomirlarning ko’pi shu tarafda va ularni charchatib qo’ymaslik ahamiyatli.
examples: {r:I may have the wrong answer.} - Mening javobim noto'g'ri bo'lishi mumkin.
{r:Your friend might press the wrong button on the machine.} - Do'stingiz mashinada noto'g'ri tugmani bosib qo'yishi mumkin.
{r:Her sister may take the wrong way home.} - Uning singlisi uyga noto'g'ri yo'ldan borishi mumkin.
{r:Our lawyer might find something wrong with the contract.} - Advokatimiz shartnomada noto'g'ri narsa topishi mumkin.

text: {r:Pen}[pɛn] – ruchka. Tasavvur qiling sizning {h:ruchka} shaklidagi {p:PEN}alingiz bor. Yana bir misol mashhur multfilm obrazi Piter Pen bo’lishi mumkin. Bu vaziyatda siz Piter {p:Pen}ning ruchka tayyorlayotganini tasavvur qiling.
examples: {r:I might not buy a new pen.} - Men yangi ruchka sotib olmasligim mumkin.
{r:Which pen do you prefer? Red or blue pen?} - Qaysi ruchkani afzal ko'rasiz? Qizil yoki ko'k?
{r:What did you write with a pen?} - Ruchka bilan nimani yozdingiz?
{r:His wife might forget to bring a pen to the meeting.} - Uning rafiqasi yig'ilishga ruchka olib kelishni unutishi mumkin.

text: {r:Explanation}[ˌɛkspləˈneɪʃən] - tushuntirish, izoh. Explain(tushuntirmoq) so'zidan yasalgan.
examples: {r:The teacher may give a better explanation.} - O'qituvchi yaxshiroq tushuntirish berishi mumkin.
{r:Your friend might need further explanation about the plan.} - Do'stingizga reja haqida qo'shimcha tushuntirish kerak bo'lishi mumkin.
{r:Her husband may ask for an explanation of the problem.} - Uning eri muammoga tushuntirish so'rashi mumkin.
{r:Our lawyer might find a clear explanation in the documents.} - Advokatimiz hujjatlarda aniq tushuntirish topishi mumkin.

text: {r:Lucky}[ˈlʌki] - omadli.
examples: {r:We may get lucky with the weather for our trip.} - Biz sayohatimiz uchun ob-havo bilan omadimiz kelishi mumkin.
{r:Your team might feel lucky today after the win.} - Jamoangiz g'alabadan keyin bugun omadli his qilishi mumkin.
{r:His sister may not be so lucky next time.} - Uning singlisi keyingi safar unchalik omadli bo'lmasligi mumkin.
{r:He hit and kick me hard. But I am lucky because nothing happened.} - U meni urdi va tepdi. Ammo omadli ekanman chunki menga hech narsa qilmadi.

text: {r:Way}[weɪ] – yo'l. Agar kachoklar {h:yo’l}idan bormoqchi bo'lsang, {p:VEY} ich.
examples: {r:This may not be the fast way to solve the problem.} - Bu muammoni hal qilishning eng tez yo'li bo'lmasligi mumkin.
{r:You might lose your way in the big city.} - Siz katta shaharda yo'ldan adashishingiz mumkin.
{r:Her husband may show us the way to the shop.} - Uning eri bizga do'kongacha yo'lni ko'rsatishi mumkin.
{r:There might be another way to complete the task.} - Vazifani bajarishning boshqa yo'li bo'lishi mumkin.

text: {r:Fish}[fɪʃ] – baliq. Mana bu ‘Baliqmisan {h:baliq}’ filmining a{p:FISH}asi.
examples: {r:We may go fishing tomorrow morning.} - Biz ertaga ertalab baliq oviga borishimiz mumkin.
{r:May I eat fish?} - Baliq yesam maylimi?
{r:Your child may not like this kind of fish.} - Farzandingizga bu turdagi baliq yoqmasligi mumkin.
{r:Their parents might cook fish for dinner.} - Ularning ota-onasi kechki ovqatga baliq pishirishlari mumkin.

text:
{r:Possible}[ˈpɒsəbəl] – iloji bo’lgan, ehtimoli bo'lgan, amalga oshishi mumkin bo'lgan.
 Dadam Rossiyada Sibirda ishlaydi. Bir kuni ular {p:POS}ilka {p:Sibir}dan jo’natibdilar. Posilkaning ichida muz bo’lagi bor ekan va u erimabdi, garchi havo issiq bo’lishiga qaramasdan. Demak issiqda ham muzni eritmaslikni {h:iloji bor ekan}.
examples: {r:It is possible to change the date of the meeting.} - Yig'ilish sanasini o'zgartirishning imkoni bor.
{r: This might be a possible danger.} - Bu ehtimoliy xatar bo'lishi mumkin.
{r:Her husband may consider all possible options.} - Uning eri barcha mumkin bo'lgan variantlarni ko'rib chiqishi mumkin.
{r:There might be possible solutions to our problem.} - Muammomizga mumkin bo'lgan yechimlar bo'lishi mumkin.

text: {r:Politics}[ˈpɒlɪtɪks] – siyosat. Nemislarda bir maqol bor. ‘’ Uyda {p:POL TEKIS} bo’lsa, keyin {h:“siyosat”} haqida o’ylanadi”. Ma’nosi shuki inson to’q bo’lsagina, iqtisodiy muammolari bo’lmasa keyin siyosat haqida o’ylashga vaqti bo’ladi.
examples: {r:You can discuss politics with your friends carefully.} - Siz do'stlaringiz bilan siyosat haqida ehtiyotkorlik bilan suhbatlashishingiz mumkin.
{r:His wife can explain the political situation.} - Uning rafiqasi siyosiy vaziyatni tushuntirishi mumkin.
{r:Our children cannot ignore politics in their country.} - Farzandlarimiz o'z mamlakatidagi siyosatni e'tiborsiz qoldira olmaydi.
{r:Everybody is interested in racing and politics in France.} - Fransiyada har bir kishi poyga va siyosatga qiziqadi.

text: {r:Interesting}[ˈɪntrəstɪŋ] - qiziqarli, interesno. Interest(qiziqish) so'zidan yasalgan. Ba'zan o'zbek tilida ham rus tilidan o'zlashgan
examples: {r:I find this book very interesting.} - Men bu kitobni juda qiziqarli deb topdim.
{r:Your teacher can make the lesson more interesting.} - O'qituvchingiz darsni qiziqarliroq qilishi mumkin.
{r:Their buyer cannot ignore such an interesting offer.} - Ularning xaridori bunday qiziqarli taklifni e'tiborsiz qoldira olmaydi.
{r:I think watching a movie is interesting but reading is just the opposite.} - Mening o'ylashimcha kino ko'rish qiziqarli o'qish esa teskarisi.

text: {r:Pencil}[ˈpensəl] - qalam. Tasavvur qiling shamollab qolib bir pachka {p:PENSIL}in oldingiz va ochib qarasangiz pensilin o'rniga {h:qalamlar} turibdi ichida.
examples: {r:You can use this pencil for drawing.} - Siz bu qalamni chizish uchun ishlatishingiz mumkin.
{r:Her friend could lend me a pencil.} - Uning do'sti menga qalam berishi mumkin edi.
{r:Their child cannot lose their pencils.} - Ularning farzandi o'z qalamlarini yo'qota olmaydi.
{r:He is able to break the pencil with one hand.} - U qalamni bitta qo'li bilan sindira oladi.

text: {r:Ticket}[ˈtɪkɪt] – bilet. Mana bu haykalni tomosha qiling. Bu tik yurgan it haykali. Bu {p:tik it}ni ko’rish uchun millionlab odamlar {h:bilet} sotib olishadi va mazza qilib tomosha qilishadi.
examples: {r:You can buy the ticket online for a good price.} - Yaxshiroq narx uchun chiptani onlayn sotib olishingiz mumkin.
{r:Where can I find a cheap ticket?} - Arzon chiptani qayerdan topa olaman?
{r:They cannot buy the ticket if they can't afford it.} - Agar ularning qurbi yetmasa, chiptani sotib ololmaydilar.
{r:Nobody wants an expensive ticket.} - Hech kim qimmat biletni xohlamaydi.

text: {r:Luxurious}[lʌɡˈʒʊəriəs] - hashamatli. Luxury(hashamat) so'zidan yasalgan.
examples: {r:I am not able to buy a luxurious car now.} - Men hozir hashamatli mashina sotib ololmayman.
{r:They are rich. They can build a luxurious kitchen.} - Ular boy. Ular hashamatli oshxona qura oladilar.
{r:She cannot go on a luxurious trip.} - U hashamatli sayohatga bora olmaydi.
{r:My parents can dream of a luxurious vacation.} - Ota-onam hashamatli ta'tilni orzu qilishi mumkin.

text: {r:Pronunciation}[prəˌnʌnsiˈeɪʃən] - talaffuz. Pronounce(talaffuz qilmoq) so'zidan yasalgan.
examples: {r:You are able to improve your pronunciation every day.} - Siz har kuni talaffuzingizni yaxshilashingiz mumkin.
{r:I have a different pronunciation.} - Mening farqli talaffuzim bor.
{r:Their friends can try to understand my pronunciation.} - Ularning do'stlari mening talaffuzimni tushunishga harakat qilishlari mumkin.
{r:This woman can help me with pronunciation if I ask.} - Agar so'rasam, bu ayol talaffuzda menga yordam berishi mumkin.

text: {r:Wooden}[ˈwʊdən] - yog'ochdan qilingan. Wood(yog'och) so'zidan yasalgan. Mnemonik namuna uchun 19 - darsdagi wood ga qarang.
examples: {r:This man was able to build a wooden fence for the garden.} - Bu kishi bog' uchun yog'och panjara qurishi mumkin edi.
{r:His wife can paint the old wooden chair.} - Uning rafiqasi eski yog'och stulni bo'yashi mumkin.
{r:This wooden house is always cool.} - Bu yog'ochli uy har doim salqin.
{r:How can I build a wooden house.} - Qanday qilib yog'och uy qursam bo'ladi.

text: {r:Hate}[heɪt] – nafrat. Men mana bu itning yangi egasiman. Uning aytishicha oldingi egalarining barcha uni ‘{p:hey it}’ deya kamsitishgan. Men esa unga odamdek munosabat qilaman, meni yaxshi ko’radi, oldingi egalaridan esa {h:nafratlanadi}.
examples: {r:You cannot hate anyone.} - Siz hech kimdan nafratlana olmaysiz.
{r:Her dog cannot hate this food, it's good.} - Uning iti bu ovqatni nafratlamasligi kerak, u yaxshi.
{r:They cannot hide their hate, it's better to talk.} - Ular o'z nafratlarini yashira olmaydilar, gaplashish kerak.
{r:Aziza cannot hate this place because this is her birthplace.} - Aziza bu joydan nafratlana olmaydi chunki bu yer uning tug'ilgan joyi.

text: {r:Correct}[kəˈrekt] – to’g’ri, to’g’rilamoq. Tasavvur qiling 2000 – yillarda universitetda o’qigansiz. O’quv muassasasida {p:KAR REKT}or bo’lar edi, oldidagi yordamchisi rektor chala eshitgan narsasini {h:to’g’rilab} yetkazib turar edi.
examples: {r:Perhaps, I can correct my mistakes in the report.} - Ehtimol men hisobotdagi xatolarimni tuzata olarman.
{r:Your teacher can also correct the document.} - O'qituvchingiz ham hujjatni diqqat bilan tuzatishi mumkin.
{r:Their lawyer is also able to correct the problem in the contract.} - Ularning advokati ham shartnomadagi muammoni tuzatishi mumkin.
{r:What you said is completely correct.} - Aytganingiz butunlay to'g'ri.

text: {r:Grandfather}[ˈɡrændfɑːðər] - bobo, buva.
examples: {r:You can visit your grandfather this weekend.} - Siz bu dam olish kunlari bobongizga tashrif buyurishingiz mumkin.
{r:Her child can call her grandfather more often.} - Uning farzandi bobosiga tez-tez qo'ng'iroq qilishi mumkin.
{r:They cannot forget their grandfather’s wise stories.} - Ular bobolarining dono hikoyalarini unuta olmaydi.
{r:My grandfather can boil milk under the sun.} - Mening bobom quyosh ostida sut qaynata oladi.(quyoshning issiqligi bilan)

text: {r:Grandmother}[ˈɡrændmʌðər] - buvi.
examples: {r:My grandmother can bake delicious pies for the family.} - Buvim oila uchun mazali pirog pishirishi mumkin.
{r:Our grandmother can speak three languages fluently.} - Buvimiz uchta tilni ravon gapiroladi.
{r:Your grandmother can tell wonderful stories to the children.} - Buvingiz bolalarga ajoyib hikoyalar aytib berishi mumkin.
{r:Her grandmother could build statues from ice in winter.} - Uning buvisi qishda muzdan haykallar qura olgan.

text: {r:Finally}[ˈfaɪnəli] - nihoyat, oxiri. Final(yakuniy) so'zidan yasalgan.
examples: {r:We can finally visit the new museum next month.} - Biz nihoyat kelasi oy yangi muzeyga borishimiz mumkin.
{r:They are finally able to buy their dream house this year.} - Ular bu yil orzu qilgan uylarini nihoyat sotib olishlari mumkin.
{r:I can finally understand this grammar after this lesson.} - Men bu darsdan keyin bu grammatikani nihoyat tushunishim mumkin.
{r:Finally I have arrived in my town.} - Nihoyat shaharchamga yetib keldim.

text: {r:Beach}[biːtʃ] – plyaj. Tasavvur qiling mikroblar siz chekkan sigaret {p:BICH}oki ustida o’zlari uchun {h:plyaj} qurishibdi.
examples: {r:You can find beautiful shells on this beach.} - Siz bu plyajda chiroyli chig'anoqlar topishingiz mumkin.
{r:Our family can swim here every summer.} - Oilamiz har yoz bu yerda suzishi mumkin.
{r:You can see a beautiful helicopter of rich man here on this beach.} - Boy kishining vertolyotini shu yerda plyajda ko'rishing mumkin.
{r:They can watch amazing sunsets here.} - Ular bu yerda ajoyib quyosh botishlarini tomosha qilishlari mumkin.

text: {r:Great}[ɡreɪt] – buyuk, zo’r. Oxirgi paytlarda {p:G}o’shtxonalarga {p:REYD}lar uyushtirilyapti. Maqsad xalqqa sifatli, {h:zo’r} go’shtlar yetkazilishi.
examples: {r:You can make great results in your studies.} - Siz o'qishingizda ajoyib natijalar qila olasiz.
{r:Great people can accomplish great things.} - Buyuk odamlar buyuk ishlar qila oladi.
{r:We can see great progress in your English by next month.} - Kelasi oyga qadar sizning ingliz tilingizda katta yutuqlarni ko'rishimiz mumkin.
{r:Parkent is a great mountainous place.} - Parkent ajoyib tog'li hudud.

text: {r:Family}[ˈfæməli] – oila. Sizning {p:family}angiz bu {h:oila} a'zolaringiz bilan bo’lishishingiz lozim bo’lgan birinchi narsa.
examples: {r:Our family can host ten guests for the dinner.} - Bizning oilamiz kechki ovqat uchun o'n mehmonga mezbonlik qilishi mumkin.
{r:This family members all differ from each other.} - Bu oila a'zolarining hammasi bir-biridan farq qiladi.
{r:You can learn much from your family's experience.} - Siz oilangiz tajribasidan ko'p narsa o'rganishingiz mumkin.
{r:We can spend holidays together as a family.} - Biz bayramlarni oila bo'lib birga o'tkazishimiz mumkin.

text: {r:Station}[ˈsteɪʃən] - stansiya, bekat.
examples: {r:I can meet you at the station at 5 PM.} - Men siz bilan stansiyada soat 5 da uchrashishim mumkin.
{r:We can catch the next train from this station.} - Biz bu stansiyadan keyingi poyezdni ushlab olishimiz mumkin.
{r:Your friend can buy tickets at that station.} - Do'stingiz chiptalarni shu bekatdan sotib olishi mumkin.
{r:We are going to meet at the station.} - Biz bekatda uchrashmoqchimiz.

text: {r:Apple}[ˈæpəl] - olma. Iphone ishlab chiqaruvchi {p:Apple} kompaniyasining logosida tishlangan {h:olmani} ko'rishingiz mumkin.
examples: {r:She can make delicious apple juice for the children.} - U bolalar uchun mazali olma sharbati tayyorlashi mumkin.
{r:We can pick apples from our tree before they fall.} - Biz daraxtimizdan olmalarni tushishidan oldin terib olishimiz mumkin.
{r:You can bake an apple pie for the party.} - Siz ziyofat uchun olmali pirog pishirishingiz mumkin.
{r:They can harvest many apples this year to sell.} - Ular bu yil sotish uchun ko'p olma yig'ib olishlari mumkin.

text: {r:Suit}[suːt] – mos kelmoq; kostyum-shim. Tadqiqotlar natijasi ko’rsatyaptiki ona {p:SUT}iga eng yaqin ‘{h:mos keluvchi}’ ozuqa bu sigir SUTi.
examples: {r:This picture can suit our wall well.} - Bu rasm bizning devorga yaxshi mos kelishi mumkin.
{r:That color can suit you perfectly.} - Bu rang sizga juda mos kelishi mumkin.
{r:I can find a suit for the interview tomorrow.} - Men ertaga intervyu uchun kostyum topishim mumkin.
{r:Their husband can wear a formal suit to the meeting.} - Ularning eri yig'ilishga rasmiy kostyum kiyishi mumkin.

text: {r:Ladder}[ˈlædər] – narvon. Agar led lampochkalarini o’rnatmoqchi bo’lsangiz stulga chiqib o’rnatmang. {p:LEDLAR}ga albatta {h:narvon} olib keling va narvonga chiqib o’rnating e’tibor bilan.
examples: {r:You can use this ladder to reach the roof.} - Siz bu narvonni tomga chiqish uchun ishlatishingiz mumkin.
{r:We can paint the house using that ladder.} - Biz u narvon yordamida uyni bo'yashimiz mumkin.
{r:His father can fix the ladder before using it.} - Uning otasi narvonni ishlatishdan oldin tuzatishi mumkin.
{r:This ladder is mine.} - Bu narvon meniki.

text: {r:Remember}[rɪˈmɛm.bɚ] – eslamoq. O’n yildan beri bitta remen taqaman, yirtilab ham eskirib ham ketmaydi. Nega unaqa ekan deb o’ylasam, keyin {h:esladim} axir bu {p:REMEN BR}aziliyadan keltirilgan importniy remen.
examples: {r:I can remember this bus. It had dirty seats.} - Men bu avtobusni eslay olaman. Uning kir o'rindiqlari bor edi
{r:Can you still remember how chocolate is produced?} - Shokolad qanday ishlab chiqarilishini hali ham eslay olasizmi?
{r:She can remember the song.} - U qo'shiqni eslay oladi.
{r:They can remember everything.} - Ular hamma narsani eslay oladi.

text: {r:Or}[ɔːr] – yoki. Chiroyli qizga bir kunda ikki sovchi kelibdi. Endi u {p:Or}if {h:yoki} {p:Or}tiqni tanlashi kerak.
examples: {r:Can your husband help me, or should I ask someone else?} - Eringiz menga yordam bera oladimi yoki boshqa kimdandir so'rashim kerakmi?
{r:Normally I drink tea or coffee in the morning} - Odatda ertalab choy yoki kofe ichaman.
{r:Their children can’t decide between apples or oranges.} - Ularning farzandlari olma yoki apelsin o'rtasida qaror qila olmayapti.
{r:My brother can buy bread or rice for dinner.} - Akam kechki ovqat uchun non yoki guruch sotib olishi mumkin.

text: {r:Too}[tuː] - ham; juda
examples: {r:Can your friend come too, or is he busy?} - Do'stingiz ham kela oladimi yoki bandmi?
{r:She could drink too much water} - U juda ko'p suv ichib qo'ya olardi.
{r:They can’t stay too late at the party.} - Ular ziyofatda juda kech qolib ketolmaydi.
{r:My friends could join us too for the movie.} - Do'stlarim ham film ko'rishga bizga qo'shilishi mumkin.
{r:I am busy too.} - Men ham bandman.
{r:I am too busy.} - Men juda bandman.

text: {r:Past}[pɑːst] – o’tgan, oldingi. Bu kishi {h:oldingi} muammolarni qo’zg’ayveradi, hammani asabiga tegadi, juda {p:past} odam.
examples: {r:Can you explain what happened in your past?} - O'tmishingizda nima bo'lganini tushuntira olasizmi?
{r:Could her grandmother remember the past events?} - Uning buvisi o'tmishdagi voqealarni eslay olarmidi?
{r:They can’t change their past decisions.} - Ular o'zlarining o'tmishdagi qarorlarini o'zgartira olmaydi.
{r:I used to steal cars in the past.} - O'tmishda mashina o'girlardim.

text: {r:Everything}[ˈevriθɪŋ] - hamma narsa, hammasi(narsalarga nisbatan). Every(hamma) va thing(narsa) so'zlarining birlashuvidan yasalgan.
examples: {r:Can your assistant check everything before we leave?} - Ketishimizdan oldin yordamchingiz hamma narsani tekshira oladimi?
{r:I was rich and I could buy everything.} - Men boy edim va hamma narsa sotib ololardim.
{r:They can’t do everything alone, they need help.} - Ular hamma narsani o'zlari qila olmaydi, ularga yordam kerak.
{r:We finished everything until midnight.} - Tun yarmigacha hamma narsani tugatdik.

text: {r:Borrow}[ˈbɒroʊ] – qarz olmoq. Tasavvur qiling siz aynan siz Yulduz Usmonovaning {p:BIRROV}i uchun 15 000$ {h:qarz oldingiz} va Yulduz opa pulni olib qo’yib kelmadi.
examples: {r:Can I borrow your pen, or do you need it?} - Ruchkangizni olishim mumkinmi yoki sizga kerakmi?
{r:Could her friend borrow a book from the library?} - Uning do'sti kutubxonadan kitob olishi mumkinmi?
{r:Their business can’t borrow money from anyone now.} - Ularning biznesi hozir hech kimdan pul olisha olmaydi.
{r:My parents could lend me what I need to borrow.} - Ota-onam menga kerakli narsalarni berib turolardi.

text: {r:Chess}[tʃes] - shaxmat. Tasavvur qiling televizorni yoqsangiz shaxmatchilar {p:CHES}noklarni {h:shaxmat} donalari sifatida foydalanib musobaqa o'tkazishyapti.
examples: {r:Can your brother play chess, or does he prefer cards?} - Akangiz shaxmat o'ynay oladimi yoki kartalar bilan o'ynashni afzal ko'radimi?
{r:Could her teacher teach her how to play chess?} - Uning o'qituvchisi unga shaxmat o'ynashni o'rgatolarmidi?
{r:They can’t win at chess against a master.} - Ular ustalarga qarshi shaxmatda g'alaba qozona olmaydi.
{r:My parents could play chess with me in the evenings.} - Ota-onam kechqurun men bilan shaxmat o'ynolardi.

text: {r:Quietly}[ˈkwaɪətli] - sokin, jimjit. Quiet so'zining ravish shakli.
examples: {r:Can you speak quietly, or is it too noisy here?} - Siz ohista gapira olasizmi yoki bu yer juda shovqinmi?
{r:Could her child work quietly in the library?} - Uning farzandi kutubxonada jimjit ishlay olarmidi?
{r:Our dog can’t sit quietly for long periods.} - Itimiz uzoq vaqt jimjit o'tira olmaydi.
{r:My parents could read quietly in the evening.} - Ota-onam kechqurun jimjit kitob o'qishi mumkin edi.

text: {r:Noisy}[ˈnɔɪzi] - shovqinli. Noise(shovqin) so'zidan yasalgan. Mnemonik namuna uchun 19- darsdagi noise ga qarang.
examples: {r:Our school is too noisy.} - Maktabimiz juda shovqin.
{r:Can her husband study in a noisy environment?} - Uning eri shovqinli muhitda o'qiy oladimi?
{r:They can’t concentrate when it’s too noisy.} - Shovqin bo'lganda ular diqqatni jamlaya olmaydi.
{r:We don't like noisy places.} - Biz shovqinli joylarni yoqtirmaymiz.

text: {r:Loudly}[ˈlaʊdli] - baland ovozda. Loud(ovoz va tovushlarga nisbatan baland so'zi) so'zining ravish shakli.
examples: {r:Can you speak loudly,please?} - Siz baland ovozda gapira olasizmi, iltimos?
{r:Could her friend sing loudly at the concert?} - Uning do'sti kontsertda baland ovozda qo'shiq aytolarmidi?
{r:They can’t hear you if you don’t speak loudly.} - Agar baland ovozda gapirmasangiz, ular sizni eshitolmaydi.
{r:Everybody usually speaks loudly here.} - Bu yerda odatda hamma baland ovozda gapiradi.

text: {r:Sandy}[ˈsændi] - qumli, qumloq. Sand(qum) so'zidan yasalgan. Mnemonik namuna uchun 19 - darsdagi sand ga qarang.
examples: {r:Can your dog walk on the sandy beach for hours?} - Itingiz qumli plyajda soatlab yura oladimi?
{r:Can his child build a sandy castle near the water?} - Uning farzandi suv yaqinida qumdan qal'a qura oladimi?
{r:Can we go to the sandy beach on a holiday.} - Ta'tilda qumli plyajga bora olamizmi?
{r:You can't grow anything on this sandy soil.} - Bu qumli tuproqda hech narsa o'stira olmaysan.

text: {r:Sudden}[ˈsʌdən] - to'satdan, qo'qqisdan. Tasavvur qiling siz Dubayda yurganingizda {h:to'satdan} Dizayndagi {p:SADIN}i ko'rib qoldingiz mana bu yigitga o'xshab.
examples: {r:Can sudden weather changes affect our plans?} - To'satdan ob-havo o'zgarishlari rejalarimizga ta'sir qilishi mumkinmi?
{r:Could your lawyer predict this sudden problem?} - Advokatingiz bu to'satdan muammoni oldindan aytib berolarmidi?
{r:Our business can't prepare for every sudden expense.} - Biznesimiz har bir to'satdan bo'ladigan xarajat uchun tayyorlana olmaydi.
{r:How could they ignore such a sudden danger?} - Ular qanday qilib bunday to'satdan xavfni e'tiborsiz qoldirishdi?

text: {r:With}[wɪð] – bilan. Yosh endi uylangan yigit mabodo 'Amerikaga {p:VIZ}a olsam xotinim {h:bilan} ketardim' deb o'ylayapti.
examples: {r:Can you come with me to the market?} - Siz men bilan bozorga borolasizmi?
{r:Why couldn't her husband agree with our idea?} - Nega uning eri bizning fikrimizga rozi bo'lolmasdi?
{r:Can we discuss this with your teacher?} - Biz buni o'qituvchingiz bilan muhokama qila olamizmi?
{r:How could they work with such noise?} - Ular qanday qilib shunday shovqin bilan ishlay olishadi?

text: {r:Everywhere}[ˈevriˌwer] - hamma yerda, hamma yerga.
examples: {r:Can you find taxis everywhere here?} - Bu yerda hamma joyda taksi topa olasizmi?
{r:Free hospitals are everywhere in Uzbekistan.} - Tekin shifoxonalar O'zbekistonda hamma yerda.
{r:Can't they deliver food everywhere in the city?} - Ular ovqatni shaharning hamma joyiga yetkaza olmaydimi?
{r:How could tourists go everywhere without a map?} - Sayyohlar xaritasiz qanday qilib hamma joyga bora olishadi?

text: {r:Wheel}[wiːl] – g’ildirak, balon. Mana bu yuzlab {p:VIL}kalardan yasalgan {h:g’ildirak}.
examples: {r:Can your father fix the bicycle wheel?} - Otangiz velosiped g'ildiragini tuzata oladimi?
{r:These wheels are expensive.} - Bu balonlar qimmat.
{r:Car wheels are more expensive in comparison with truck wheels} - Mashina g'ildiraklari yuk mashinasi g'ildraklari bilan solishtirganda biroz qimmat.
{r:How could the wheel come off so easily?} - G'ildirak qanday qilib shunday osongina chiqib ketdi?

text: {r:Dentist}[ˈdentɪst] - stomatolog.
examples: {r:Can the dentist see me tomorrow morning?} - Tish shifokori ertaga ertalab meni ko'rib qo'yoladimi?
{r:Why didn't your child visit the dentist earlier?} - Nega farzandingiz tish shifokoriga oldinroq bormadi?
{r:Can't we find a good dentist nearby for an emergency?} - Biz favqulodda vaziyat uchun yaqin atrofdagi yaxshi tish shifokorini topa olmaymizmi?
{r:Dentists are making much money these days.} - Shu kunlarda tish doktorlari ko'p pul qilishyapti.

text: {r:Instance}[ˈɪnstəns] – namuna, misol. Bizning institutda ba'zi odobsiz harakatlar uchun o’qishdan chetlatilishingiz mumkin. {p:INST}da {p:NOS} chekish va tuplash {h:misol uchun} shulardan biri.
examples: {r:Can you give me another instance of this rule?} - Menga bu qoidaning yana bir misolini keltira olasizmi?
{r:Another instance is doctors cannot grow beard in this hospital.} - Boshqa misol esa bu kasalxonada doktorlar soqol o'stira olmaydi.
{r:For instance, icecream is not produced in this country.} - Masalan, bu davlatda muzqaymoq ishlab chiqarilmaydi.
{r:I don't need your advice, your help, or your explanation, for instance.} - Menga sizning maslahatingiz, yordamingiz yoki masalan tushuntirishingiz kerak emas.

text:
{r:Better}[ˈbetər] – yaxshiroq. 
 Tasavvur qiling mikroblar betingizda dehqonchilik qilyapti. Hatto {p:BET}ingizni {p:TR}aktorda ham haydayapti {h:yaxshiroq} va unumdor qilish uchun. Albatta bu narsalar bizning ko’zimizga ular juda kichkina bo’lganligi uchun ko’rinmaydi.
examples: {r:Can we expect better weather tomorrow for our trip?} - Ertaga sayohatimiz uchun yaxshiroq ob-havo kutolamizmi?
{r:Why couldn't your friend find a better solution?} - Nega do'stingiz yaxshiroq yechim topolmadi?
{r:We can have better results.} - Biz yaxshi natijalar qilolamiz.
{r:How could she feel better so quickly after being ill?} - U kasal bo'lganidan keyin qanday qilib shunday tez yaxshi his qila boshladi?

text: {r:Ill}[ɪl] – kasal. Yomon qizlarga {p:IL}akishib qolish hozir keng tarqalgan {h:kasallik}.
examples: {r:Can the doctor see me if I feel ill today?} - Agar o'zimni yomon his qilsam, shifokor bugun meni ko'rib qo'yoladimi?
{r:Don't go to school. You are ill today.} - Maktabga borma. Bugun sen kasalsan.
{r:Sorry! I feel better now} - Kechirasiz! Men hozir yaxshiroq his qilyapman.
{r:Don't drink cold water. You will get ill later.} - Sovuq suv ichma keyinroq kasal bo'lib qolasan.

text: {r:Public}[ˈpʌblɪk] – omma, jamoat. Karantin payt odamlar ogoh bo’lishdi va qoidalarga amal qilishdi. Omma viruslardan saqlanish uchun {p:PA}ket {p:BILAK}igacha kiyib oldi. Chunki rezina qo’lqoplar talab yuqoriligidan yetmayotgan edi.
examples: {r:Can we use public transport at night safely?} - Biz tunda jamoat transportidan xavfsiz foydalana olamizmi?
{r:How can we improve public opinion?} - Qanday qilib jamoatchilik fikrini yaxshilay olamiz?
{r:Can they keep public places clean for everyone?} - Ular jamoat joylarini hamma uchun toza saqlay oladimi?
{r:Why can't we win public support?} - Nega jamoatchilik qo'lloviga erisha olmaymiz?

text: {r:Traffic}[ˈtræfɪk] so‘zi o‘zbek tilida 'harakat', 'yo‘l harakati', 'transport oqimi', 'qatnov' degan ma’nolarni anglatadi. U turli kontekstlarda ishlatiladi.
examples: {r:The traffic is very heavy this morning.} - Bugun ertalab yo‘l harakati juda zich.
{r:We were late because of traffic.} - Zich transport oqimi sababli biz kechikdik.
{r:Traffic lights control the flow of vehicles.} - Svetoforlar transport harakatini boshqaradi.
{r:There was a long traffic jam on the highway.} - Trassada katta tirbandlik bor edi.

text: {r:Possibly}[ˈpɒsəbli] – Iloji boricha, ehtimol. Kecha bizning uyimizga g’alati posilka kelibdi. {p:PAS}ilka {p:SIMLI} ekan, ya’ni hamma tarafdan sim bilan o’ralgan. Ehtimol bu qutida portlovchi modda yoki qandaydir kimyoviy element bordir. {h:Iloji boricha} ehtiyot bo'lib huquq posbonlarini chaqirdim.
examples: {r:Students must possibly finish this work today.} - Talabalar bu ishni iloji boricha bugun tugatishlari kerak.
{r:The doctor must possibly attend the meeting.} - Doktor yig'ilishda iloji boricha qatnashishi kerak.
{r:Possibly he will recover.} - Ehtimol, u tuzalib ketar.
{r:The family must possibly prepare for the trip.} - Oila imkoni boricha sayohatga tayyorlanishi kerak.

text: {r:Necessary}[ˈnesəseri] - zarur, muhim. Nestle semiz odamlarni tez ozdiruvchi suv ishlab chiqaryapti. 3 oy ichida keskin vazn yo'qotib oddiy odamlardek ko'rinishga ega bo'lasiz. Ozmoqchi bo'lsangiz {p:NES}tle {p:SUVI}ni iste'mol qilishingiz {h:zarur}.
examples: {r:You must bring all necessary things.} - Siz barcha zarur narsalarni olib kelishingiz kerak.
{r:She must complete the necessary work.} - U zarur ishni tugatishi kerak.
{r:We must not ignore the necessary rules.} - Biz zarur qoidalarni e'tiborsiz qoldirmasligimiz kerak.
{r:Teachers must provide the necessary help.} - O'qituvchilar zaruriy yordamni ko'rsatishi kerak.

text: {r:Sad}[sæd] – g’amgin, xafa. Agar burger yoki nonga {p:SED}ana sepib yuborishgan bo’lsa bu meni juda {h:xafa qiladi.} Sedana ta'mini yomon ko’raman.
examples: {r:You must not feel sad about the news.} - Siz yangilikdan xafa bo'lmasligingiz kerak.
{r:He must try to become positive not sad.} - U ijobiy bo'lishga harakat qilishi kerak.
{r:They must not make others sad.} - Ular boshqalarni xafa qilmasligi kerak.
{r:Luxury can possibly make a sad man happy again.} - Hashamat xafa kishini yana xursand qilishi mumkin.

text: {r:Touch}[tʌtʃ] - tegmoq. Juda ham irimchiman. Yaqinda bir qimmat mashinani ko'rib qoldim va menga ham nasib qilsin deya bu {p:TACH}kani hammayog'iga {h:tegib} ko'rdim. 'Yuqsin - yuqsin' qildimda!
examples: {r:You must not touch the hot water.} - Siz issiq suvga tegmasligingiz kerak.
{r:Children must not touch the cake.} - Bolalar tortga tegmasligi kerak.
{r:You must not touch the old things.} - Sen eski narsalarga tegmasliging kerak.
{r:Don't touch this butter and milk. This is for your grandfather.} - Bu sariyog' va sutga tegma. Bu bobong uchun.

text: {r:Useful}[ˈjuːsfəl] – foydali. {p:YUZ}ta {p:FIL}ingiz bo’lganda cho’ntagingizga qanday {h:foydali} bo’lardiya? Zoopark ochib qo’yardingiz, odamlar fillaringizni tomosha qilish va haydab ko’rish uchun pul to’lashardi va boyib ketgan bo’lardingiz.
examples: {r:You must find this tool useful.} - Siz bu asbobni foydali deb topshingiz kerak.
{r:Students must learn useful things.} - Talabalar foydali narsalarni o'rganishi kerak.
{r:They must not waste useful time.} - Ular foydali vaqtni isrof qilmasligi kerak.
{r:Teachers must share useful advice.} - O'qituvchilar foydali maslahatlar berishi kerak.

text: {r:Immediate}[ɪˈmiːdiət] – darhol, tez, zudlik bilan. Tasavvur qiling yuqoridan buyruq keldi. “Qo’shiqchi {p:IM}ron {p:MADANIYAT} vaziri etib tayinlansin {h:darhol.}”
examples: {r:We need an immediate answer to the question.} - Bizga savolga zudlik bilan javob kerak.
{r:There was an immediate need for water.} - Suvga zudlik bilan ehtiyoj bor edi.
{r:The child wants immediate attention.} - Bola zudlik bilan e'tibor istaydi.
{r:He needs immediate help with his leg.} - Uning oyog'iga zudlik bilan yordam kerak.

text: {r:Patient}[ˈpeɪʃənt] - sabrli; patsient, bemor. {p:PESHONAD}a ajinlarimni operatsiya qilib yo'q qilib yuborish uchun 17 kun operatsiya qilishdi. Doktorlar ham, men ham juda {h:sabrli} ekanmiz.
examples: {r:You must be patient with the process.} - Siz jarayon bo'yicha sabrli bo'lishingiz kerak.
{r:She must be patient for the answer.} - U javobni sabr bilan kutishi kerak.
{r:I feel sleepy now. I can't be patient anymore.} - Uyqusiragan his qilyapman o'zimni. Boshqa sabrli bo'lolmayman
{r:Teachers must teach students to be patient.} - O'qituvchilar talabalarga sabrli bo'lishni o'rgatishi kerak.

text: {r:Full}[fʊl] – to’la, to'q. {p:Full}ham jamoasi yana Angliya premier ligasiga qaytdi, stadion hozir muxlislar bilan {h:to’lgan.} Bu hikoya asosan futbol muxlislariga tushunarli bo’lishi mumkin.
examples: {r:I don't want to eat anything because i am full.} - Hech narsa yeyishni xohlamayman chunki to'qman.
{r:This bag is full of money.} - Bu sumka pul bilan to'la.
{r:They must not leave the box half full.} - Ular qutini yarim to'liq qoldirmasligi kerak.
{r:Football players are coming and the stadium is full. Probably it is going to be an interesting match.} - Futbol o'yinchilari kelyapti va stadion to'la. Katta ehtimol bugun qiziqarli o'yin bo'ladi.

text: {r:Safe}[seɪf] - tinch, xavfsiz. Pul saqlash uchun ishlatiladigan sandiqlar {p:seyf} deb atalashini bilasiz to'g'rimi? Aslida bu so'z ingliz tilidagi aynan shu so'zdan olingan va pul saqlash uchun {h:xavfsiz} joy ma'nosini bildiradi. Demak 'safe' bu 'xavfsiz' degani.
examples: {r:You must stay safe during the trip.} - Siz sayohat davomida xavfsiz bo'lishingiz kerak.
{r:You are not safe in the dark. Come home early.} - Qorong'ida xavfsiz emassan. Uyga ertaroq kel.
{r:Will I be safe in this town?} - Bu shaharchada xavfsiz bo'lamanmi?
{r:Sure. Nobody is going to hurt you.} - Albatta. Hech kim senga zarar yetkazmaydi.

text: {r:Light}[laɪt] – yorug’; chiroq, svet. Qorong’i payt {p:LAY}cha {p:IT}ni ko’zlaridan {h:yorug’lik} chiqadi.
examples: {r:You must turn off the lights before leaving.} - Siz ketishdan oldin chiroqlarni o'chirishingiz kerak.
{r:She must check the lights regularly.} - U chiroqlarni muntazam tekshirishi kerak.
{r:We made a comparison between sunlight and moonlight.} - Biz quyosh nuri va oy nurini taqqosladik.
{r:It is night time now but it is still light outside.} - Hozir tun vaqti lekin tashqarida hali ham yorug'.
{My room is not very light.} - Xonam juda ham yorug' emas.

text: {r:Enough}[ɪˈnʌf] – yetarli. O’tkir Shodmonov ‘’O’zbekiston futbolda yutqazib qo’ydi, shuning uchun {p:ENA F}utbol endi ko’rmayman, {h:yetadi} shu’’ dedi.
examples: {r:You must have enough water for the trip.} - Safar uchun yetarli suv olishingiz kerak.
{r:We must save enough money.} - Biz yetarli pul to'plashimiz kerak.
{r:Students must get enough sleep before exams.} - Talabalar imtihon oldidan yetarli uyqu olishlari(uxlashlari) kerak.
{r:The food must be enough for all guests.} - Ovqat barcha mehmonlar uchun yetarli bo'lishi kerak.

text: {r:Glass}[ɡlɑːs] – shisha;ko'zoynak. {p:Gilos} vaqt o’tib chirib yoki so’lib qolmasligi uchun uni kislorodsiz muhitda {h:shisha} idishda saqlash kerak.
examples: {r:You must wear safety glasses in the lab.} - Laboratoriyada xavfsizlik ko'zoynaklarini taqishingiz kerak.
{r:Do you know glass is made from sand?} - Shisha qumdan qilinishini bilasizmi?
{r:The window glass must be replaced today.} - Deraza oynasi bugun almashtirilishi kerak.
{r:The glasses must be cleaned before the party.} - Ko'zoynaklar ziyofat oldidan tozalanishi kerak.

text: {r:Tonight}[təˈnaɪt] - bugun kechqurun. Today(bugun) ning qisqartirilgan shakli va night(tun) so'zlarining birlashuvidan yasalgan.
examples: {r:You must finish the report tonight.} - Hisobotni bugun kechqurun tugatishingiz kerak.
{r:We must decide about your future tonight.} - Kelajaging haqida bugun kechgacha qaror qilishimiz kerak.
{r:Guests must arrive tonight.} - Mehmonlar bugun kechqurungacha kelishlari kerak.
{r:I must call you tonight.} - Men bugun tunda sizga telefon qilishim kerak.

text: {r:Opposition}[ˌɒpəˈzɪʃən] - muxolifat; qarshilik. Oppose(qarshi chiqmoq) so'zidan yasalgan.
examples: {r:I had no opposition from my parents.} - Ota-onamdan qarshilik bo'lmadi.
{r:We must respect opposition opinions.} - Biz muxolifat fikrlarini hurmat qilishimiz kerak.
{r:This newspaper is about opposition.} - Bu gazeta muxolifat haqida.
{r:Leaders must listen to opposition voices.} - Rahbarlar muxolifat ovozlarini tinglashlari kerak.

text: {r:Truly}[ˈtruːli] - haqiqatdan, chinakam. True(to'g'ri, rost) so'zining ravish shakli.
examples: {r:You must truly understand the rules.} - Siz qoidalarni haqiqatdan ham tushunishingiz kerak.
{r:We must be truly honest with each other.} - Biz bir-birimizga chinakam rostgo'y bo'lishimiz kerak.
{r:Your arrival will truly make your parents happy.} - Kechirim chinakam yaxshi bo'lishi kerak.
{r:I truly hate yellow pencils.} - Men haqiqatdan sariq qalamlardan nafratlanaman.

text: {r:Movement}[ˈmuːvmənt] - harakat. Move(harakatlantirmoq; ko'chmoq) so'zidan yasalgan.
examples: {r:Patients must do regular movement work.} - Bemorlar muntazam harakat qilishlari kerak.
{r:We must support the environmental movement.} - Biz atrof-muhit harakatini qo'llab-quvvatlashimiz kerak.
{r:Independence movement must fight from the beginning to the end.} - Ozodlik harakati boshidan oxirigacha kurashishi kerak.
{r:Workers must control every movement.} - Ishchilar har bir harakatni nazorat qilishlari kerak.

text: {r:Clearly}[ˈklɪərli] - aniq, tiniq, ochiq, tushunarli. Clear so'zining ravish shakli.
examples: {r:Instructions must be written clearly.} - Ko'rsatmalar aniq yozilishi kerak.
{r:You must speak clearly during a talk.} - Suhbat paytida aniq gapirishingiz kerak.
{r:The writer must explain clearly.} - Yozuvchi aniq-tiniq tushuntirishi kerak.
{r:Students must explain answers clearly.} - Talabalar javoblarni aniq tushuntirishlari kerak.

text: {r:Quick}[kwɪk] – tez. Agar {p:KUYUK} hidni sezsangiz {h:tez} qoching.
examples: {r:You must be quick with your decision.} - Qaroringizni tez qabul qilishingiz kerak.
{r:We must find a quick solution.} - Biz tez yechim topishimiz kerak.
{r:The response must be quick and accurate.} - Javob tez va aniq bo'lishi kerak.
{r:Beginners are not usually quick.} - Boshlang'ichlar odatda tez emas.

text: {r:Maximum}[ˈmæksɪməm] - maksimal, maksimum.
examples: {r:Guys can jump a maximum of 6 meters, and girls 4 meters.} - Yigitlar maksimal 6 metrga va qizlar 4 metrga sakray oladi.
{r:The temperature must not exceed maximum.} - Harorat maksimaldan oshmasligi kerak.
{r:I don't want a middle level, I want maximum efficiency.} - Men o'rtacha darajani xohlamayman, men maksimal samaradorlikni xohlayman.
{r:This class must take a maximum of 32 students.} - Bu sinf maksimal 32 ta o'quvchini qabul qila oladi.

text: {r:Lecture}[ˈlektʃər] - leksiya; leksiya o'qimoq.
examples: {r:You must attend tomorrow's lecture.} - Ertangi ma'ruzaga qatnashishingiz kerak.
{r:Phones must be silent during lectures.} - Ma'ruzalar davomida telefonlar ovozsiz rejimda bo'lishi kerak.
{r:We were having the lecture outside yesterday and suddenly the strong wind blew.} - Kecha tashqarida ma'ruzamiz bo'layotgandi va kutilmaganda kuchli shamol esib qoldi.
{r:Questions must be asked after the lecture.} - Savollar ma'ruza tugagandan so'ng berilishi kerak.

text: {r:Cloudy}[ˈklaʊdi] - bulutli. Cloud(bulut) so'zidan yasalgan. Mnemonik namuna uchun 22 - darsga qarang.
examples: {r:You should take an umbrella; it’s cloudy and cool.} - Soyabon olishingiz kerak; havo bulutli va salqin.
{r:She should stay in the house if it’s cloudy.} - Agar havo bulutli bo'lsa, u uyda qolishi kerak.
{r:Mountainous villages are very cloudy today.} - Bugun tog'li qishloqlar juda bulutli.
{r:My parents should check the weather news. It might be cloudy tomorrow.} - Ota-onam ob-havo yangiliklarini tekshirishi kerak. Ertaga havo bulutli bo'lishi mumkin.

text: {r:Careful}[ˈkeərfəl] – ehtiyotkor. Kecha ovqatlangandan keyin qornim og’ridi. KIR PULni ushlab qo’limni yuvmasdan ovqatlangandim restoranda, shundan bo’lsa kerak. Bundan keyin juda ham {h:ehtiyotkor} bo’laman ayniqsa {p:KIR PUL}dan.
examples: {r:You should be careful on the road.} - Yo'lda ehtiyot bo'lishingiz kerak.
{r:My grandfather should be careful when installing iron roof.} - Temir shifrlarni qo'yishda bobom ehtiyot bo'lishi kerak.
{r:Be careful if you compare these two.} - Agar bu ikkisini solishtirsangiz ehtiyot bo'ling.
{r:Be careful! Children are throwing oranges at us.} - Ehtiyot bo'l! Bolalar bizga mandarinlar otishyapti.

text: {r:Should}[ʃʊd] - kerak, lozim. Suv tanqis bo'lgan cho'l joylarda o'simliklar ertalabki SHUDringdan ozgina bo'lsa ham suv ichishadi va omon qolishadi. Katta muammoga duch kelgan vaqtingizda siz ham o'zingizni {p:SHUD}ringizni topishingiz {h:lozim}.
examples: {r:You should call your friend.} - Siz do'stingizga qo'ng'iroq qilishingiz kerak.
{r:She should knock the door immediately.} - U zudlik bilan eshikni taqillatishi lozim.
{r:They should not ignore the problem.} - Ular muammoni e'tiborsiz qoldirmasligi kerak.
{r:Should we go home now?} - Hozir uyga borishimiz kerakmi?

text: {r:Belt}[bɛlt] – belbog’, kamar, remen. Tasavvur qiling {p:BEL}ingizda {p:T}ovuq ramzi tushirilgan {h:kamar} tutib yuribsiz.
examples: {r:You should wear a belt in the car.} - Avtomobilda kamarni bog'lab olishingiz kerak.
{r:His belt was stolen yesterday.} - Uning kamari kecha o'g'irlandi.
{r:They should not forget to wear their belts.} - Ular kamar bog'lashni unutmasligi kerak.
{r:My parents should remind me to wear a belt.} - Ota-onam menga kamar bog'lab olishni eslatishi kerak.

text: {r:Far}[fɑː] – uzoq. Biz ertaklarda bag’rikeng farishtalar haqida o’qiymiz. Amakimning aytishicha {p:FAR}ishtalar bu yerlarda yo’q. Ular juda {h:uzoq} yerlarda yashashadi.
examples: {r:You should not go too far alone.} - Siz yolg'iz juda uzoqqa bormasligingiz kerak.
{r:We have gone far to repair a bridge.} - Biz ko'prikni ta'mirlash uchun uzoq joylarga bordik.
{r:They should not go too far from home.} - Ular uydan juda uzoqqa ketmasligi kerak.
{r:We have never traveled far.} - Biz hech qachon uzoqqa sayohat qilmaganmiz.

text: {r:Advice}[ədˈvaɪs] – maslahat. Ko’p pul topmoqchimisiz, bir {h:maslahatim} bor. Advokat bo’ling, {p:ADV}okatni {p:VAYS}aqisi bo’ling, ya’ni ko’p gapiring. Shunda ko’p klentlaringiz bo’ladi va ko’p pul topasiz.
examples: {r:You should listen to your parents’ advice.} - Siz ota-onangizning maslahatlariga quloq solishingiz kerak.
{r:She should give useful advice at least once.} - U hech bo'lmasa bir marta foydali maslahatlar berishi kerak.
{r:I should get advice from the winners.} - Men g'oliblardan maslahat olishim kerak.
{r:What is your advice to us?} - Sizning bizga maslahatingiz nima?

text: {r:Rest}[rɛst] – dam olmoq;dam. Men odatda {p:rest}oranlarda {h:dam olaman.} Sizchi, qayerda dam olishni yaxshi ko’rasiz?
examples: [center][b]get some rest/have a rest - dam olmoq.[/b][/center]
{r:You should have a rest after work.} - Ishdan keyin dam olishingiz kerak.
{r:Get rest before a busy day.} - Katta ishdan oldin yaxshilab dam ol.
{r:They should rest before the big day.} - Ular katta kun oldidan dam olishi kerak.
{r:My assistant should remind me to rest.} - Yordamchim menga dam olishni eslatishi kerak.
{r:He needs to get some rest} – U biroz dam olishi kerak.

text: {r:Resource}[ˈriːsɔːs] - resurs, manba. Bir xil so'zlar.
examples: {r:I should use resources well.} - Men resurslarni oqilona ishlatishim kerak.
{r:Our country should not waste resources.} - Mamlakatimiz resurslarni isrof qilmasligi kerak.
{r:John should share resources with others.} - Jon resurslarni boshqalar bilan ulashishi kerak.
{r:Their teacher should teach them to save resources.} - Ularning o'qituvchisi ularga resurslarni tejashni o'rgatishi kerak.

text: {r:Legend}[ˈlɛdʒənd] - afsona, legenda. Bir xil so'zlar!
examples: {r:The journalist should read about this place's legends.} - Jurnalist bu joyning afsonalari haqida o'qishi kerak.
{r:My grandmother should tell the legend to the children.} - Mening buvim bolalarga afsonani aytishi kerak.
{r:We should not forget our old legends.} - Biz o'z madaniy afsonalarimizni unutmasligimiz kerak.
{r:Anvar should share family legends with his children.} - Anvar oilaviy afsonalarni o'z farzandlari bilan ulashishi kerak.

text: {r:Accident}[ˈæksɪdənt] – baxtsiz voqea, halokat. Tasavvur qiling ‘’Muzlik davri’’ multfilmida {p:AK}angiz va {p:SID} chana uchishyapti va ikkovlon yo’lda turgan {p:ANT}enaga borib urilishdi. {h:Avariya} qilishdi.
examples: {r:You should drive carefully to avoid accidents.} - Siz avtohalokatlardan qochish uchun ehtiyotkorlik bilan haydashingiz kerak.
{r:The doctor should tell about the accident immediately.} - Shifokor halokatni darhol xabar qilishi kerak.
{r:The team should not ignore safety rules to stop accidents.} - Jamoa halokatlarning oldini olish uchun xavfsizlik qoidalarini e'tiborsiz qoldirmasligi kerak.
{r:His uncle should teach him how to work with accidents.} - Uning amakisi unga halokatlarni qanday hal qilishni o'rgatishi kerak.

text: {r:Visit}[ˈvɪzɪt] - vizit, tashrif; tashrif buyurmoq. Mening bir yomon odatim bor. Agar to'yga aytishsayu lekin {p:VIZIT}ka berishmasa men o'sha to'yga {h:bor}mayman.
examples: {r:My friend should visit the new art place.} - Mening do'stim yangi san'at muzeyiga tashrif buyurishi kerak.
{r:We should visit our grandparents more times.} - Biz buvi va bobolarimizga tez-tez tashrif buyurishimiz kerak.
{r:Tourists should visit the old city center.} - Sayyohlar eski shahar markaziga tashrif buyurishlari kerak.
{r:He stopped his visit to his hometown because of a storm.} - U ona shahriga bo'lgan tashrifni bo'ron tufayli to'xtatdi.

text: {r:Painter}[ˈpeɪntər] - rassom; bo'yoqchi. Paint(bo'yamoq) so'zidan olingan.
examples: {r:I should meet that famous painter.} - Men o'sha mashhur rassom bilan uchrashishim kerak.
{r:Young painters should study great painters.} - Yosh rassomlar buyuk rassomlarni o'rganishlari kerak.
{r:This painter should complete his artwork immediately.} - Bu rassom asarini tezda bitirishi kerak.
{r:I have an appointment with a famous painter.} - Mashhur rassom bilan uchrashuvim bor.

text: {r:Cup}[kʌp] – krushka, stakan. Mening {h:krushkamga} {p:KAP}alak rasmi tushurilgan. Nimadir issiq suyuqlik quyilsa rasmi chiqib keladi.
examples: {r:You should drink not less than 8 cups of water every day.} - Siz kuniga kamida 8 stakan suv ichishingiz kerak.
{r:My wife should buy new tea cups.} - Mening xotinim yangi choy stakanlari sotib olishi kerak.
{r:The guests should use the blue cups.} - Mehmonlar ko'k stakanlardan foydalanishlari kerak.
{r:The waiter should bring clean cups.} - Ofitsiant toza stakanlar olib kelishi kerak.

text: {r:Then}[ðɛn] – keyin; o’sha vaqtda. Rasmga qarang, avval plyaj, {h:keyin} {p:DEN}giz joylashgan.
examples: {r:He should study first, then rest.} - U avval o'qishi kerak, keyin dam olishi kerak.
{r:We should check the map, then decide.} - Biz avval xaritani tekshirib ko'rishimiz kerak, keyin qaror qilishimiz kerak.
{r:The students should listen, then ask questions.} - Talabalar avval tinglashlari kerak, keyin savol berishlari kerak.
{r:Painter should paint bread first, then fruits.} - Rassom avval nonni, keyin mevalarni chizishi kerak.

text: {r:Until}[ənˈtɪl] - 'gacha', 'qadar', '… bo‘lguncha' degan ma’nolarni anglatadi. U vaqtni bildiruvchi kontekstlarda ishlatiladi.
examples: {r:I will wait until you come.} - Sen kelgunga qadar kutaman.
{r:The shop is open until 10 PM.} - Do‘kon kechki soat 10 gacha ochiq.
{r:She didn’t sleep until midnight.} - U yarim kechagacha uxlamadi.
{r:Wait here until I return.} - Men qaytgunimcha shu yerda kut.

text: {r:Lifelong}[ˈlaɪflɒŋ] - umrbod, bir umr(lik). Life(hayot) va long(uzun) so'zlaridan yasalgan.
examples: {r:A scientist should do lifelong learning.} - Olim hayot davomida o'rganishni davom ettirishi kerak.
{r:We should keep good lifelong friends.} - Biz bir umrlik do'stlarni qadrlashimiz kerak.
{r:Her husband should make lifelong habits.} - Uning eri umrbod qoladigan odatlarni rivojlantirishi kerak.
{r:Everyone should have lifelong aims.} - Har bir insonda bir umrlik maqsadlar bo'lishi kerak.

text: {r:Hourly}[ˈaʊərli] - har soat; soatbay(oylik va ish haqi uchun). Hour(soat) so'zidan yasalgan.
examples: {r:The doctor should check the patient's temperature hourly.} - Shifokor bemorning haroratini soatlab tekshirishi kerak.
{r:Workers should take hourly rest.} - Ishchilar har soat tanaffus olishlari kerak.
{r:The bus should come hourly.} - Avtobus har soat kelishi kerak.
{r:What is an hourly pay for barbers and waiters?} - Sartarosh va ofitsiantlarga soatlik ish haqi qancha?

text: {r:Hospitable}[hɒˈspɪtəbəl] - mehmondo'st.
examples: {r:The hotel owner should be hospitable to guests.} - Mehmonxona egasi mehmonlarga mehmondo'st bo'lishi kerak.
{r:Hotels should do hospitable work.} - Mehmonxonalar mehmondo'st xizmat qilishlari kerak.
{r:Parents should teach children to be truly hospitable.} - Ota-onalar bolalarga chinakam mehmondo'st bo'lishni o'rgatishlari kerak.
{r:The restaurant staff should be more hospitable.} - Restoran xodimlari ko'proq mehmondo'st bo'lishlari kerak.

text: {r:Wipe}[waɪp] – artmoq. Tasavvur qiling {p:veyp}(elektron sigaret shunday nomlanadi)chekib pol {h:artyapsiz}.
examples: {r:Finally my wife is wiping the table.} - Nihoyat xotinim stolni artyapti.
{r:The dog should wipe its paws before entering the house.} - Kuchuk uyga kirishdan oldin panjalarini artib olishi kerak.
{r:The cleaner should wipe the windows today.} - Tozalovchi bugun derazalarni artishi kerak.
{r:Normally students wipe the board after a lesson.} - Odatda talabalar darsdan keyin doskani artib tashlashlari kerak.

text: {r:Phone}[foʊn] - telefon.
examples: {r:You should turn off your phone during meetings.} - Siz yig'ilishlar paytida telefonni o'chirib qo'yishingiz kerak.
{r:His grandmother should buy a new phone.} - Uning buvisi yangi telefon sotib olishi kerak.
{r:I lost my phone yesterday at the station.} - Men kecha telefonimni bekatda yo'qotdim.
{r:Students shouldn't use phones in class.} - Talabalar darsda telefonlardan foydalanmasliklari kerak.

text: {r:Obligation}[ɒblɪˈɡeɪʃən] – burch, vazifa, majburiyat. Mening dadam duradgor har kuni yog’ochlardan har xil buyumlar yasaydi. Yog’ochdan chiqqan mayda qipiqlar nima deyilishini bilasizmi? Ular apilka deb ataladi. Mening {h:vazifam} dadam chiqargan {p:APILKA}larni {p:SHUN}day to’g’ri mollarga olib borib ularni to’ydirish.
examples: {r:I have to fulfill my obligation.} - Men o'z majburiyatimni bajarishim kerak.
{r:She has to understand her obligation.} - U o'z majburiyatini tushunishi kerak.
{r:The team has to do its obligation.} - Jamoa o'z majburiyatini bajarishi kerak.
{r:It is my obligation to take a bath and cut my beard every day.} - Har kuni yuvinish va soqolimni kesish mening vazifam.

text: {r:Opinion}[əˈpɪnjən] - fikr. Agar qurbaqa shahzoda boshidan o'psangizu lekin qaytib shahzodaga aylanmasa, mening {h:fikrimcha} bu safar {p:O'PIN YON}idan.
examples: {r:What is your opinion on petrol price rise?} - Benzin narxi o'sishiga fikringiz qalay?
{r:Julia has to respect others’ opinions.} - Julia boshqalarning fikrlarini hurmat qilishi kerak.
{r:My opinion about horror movies is negative.} - Mening qo'rqinchli filmlarga fikrim salbiy.
{r:Her teacher has to listen to your opinion.} - Uning o'qituvchisi sizning fikringizga quloq solishi kerak.

text: {r:Personal}[ˈpɜːrsənl] - shaxsiy, personal. Person(shaxs) so'zidan olingan. O'zbek tilida ham hozirgi kunda keng qo'llanilmoqda.
examples: {r:I have to keep my personal belongings safe.} - Men shaxsiy narsalarimni xavfsiz saqlashim kerak.
{r:Anvar has to respect personal space.} - Anvar shaxsiy makonni hurmat qilishi kerak.
{r:Journalists have to share personal information.} - Jurnalistlar shaxsiy ma'lumotlarni ulashishi kerak.
{r:My brother has to teach me about personal responsibility.} - Mening akam menga shaxsiy mas'uliyat haqida o'rgatishi kerak.

text: {r:Military}[ˈmɪlɪteri] – harbiy. Ispaniyada davlatida dunyodagi eng qisqa harbiy xizmat mavjud. Ularda {h:harbiy} xizmat atigi 5 {p:MINUTLI}.
examples: {r:He has to learn about military history.} - U harbiy tarix haqida o'rganishi kerak.
{r:His father has to respect military service.} - Uning otasi harbiy xizmatni hurmat qilishi kerak.
{r:They have to join the military.} - Ular harbiy xizmatga qo'shilishi kerak.
{r:Our teacher has to explain the importance of the military.} - Bizning o'qituvchimiz harbiy xizmatning ahamiyatini tushuntirishi kerak.

text: {r:Low}[loʊ] – past. Uzuklar hukmdoridagi past bo’yli elflarni eslaysizmi. Ular juda ko’p {p:LOV}iya yeganligi uchun shunday {h:past} bo’yli ekan.
examples: {r:I have to keep the volume low.} - Men ovozni past saqlashim kerak.
{r:She has to speak in a low voice.} - U past ovozda gapirishi kerak.
{r:I bought this bag at a low cost.} - Men bu sumkani past narxda sotib oldim.
{r:I come from a low income family.} - Men past daromadli oiladanman.

text: {r:Wonder}[ˈwʌndər] – bilishni xohlamoq, o'ylamoq; hayratlanmoq. Yangi uy sotib oldim, {p:vanna der}azasi juda antiqa ekan, pushti rangda ushlagichi chinnidan. Nimaga bunday ekan deb {h:bilishni xohladim} va {h:hayratlandim}.
examples: {r:We have to wonder about the future.} - Biz kelajak haqida o'ylashimiz kerak.
{r:John has to wonder why it happened.} - John nima uchun bu sodir bo'lganini o'ylashi kerak.
{r:Our team has to wonder about new plans.} - Bizning jamoamiz yangi rejalar haqida o'ylashi kerak.
{r:Your decision caused much wonder.} - Sening qaroring ko'p hayratlarga sabab bo'ldi.
{r:This country is full of wonders.} - Bu davlat hayratlarga to'la.

text: {r:Change}[tʃeɪndʒ] – o’zgarmoq, o’zgartirmoq; o'zgarish. Mana bu sehrli jevachka. Agar hozir sen yashayotgan joy, muhit, ish yoqmasa {p:CHAYN}a {p:J}evachkani shunda hamma narsa {h:o’zgarib} boshqa joy, muhit va ishda paydo bo’lasan.
examples: {r:I have to change my habits.} - Men o'z odatlarimni o'zgartirishim kerak.
{r:We need changes.} - Bizga o'zgarishlar kerak.
{r:They have to change their plans.} - Ular rejalarini o'zgartirishi kerak.
{r:My husband is a boring person. He never changes.} - Erim zerikarli kishi. U hech qachon o'zgarmaydi.

text: {r:Meaning}[ˈmiːnɪŋ] – ma’no. 30 yil maktabda dars berganman. Ba’zi o’quvchilarim hozirgacha xabar olib turishadi. Agar ko’chada yurgan paytim mashinasi bilan kelib {p:‘’MINING} ustoz sizni oborib qo’yaman’’ deyishi men uchun katta {h:ma’noni} bildiradi.
examples: {r:You have to understand the meaning of this word.} - Siz bu so'zning ma'nosini tushunishingiz kerak.
{r:A teacher has to explain the meaning clearly.} - O'qituvchi ma'noni aniq tushuntirishi kerak.
{r:His cat has to understand the meaning of 'no'.} - Uning mushugi 'yo'q' so'zining ma'nosini tushunishi kerak.
{r:Our husbands have to teach us the meaning of responsibility.} - Bizning erlarimiz bizga mas'uliyatning ma'nosini o'rgatishi kerak.

text: {r:Scientist}[ˈsaɪəntɪst] - olim. Science(ilm) so'zidan yasalgan.
examples: {r:I have to meet the scientist tomorrow.} - Men ertaga olim bilan uchrashishim kerak.
{r:Nargiza has to listen to the scientist’s advice.} - Nargiza olimning maslahatiga quloq solishi kerak.
{r:Lawyers have to agree with the scientist.} - Advokatlar olim bilan bir fikrga kelishi kerak.
{r:Your teacher has to respect the scientist’s work.} - Sizning o'qituvchingiz olimning ishini hurmat qilishi kerak.

text: {r:Windy}[ˈwɪndi] - shamolli. Wind(shamol) so'zidan yasalgan. Mnemonik namuna uchun 24 - darsdagi wind ga qarang.
examples: {r:It is windy twice a week.} - Haftada ikki marta shamolli bo'lyapti.
{r:She has to close the windows; it’s windy.} - U derazalarni yopishi kerak; hozir shamolli.
{r:Driver has to drive home now; it is windy.} - Haydovchi bu shamolli havoda tezroq uyga haydashi kerak.
{r:When is the next windy day?} - Keyingi shamolli kun qachon?

text: {r:Logical}[ˈlɒdʒɪkl] - mantiqiy, logichniy. Logic(mantiq) so'zidan yasalgan.
examples: {r:You have to think logically to solve this puzzle.} - Bu jumboqni hal qilish uchun mantiqiy fikrlashingiz kerak.
{r:It is logical to expect only lies from a liar.} - Yolg'onchidan faqat yolg'on gaplarni kutish mantiqli.
{r:The doctor has to make logical decisions based on facts.} - Shifokor faktlarga asoslangan mantiqiy qarorlar qabul qilishi kerak.
{r:Your opinion is not very logical.} - Sening fikring unchalik ham mantiqiy emas.

text: {r:Owner}[ˈoʊnər] - egasi. Own(egalik qilmoq) so'zidan yasalgan.
examples: {r:The owner is a big liar.} - Bu yerning egasi katta yolg'onchi.
{r:We have to contact the owner before making changes.} - O'zgarishlar kiritishdan oldin egasiga murojaat qilishimiz kerak.
{r:His brother is the owner of this cinema.} - Uning akasi bu kinoteatrning egasi.
{r:He was a needy person first. Then he suddenly became a bank owner.} - U avval muhtoj kishi edi. Keyinchalik to'satdan bank egasiga aylandi.

text: {r:Celebrity}[səˈlebrɪti] – shou biznes yulduzlari. Amerika shou biznes yulduzlarining g’alati qiliqlari bor. Yaqinda {p:SELE}na Gomez {p:BRIT}vani reklama qilib chiqibdi. Baraka topgur sen qiz bola bo’lsang nima qilasan britvani reklama qilib?
examples: {r:Celebrities have to be careful about their public image.} - Mashhurlar o'zlarining omma oldidagi imidjiga ehtiyotkorlik bilan qarashi kerak.
{r:I met this celebrity twice.} - Men bu yulduzni ikki marta uchratganman.
{r:The cinema owner has to provide security for celebrities.} - Kinoteatr egasi mashhurlar uchun xavfsizlikni ta'minlashi kerak.
{r:She has to write about exactly these celebrities.} - U aynan mana shu yulduzlar haqida yozishi kerak.

text: {r:Gradual}[ˈɡrædʒuəl] – asta-sekin, bosqichma-bosqich. Tasavvur qiling siz qo’li gul mohir ustasiz. Kichkina {p:GARAJ}ingizni{p: VIL}laga aylantirib tashladingiz {h:bosqichma-bosqich}.
examples: {r:We have to make gradual improvements.} - Biz asta-sekin yaxshilanishlarga erishishimiz kerak.
{r:The changes have to be implemented gradually.} - O'zgarishlar asta-sekin amalga oshirilishi kerak.
{r:Her brother is making gradual results.} - Uning akasi asta-sekin natijalar qilyapti.
{r:The patient has to show gradual improvement.} - Bemor asta-sekin yaxshilanishi kerak.

text: {r:Gesture}[ˈdʒestʃər] – imo-ishora, jest(rus tilida). Siz rasmda ko’rib turgan imo-ishora shashlikchilar orasida juda keng tarqalgan. Agar mijoz shu {h:ishorani} ko’rsatsa bu “{p:JIZ}zani {p:CHIR}oyli, mazzali qilib bering” degani bo’ladi.
examples: {r:What is the meaning of this gesture?} - Bu ishoraning ma'nosi nima?
{r:A speaker has to use appropriate gestures.} - Nutq so'zlovchi mos imo-ishoralardan foydalanishi kerak.
{r:His friend has to appreciate kind gestures.} - Uning do'sti yaxshi imo-ishoralarni qadrlashi kerak.
{r:Our teacher has to explain gestures in language classes.} - Bizning o'qituvchimiz til darslarida imo-ishoralarni tushuntirishi kerak.

text: {r:Related}[rɪˈleɪtɪd] - bog‘liq, aloqador, qarindosh. 'Related' so‘zi o‘zbek tilida 'bog‘liq', 'aloqador', 'qarindosh' degan ma’nolarni anglatadi. U turli kontekstlarda ishlatiladi: 1) 'These two topics are closely related.' — 'Bu ikki mavzu bir-biri bilan chambarchas bog‘liq.' 2) 'Is he related to you?' — 'U sizga qarindoshmi?' 3) 'She studies subjects related to biology.' — 'U biologiyaga aloqador fanlarni o‘rganadi.' 4) 'His illness is related to stress.' — 'Uning kasalligi stress bilan bog‘liq.'
examples: {r:I have to study all related materials.} - Men tegishli barcha materiallarni o'rganishim kerak.
{r:The two are not related.} - Bu ikkitasi qarindosh emas.
{r:Anvar has to find information related to our topic.} - Anvar mavzumizga tegishli ma'lumotlarni topishi kerak.
{r:I have news related to politics.} - Menda siyosatga aloqador yangiliklar bor.

text: {r:Employee}[ɛmˈplɔɪ.iː] – xodim, ishchi. Siz mana bu rasmni oldin ko’rgan bo’lsangiz kerak. Bular Xitoy {p:IMP}eratorining {p:LOY}dan yasalgan saroy {h:xodimlar}i. Qadimgi Xitoyliklar bu haykallar imperator vafotidan keyin ham unga xizmat qilishiga ishonishgan.
examples: {r:The company has over 500 employees.} – Kompaniyada 500 dan ortiq xodim ishlaydi.
{r:She is a loyal and hardworking employee.} – U sodiq va mehnatkash xodim.
{r:Every employee must attend the meeting.} – Har bir xodim yig‘ilishga qatnashishi kerak.
{r:New employees receive training.} – Yangi xodimlar treningdan o‘tadilar.

text: {r:Policy}[ˈpɒlɪsi] – siyosat, dastur. Dehqon amakim mahallasi chekkasidagi yerni o’zlashtirib tarvuz ekibdi va keyinchalik dadam ularni ogohlantirdilar ‘’Ey bu {p:polizi}ngni davlat yeriga ekkansan, davlat {h:siyosati} o’zboshimchalik bilan yer o’zlashtirishga qarshi’’.
examples: {r:Employees have to follow company policies.} - Xodimlar kompaniya qoidalariga amal qilishlari kerak.
{r:Her intention is to change the company policies.} - Uning niyati kompaniya siyosatini o'zgartirish.
{r:Keeping cities clean is a government policy.} - Shaharlarni toza saqlash bu hukumat siyosati.
{r:The school has to enforce its attendance policy.} - Maktab darsga qatnash qoidalarini qat'iy tatbiq etishi kerak.

text: {r:Actually}[ˈæktʃuəli] – aslida. Telefonimni sotish uchun bozorga olib bordim va xaridorlardan biri ‘’Aka buni 500 000 ga ham ololmayman {h:aslida}, chunki {p:EK}rani {p:SHILI}nib ketgan’’ dedi.
examples: {r:Actually John has to do the work, not just plan it.} - John aslida ishni qilishi kerak, shunchaki planlashtirmasdan.
{r:The scientist has to actually understand the concepts.} - Olim bu konsepsiyalarni aslida tushunishi kerak.
{r:Actually we have to practice what we learn.} - Biz o'rgangan narsalarimizni amalda qo'llashimiz kerak.
{r:Clear sky is not blue actually.} - Musaffo osmon rangi aslida ko'k emas.

text: {r:Nation}[ˈneɪʃən] - millat, xalq. 19 - asrda Xitoy Yevropa davlatlariga bo'ysunmagan qudratli imperiya edi. Yevropaliklar bu millatni sindirish uchun {p:NASHAN}i mamlakatga kiritishni boshlaydi va tez orada {h:millat} xarob bo'lishiga erishadi.
examples: {r:Citizens have to respect national symbols.} - Fuqarolar milliy ramzlarni hurmat qilishi kerak.
{r:I have to learn about my nation's history.} - Men millatim tarixini o'rganishim kerak.
{r:This nation is ready to do everything to have independence.} - Bu millat mustaqillikka erishish uchun hamma narsaga tayyor.
{r:Our leaders have to unite the nation.} - Bizning rahbarlarimiz millatni birlashtirishi kerak.

text: {r:Nervous}[ˈnɜːrvəs] - nervniy, asabiy.
examples: {r:You have to control nervous feelings before speaking.} - Gapirishdan oldin asabiy hissiyotlaringizni boshqarishingiz kerak.
{r:He was nervous about being late for his job appointment.} - U ish uchrashuviga kechikishidan xavotirda edi.
{r:Take a shower if you are nervous.} - Agar asabiy bo'lsangiz dush qabul qiling.
{r:I am a quiet guy. I don't get nervous quickly.} - Men juda sokin yigitman. Tez asabiy bo'lmayman.

text: {r:Polite}[pəˈlaɪt] - odobli, xushfe'l. Biz aka-ukalar hammamiz {h:odobli} bo'lib katta bo'ldik. Chunki dadamiz qattiqqo'l edilar. 'Agar beodoblik qilsak, silarga naryad, {p:POL ART}asan' der edilar.
examples: {r:Our children would like to be more polite.} - Bizning bolalarimiz yanada odobliroq bo'lishni xohlashadi.
{r:I’d like to learn how to be polite.} - Men qanday qilib odobli bo'lishni o'rganishni xohlayman.
{r:Everybody is polite in my town.} - Mening shaharchamda har bir kishi odobli.
{r:My grandfather would like to teach his grandchildren politeness.} - Bobom nevaralariga odob-axloqni o'rgatishni xohlardi.

text: {r:Tomato}[təˈmɑːtoʊ] - pomidor. Menimcha bu yerda {p:tomat} so'zini eslash kifoya!
examples: {r:Would your mother like a tomato in her salad?} - Onangiz salatiga pomidor qo'shishni xohlaydimi?
{r:My uncle would like to grow tomatoes in his garden.} - Amakim bog'ida pomidor o'stirishni xohlaydi.
{r:Julia wouldn't like to eat raw tomatoes.} - Julia xom pomidor yeyishni xohlamaydi.
{r:The chef would like to make tomato soup.} - Oshpaz pomidor sho'rva tayyorlashni xohlardi.

text: {r:Career}[kəˈrɪər] - karyera. Bir xil so'zlar!
examples: {r:Would the scientist like to pursue a career in science?} - Olim fanda karyera qilishni xohlaydimi?
{r:I’d like to choose a career that I love.} - Men o'zim yoqtirgan karyerani tanlashni xohlayman.
{r:They wouldn't like to give up on their career dreams.} - Ular karyera orzularidan voz kechishni xohlashmaydi.
{r:His parents would like to support his career choice.} - Uning ota-onasi uning karyera tanlovini qo'llab-quvvatlashni xohlardi.

text: {r:Effect}[ɪˈfekt] - ta'sir, effekt, oqibat. Bir xil so'zlar!
examples: {r:Would the buyer like to know the effect of this decision?} - Xaridor ushbu qarorning oqibatini bilishni xohlaydimi?
{r:I’d like to understand the effect of my actions.} - Men o'z harakatlarimning oqibatini tushunishni xohlayman.
{r:The company wouldn't like to ignore the negative effects.} - Kompaniya salbiy oqibatlarni e'tiborga olmaslikni xohlamaydi.
{r:Their teacher would like to explain the long-term effects.} - Ularning o'qituvchisi uzoq muddatli ta'sirlarini tushuntirishni xohlardi.

text: {r:Sign}[saɪn] – belgi; imzolamoq. Ibn Sinoning asl ismi Husayn bo’lgan. Uning kelajakda yetuk olim bo’lishi go’dakligidan ma'lum edi, shuning belgilari bor edi. Masalan u 2 yoshida o’qishni o’rganadi, 10 yoshida qo’llanma yozadi. Hu{p:SAYN} olimlik {h:belgi}lariga boy edi.
examples: {r:Would you like to see the sign?} - Belgini ko'rishni xohlaysizmi?
{r:My dog would like to follow the sign to the park.} - Mening itim bog'ga borish uchun belgiga amal qilishni xohlaydi.
{r:They wouldn't like to miss the sign.} - Ular belgini o'tkazib yuborishni xohlashmaydi.
{r:The police officer would like to point out the sign.} - Politsiya xodimi belgini ko'rsatishni xohlardi.

text: {r:Favour}[ˈfeɪvər] – iltifot, marhamat; yordam ko’mak. Doimo kulib turishi bilan mashhur bo’lgan qo’shiqchi Alisher {p:FAY}z {p:VR}achlik bilan shug’ullanyapti endi. Odamlarni ham bitta kulib qo’yishi bilan davolab yuboryapti ekan. Eng muhimi hammaga {h:iltifot} ko’rsatib konsultatsiyaga pul olmayapti.
examples: {r:Would you like to do me a favor?} - Menga yordam bera olasizmi?
{r:Anvar would like to ask for a small favor.} - Anvar kichik bir yordam so'rashni xohlaydi.
{r:The politician does not want to refuse a favor.} - Siyosatchi yordamni rad etishni xohlamaydi.
{r:My neighbor would like to return the favor.} - Mening qo'shnim yordamni qaytarishni xohlardi.

text: {r:Marry}[ˈmæri] – turmush qurmoq, uylanmoq, tegmoq. Malika turmush qurish uchun eng mohir merganlarni yig’ibdi va dedi ‘’Bilaman hammangiz kuchli mergansiz, lekin yuragimni zabt etgan {p:MER}ganga {h:tegaman}’’
examples: {r:Would Julia like to marry someday?} - Julia bir kuni turmush qurishni xohlaydimi?
{r:She wants to marry a rich guy.} - U boy yigitga tegishni xohlaydi.
{r:25 is the perfect age to marry.} - 25 turmush qurish uchun mukammal yosh.
{r:He wants to marry a rich girl.} - U boy qizga uylanishni xohlaydi.

text: {r:Dress}[dres] – kiyim; kiyinmoq. Boradigan joyga a{p:dres}ga qarab {h:kiyinish} kerak, to’yga kostyum shim, ko’chaga yengil kiyim, uxlaganda esa pijama.
examples: {r:This dress suits you.} - Bu kiyim sizga mos tushadi.
{r:I’d like to buy a new dress for the party.} - Men ziyofat uchun yangi ko'ylak sotib olishni xohlayman.
{r:The celebrity wouldn't like to choose a casual dress.} - Mashhur shaxs oddiy ko'ylak tanlashni xohlamaydi.
{r:Her grandmother would like to see her in a traditional dress.} - Uning buvisi uni an'anaviy ko'ylakda ko'rishni xohlardi.

text: {r:Aunt}[ɑːnt] – xola, amma. Bu yil barcha xola va ammalarim tug’ilgan kuniga {p:ANT}ena sovg’a qildim.
examples: {r:My aunt lives in another city.} - Xolam boshqa shaharda yashaydi.
{r:His aunt hit the ball very hard.} - Uning xolasi to‘pni juda qattiq urdi.
{r:Her aunt always tells funny stories.} - Uning ammasi har doim kulgili hikoyalar aytadi.
{r:I love spending time with my aunt.} - Men xolam bilan vaqt o‘tkazishni yaxshi ko‘raman.

text: {r:Uncle}[ˈʌŋ.kəl] – tog‘a, amaki. Tasavvur qiling sizning birdaniga {p:ANGL}iyalik {h:amakingiz} paydo bo’lib sizga million funt meros qoldirganini aytayapti.
examples: {r:My uncle is a doctor.} - Tog‘am shifokor.
{r:She visited her uncle last summer.} - U o‘tgan yozda amakisini ziyorat qildi.
{r:Perhaps, my uncle is asleep now.} - Balkim tog'am uxlayotgandir.
{r:I saw my uncle only once in life.} - Men amakimni hayotimda faqat bir marta ko'rganman.

text: {r:Preference}[ˈprefrəns] - afzallik berish, xohish, tanlov. 'Preference' so‘zi o‘zbek tilida 'afzallik berish', 'xohish', 'tanlov' degan ma’nolarni anglatadi. U turli kontekstlarda ishlatiladi: 1) 'I have a preference for tea over coffee.' — 'Men choyni qahvadan afzal ko‘raman.' 2) 'Her preference was to stay home.' — 'Uning xohishi uyda qolish edi.' 3) 'We try to consider customer preferences.' — 'Biz mijozlarning xohishlarini hisobga olishga harakat qilamiz.' 4) 'Color preference varies from person to person.' — 'Rangga bo‘lgan afzallik har bir kishida har xil bo‘ladi.'
examples: {r:I would like to know your tea preference.} - Men sizning choyga bo'lgan xohishingizni bilishni xohlar edim.
{r:Our team would like to satisfy your food preferences.} - Bizning jamoamiz sizning ovqatlanish istaklaringizni qondirishni xohlaydi.

text: {r:Understandable}[ˌʌndərˈstændəbl] - tushunarli. Understand(tushunmoq) so'zidan yasalgan.
examples: {r:Everything is understandable.} - Hamma narsa tushunarli.
{r:Would you like me to make it more understandable?} - Buni yanada tushunarli qilishimni xohlaysizmi?
{r:The committee would like the instructions to be understandable.} - Qo'mita ko'rsatmalar(instruksiyalar) tushunarli bo'lishini xohlaydi.
{r:Your hunger and thirst are understandable.} - Sening ochliging va chanqoqliging tushunarli.

text: {r:Thought}[θɔːt] - fikr, o'y. Think(o'ylamoq) so'zidan yasalgan. {p:SOAT} muxlisi sifatida mening {h:fikru-o'yim} Roleks soatlari haqida.
examples: {r:I would like to hear your thoughts.} - Men sizning fikrlaringizni eshitishni xohlayman.
{r:Would your friend like to share his thoughts?} - Do'stingiz o'z fikrlarini ulashishni xohlaydimi?
{r:The philosopher would like more time for thought.} - Faylasuf fikr yuritish uchun ko'proq vaqt xohlaydi.
{r:What are your thoughts on this problem?} - Bu muammo bo'yicha fikrlaringiz qanday?

text: {r:Hater}[ˈheɪtər] - negativchi, heyter, nafrat qiluvchi, yomon ko‘ruvchi, tanqidchi. 'Hater' so‘zi o‘zbek tilida 'nafrat qiluvchi', 'yomon ko‘ruvchi', 'tanqidchi' degan ma’nolarni anglatadi. U ko‘pincha kimnidir yoki nimanidir asosiz yomon ko‘radigan yoki tanqid qiladigan odamni ifodalash uchun ishlatiladi.
examples: {r:Don’t listen to the haters.} - Nafrat qiluvchilarga quloq solma.
{r:She has a lot of support, but also many haters.} - U ko‘p qo‘llab-quvvatlovchilar bilan birga ko‘p negativchilarga ham ega.
{r:We all have haters.} - Biz hammamizning heyterlarimiz bor.
{r:Ignore the haters and continue.} - Tanqidchilarga e’tibor bermay davom et.

text: {r:Perfect}[ˈpɜːrfɪkt] – mukammal. {p:PERFEKT}um mobayl aloqa operatorini eslaysizmi. Ingliz tilidan tarjima qilganda “{h:Mukammal} aloqa operatori” ma’nosini bildiradi. Kompaniya shunchalik mukammal ediki oxiri yopilib ketdi.
examples: {r:My sister would like to find the perfect gift.} - Mening singlim mukammal sovg'ani topishni xohlaydi.
{r:Would you like the perfect vacation spot?} - Mukammal dam olish joyini xohlaysizmi?
{r:The team would like to achieve perfect results.} - Jamoa mukammal natijalarga erishishni xohlashadi.
{r:We would like to create perfect memories.} - Biz mukammal xotiralar yaratishni xohlaymiz.

text: {r:Gloves}[ɡlʌvz] – qo’lqop. Dadam bir paytlar globus sotib olgan ekan. Hech kim lekin u bilan qiziqmaydi ham, tomosha ham qilmaydi. Hozir qishda bitta tegayotgan foydasi {p:GLOBUS}ga {h:qo’lqop} ilib qo’yamiz.
examples: {r:I would like to buy warm gloves.} - Men issiq qo'lqop sotib olishni xohlayman.
{r:Would your brother like leather or wool gloves?} - Akangiz teri yoki jun qo'lqop xohlaydimi?
{r:He would like his gloves cleaned.} - U qo'lqoplarini tozalashni xohlaydi.
{r:They would like to find matching gloves.} - Ular mos keladigan qo'lqoplarni topishni xohlashadi.

text: {r:Eager}[ˈiːɡər] – chanqoq, g’ayratli. Mana bu futbolchini taniysizmi? Futbol muxlislari yaxshi taniydi. Uning gol urmaslikka, urolmaslikka chanqog'i juda kuchli. Uning ismi {p:IGOR} bo’lib bu so’z ingliz tilida {h:chanqoqli} va g’ayratli ma'nolarini bildiradi.
examples: {r:The teacher would like to see eager students.} - O'qituvchi chanqoq talabalarni ko'rishni xohlaydi.
{r:Would you like to work with eager colleagues?} - Chanqoq hamkasblar bilan ishlashni xohlaysizmi?
{r:Nargiza would like to maintain her eager attitude.} - Nargiza o'zining chanqoq munosabatini saqlab qolishni xohlaydi.
{r:The coach would like to reward eager participants.} - Murabbiy g'ayratli qatnashuvchilarni mukofotlashni xohlaydi.

text: {r:Right}[raɪt] - to'g'ri, haq.
