examples: {r:She was right about the weather forecast.} - U ob-havo bashorati haqida haq edi.
{r:The scientist proved that his calculations were right.} - Olim hisob-kitoblari to‘g‘ri ekanini isbotladi.
{r:They were right to invest in that company.} - Ular ushbu kompaniyaga sarmoya kiritganlari to‘g‘ri edi.
{r:Your father was right to follow his instincts.} - Otangiz o‘z sezgisiga ergashganida haq edi.

text: {r:Train}[treɪn] - mashq qildirmoq, o'rgatmoq; tayyorlanmoq, mashq qilmoq. {h:Mashq qildirtirib} o'rgatuvchi insonni kim deb ataymiz? Albatta ustoz yoki {p:TREN}er. Biz keng qo'llaydigan trener so'zi aynan 'train' so'zidan olingan.
examples: {r:My countryman trained for months for the marathon.} - Vatandoshim marafonga tayyorlanish uchun bir necha oy mashq qildi.
{r:My teacher trains students in public speaking.} - Mening o'qituvchim talabalarga nutq so‘zlashni o‘rgatadi.
{r:They trained their dog to follow commands.} - Ular itlarini buyruqlarga bo‘ysunishga o‘rgatishdi.
{r:The company trains new employees in customer service.} - Kompaniya yangi xodimlarini mijozlarga xizmat ko‘rsatishga tayyorlaydi.
{r:Get some rest before training young guys and girls.} - Yosh yigit va qizlarni mashq qildirishdan oldin biroz dam oling.

text: {r:Iron}[ˈaɪərn] – temir. Tasavvur qiling {h:temir}ga {p:ayron} quydingiz va u erib ketdi, ayron muzdek bo’lsa ham.
examples: {r:The bridge is made of solid iron.} - Ko‘prik mustahkam temirdan qurilgan.
{r:My mother bought an iron kazan for cooking.} - Mening onam pishirish uchun temir qozon sotib oldi.
{r:These walls are hard like iron.} - Bu devorlar temirdek qattiq.
{r:The iron door was too heavy to move.} - Temir eshik siljitish uchun juda og‘ir edi.

text: {r:Brown}[braʊn] – jigarrang. Tasavvur qiling {p:BRA}zilyada {p:UN}iversitetlarning hammasi {h:jigarrangga} bo’yalgan.
examples: {r:I have a brown bag.} - Mening jigarrang sumkam bor.
{r:The artist bought a brown dress.} - Rassom jigarrang ko'ylak sotib oldi.
{r:Children don’t like brown shoes.} - Bolalar jigarrang poyabzalni yoqtirmaydi.
{r:His cat has a brown tail.} - Uning mushugining jigarrang dumi bor.

text: {r:Foreign}[ˈfɒrɪn] – chet elga oid. {h:Chet tili}ni o’rganishim kerak edi. Shuning uchun {p:FOR}sajni {p:IN}gliz tilida ko’ra boshladim va ancha inglizcha o’rgandim.
examples: {r:I met a foreign friend.} - Men chet ellik do'st bilan uchrashdim.
{r:My uncle is able to speak a foreign language.} - Mening amakim chet tilida gapira oladi.
{r:Tourists often don’t understand foreign cultures.} - Sayyohlar ko'pincha chet el madaniyatlarini tushunmaydi.
{r:The journalist is ready to visit a foreign country.} - Jurnalist chet elga borishga tayyor.

text: {r:Red}[red] – qizil. {p:Red}iska men bilgan eng {h:qizil} sabzavot.
examples: {r:I like red apples.} - Menga qizil olmalar yoqadi.
{r:She wore red jeans.} - U qizil jinsi kiygan edi.
{r:The shop doesn’t have red flowers.} - Do'konda qizil gullar yo'q.
{r:Our team painted the door red.} - Bizning jamoamiz eshikni qizilga bo'yadi.

text: {r:Meal}[miːl] – ovqat. Siz bu vaziyatda {p:MIL}tiq shaklidagi {h:ovqatni} tasavvur qilishingiz mumkin.
examples: {r:I cooked a delicious meal.} - Men mazali ovqat pishirdim.
{r:My brother enjoyed the meal.} - Akam ovqatdan zavqlandi.
{r:Some people don’t like spicy meals.} - Ba'zi odamlar achchiq ovqatlarni yoqtirmaydi.
{r:My aunt prepared a special meal.} - Xolam maxsus ovqat tayyorladi.

text: {r:Delicious}[dɪˈlɪʃəs] - mazali, totli. Bir kuni bir delfin bilan gaplashib qoldim. '{p:DEL}fin {p:ISHIZ} nima'desam '{h:Mazzali}, ovqatlar pishirish, men dengiz olamining oshpaziman' dedi.
examples: {r:The cake was delicious.} - Tort mazali edi.
{r:Maftuna was surprised by this delicious soup.} - Maftuna mazali sho'rvadan hayratlandi.
{r:Many guests didn’t find the food delicious.} - Ko'plab mehmonlar ovqatni mazali deb topmadilar.
{r:His wife cooked a delicious dinner.} - Uning rafiqasi mazali kechki ovqat pishirdi.

text: {r:Modern}[ˈmɒdərn] - zamonaviy. '{p:Modern} Sergeli' ko'p qavatli uy loyihasi haqida eshitgan bo'lsangiz kerak. Bu yerdagi 'Modern' so'zi zamonaviy degani.
examples: {r:I live in a modern house close to my work.} - Men ishimga yaqin bo'lgan zamonaviy uyda yashayman.
{r:Our company uses modern technology.} - Bizning kompaniyamiz zamonaviy texnologiyalardan foydalanadi.
{r:They don’t like modern art.} - Ular zamonaviy san'atni yoqtirmaydi.
{r:The buyer bought modern furniture.} - Xaridor zamonaviy mebel sotib oldi.

text: {r:Horrible}[ˈhɒrəbl] – ujas, daxshatli, qo’rqinchli. Men Toshkentga mashhur XOR jamoasi keldi desa rosa qiziqib {p:XOR}ga {p:BIL}et olibman. Kirsam do’ng’ir dung’ir rosa shovqin bo’lyapti. Musiqa konsertiga emas balki {h:ujas} kinoga kirgandek bo’ldim.
examples: {r:The weather was horrible.} - Ob-havo dahshatli edi.
{r:My friend had a horrible dream.} - Do'stim dahshatli tush ko'rdi.
{r:These critics don’t like horrible movies.} - Bu tanqidchilar dahshatli filmlarni yoqtirmaydi.
{r:His friend told a horrible story.} - Uning do'sti dahshatli hikoya aytdi.

text: {r:Smell}[smel] – hid; hidi kelmoq. {p:S}ariq {p:MEL}ni yoqtirmayman. Undan boshqa bir sariq narsani ya’ni peshobning {h:hidi} keladi.
examples: {r:The flowers have a nice smell.} - Gullarning yoqimli hidi bor.
{r:My sister doesn’t like the smell of fish.} - Singlim baliq hidini yoqtirmaydi.
{r:This liar man smelled bad.} - Bu yolg'onchi kishi yomon sasidi.
{r:The chef prepared food with a pleasant smell.} - Oshpaz yoqimli hidli ovqat pishirdi.

text: {r:Taste}[teɪst] – ta'm, maza. Ochlik zamonlarda tolni ham, terakni ham yeyishgan ekan. Bobomning aytishicha {p:TE}rak {p:YUZT}a xil {h:ta'm}ga ega. Po’stlog’ini yesangiz shirin, ildizi taxir, bargi nordon, yog’ochi sho’r, sho’rva qilib pishirsangiz esa mazali.
examples: {r:The soup has a good taste.} - Sho'rvaning mazasi yaxshi.
{r:She doesn’t like the taste of coffee.} - U kofe mazasini yoqtirmaydi.
{r:The children enjoyed the taste of the cake.} - Bolalar tortning mazasidan zavqlandilar.
{r:The chef added salt to improve the taste.} - Oshpaz ta'mni yaxshilash uchun tuz qo'shdi.

text: {r:Sound}[saʊnd] – ovoz. Tasavvur qiling {p:SAUNAD}asiz va bor {h:ovozingiz} bilan butun dunyoga baqiryapsiz.
examples: {r:The music has a relaxing sound.} - Musiqaning tinchlantiruvchi ohangi bor.
{r:My grandmother doesn’t like loud sounds.} - Buvim baland ovozlarni yoqtirmaydi.
{r:They heard a strange sound.} - Ular g'alati ovoz eshitishdi.
{r:The bird enjoys the sound of rain.} - Qush yomg'ir ovozidan zavqlanadi.

text: {r:Cook}[kʊk] – pishirmoq, tayyorlamoq. Tasavvur qiling dunyodagi eng katta {p:KUK}uruz {h:tayyorlayapsiz.} Kattaligi uyingizdan ham katta, lekin yomg’ir yog’dida kukuruzingiz erib ketdi.
examples: {r:I cook my food when I get hourly break from the job.} - Men ishdan bir soatlik tanaffus olganimda o'z ovqatimni pishiraman.
{r:I am still a beginner in cooking.} - Ovqat tayyorlashda hali ham boshlang'ichman.
{r:This cooking method saves time.} - Bu pishirish usuli vaqtni tejaydi.
{r:Our cooking teacher is professional.} - Bizning oshpazlik o'qituvchimiz professional.

text: {r:Wonderful}[ˈwʌndərfəl] - ajoyib, hayratlanarli. Wonder so'zidan yasalgan.
examples: {r:We had a wonderful time.} - Biz ajoyib vaqt o'tkazdik.
{r:This tea has a wonderful smell.} - Bu choyning ajoyib hidi bor.
{r:You're a wonderful friend.} - Siz ajoyib do'stsiz.
{r:The weather is wonderful today.} - Bugun ob-havo ajoyib.

text: {r:Dangerous}[ˈdeɪndʒərəs] - xavfli. Danger(xavf) so'zidan yasalgan.
examples: {r:Swimming here is dangerous.} - Bu yerda suzish xavfli.
{r:That's a dangerous city.} - Bu xavfli shahar.
{r:The chemicals are dangerous.} - Kimyoviy moddalar xavfli.
{r:He makes dangerous decisions.} - U xavfli qarorlar qabul qiladi.

text: {r:Fresh}[freʃ] - yangi, barra, svejiy. Agar charchoqni his qilsam bitta {p:FLESH} ichaman va {h:svejiy} his qilaman o'zimni.
examples: {r:I love fresh vegetables.} - Men yangi sabzavotlarni yaxshi ko'raman.
{r:The bread is fresh from the oven.} - Non pechdan yangi chiqqan.
{r:Let's get fresh air.} - Yangi havo olaylik.
{r:Maftuna does not have fresh ideas.} - Maftunaning yangi g'oyalari yo'q.

text: {r:Sharp}[ʃɑːrp] – o’tkir. Pichog’imni nega o’tkirlayotganimni bilasizmi? Agar {p:SHARP}alarni ko’rsam shu bilan hujum qilaman. Sharpalar {h:o’tkir} jismlardan qo’rqishar ekan.
examples: {r:Be careful, the knife is sharp.} - Ehtiyot bo'ling, pichoq o'tkir.
{r:He has sharp eyesight.} - Uning ko'rish qobiliyati(zreniyasi) o'tkir.
{r:Rustam is a lifelong learner. He has a sharp knowledge.} - Rustam bir umrlik o'rganuvchi. U o'tkir bilimga ega.
{r:She gave a sharp answer.} - U o'tkir javob berdi.

text: {r:Suitable}[ˈsuːtəbl] - mos. Suit(mos kelmoq) so'zidan yasalgan.
examples: {r:Is this dress suitable?} - Bu ko'ylak mos keladimi?
{r:Find a suitable time to call.} - Qo'ng'iroq qilish uchun mos vaqt toping.
{r:The movie isn't suitable for children.} - Film bolalar uchun mos emas.
{r:We need a suitable answer.} - Bizga mos javob kerak.

text: {r:Incorrect}[ˌɪnkəˈrekt] - noto'g'ri. Correct(to'g'ri) so'zining teskarisi
examples: {r:Your answer is incorrect.} - Javobingiz noto'g'ri.
{r:That's an incorrect assumption.} - Bu noto'g'ri taxmin.
{r:Your explanation is incorrect.} - Sizning tushuntirishingiz noto'g'ri.
{r:He gave incorrect directions.} - U noto'g'ri yo'nalish berdi.

text: {r:Ideal}[aɪˈdiːəl] - ideal, zo'r. O'zbekcha va inglizcha variantlari talaffuzda farq qiladi.
examples: {r:The weather is ideal today.} - Bugun ob-havo ideal.
{r:She found an ideal apartment.} - U ideal kvartira topdi.
{r:This temperature is ideal.} - Bu harorat ideal.
{r:Perhaps an ideal home is being built.} - Ehtimol ideal uy shu yerda qurilyapti.

text: {r:Information}[ˌɪnfərˈmeɪʃn] - informatsiya.
examples: {r:This book has useful information.} - Bu kitobda foydali ma'lumotlar bor.
{r:The information desk is there.} - Ma'lumotlar stoli shu yerda.
{r:I need more information.} - Menga ko'proq ma'lumot kerak.
{r:His information was incorrect.} - Uning ma'lumoti noto'g'ri edi.

text: {r:Soup}[suːp] - sho'rva, sup. Rus tilidan o'zlashgan sup so'zi o'zbek tilida ham keng qo'llaniladi.
examples: {r:The soup bowl is empty.} - Sho'rva kosasi bo'sh.
{r:She makes great soup.} - U ajoyib sho'rva pishiradi.
{r:This soup spoon is too big.} - Bu sho'rva qoshiqi juda katta.
{r:We need soup ingredients.} - Bizga sho'rva mahsulotlari kerak.

text: {r:Quickly}[ˈkwɪkli] – tezda. Yaxshi bir olivya salat tayyorlash uchun kartoshkani {h:KUBIKLI} qilib {p:tez} tug’rash kerak.
examples: {r:I finished my homework quickly.} - Men uy vazifamni tezda tugatdim.
{r:Sardor can absorb knowledge quickly.} - Sardor bilimni tez o'zlashtira oladi.
{r:Drink water quickly if you are thirsty.} - Agar chanqagan bo'lsang tezda suv ich.
{r:The cleaning team cleaned the house quickly.} - Tozalash jamoasi uyni tez tozaladi.

text: {r:Suddenly}[ˈsʌdənli] - tosatdan. Sudden(to'satdan) so'zining ravish shakli.
examples: {r:The lights went out suddenly.} - Chiroqlar to'satdan o'chdi.
{r:He appeared suddenly at the door.} - U to'satdan eshikda paydo bo'ldi.
{r:The audience didn’t expect it to happen suddenly.} - Tomoshabinlar buni to'satdan sodir bo'lishini kutmagandi.
{r:My boss called me suddenly.} - Mening xo'jayinim menga to'satdan qo'ng'iroq qildi.

text: {r:Badly}[ˈbædli] - yomon. Bad(yomon) so'zining ravish shakli.
examples: {r:I played the game badly.} - Men o'yinni yomon o'ynadim.
{r:He sang the song badly.} - U qo'shiqni yomon aytdi.
{r:Their team doesn’t want to perform badly.} - Ularning jamoasi yomon ijro etishni xohlamaydi.
{r:The new chef cooked the meal badly.} - Yangi oshpaz ovqatni yomon pishirdi.

text: {r:Carefully}[ˈkeərfəli] - ehtiyotkorlik bilan. Careful(ehtiyotkor) so'zining ravish shakli.
examples: {r:I am reading this unique book carefully.} - Men bu noyob kitobni diqqat bilan o'qiyapman.
{r:He drove the car carefully.} - U mashinani ehtiyotkorlik bilan haydadi.
{r:These workers don’t move things carefully.} - Bu ishchilar narsalarni ehtiyotkorlik bilan siljitmaydi.
{r:We have to put things on shelf carefully.} - Biz narsalarni javonga ehtiyotkorlik bilan qo'yishimiz kerak.

text: {r:Heavily}[ˈhevɪli] - og'ir, kuchli. Heavy(og'ir) so'zining ravish shakli.
examples: {r:It rained heavily last night.} - Kecha kuchli yomg'ir yog'di.
{r:He breathed heavily after running.} - U yugurishdan keyin og'ir nafas oldi.
{r:The women usually don’t carry heavy bags.} - Ayollar odatda og'ir sumkalarni ko'tarmaydi.
{r:The tired traveler slept heavily after the trip.} - Charchagan sayohatchi sayohatdan keyin og'ir uxladi.

text: {r:Easily}[ˈiːzɪli] - osonlik bilan. Easy(oson) so'zining ravish shakli.
examples: {r:I solved the problem easily.} - Men muammoni oson hal qildim.
{r:He learned the lesson easily.} - U darsni oson o'rgandi.
{r:The athletes don’t give up easily.} - Sportchilar osonlikcha taslim bo'lmaydi.
{r:My mother can use this phone freely and easily.} - Onam bu telefondan erkin va osonlik bilan foydalana oladilar.

text: {r:Slowly}[ˈsloʊli] - sekinlik bilan. Slow(sekin) so'zining ravish shakli.
examples: {r:I walked slowly in the park.} - Men bog'da sekin yurdim.
{r:He spoke slowly to explain.} - U tushuntirish uchun sekin gapirdi.
{r:The snails move slowly.} - Shilliq qurtlar sekin harakatlanadi.
{r:The old man ate his meal slowly.} - Keksa odam ovqatni sekin yedi.

text: {r:Well}[wel] – yaxshi(good ning ravish shakli). Meni veligim do’nga ham chiqadi, qorda ham yuradi, teshilib qolmaydi. Juda {h:yaxshi} {p:VEL}ik.
examples: {r:I did well in the exam.} - Men imtihonda yaxshi natija ko'rsatdim.
{r:She sings well.} - U yaxshi qo'shiq aytadi.
{r:The new players don’t play well as a team.} - Yangi o'yinchilar jamoa sifatida yaxshi o'ynamaydi.
{r:The master chef cooked the meal well.} - Bosh oshpaz ovqatni yaxshi pishirdi.

text: {r:Health}[helθ] – sog’liq. Futbol hakami kasal bo’lib qolibdi va uning xotini ‘’Siz futbol o’yinlarini {p:holis} boshqarmagansiz, shuning uchun {h:sog’liq} bezovta qilyapti’’ debdi.
examples: {r:I take care of my health.} - Men o'z sog'ligimga g'amxo'rlik qilaman.
{r:He focuses on his health.} - U o'z sog'ligiga e'tibor qaratadi.
{r:Good doctors don’t ignore their health.} - Yaxshi shifokorlar o'z sog'lig'ini e'tiborsiz qoldirmaydi.
{r:Celebrities care about their health too much.} - Yulduzlar sog'lig'i haqida juda qayg'uradi.

text: {r:Care}[keər] – g’amxorlik qilmoq, qarab turmoq; g'amxorlik, e'tibor. {p:KER}osin ishlab chiqarish murakkab ish. Uning ustida har kuni {h:e’tibor} bilan ishlanishi kerak.
examples: {r:I handle the situation with care.} - Men vaziyatni ehtiyotkorlik bilan hal qilaman.
{r:She treats her belongings with care.} - U o'z narsalariga ehtiyotkorlik bilan munosabatda bo'ladi.
{r:The gardeners don’t take care of the garden.} - Bog'bonlar bog'ga g'amxo'rlik qilmaydi.
{r:The kind nurse takes care of patients.} - Mehribon hamshira bemorlarga g'amxo'rlik qiladi.
{r:I don't care.} - Menga farqi yo'q.

text: {r:Shout}[ʃaʊt] – baqirmoq. {p:SHA}vkat {p:UD}arnik chaladi uyida kuni bo’yi qo’shnilariga xalaqit berib. Qo’shnilari esa g’azabga to’lib {h:baqiradi} keyin.
examples: {r:He suddenly shouted for help.} - U tosatdan yordam soʻrab baqirdi.
{r:Two singers were shouting to each other angrily.} - Ikkita qo'shiqchi bir-biriga g'azab bilan baqirayotgan edi.
{r:She called loudly but didn't shout.} - U baland ovozda chaqirdi, lekin baqirmadi.
{r:The children played happily, shouting sometimes.} - Bolalar xursandlik bilan o'ynashdi, ba'zida baqirishdi.

text: {r:Quit}[kwɪt] – to’xtatmoq, tugatmoq, tashlamoq, bo’shamoq(ishdan). Mening kashanda do’stim ota-onasiga shart qo’yibdi ‘Agar hisob-raqamimga 10 000$ tashlab {p:KVIT}ansiyasini ko’rsatsangiz chekishni {h:tashlayman}’ deb.
examples: {r:He quit working immediately.} - U darhol ishdan ketdi.
{r:She quit smoking gradually last year.} - U o'tgan yili asta-sekin chekishni tashladi.
{r:The software quits unexpectedly sometimes.} - Dastur ba'zida kutilmaganda to'xtab qoladi.
{r:The team members quit the team regretfully.} - Jamoa a'zolari afsus bilan jamoani tark etishdi.

text: {r:Innovation}[ˌɪnəˈveɪʃn] - innovatsiya.
examples: {r:The company needs innovations.} - Kompaniyaga innovatsiyalar zarur.
{r:She is speaking about her innovations carefully.} - U o'z innovatsiyalari haqida ehtiyotkorlik bilan gapirib beryapti.
{r:The startup grows rapidly through innovation.} - Startap innovatsiya orqali tez o'smoqda.
{r:We can help the Earth with innovations.} - Biz innovatsiyalar bilan Yer sayyorasiga yordam bera olamiz.

text: {r:Intelligent}[ɪnˈtelɪdʒənt] - aqlli, intelligent.
examples: {r:His wife is very intelligent.} - Uning xotini juda aqlli.
{r:A pen was invented by an intelligent man.} - Ruchka aqlli odam tomonidan ixtiro qilingan.
{r:Dogs can learn surprisingly intelligent tricks.} - Itlar ajablanarli darajada aqlli fokuslarni o'rganishi mumkin.
{r:I am lucky to have an intelligent husband.} - Intelligent erim borligi uchun omadliman.

text: {r:Green}[ɡriːn] - yashil.
examples: {r:The traffic light turned green quickly.} - Svetofor birdan yashilga aylandi.
{r:The trees looked freshly green after rain.} - Daraxtlar yomg'irdan keyin yangilangan yashil rangda edi.
{r:She painted the wall green.} - U devorni yashil rangga bo'yadi.
{r:My father used to prefer green to blue.} - Mening dadam yashil rangni ko'kdan afzal ko'rardi.

text: {r:Inherit}[ɪnˈherɪt] – meros qilib olmoq, meros olmoq. Men Indiyada elchi bo’lib ishlagan bobomdan {p:IN}diya {p:XARIT}asini faqat {h:meros} qilib olganman.
examples: {r:She will inherit the property automatically.} - U mulkni avtomatik ravishda meros qilib oladi.
{r:How much money have you inherited from your grandfather?} - Bobongizdan qancha pul meros qilib oldingiz?
{r:The children inherited the business unexpectedly.} - Bolalar biznesni kutilmaganda meros qilib olishdi.
{r:Did you inherit a fish farm from your uncle?} - Amakingizdan baliq fermasini meros qilib oldingizmi?

text: {r:Understanding}[ˌʌndərˈstændɪŋ] - tushunadigan, e'tiborli. Understand(tushunmoq) so'zidan yasalgan.
examples: {r:I want to have an understanding boss.} - Men tushunadigan boshlig'im bo'lishini xohlayman.
{r:He explained the rules patiently with great understanding.} - U qoidalarni sabr bilan tushuntirdi.
{r:My aunt was an understanding woman.} - Xolam e'tiborli ayol edi.
{r:The kind teacher smiled, showing understanding.} - Mehribon o'qituvchi jilmaydi, tushunganini ko'rsatib.

text: {r:Illness}[ˈɪlnəs] - kasallik. Ill(kasal) so'zidan yasalgan.
examples: {r:He recovered from illness quickly.} - U kasallikdan tez tuzaldi.
{r:The news spread quickly about her illness.} - Uning kasal ekanligi to'g'risidagi yangilik tez tarqaldi.
{r:The doctor gave a wrong explanation of her illness.} - Doktor uning kasalligi haqida noto'g'ri tushuntirish berdi.
{r:You can recover from this illness quickly.} - Bu kasallikdan tez tuzalib ketishing mumkin.

text: {r:Pregnant}[ˈpreɡnənt] – homilador. Tasavvur qiling ayolingiz {h:homilador.} Hozir {p:PIROG} va {p:NON}ga boshi qorong’i bo’lgan.
examples: {r:Pregnant women walk heavily.} - Homilador ayollar og'irroq yuradi.
{r:I took care of my pregnant wife last year.} - Men homilador ayolimga qaradim o'tgan yili.
{r:That pregant girl used to eat only fish.} - O'sha homilador qiz faqat baliq yerdi.
{r:Pregnant women must not get nervous.} - Homilador ayollar asabiylashmasliklari kerak.

text: {r:Breathe}[briːð] – nafas olmoq. Breath - nafas(ot shakli). Tasavvur qiling baland joydan tushib ketdingiz va 'endi tamomman' deb o’yladingiz. Hayriyatki katta {p:brizi}nt to’shalgan ekan, siz {h:nafas olyapsiz.} “Xudoga shukr omon qoldim brizint senga rahmat” dedingiz.
examples: {r:Take a deep breath and relax.} – Chuqur nafas oling va tinchlaning.
{r:He could hardly breathe after running.} – Yugurgandan keyin u zo‘rg‘a nafas olardi.
{r:She breathed slowly to calm herself.} – U o‘zini tinchlantirish uchun sekin nafas oldi.
{r:We need fresh air to breathe.} – Nafas olish uchun bizga toza havo kerak.

text: {r:Deep}[diːp] – chuqur. Tasavvur qiling siz diplomingiz ish topishga umuman yordam berolmagani sababli okeanning {h:chuqur} bir joyiga sho’ng’idingizda {p:dip}lomni o’sha yerga tashlab keldingiz.
examples: {r:The water is very deep.} – Suv juda chuqur.
{r:He took a deep breath.} – U chuqur nafas oldi.
{r:They had a deep conversation.} – Ular chuqur suhbatlashishdi.
{r:This hole is very deep.} – Bu o'ra juda chuqur.

text: {r:White}[waɪt] - oq. Bu vaziyatda {p:VAYIT} (Vohid ismli shaxslarni shunday atashadi ko'pincha) yoki Abdu{p:vayit} ismli odamning yuzi {h:oqarib} ketganligini tasavvur qilishingiz mumkin.
examples: {r:She can probably lend me her white car.} - Balki u oq mashinasini menga berib tura olar.
{r:Excuse me, are there white flowers in the garden?} - Kechirasiz, bog'da oq gullar bormi?
{r:There isn’t any white paint left.} - Oq bo'yoq qolmagan.
{r:There aren’t many white shirts in the shop.} - Do'konda ko'p oq ko'ylak yo'q.

text: {r:Behind}[bɪˈhaɪnd] – orqasida. {p:BI}lak {p:HAYD}ovchining asosiy a’zosi, kerak bo’lsa {h:orqasida} ham qo’li bo’lsa yaxshi bo’lardi.
examples: {r:Probably there is a cat behind the door.} - Balki eshik orqasida mushuk bordir.
{r:Are there books behind the shelf?} - Javon orqasida kitoblar bormi?
{r:There isn’t anyone behind the tree.} - Daraxt orqasida hech kim yo'q.
{r:There aren’t any chairs behind the table.} - Stol orqasida stullar yo'q.

text: {r:Salt}[sɔːlt] – tuz. Oyog’ingizda {h:tuz} yig’ilyaptimi {p:salt}o oting. Har safar salto otganingizda tizzangizdagi tuzlar to’kila boshlaydi.
examples: {r:There is hardly any salt on the table.} - Stolda deyarli tuz yo'q.
{r:Are there salt shakers in the kitchen?} - Oshxonada tuzdonlar bormi?
{r:There isn’t enough salt in the soup.} - Sho'rvada yetarlicha tuz yo'q.
{r:There aren’t any salt packets left.} - Tuz paketlari qolmagan.

text: {r:Nowhere}[ˈnoʊwer] - hech qayer, hech qayerda, hech qayerga.
examples: {r:There is nowhere to sit in the park.} - Bog'da o'tiradigan hech qayer yo'q.
{r:There are apples nowhere} - Olmalar hech qayerda yo'q
{r:There is nowhere to hide.} - Yashirinadigan hech qayer yo'q.
{r:There is nowhere to go for us.} - Bizga boradigan hech joy yo'q.

text: {r:Solar}[ˈsoʊlər] - quyoshga oid. Mana bu apparat {h:quyosh} nuri yordamida suvni {p:SOLYAR}kaga aylantirib beradi.
examples: {r:There is a solar panel on the roof.} - Tomda quyosh paneli bor.
{r:Are there solar lights in the garden?} - Bog'da quyosh chiroqlari bormi?
{r:There isn’t enough solar energy today.} - Bugun quyosh energiyasi yetarli emas.
{r:My grandfather has finally bought a solar panel.} - Bobom nihoyat quyosh paneli sotib oldi.

text: {r:Intensive}[ɪnˈtensɪv] - keng ko'lamli, intensiv. Bir xil so'zlar!
examples: {r:There is an intensive course next week.} - Keyingi hafta intensiv kurs bor.
{r:Are there intensive training sessions?} - Intensiv mashg'ulotlar bormi?
{r:There isn’t enough time for intensive study.} - Intensiv o'qish uchun vaqt yetarli emas.
{r:There aren’t any intensive programs available.} - Intensiv dasturlar mavjud emas.

text: {r:Jury}[ˈdʒʊri] - jyuri, hakam (sud zalidagi). Bir xil so'zlar!
examples: {r:There is a jury in the courtroom.} - Sud zalida hakamlar hay'ati bor.
{r:Are there jury members discussing the case?} - Hakamlar hay'ati a'zolari ishni muhokama qilmoqdami?
{r:This corrupt jury lives in a luxurious house.} - Bu poraxor sudya hashamatli uyda yashaydi.
{r:There aren’t any jury decisions yet.} - Hakamlar hay'atining qarori hali yo'q.

text: {r:Hope}[hoʊp] – umid, umid qilmoq. Mol o’g’rilarning taktikasini bilasizmi? Ho’kizni o’g’irlashadi, keyin esa {p:ho’}kizni {p:up}a qilishadi, egasi qidirib kelib tanib qolmasliklariga {h:umid} qilib shunday qilishadi.
examples: {r:There is hope for a better future.} - Yaxshi kelajak uchun umid bor.
{r:Are there hopes that the situation will improve?} - Vaziyat yaxshilanadi degan umidlar bormi?
{r:I hope payment systems will start working.} - Umid qilamanki to'lov tizimi ishlashni boshlaydi.
{r: We hope love will finally win and hate will lose.} - Umid qilamizki oxir-oqibat muhabbat g'alaba qozonadi, nafrat esa yengiladi.
{r:I hope I can get some rest before the work.} - Umid qilamanki ishdan oldin biroz dam olaman.

text: {r:Argument}[ˈɑːrɡjumənt] - bahs, munozara, bahsga bo'lgan fikr. Argue(bahslashmoq) so'zidan yasalgan. Hozirgi argument o'zbek tilida ham keng qo'llanilyapti.
examples: {r:There is an argument between the two friends.} - Ikki do'st o'rtasida tortishuv bor.
{r:Are there arguments about the new policy?} - Yangi siyosat haqida bahslar bormi?
{r:There isn’t any argument against the plan.} - Rejaga qarshi hech qanday qarshi fikr yo'q.
{r:After a long argument with my brother, I decided to quit smoking.} - Akam bilan uzoq tortishuvlardan so'ng chekishni tashlashga qaror qildim.

text: {r:Population}[ˌpɒpjuˈleɪʃn] - aholi.
examples: {r:There is a large population in this city.} - Bu shaharda katta aholi bor.
{r:Are there population growth concerns?} - Aholi sonining o'sishi haqida tashvishlar bormi?
{r:There isn’t enough space for the population.} - Aholi uchun yetarlicha joy yo'q.
{r:There is a sudden population growth in India.} - Hindistonda kutilmagan aholi o'sish darajasi bor.

text: {r:Useless}[ˈjuːsləs] - befoyda. Use(foyda) so'zining teskarisi.
examples: {r:There is a useless old computer in the garage.} - Garajda foydasiz eski kompyuter bor.
{r:Are there useless cars here?} - Bu yerda eski befoyda mashinalar bormi?
{r:Is there anything useless we can remove?} - Biz olib tashlashimiz mumkin bo'lgan foydasiz narsa bormi?
{r:My child broke this pencil and it has become useless.} - Mening bolam bu qalamni sindirib qo'ydi va qalam befoydaga aylandi.

text: {r:Seem}[siːm] – tuyulmoq, ko'rinmoq. Simba ko’p vaqt uyidan uzoqda bo’ldi. Bir kuni she’rlar to’dasini yovuz amakisidan qutqarish uchun Simba qaytdi va hozirda ancha kuchli va yetuk {h:ko’ringan} {p:SIM}baga she’rlar ham ishonib ortidan ergashishdi va yovuz hukmdorni yengib tinch hayot kechira boshlashdi.
examples: {r:There seems to be a problem.} - Muammo bor ko'rinadi.
{r:He seems angry.} - U jahldor tuyulyapti.
{r:They seemed hospitable.} - Ular mehmondo'st ko'rindi.
{r:You seem to be doing well.} - Ko'rinishidan yaxshi qilyapsan.

text: {r:Consider}[kənˈsɪdər] – ko'rib chiqmoq, ustida o'ylamoq, hisobga olmoq.
examples: {r:There is much to consider before deciding.} - Qaror qilishdan oldin ko'p narsalarni hisobga olish kerak(o'ylab ko'rish kerak).
{r:Are there many factors to consider?} - Hisobga olish kerak bo'lgan ko'p omillar bormi?
{r:Is there anything else to consider?} - Hisobga olish kerak bo'lgan yana biror narsa bormi?
{r:I am considering quitting the job.} - Ishdan ketish variantini ko'rib chiqyapman.

text: {r:Oxygen}[ˈɒksɪdʒən] – kislorod. Agar OQ SEDAN mashinasini olmoqchi bo’lsangiz bu yaxshi tanlov. Chunki metan, elektr yoki benzinga pul sarflashingiz shart emas. {p:OQ SEDAN} {h:kislorod} bilan ham yura oladigan mashina.
examples: {r:There is less oxygen at high altitudes.} - Balandlikda kislorod kamroq.
{r:Pregnant women need more oxygen.} - Homilador ayollarga ko'proq kislorod kerak.
{r:Is there enough oxygen in this room?} - Ushbu xonada yetarli kislorod bormi?
{r:Everything needs oxygen to live.} - Hamma narsaga yashash uchun kislorod kerak.

text: {r:Bee}[biː] – asalari. Asalarilar {p:BI}laynni sudga berishibdi {h:asalari}larga tegishli sariq qora timsolni o’zlashtirib olgani uchun.
examples: {r:These flowers are not suitable for bees.} - Bu gullar asalarilar uchun mos emas.
{r:Are there too many bees near the hive?} - Asalari uyasi yaqinida juda ko'p asalari bormi?
{r:Is there a bee in this room?} - Bu xonada asalari bormi?
{r:Black and yellow colors have become the symbol for bees.} - Qora va sariq ranglar asalarilar uchun ramzga aylangan.

text: {r:Sunglasses}[ˈsʌnˌɡlɑːsɪz] - ko'zoynak, ochki. Sun(quyosh) va glass(oyna) so'zlarining birlashuvidan yasalgan.
examples: {r:I need sunglasses on a sunny beach.} - Menga quyoshli plyaj uchun ko'zoynaklar kerak.
{r:Are there cheap sunglasses at the market?} - Bozorda arzon quyosh ko'zoynaklar bormi?
{r:Is there UV protection in these sunglasses?} - Bu quyosh ko'zoynaklarida ultrabinafsha nurlardan himoya bormi?
{r:Have you ever seen wooden sunglasses?} - Yog'ochdan qilingan ko'zoynaklarni hech ko'rganmisiz?

text: {r:Patiently}[ˈpeɪʃntli] - sabr bilan. Patient(sabrli) so'zining ravish shakli.
examples: {r:There is someone waiting patiently outside.} - Tashqarida sabr bilan kutayotgan kimdir bor.
{r:Are there students listening patiently?} - Sabr bilan tinglayotgan talabalar bormi?
{r:Is there anyone working patiently on this?} - Bu bo'yicha sabr bilan ishlayotgan biron kim bormi?
{r:There are not many people waiting patiently.} - Sabr bilan kutayotgan odamlar ko'p emas.

text: {r:Fully}[ˈfʊli] - to'liq, to'la. Full(to'la) so'zining ravish shakli.
examples: {r:There is a fully charged battery.} - To'liq zaryadlangan batareya bor.
{r:I fully support you.} - Men sizni to'liq qo'llab-quvvatlayman.
{r:Is there a fully equipped kitchen?} - To'liq jihozlangan oshxona bormi?
{r:Your answer to my question is fully correct.} - Mening savolimga sizning javobingiz butunlay to'g'ri.

text: {r:Safely}[ˈseɪfli] - xavfsiz. Safe(xavfsiz) so'zining ravish shakli.
examples: {r:There is a child playing safely in the yard.} - Hovlida xavfsiz o'ynayotgan bola bor.
{r:There is nowhere to live safely.} - Xavfsiz yashasa bo'ladigan hech qayer yo'q.
{r:With this truck you can transport petrol safely.} - Bu trak bilan benzinni xavfsiz tashisang bo'ladi.
{r:These guys want to work safely.} - Bu yigitlar xavfsiz ishlashni xohlaydi.

text: {r:Rob}[rɒb] - o'g'irlamoq. Hozirgi davrda texnologiya rivojlanib {p:ROB}otlar endi yoppasiga {h:o'g'irlik qilish} bilan shug'ullanmoqda.
examples: {r:There is a man trying to rob the shop.} - Do'kondan o'g'irlik qilmoqchi bo'lgan odam bor.
{r:Who robbed my ladder yesterday?} - Kecha mening narvonimni kim o'g'irladi?
{r:Is there any way to prevent robbery?} - O'g'irlikni oldini olishning biror usuli bormi?
{r:That girl has robbed my money.} - O'sha qiz mening pullarimni o'g'irlab ketdi.

text: {r:Relation}[rɪˈleɪʃn] - munosabat, aloqa.
examples: {r:There was a good relation between the neighbors.} - Qo'shnilar o'rtasida yaxshi munosabat bor edi.
{r:Were there relations with other countries during that time?} - O'sha vaqtda boshqa mamlakatlar bilan munosabatlar bormidi?
{r:There wasn’t any relation to the topic in his speech.} - Uning nutqida mavzu bilan hech qanday aloqa yo'q edi.
{r:These two countries have no relations now.} - Bu ikki davlatlar hozirda munosabatga ega emas.

text: {r:Pack}[pæk] - paket; narsalarni jamadonga taxlamoq yoki joylashtirmoq. Pack bu biz bilgan paket, lekin bu so'zning fe'l ma'nosi (narsalarni yig'ishtirmoq) keng qo'llaniladi.
examples: {r:I need to pack my suitcase for the trip.} - Men sayohat uchun chamadonimni yig'ishtirishim kerak.
{r:She always packs a few things when she travels.} - U sayohat qilganda har doim kam narsa yig'ishtiradi.
{r:Pack your belongings and leave the house.} - Narsalaringni yig'ishtir va uydan ket.
{r:He is packing a gift for his friend.} - U do'sti uchun sovg'a o'ramoqda.

text: {r:Corner}[ˈkɔːrnər] - burchak. Tasavvur qiling, siz {p:KONOR} MakGregorni {h:burchak}ka tiqib dodini berib uryapsiz.
examples: {r:There was a cat sleeping in the corner of the room.} - Xonaning burchagida mushuk uxlayotgan edi.
{r:Was there an iron chair in the corner?} - Burchakda temir stul bormidi?
{r:There wasn’t any light in the dark corner of the attic.} - Cherdakning qorong'u burchagida yorug'lik yo'q edi.
{r:There weren’t any decorations in the corner of the empty room.} - Bo'sh xonaning burchagida hech qanday bezaklar yo'q edi.

text: {r:Wallet}[ˈwɑːlɪt] - hamyon. Bobom yurak uchun ichadigan validol dorisini juda ehtiyot qiladi. Ko'pincha {p:VALID}olni {h:hamyoni} ichiga solib yuradi, pulni asragandek asraydi.
examples: {r:Your wallet does not suit your trousers.} - Sening hamyoning shimingga mos tushmaydi.
{r:Everything depends on your wallet.} - Hammasi sizning hamyoningizga bog'liq.
{r:There wasn’t any money in the wallet, unfortunately.} - Afsuski, hamyonda pul yo'q edi.
{r:He is sad because he lost his wallet.} - U hozir g'amgin chunki hamyonini yo'qotib qo'ydi.

text: {r:Robbery}[ˈrɑːbəri] - o'g'irlik. Rob(o'g'irlamoq) so'zidan yasalgan. Mnemonik namuna uchun 32-darsdagi rob ga qarang.
examples: {r:There was a robbery at the bank last night.} - Kecha bankda talonchilik sodir bo'lgan edi.
{r:Robberies are happening everywhere these days.} - O'g'irliklar shu kunlarda hamma yerda sodir bo'lyapti.
{r:There wasn’t any evidence of the robbery at the crime scene.} - Jinoyat joyida talonchilikning hech qanday dalili yo'q edi.
{r:Robbery happened quietly last night.} - O'g'irlik kecha tunda jimjitlik bilan sodir etilgan.

text: {r:Queue}[kjuː] - navbat. Tasavvur qiling, siz juda go'zal qizsiz va sizga uylanmoqchi bo'lgan ehtimoliy {p:KUYO}vlar darvozangiz tagida uzun {h:navbat} hosil qilib turishadi.
examples: {r:There was a long queue at the ticket counter this morning.} - Bugun ertalab chiptalar oynasida uzun navbat bor edi.
{r:Were there queues everywhere during the big sale?} - Katta sotuv paytida hamma joyda navbatlar bormidi?
{r:There wasn’t any queue at the entrance to the museum.} - Muzey kirish joyida navbat yo'q edi.
{r:How long is this queue?} - Bu navbat qanchalar uzun?

text: {r:Yell}[jel] – baqirmoq. Bilasizmi nega Titanik cho’kib ketgan? Chunki hech kim aysbergni ko’rib “{p:YEL}kanlarni tushiring, to’xtaymiz” deb {h:baqir}magan.
examples: {r:There was a loud yell from the next room.} - Keyingi xonadan qichqiriq eshitildi.
{r:My teacher yells at me for being late.} - Ustozim kechikkanim uchun baqiradi.
{r:There wasn’t any yell during the quiet meeting.} - Jim yig'ilish paytida hech qanday qichqiriq bo'lmagan edi.
{r:Please, don't yell at her.} - Iltimos unga baqirma.

text: {r:Legal}[ˈliːɡl] - qonuniy, legal. Bir xil so'zlar!
examples: {r:That was a fair legal choice.} - Bu adolatli qonuniy tanlov edi.
{r:Are your workers legal migrants?} - Ishchilaringiz qonuniy migrantlarmi?
{r:I am interested in a legal side of this action.} - Men bu harakatning qonuniy tarafiga qiziqyapman.
{r:Their actions had no legal problems.} - Ularning harakatlari qonuniy muammolarga olib kelmadi.

text: {r:Leader}[ˈliːdər] - rahbar, lider. Bir xil so'zlar!
examples: {r:Our team had a good leader.} - Jamoamizda yaxshi rahbar bor edi.
{r:Leaders were from different places at the meeting.} - Turli joylardan rahbarlar uchrashuvda bor edi.
{r:There was no clear leader to show them the way.} - Ularga yo'l ko'rsatadigan aniq rahbar yo'q edi.
{r:No leaders were present at the morning talk.} - Ertalabki suhbatda hech qanday rahbar qatnashmadi.

text: {r:Strong}[strɔːŋ] - kuchli, baquvvat. Agar Arnold Shvarsneggerdek {h:baquvvat} bo'lmoqchi bo'lsangiz, o'zimizning milliy brend {p:STRO}bar iste'mol qiling.
examples: {r:A strong wind blew last night.} - Kecha kuchli shamol esdi.
{r:Were there strong ideas about the new rule?} - Yangi qoida haqida kuchli fikrlar bormidi?
{r:There was no strong proof to show he was right.} - Uning haq ekanligini ko'rsatish uchun kuchli dalil yo'q edi.
{r:It is necessary to be strong at this time.} - Hozirgi vaqtda kuchli bo'lish juda muhim.

text: {r:Weak}[wiːk] – kuchsiz, ojiz. Barselona jamoasi muxlislari Viktor Valdezni yaxshi eslashsa kerak. Viktor jamoa Messi boshchiligida eng gullagan davrida darvozani qo’riqlar edi. Jamoa akademiyasidan chiqqan {p:VIK}tor davrida darvoza jamoaning eng {h:kuchsiz} nuqtasi bo’lib qolaverdi. Ko’pchilikning aytishicha, faqatgina jamoadoshlari bilan do’stona aloqasigina Viktorni Barsadek klubda o’ynashiga sabab bo’lgan.
examples: {r:The Wi-Fi signal was weak yesterday.} - Kecha Wi-Fi signali zaif edi.
{r:Were weak and useless ideas presented in the meeting?} - Yig'ilishda zaif va befoyda fikrlar aytildimi?
{r:Was there a weak spot in the plan?} - Rejada zaif joy bormidi?
{r:Independence movement was weak at that time.} - Mustaqillik harakati o'sha paytlarda zaif edi.

text: {r:Actual}[ˈæktʃuəl] – haqiqiy, asl. Televizorda xorij kanalida osh tayyorlashyapti, suvni ozgina ko’p quyib qo’yishibdi. {h:Aslida} bu {p:EK}randagi {p:SHUVL}a bo’lib qoldi.
examples: {r:The system had an actual problem.} - Tizimda haqiqiy muammo bor edi.
{r:Were there actual people who saw the event?} - Voqeani haqiqiy odamlar ko'rganmimi?
{r:Was there any actual harm to the car?} - Mashinaga haqiqiy zarar yetdimi?
{r:There were no actual reasons to worry.} - Xavotirlanish uchun asl sabablar yo'q edi.

text: {r:Personally}[ˈpɜːrsənəli] - shaxsan. Person(shaxs) so'zidan yasalgan.
examples: {r:Personally you don't care enough about the team.} - Shaxsan sen jamoa haqida yetarlicha qayg'urmaysan.
{r:Did the boss speak personally to each worker?} - Boshliq har bir ishchi bilan shaxsan gaplashdimi?
{r:I personally believe it will rain today.} - Men shaxsan bugun yomg'ir yog'adi deb o'ylayman.
{r:She gave the gift personally to her mother.} - U sovg'ani onasiga shaxsan berdi.

text: {r:Tasty}[ˈteɪsti] - mazali. Taste(tam) so'zidan yasalgan.
examples: {r:The party had a very tasty cake.} - Ziyofatda juda mazali tort bor edi.
{r:Were there tasty foods from different countries at the festival?} - Festivalda turli mamlakatlarning mazali taomlari bormidi?
{r:Was there anything tasty for people who don't eat meat?} - Go'sht yemaydiganlar uchun mazali narsa bormidi?
{r:That restaurant didn't have tasty food for children.} - O'sha restoranda bolalar uchun mazali ovqat yo'q edi.

text: {r:Boss}[bɒs] - boshliq, shef.
examples: {r:That company had a strict boss.} - U kompaniyada qattiqqo'l boshliq bor edi.
{r:Our boss should answer the call immediately.} - Boshlig'imiz qo'ng'iroqqa tezda javob berishi kerak.
{r:She has an understanding boss.} - Uning tushunadigan boshlig'i bor.
{r:It is possible that our boss will build a luxurious house from the bribe money.} - Ehtimol bizning boshliq olgan pora pullaridan hashamatli uy quradi.

text: {r:Onion}[ˈʌnjən] – piyoz. Bilasanmi dunyodagi eng savobli ish qaysi? Agar {p:ONANG}ni ko’zlari achimasin deb osh qilayotganda {h:piyoz}ini o’zing tug’rab bersang, ana shu katta savob.
examples: {r:The salad had too much onion.} - Salatda ortiqcha piyoz bor edi.
{r:Were there fresh onions at the market this morning?} - Bugun ertalab bozorda yangi piyozlar bormidi?
{r:Onion is becoming more expensive these days.} - Piyoz shu kunlarda qimmatlashib ketyapti.
{r:Yesterday, we bought 10 kg of onion.} - Kecha biz 10 kg piyoz sotib oldik.

text: {r:Potato}[pəˈteɪtoʊ] - kartoshka.
examples: {r:Potatoes are cheap and useful.} - Kartoshka arzon va foydali.
{r:There was a potato seller in our meeting yesterday.} - Kechagi uchrashuvimizda kartoshka sotuvchisi ham bor edi.
{r:Wash and wipe the potato before cutting it.} - Kartoshkani kesishdan oldin yuv va artib tashla
{r:There were not enough potatoes for everyone.} - Hammaga yetarli kartoshka yo'q edi.

text: {r:Vegetable}[ˈvedʒtəbl] – sabzavot. Tibbiyot fanlari doktorining aytishicha, kechqurun dori ichmaslik kerak ekan. O’rniga sabzavot yeyish kerak. Chunki {h:sabzavotlar}ning o’zi {p:VECH}erniy {p:TABL}etka. Shunday ekan, shamollasangiz yoki boshingiz og’risa kechki payt sabzavot yeng. (Namuna topish uchun yozildi yuqoridagi matn haqiqatga mos kelmaydi)
examples: {r:Vegetables are necessary for my health.} - Sabzavotlar sog'lig'im uchun zarur.
{r:Do you have enough vegetables?} - Yetarlicha sabzavotlaring bormi?
{r:Was there any vegetable you didn't like as a child?} - Bola paytingizda yoqtirmagan sabzavotingiz bormidi?
{r:I am eager to buy all the vegetables in your shop.} - Do'koningdagi barcha sabzavotlarni sotib olishga chanqoqman.

text: {r:Signature}[ˈsɪɡnətʃər] – imzo. Tasavvur qiling, pasport stolida ishlaysiz. Har kim pasportini olib ketayotganda pasportni olganligi haqida imzo chekishi kerak. Agar bu qoidani unutib ketib qolayotgan bo’lsa, ishxonada SIGNAL CHALinadi va fuqaro orqasiga qaytariladi. Xullas, {h:imzo} chekmasangiz {p:SIGNAL CHAL}inadi.
examples: {r:I advise you to change your signature.} - Imzoyingni o'zgartirishni maslahat beraman.
{r:Did you see any signatures on the wall?} - Devorda biron imzo ko'rdingizmi?
{r:His signature is very clear.} - Uning imzosi juda ozoda.
{r:The letter needed her signature.} - Xatga uning imzosi kerak edi.

text: {r:Fog}[fɒɡ] – tuman. Mana bu {p:FOK}usnik pushti rangli {h:tuman} chaqira olish qobiliyatiga ega.
examples: {r:There was thick fog this morning.} - Bugun ertalab qalin tuman bor edi.
{r:The fog made it hard to see.} - Tuman ko'rishni qiyinlashtirdi.
{r:Is there fog in the mountains?} - Tog'larda tuman bormi?
{r:We drove slowly because of the fog.} - Tuman tufayli sekin haydadik.

text: {r:Light}[laɪt] –  yengil. 28 - darsda light ning "yorug'", "chiroq" ma'nosini o'rgangan edik. Undan tashqari uning yana bir muhim ma'nosi bor. Bu so'z shuningdek 'yengil' ma'nosini bildirib heavy(og'ir) so'zining antonimi hisoblanadi.
examples: {r:Hasanboy is a light weight champion.} - Hasanboy yengil vazn chempioni.
{r:My car wheels are very light.} - Mashinam balonlari juda yengil.
{r:This box is very light.} - Bu quti juda yengil.
{r:My bag is light.} - Mening sumkam yengil.

text: {r:Employ}[ɪmˈplɔɪ] – ishga olmoq, ish bermoq. Ishlashni xohlaysizmi, men sizga {h:ish beraman.} Xitoydan {p:IMP}ortniy {p:LOY} olib kelaman va undan juda mustahkam g’isht tayyorlaymiz. Ish juda oson, joylashish uchun quyidagi telefon raqamlariga qo’ng’iroq qiling.
examples: {r:He will employ a new worker.} - U yangi ishchi ishga oladi.
{r:Does your company employ many people?} - Sizning kompaniyangiz ko'p odamni ishga oladimi?
{r:They did not employ Sarah.} - Ular Sarani ishga olishmadi.
{r:We want to employ good people.} - Biz yaxshi odamlarni ishga olishni xohlaymiz.

text: {r:Impossible}[ɪmˈpɒsəbl] – imkonsiz. Amerikada deyarli {h:imkonsiz} narsani uddalashdi. Pochta kompaniyasi {p:IM}oratni {p:PASIL}kada jo’natishdi va hayratlarga sababchi bo’lishdi.
examples: {r:It is impossible to fly without a plane.} - Samolyotsiz uchish imkonsiz.
{r:That was hardly an impossible task.} - Bu deyarli imkonsiz vazifa edi.
{r:Is it impossible to learn all words?} - Barcha so'zlarni o'rganish imkonsizmi?
{r:It is not impossible to win the game.} - O'yinni yutish imkonsiz emas.

text: {r:Immediately}[ɪˈmiːdiətli] - tezda, zudlik bilan. Immediate(tez, darhol) so'zining ravish shakli.
examples: {r:Come home immediately.} - Darhol uyga keling.
{r:He said it immediately.} - U buni darhol aytdi.
{r:Can you answer me immediately?} - Menga darhol javob bera olasizmi?
{r:She left the room immediately.} - U darhol xonadan chiqib ketdi.

text: {r:Terrible}[ˈterəbl] – dahshatli, yoqimsiz, yomon. Har kungi rejalarni yozib yurish uchun bloknot sotib oldim. Lekin ustidagi muqovasi menga yoqmadi va shunda o’zim qo’y terisidan muqova tayyorlashga qaror qildim. Ammo {p:TERI}dan {p:BL}oknot juda {h:yoqimsiz} bo’lar ekan. Teridan yaxshi, silliq pergament tayyorlay olmadim va mening muqovamda qo’y junlari soch tolasidek osilib turar edi.
examples: {r:The weather is terrible today.} - Bugun ob-havo dahshatli.
{r:It was a terrible noise.} - Bu dahshatli shovqin edi.
{r:Do you feel terrible?} - Siz o'zingizni dahshatli his qilyapsizmi?
{r:That was a terrible film.} - Bu dahshatli film edi.

text: {r:Increase}[ɪnˈkriːs] – oshirmoq, oshmoq, ko'paymoq; oshish, ko'payish. Toshkent {p:in}stitutida {p:kris}a, poraxo’rlar hali ham ko’p. Ular soni {h:oshib bormoqda}.
examples: {r:The prices will increase.} - Narxlar oshadi.
{r:Did the number of people increase?} - Odamlar soni ko'paydimi?
{r:We need to increase our speed.} - Biz tezligimizni oshirishimiz kerak.
{r:His work will increase.} - Uning ishi ko'payadi.

text: {r:Decrease}[dɪˈkriːs] – kamaymoq, pasaymoq; kamayish. Bizning universitetimiz dekani universitet hududida “{p:DEK}an {p:RES}torani” nomli restoran ochgan. Agar bu restoranda ovqatlansangiz, vazningiz {h:kamayib} {h:ketadi.} Semiz bo’lsangiz shu yerga keling.
examples: {r:The noise will decrease tonight.} - Shovqin bugun tunda kamayadi.
{r:Did the number of cars decrease?} - Mashinalar soni kamaydimi?
{r:We need to decrease the use of water.} - Biz suv ishlatishni kamaytirishimiz kerak.
{r:His weight will decrease.} - Uning vazni kamayadi.

text: {r:Improve}[ɪmˈpruːv] – yaxshilamoq, o’stirmoq, rivojlantirmoq. Jahongir Foziljonov chet eldan rubob olib keltiribdi va boshqalarga maqtanibdi: “Mana bu {p:IMPR}tniy {p:RUB}ob, 10 000$ ga oldim, mana shu rubob bilan men o’zbek estradasini keskin {h:rivojlantiraman}”.
examples: {r:You need to improve your English.} - Siz ingliz tilingizni yaxshilashingiz kerak.
{r:Did your work improve?} - Sizning ishingiz yaxshilandimi?
{r:She wants to improve her house.} - U uyini yaxshilashni xohlaydi.
{r:It will improve your life.} - Bu hayotingizni yaxshilaydi.

text: {r:Concentrate}[ˈkɒnsəntreɪt] - diqqatni jamlamoq, konsentratsiya qilmoq. Bir xil so'zlar!
examples: {r:It is hard to concentrate now.} - Hozir diqqatni jamlash qiyin.
{r:Please concentrate on your book.} - Iltimos, kitobingizga diqqat qiling.
{r:Can you concentrate on the task?} - Vazifaga diqqat qila olasizmi?
{r:I cannot concentrate with this noise.} - Bu shovqin bilan diqqat qila olmayman.

text: {r:Act}[ækt] – harakat qilmoq; o’zini qandaydir xarakterda tutmoq. Bu so’z ham fe’l, ham ot bo’lishi mumkin. E’tibor bersangiz, aktyor va aktiv so’zlari ham aynan shu so’zdan olinganini sezishingiz mumkin.
examples: {r:It is time to act.} - Harakat qilish vaqti keldi.
{r:She will act in a play.} - U spektaklda o'ynaydi.
{r:Did he act in a good way?} - U o'zini yaxshi tutdimi?
{r:You must act well.} - Sen o'zingni yaxshi tutishing kerak.
{r:We must act now.} - Biz hozir harakat qilishimiz kerak.

text: {r:Repeat}[rɪˈpiːt] – takrorlamoq. Hozir san’at oldingidan ham bachkanalashib ketgan. Oldin odamlar qo’shiq, rep aytardi. Hozir {p:REP IT}lar chiqib ketgan. Repper itlar o’zidan to’qib nimadir aytolmasa ham mashhur replarning itcha versiyasini {h:takrorlab} aytib beradi.
examples: {r:It is not difficult to repeat this word.} - Bu so'zni takrorlash qiyin emas.
{r:Did you repeat my name?} - Siz mening ismimni takrorladingizmi?
{r:She likes to repeat songs.} - U qo'shiqlarni takrorlashni yaxshi ko'radi.
{r:We must repeat this lesson.} - Biz bu darsni takrorlashimiz kerak.

text: {r:Cookie}[ˈkʊki] – pechenye. Shirinliklar olami ham kreativlikka va fantaziyalarga boy. Kecha xotinim {p:KUKI}rizli {h:pechenye} tayyorlab berdi. G’arch g’urch qiladigan ovozi bor ekan, mazza qilib yedim.
examples: {r:I like to eat cookies.} - Men pechenyelarni yaxshi ko'raman.
{r:Did you make these cookies?} - Bu pechenyelarni siz qildingizmi?
{r:My child wants a cookie.} - Bolam pechenye xohlaydi.
{r:It is my obligation to make cookies for my mother.} - Onamga pechenye tayyorlash bu mening vazifam.

text: {r:Dependent}[dɪˈpendənt] - qaram, bog'liq. Depend(bog'liq bo'lmoq) so'zidan yasalgan.
examples: {r:A child is dependent on parents.} - Bola ota-onaga bog'liq.
{r:Are you dependent on coffee?} - Siz qahvaga qaram bo‘lib qolgansizmi?
{r:He is dependent on his job.} - U o'z ishiga bog'liq.
{r:The result was dependent on our work.} - Natija ishimizga bog'liq edi.

text: {r:Ideally}[aɪˈdiːəli] so‘zi o‘zbek tilida "eng yaxshi holatda", "ideal tarzda", "afzal holatda" degan ma’nolarni anglatadi. U orzu qilingan, eng maqbul yoki eng to‘g‘ri holatni ifodalash uchun ishlatiladi. 1) "Ideally, we should finish the project by Friday." — "Eng yaxshi holatda, biz loyihani jumagacha tugatishimiz kerak." 2) "Ideally, children should get 8 hours of sleep." — "Ideal tarzda, bolalar 8 soat uxlashlari kerak." 3) "Ideally, the new system will save us time and money." — "Afzal holatda, yangi tizim bizga vaqt va pul tejaydi." 4) "Ideally, I’d like to live near the sea." — "Eng yaxshi holatda, men dengiz yaqinida yashashni xohlayman.
examples: {r:Ideally, we will go home early.} - Eng yaxshi holatda, biz uyga erta boramiz.
{r:Do you want to live ideally?} - Siz ideal tarzda yashashni xohlaysizmi?
{r:Ideally, the weather will be sunny.} - Eng yaxshi holatda, ob-havo quyoshli bo'ladi.
{r:We should ideally start now.} - Hozir boshlasak ideal bo'lar edi.

text: {r:Myth}[mɪθ] - afsona, mif. {p:Mif} sodasi kirlarni toza yuvishi bilan {h:afsona}ga aylangan.
examples: {r:It is an old myth.} - Bu eski afsona.
{r:Do you believe in this myth?} - Siz bu afsonaga ishonasizmi?
{r:Some people like a good myth.} - Ba'zi odamlar yaxshi afsonani yoqtiradi.
{r:That story is just a myth.} - Bu hikoya shunchaki afsona.

text: {r:Promise}[ˈprɒmɪs] – va'da; va'da bermoq. {p:Pro}kurorlar {p:mis} haykalni ishxonalarida saqlashadi. Misdan yasalgan ushbu adolat haykalining ko’zlari yopilgan va bu poraxo’rlik, tanish bilishlikka yo’q deyman degani. Bu haykal prokurorlarga vatan oldidagi burchi va adolatli bo’lishga berilgan {h:va'dasini} eslatib turadi.
examples: {r:He made a promise to me.} - U menga va'da berdi.
{r:Did you keep your promise?} - Siz va'dangizni bajardingizmi?
{r:I always keep my promise.} - Men har doim va'damda turaman.
{r:It is my promise to help you.} - Senga yordam berish bu mening va'dam.
{r:She did not break her promise.} - U va'dasini buzmadi.

text: {r:Miss}[mɪs] – sog’inmoq. Bolaligimda {p:mis} yig’ar edik, uni sotib cho’ntaklarimiz kengayardi. O’sha davrlarni {h:sog’inaman}.
examples: {r:I miss my family.} - Men oilamni sog'inaman.
{r:It is dangerous to miss smoking.} - Chekishni sog‘insang, bu xavfli.
{r:She will miss her home.} - U uyini sog'inadi.
{r:It is windy now and I am missing quiet times.} - Hozir shamolli va men sokin paytlarni sog'inyapman.

text: {r:Insist}[ɪnˈsɪst] so‘zi o‘zbek tilida "qattiq turib olmoq", "talab qilmoq", "ta’kidlamoq" degan ma’nolarni anglatadi. Bu so‘z biror narsani qat’iy tarzda aytish yoki amalga oshishini talab qilish holatlarida ishlatiladi. 1) "He insisted on paying for dinner." — "U kechki ovqat uchun to‘lashga qattiq turib oldi." 2) "She insisted that everything was fine." — "U hammasi joyida ekanini ta’kidladi." 3) "They insisted we stay for dessert." — "Ular bizning shirinlikka qolishimizni talab qilishdi." 4) "I didn’t want to go, but he insisted." — "Men borishni xohlamadim, lekin u qattiq turib oldi.
examples: {r:He will insist on his idea.} - U o'z g'oyasida qattiq turib oladi.
{r:Did you insist on leaving?} - Siz ketaman deb turib oldingizmi?
{r:She insists on playing chess again.} - U yana shaxmat o'ynaymiz deb turib oladi.
{r:They did not insist on money.} - Ular pul deb turib olishmadi.

text: {r:Honey}[ˈhʌni] – asal. Adashmasam, {h:Asal}{p:xoney} ismli taniqli blogger bor edi. Qiziqarlisi, uning ismida ham asal so’zining o’zbekchasi, ham inglizcha tarjimasi bor edi.
examples: {r:I like to eat honey.} - Men asalni yaxshi ko'raman.
{r:Is there honey in this tea?} - Bu choyda asal bormi?
{r:My child likes honey with bread.} - Bolam asalli nonni yoqtiradi.
{r:We have fresh honey.} - Bizda yangi asal bor.

text: {r:Flow}[floʊ] – oqmoq; oqim. Tasavvur qiling, siz tanigan Farhod ismli inson loviya ekibdi va juda kam hosil olibdi. Kombayn hosilini terib yig’ib bersa, atigi 100 kg hosil chiqibdi gektaridan. Jahli chiqqan {p:F}arhod {p:LOV}iyalarini suvga {h:oqizib} yuboribdi.
examples: {r:The river will flow fast.} - Daryo tez oqadi.
{r:Did the water flow?} - Suv oqdimi?
{r:We watch the river flow.} - Biz daryo oqimini tomosha qilamiz.
{r:Her hair will flow in the wind.} - Uning sochlari shamolda hilpiraydi.

text: {r:Any}[ˈeni] – har; har qanday, qaysidir, qanchadir. {h:Har qanday} yigitga {p:enli} yelka yarashadi.
examples: {r:Do you have any money?} - Sizda qanchadir pul bormi?
{r:Is there any water here?} - Bu yerda qanchadir suv bormi?
{r:I don't have any brothers.} - Mening hech qanday akalarim yo'q.
{r:It is not hard to learn any language.} - Har qanday tilni o'rganish qiyin emas.

text: {r:Anything}[ˈeniθɪŋ] - biror narsa, har narsa. 62-darsda bu so'z chuqurroq grammatik tahlil qilingan.
examples: {r:You can take anything you want in my shop.} - Mening do'konimdan xohlagan narsani olishing mumkin.
{r:What did you see there?} - Siz u yerda nima ko'rdingiz?
{r:I did not find anything today.} - Men bugun hech narsa topmadim.
{r:Is there anything to eat?} - Yeyishga biror narsa bormi?

text: {r:Soon}[suːn] – tez orada. {h:Tez orada} seni {p:sun}nat qilamiz bolakay.
examples: {r:You will soon see my paintings.} - Tez orada chizma rasmlarimni ko'rasiz.
{r:What will start soon?} - Tez orada nima boshlanadi?
{r:We will go soon.} - Biz tez orada boramiz.
{r:The work finished soon.} - Ish tezda tugadi.

text: {r:Lovely}[ˈlʌvli] - ajoyib, sevimli, go'zal. Love(sevgi) so'zidan yasalgan.
examples: {r:Who has lovely sunglasses?} - Kimda ajoyib ochkilar bor?
{r:Uzbekistan is a lovely and hospitable country.} - O'zbekiston ajoyib va mehmondo'st davlat.
{r:It is a lovely day today.} - Bugun ajoyib kun.
{r:We saw a lovely cat.} - Biz ajoyib mushukni ko'rdik.

text: {r:Anybody}[ˈenibədi] - kimdir, har kim. 62-mavzuda anybody va shunga o'xshagan so'zlar haqida atroflicha o'rganasiz.
examples: {r:Did anybody call you?} - Sizga kimdir qo'ng'iroq qildimi?
{r:Anybody can learn English} - Har kim inglizcha o'rganishi mumkin.
{r:I did not see anybody.} - Men hech kimni ko'rmadim.
{r:Can anybody help me?} - Menga kimdir yordam bera oladimi?

text: {r:Cheese}[tʃiːz] – pishloq. Odatda pishloq sutdan tayyorlanadi. Lekin mana bu pishloq shunisi bilan farqliki, uni tayyorlashda faqat {p:CHIS}nok ishlatiladi.
examples: {r:Who wants cheese?} - Kim pishloq xohlaydi?
{r:What did you eat with cheese?} - Siz pishloq bilan nima yedingiz?
{r:I like to eat cheese with bread.} - Men nonga pishloq bilan yeyishni yaxshi ko'raman.
{r:Is there cheese in the fridge?} - Muzlatgichda pishloq bormi?

text: {r:Pleased}[pliːzd] - mamnun, xursand. Agar bolalarim xafa bo'lsa, men ularning {h:xursand} bo'lishi uchun {p:PLEYST}eyshnga olib boraman.
examples: {r:They are finally pleased with your results.} - Nihoyat ular sizning natijangizdan xursand.
{r:What made her pleased?} - Uni nima xursand qildi?
{r:I am pleased to see you.} - Sizni ko'rganimdan xursandman.
{r:Were they pleased with the present?} - Ular sovg'adan mamnun bo'ldimi?

text: {r:Rest}[rest] - qolgan(lar)i. 29-darsda 'rest' so'zining 'dam olmoq' ma'nosini o'rgangan edik. Quyidagi misollar orqali biz bugun uning ikkinchi ma'nosini ham ko'rib chiqamiz.
examples: {r:Who ate the rest of the cake?} - Tortning qolganini kim yedi?
{r:What did you do for the rest of the day?} - Kunning qolgan qismida nima qildingiz?
{r:I will finish the rest of the work.} - Men ishning qolgan qismini tugataman.
{r:The rest of the money is in the bag.} - Pulning qolgani sumkada.

text: {r:Fortune}[ˈfɔːrtʃuːn] – omad, saodat; boylik. Mashhur Forsaj filmi rejissyori asli Xitoylik Jastin Lin ekanligini bilasizmi? Aslida uyalchang xarakterga ega Jastinga {p:FOR}saj {p:CHIN}dan ham omad va katta {h:boylik} olib kelgan. Taxminlarga ko’ra uning boyligi 200 million dollardan ortiq daromadni tashkil etadi.
examples: {r:Who found the fortune?} - Omadni kim topdi?
{r:What did he get from his fortune?} - U o'z boyligidan nima oldi?
{r:It was a big fortune.} - Bu katta boylik edi.
{r:Good fortune came to them.} - Ularga yaxshi omad keldi.

text: {r:Sick}[sɪk] – kasal. Uzoq yillardan beri doktor bo’lib ishlayotgan do’stim, agar erkak bemorlar kelsa, “Nima {p:SIG}aret chekasizmi?” deydi. Chunki sigaret barcha {h:kasal}liklarning boshlanishi.
examples: {r:Who is sick today?} - Bugun kim kasal?
{r:What made her sick?} - Uni nima kasal qildi?
{r:I feel sick and sleepy.} - Men o'zimni uyquchan va kasal his qilyapman.
{r:The child was sick last night.} - Bola kecha kechqurun kasal edi.

text: {r:Hopefully}[ˈhoʊpfəli] - umid qilamizki(qilamanki). Hope(umid qilmoq) so'zidan yasalgan.
examples: {r:Hopefully, the weather will be good.} - Umid qilamizki, ob-havo yaxshi bo'ladi.
{r:Hopefully, he will come soon.} - Umid qilamizki, u tez orada keladi.
{r:Hopefully, we will finish on time.} - Umid qilamizki, biz o'z vaqtida tugatamiz.
{r:Hopefully, I will learn all words.} - Umid qilamanki, men barcha so'zlarni o'rganaman.

text: {r:Seemingly}[ˈsiːmɪŋli] - ko'rinishidan. Seem(tuyulmoq) so'zidan yasalgan.
examples: {r:Who is seemingly happy?} - Ko'rinishidan kim baxtli?
{r:What seems to be the problem?} - Nima muammo bo'lib tuyuladi?
{r:He was seemingly tired.} - U ko'rinishidan charchagan edi.
{r:The sky was seemingly clear.} - Osmon ko'rinishidan tiniq edi.

text: {r:Considerate}[kənˈsɪdərət] so‘zi o‘zbek tilida "e’tiborli", "o‘ylab ish tutadigan", "boshqalarni hurmat qiladigan" degan ma’nolarni anglatadi. Bu so‘z odatda boshqalarning his-tuyg‘ularini, ehtiyojlarini inobatga oladigan, muloyim va hurmatli odamni tasvirlashda ishlatiladi. 1) "She is very considerate of other people’s feelings." — "U boshqalarning his-tuyg‘ulariga juda e’tiborli." 2) "It was considerate of him to call and check on me." — "Uning qo‘ng‘iroq qilib ahvolimni so‘rashi e’tiborli harakat edi." 3) "Please be considerate and turn down the music." — "Iltimos, e’tiborli bo‘ling va musiqa ovozini pasaytiring." 4) "A considerate driver always yields to pedestrians." — "E’tiborli haydovchi har doim piyodalarga yo‘l beradi.
examples: {r:Who is a considerate person?} - Kim e'tiborli odam?
{r:What did he do that was considerate?} - U e'tiborli nima ish qildi?
{r:She is a very considerate friend.} - U juda e'tiborli do'st.
{r:Be considerate to others.} - Boshqalarga e'tiborli bo'ling.

text: {r:Relative}[ˈrelətɪv] – qarindosh; nisbiy. Tasavvur qiling, {p:RE}diska ekib {p:LATIF} boy bo’lib ketibdi va {h:qarindosh}larini rosa sovg’a-salom va pullar bilan siylabdi. Endi siz balki Latif menga ham uzoqroq qarindoshdir deya surishtiruvni boshladingiz.
examples: {r:Who is your relative?} - Sizning qarindoshingiz kim?
{r:What is your relation to this person?} - Bu odamga nisbatan sizning aloqangiz nima?
{r:My teacher is my distant relative.} - O'qituvchim mening uzoq qarindoshim.
{r:They are my relatives.} - Ular mening qarindoshlarim.

text: {r:National}[ˈnæʃnəl] - milliy. Nation(millat) so'zidan yasalgan.
examples: {r:Who sings the national anthem?} - Milliy madhiyani kim aytadi?
{r:What is your national color?} - Sizning milliy rangingiz nima?
{r:It is a national holiday today.} - Bugun milliy bayram.
{r:We have a national team.} - Bizda milliy jamoa bor.

text: {r:Considerable}[kənˈsɪdərəbl] – talaygina, anchagina. Men qishloq joyda yashayman va har kuni uyga suv tashishim kerak. Agar chelakda tashisam, u suv urvoq ham bo’lmaydi. Agar {p:KANSTR BIL}an tashisam, bir hafta mazza qilib ishlataman {h:talaygina} suvni.
examples: {r:Who made a considerable effort?} - Kim katta harakat qildi?
{r:Actually our military has considerable responsibilities.} - Aslida bizning harbiylarimizning ulkan ma'suliyati bor.
{r:There was a considerable noise.} - Talaygina shovqin bor edi.
{r:She has considerable knowledge.} - Uning talaygina bilimi bor.

text: {r:Translate}[trænsˈleɪt] – tarjima qilmoq. Men Leytenant Sobirov Chirchiqda harbiy sohada ishlayman, lekin Toshkentda yashayman. Har kuni Toshkentdan Chirchiqqa jamoat transportida qatnayman. Transportda juda ko’p hind talabalarini uchrataman va ularga konduktor bilan gaplashishga yordam beraman, ingliz tilini bilganligim uchun. Xullas, jamoat {p:TRANS}portida {p:LEYT}enant {h:tarjimonlik} bilan shug’ullanadi, Chirchiqda esa davlat xizmati bilan.
examples: {r:Can you translate this word?} - Bu so'zni tarjima qila olasizmi?
{r:Who can translate from English to Uzbek?} - Ingliz tilidan o'zbek tiliga kim tarjima qila oladi?
{r:I need to translate a letter.} - Men xatni tarjima qilishim kerak.
{r:She did not translate the book.} - U kitobni tarjima qilmadi.

text: {r:Follow}[ˈfɒloʊ] – ergashmoq;rioya qilmoq. Bizni shaharda ajoyib folbin bor. Boshqa folbinlar qo’lga qarab yoki karta bilan fol ochsalar, bu {p:FOL}bin {p:LOV}iyaga qarab fol ochadi va ‘’menga {h:ergashib} quyidagi so’zlarni qaytaring’’ deydi.
examples: {r:Who will follow us?} - Bizga kim ergashadi?
{r:What rules do you follow?} - Siz qaysi qoidalarga rioya qilasiz?
{r:He followed me only once.} - U menga faqat bir marta ergashdi.
{r:New learners follow the rules.} - Yangi o'rganuvchilar qoidalarga rioya qilishadi.

text: {r:Material}[məˈtɪəriəl] - material. O'zbekcha va inglizcha variantlari talaffuzda farq qiladi.
examples: {r:What material is this shirt made of?} - Bu ko'ylak qaysi materialdan qilingan?
{r:Who works with different materials?} - Turli materiallar bilan kim ishlaydi?
{r:I need new material for my dress.} - Menga ko'ylagim uchun yangi material kerak.
{r:This is a strong material.} - Bu kuchli material.

text: {r:Original}[əˈrɪdʒənl] - original. O'zbekcha va inglizcha variantlari talaffuzda farq qiladi.
examples: {r:Who wrote the original story?} - Original hikoyani kim yozdi?
{r:What is the original idea?} - Original g'oya nima?
{r:This is the original book.} - Bu original kitob.
{r:Did you see the original picture?} - Original rasmni ko'rdingizmi?

text: {r:Demand}[dɪˈmænd] – talab; talab qilmoq. Boy bo'lish uchun nima qilish kerak? Bozorda nimaga talab yuqori ekanligini topish kerak. Oxirgi yillarda qurilish biznesi rivojlayotganini ko'rib siz eng ko'p {h:talab} {p:SEMENT}da degan xulosaga keldingiz va sement sotishga kirishmoqchisiz.
examples: {r:He demanded an explanation from his friend.} - U do‘stidan izoh talab qildi.
{r:The workers demanded higher wages.} - Ishchilar yuqori maosh talab qilishdi.
{r:There is a high demand for smartphones.} - Smartfonlarga katta talab bor.
{r:She demanded that the door be locked.} - U eshikning qulflanishini qat’iy talab qildi.

text: {r:Like}[laɪk] – o‘xshash, o'xshab (sifat so'z turkumiga xos so'z). Avval like ning 'yoqtirmoq' ma'nosini o'rgangan edik. Lekin bu so'zning ma'nolari ko'p. Uning bu ma'nosi sifat so'z turkumiga xos va ko'pincha look(ko'rinmoq) so'zi bilan birga kelib o'xshamoq ma'nosini bildiradi.
examples: {r:I am intelligent like my father.} - Men otamga o'xshab aqlliman.
{r:Do they look like each other?} - Ular bir-biriga o‘xshaydimi?
{r:She is like a teacher.} - U o‘qituvchiga o‘xshaydi.
{r:This place is like a museum.} - Bu joy muzeyga o‘xshaydi.
{r:I look like my father.} - Men otamga o'xshayman.

text: {r:Marriage}[ˈmærɪdʒ] - nikoh, oila qurish. Marry(uylanmoq, tegmoq) so'zidan olingan. Mnemonik namuna uchun 36-darsga qarang.
examples: {r:Who did you go to the marriage ceremony with?} - To'y marosimiga kim bilan bordiz?
{r:What was the marriage ceremony like?} - To'y marosimi qanday edi?
{r:Who were they talking about during the marriage preparations?} - To'y tayyorgarliklari paytida kim haqida gaplashishayotgan edi?
{r:Which marriage are you looking forward to?} - Qaysi nikohni intizorlik bilan kutyapsiz?

text: {r:Respond}[rɪˈspɒnd] – javob bermoq. Toshkentda lag’monxonaga kirdingiz va yegan lag’moningiz ta’mi sizga ma’qul kelmadi va ofitsiantlardan birini chaqirdingiz. U esa “Agar shikoyat va takliflaringiz bo’lsa, {p:RES}toran egasi {p:PAND}aga murojaat qiling. U sizning shikoyatlaringizga {h:javob beradi}” dedi. Restoran egasi Kungfu Pandadagi Po ekan.
examples: {r:Who did you respond to about the urgent request?} - Shoshilinch so'rov haqida kimga javob berdingiz?
{r:What was her response like to the unexpected news?} - Kutilmagan yangilikka uning javobi qanday edi?
{r:Which issue did the manager respond to first?} - Menejer birinchi navbatda qaysi masalaga javob berdi?
{r:What did they respond with when asked about the delay?} - Kechikish haqida so'ralganda ular nima bilan javob berishdi?

text: {r:Rise}[raɪz] - ko'tarilmoq; ko'tarilish. Siz kecha tunda tush ko'rdingiz. Tushingizda rosa amalingiz {h:ko'tarilib} ketibdi. Raislarning {p:RAIS}i bo'libsiz, ya'ni tuman hokimi.
examples: {r:What was the sun's rise like this morning?} - Bugun ertalab quyoshning chiqishi qanday edi?
{r:Crime rates have risen considerably.} - Jinoyat darajasi anchagina o'sdi.
{r:He hardly rose to fame.} - U zo'rg'a mashhurlikka ko'tarildi.
{r:Where did the smoke rise from?} - Tutun qayerdan ko'tarildi?

text: {r:Weigh}[weɪ] – qanchadir vaznda bo’lmoq. Sport bilan shug’ullanib vazn to’plamoqchi bo’lganlar eng yaxshi sport ozuqasi qaysi ekanligini yaxshi bilishadi. Bu albatta {p:whey} sport ozuqasi.
examples: {r:How much do you weigh?} - Qancha vazning?
{r:I weigh just 50kg.} - Men atigi 50kg man.
{r:I should know how much these potatoes and onions weigh.} - Bu kartoshka va piyozlar qancha tosh bosishini bilishim kerak.
{r:Which ingredients do you need to weigh out?} - Qaysi ingredientlarni tortib olishingiz kerak?

text: {r:Action}[ˈækʃn] - harakat, chora.
examples: {r:I mainly took useless actions at that time.} - Men o'sha vaqti asosan befoyda harakatlar qildim.
{r:Take actions before it is late.} - Choralar ko'r kech bo'lmasidan.
{r:What immediate actions did you take?} - Qanday tez choralar ko'rdingiz?
{r:We must take suitable actions quickly.} - Biz tezda mos choralar ko'rishimiz kerak.

text: {r:Belong}[bɪˈlɒŋ] – tegishli bo’lmoq, a’zo bo’lmoq. Shaharning ziyoli va zodagon qatlamiga {h:tegishli} inson sifatida shakllanmoqchimisiz? Unda birinchi teatrga {p:BIL}et {p:ONG.} Chunki teatrda shunday insonlar yig’iladi va siz ham ulardan biriga aylanasiz.
examples: {r:Who do these keys belong to?} - Bu kalitlar kimga tegishli?
{r:What was the old photograph like that belonged to your grandmother?} - Buvingizga tegishli eski fotosurat qanday edi?
{r:Which club does she belong to?} - U qaysi klubga a'zo?
{r:This money belongs to me.} - Bu pul menga tegishli.

text: {r:Worry}[ˈwʌri] – xavotir; xavotir olmoq. Bu yil yozda varenya(murabbo) tayyorlayapman. Lekin shu {p:VARY}enani chumolilar mendan oldin yeb tugatishidan {h:xavotir} olyapman.
examples: {r:What are you worrying about?} - Nima haqida xavotirlanyapsiz?
{r:What was his worry like before the big presentation?} - Katta taqdimotdan oldin uning xavotiri qanday edi?
{r:Who did she worry for during the difficult times?} - Qiyin paytlarda u kim uchun xavotirlanardi?
{r:Which problem did they worry most about?} - Ular ko'proq qaysi muammo haqida tashvishlanishdi?

text: {r:Respect}[rɪˈspekt] – hurmat; hurmat qilmoq. Yaponiyada Pokemonni juda sevishadi va {h:hurmat qilishadi} va hatto {p:RES}toran ochishgan {p:PIK}achu nomiga.
examples: {r:Who do you have the most respect for in your life?} - Hayotingizda kimga eng ko'p hurmat qilasiz?
{r:What was the respect shown to the veterans like?} - Veteranlarga ko'rsatilgan hurmat qanday edi?
{r:I fully respect your argument.} - Men sizning argumentingizni to'liq hurmat qilaman.
{r:Nobody respects my weak boss.} - Mening kuchsiz boshlig'imni hech kim hurmat qilmaydi.

text: {r:Relatively}[ˈrelətɪvli] – nisbatan. Siz va qo’shningiz uy sotyapsizlar. Siz o’zingiz sotyapsiz, qo’shningiz esa rieltor yollayapti. Oqibatda sizning qo’shingiz {h:‘’nisbatan’’} qimmatroq narxga sota oldi, chunki u {p:RIELTORLI} sotuvchi.
examples: {r:What was the difficulty like, relatively speaking?} - Qiyinchilik qanday edi, nisbatan aytganda?
{r:What country has relatively more oxygen?} - Qaysi davlatda kislorod nisbatan ko'proq?
{r:Which signature is relatively more beautiful?} - Qaysi imzo nisbatan chiroyliroq?
{r:Where is the new office located relatively close to?} - Yangi ofis qayerga nisbatan yaqin joylashgan?

text: {r:Lightly}[ˈlaɪtli] – yengilgina, muloyimlik bilan; ozgina, biroz. Agar LED chiroqlarini tez, shoshib o’rnatsa, tez buzilib qoladi. {p:LEDLI} patronlarni {h:muloyimlik bilan}, sekin o’rnatish kerak.
examples: {r:It is snowing lightly.} - Biroz qor yog'yapti.
{r:What was the rain falling like, lightly or heavily?} - Yomg'ir qanday yog'ayotgan edi, yengilmi yoki kuchlimi?
{r:Who handled the fragile package lightly?} - Mo'rt paketni kim ehtiyotkorlik bilan ushladi?
{r:She was drawing something lightly.} - U muloyimlik bilan nimadir chizayotgan edi.

text: {r:Improvement}[ɪmˈpruːvmənt] - yaxshilanish, rivojlanish. Improve(yaxshilanmoq) so'zidan yasalgan.
examples: {r:What kind of improvement are you hoping for?} - Qanday yaxshilanishga umid qilyapsiz?
{r:What was the improvement in her grades like?} - Uning baholaridagi yaxshilanish qanday edi?
{r:Who is responsible for this improvement in the system?} - Tizimdagi bu yaxshilanish uchun kim javobgar?
{r:Which area needs the most improvement in your opinion?} - Sizning fikringizcha, qaysi soha eng ko'p yaxshilanishga muhtoj?

text: {r:Left}[left] – chap. Doktorlarning aytishicha, {p:lift}ga {h:chap} oyoq bilan kirish kerak ekan, shundagina havo bosimini his qilmas ekansiz.
examples: {r:The milk is on the right side and the butter is on the left.} - Sut o'ng tomonda va sariyog' chapda.
{r:My left arm was injured.} - Chap qo'lim jarohatlandi.
{r:You can have a seat on the left side.} - Chap tomonga o'tirishingiz mumkin.
{r:The traffic is heavy on the left.} - Qatnov chap tarafda tig'izroq.

text: {r:Regard}[rɪˈɡɑːrd] – deb hisoblamoq; hurmat. Men Samarqandni eng toza shahar {h:deb hisoblayman.} Chunki bilasizmi, {p:REG}istonga borsangiz, bir yerda bir {p:GARD}(chang degani) topa olmaysiz.
examples: {r:I regard him as a good friend.} - Men uni yaxshi do'st deb bilaman.
{r:They regard her as a strong leader.} - Ular uni kuchli rahbar deb bilishadi.
{r:Do you regard this as important?} - Siz buni muhim deb bilasizmi?
{r:We regard his work as productive.} - Biz uning ishini mahsuldor deb bilamiz.

text: {r:Moon}[muːn] – oy. Hozir oyga turistik maqsadlarda ham borib kelsa bo’ladi. Bunday ishni qilgan birinchi o’zbek {p:MUN}isa Rizayeva bo’ldi. Raketada {h:oyga} borib aylanib keldi.
examples: {r:What was the moon like last night, full and bright?} - Kecha kechqurun oy qanday edi, to'liq va yorqinmi?
{r:What does the full moon affect?} - To'liq oy nimaga ta'sir qiladi?
{r:The opposite side of the moon has not been studied yet.} - Oyning qarama-qarshi tarafi hali o'rganilmagan.
{r:The moon looks wonderful today.} - Oy bugun ajoyib ko'rinyapti.

text:
{r:Draw}[drɔː] – chizmoq; durang. 
O'tgan zamon shakllari - drew, drawn. 
Rasm darsida juda antiqa narsa chizdim. Non yopishda ishlatiladigan {p:DRO}jni {h:chizdim}.
examples: {r:They drew the mountain} - Ular tog'larni chizishdi.
{r:Drawing is my favourite hobby.} - Chizish mening sevimli hobbiyim.
{r:What did they draw with?} - Ular nima bilan chizishdi?
{r:Which topic did the speaker draw attention to?} - Ma'ruzachi qaysi mavzuga e'tibor qaratdi?

text: {r:Attract}[əˈtrækt] – jalb qilmoq, o’ziga tortmoq. Tasavvur qiling, siz katta yoshli inson bo’lsangiz ham bolalar {p:ATRAKT}sioni sizni o’ziga {h:jalb qilaveradi.} U yerga borib berkinmachoq, batut, quvalashmachoq, kamon o’ynagingiz kelaveradi.
examples: {r:What kind of events attract a large crowd?} - Qanday tadbirlar katta olomonni jalb qiladi?
{r:What was the new exhibition like that attracted so many visitors?} - Buncha tashrifchilarni jalb qilgan yangi ko'rgazma qanday edi?
{r:This English girl attracted attention to herself.} - Bu ingliz qiz juda o'ziga tortdi.
{r:This flower attracts her attention.} - Mana shu gul uning e'tiborini jalb qiladi.

text: {r:Attention}[əˈtenʃn] – diqqat, e’tibor. Dalaga bordim mashinada, yo’llarda mayda buta o’tinlar yotgan ekan, ustidan haydayveribman. Tushib qarasam, {p:o’tin shin}alarni yorib tashlabdi {h:e'tibor}li bo’lmaganligim uchun.
examples: {r:What did the teacher demand attention for?} - O'qituvchi nima uchun e'tibor talab qildi?
{r:What was the student's attention like?} - Talabaning diqqati qanday edi?
{r:Who needs a special attention?} - Kimga maxsus e'tibor lozim?
{r:This job needs your full attention.} - Bu ish sizning to'liq e'tiboringizni talab qiladi.
[center][b]pay/give attention - e'tibor bermoq[/b][/center]
{r:Pay attention to your health, it’s more important than money.} – Sog‘lig‘ingizga e’tibor bering, bu puldan ham muhim.
{r:You should pay attention to how she speaks; it’s very polite and clear.} – Uning qanday gapirishiga e’tibor bering; juda muloyim va ravshan.

text: {r:Recommend}[ˌrekəˈmend] – maslahat bermoq, tavsiya qilmoq. Hozir dunyodagi eng arzon va sifatsiz reklama qaysiligini bilasizmi? Youtube va Instagramda {p:REK}lama {p:KOMENT}lar bo’limida bo’lsa, bu eng ahmoqonasi. “Kursimni sotib oling”, “onlayn ishlab boyib keting” kabi reklama yozishni {h:maslahat} bermayman.
examples: {r:What book did she recommend to you?} - U sizga qaysi kitobni tavsiya qildi?
{r:What was the restaurant like that your friend recommended?} - Do'stingiz tavsiya qilgan restoran qanday edi?
{r:Anvar recommended me to become independent.} - Anvar menga mustaqil bo'lishni tavsiya qilgan.
{r:Which movie do you highly recommend watching?} - Qaysi filmni juda tavsiya qilasiz?

text: {r:Satisfy}[ˈsætɪsfaɪ] - qoniqtirmoq, rioya qilmoq.
examples: {r:Who will satisfy our needs?} - Ehtiyojlarimizni kim qondiradi?
{r:What did Anvar do to satisfy his boss?} - Anvar boshlig'ini qoniqtirish uchun nima qildi?
{r:We must satisfy the rules.} - Biz qoidalarga rioya qilishimiz kerak.
{r:Does this water satisfy your thirst? Yes, but hardly.} - Bu suv chanqog'ingizni qoniqtiradimi? Ha arang qondiradi.

text: {r:Distribute}[dɪˈstrɪbjuːt] – tarqatmoq, taqsimlamoq. Men Marsda {p:DISTRIBYUT}or bo’lib ishlaganman va do’konlarga mahsulot {h:tarqatganman}.
examples: {r:Who will distribute the books?} - Kitoblarni kim tarqatadi?
{r:The government decided to distribute domestic aid packages to affected regions.} - Hukumat zarar ko'rgan hududlarga ichki yordam paketlarini tarqatishga qaror qildi.
{r:The company will distribute apples.} - Kompaniya olma tarqatadi.
{r:My mother used to distribute letters in the past.} - Onam xatlarni tarqatib yurardi o'tmishda.

text: {r:Translator}[trænsˈleɪtər] - tarjimon. Translate(tarjima qilmoq) so'zidan olingan.
examples: {r:What kind of translator do you need?} - Sizga qanday tarjimon kerak?
{r:We regard him as a great translator.} - Biz uni ajoyib tarjimon deb bilamiz.
{r:How good is this translator?} - Bu tarjimon qanchalik yaxshi?
{r:He is a new translator and he is thirsty now.} - U yangi tarjimon va u hozir chanqagan.

text: {r:Leadership}[ˈliːdərʃɪp] - rahbarlik; rahbariyat. Leader(rahbar, lider, yetakchi) so'zidan yasalgan.
examples: {r:What kind of leadership is best?} - Qanday rahbarlik eng yaxshi?
{r:How strong is their leadership?} - Ularning rahbarligi qanchalik kuchli?
{r:This group needs strong leadership.} - Bu guruhga kuchli rahbarlik kerak.
{r:Who has good leadership qualities?} - Kimda yaxshi rahbarlik sifatlari bor?

text: {r:Laptop}[ˈlæptɒp] - noutbuk, laptop. Bir xil so'zlar!
examples: {r:What is your laptop for?} - Noutbukingiz nima uchun?
{r:Which laptop is yours, the new one or the old one?} - Qaysi noutbuk sizniki, yangisi yoki eskisi?
{r:How old is your laptop?} - Noutbukingiz qancha yoshda?
{r:I have a new laptop.} - Menda yangi noutbuk bor.

text: {r:Size}[saɪz] – hajm, o'lcham. Bobom tez-tez yoshligini eslaganda aytadilar: ''Biz {p:sayuz} payti eng katta dunyodagi davlat edik, {h:razmerimiz} juda katta edi''.
examples: {r:What size do you want?} - Qanday o'lcham xohlaysiz?
{r:Which size is better for you, small or big?} - Qaysi o'lcham siz uchun yaxshi, kichikmi yoki katta?
{r:Pay attention to the size.} - O'lchamiga e'tibor ber.
{r:The car size is good.} - Mashina yaxshi o'lchamda.

text: {r:Type}[taɪp] - tur, tip. Bir xil so'zlar!
examples: {r:What type of robbery was it?} - Qanday turdagi o'g'irlik edi u?
{r:Which type of apple do you want?} - Qaysi turdagi olmani xohlaysiz?
{r:How many types of animals are there?} - Hayvonlarning qancha turlari bor?
{r:There are different types of haters.} - Negativchilarning har xil turi bor.

text: {r:Without}[wɪˈðaʊt] - ...siz, bilan emas. O'tgan darslarning birida with(bilan) so'zini o'rgangan edik. Agar unga out qo'shimchasini qo'shsak, with(bilan) ning teskarisi yasaladi.
examples: {r:A liar cannot speak without lies.} - Yolg'onchi yolg'onlarsiz gapira olmaydi.
{r:Who can live without water?} - Suvsiz kim yashay oladi?
{r:How did you do that without help?} - Siz buni yordamsiz qanday qildingiz?
{r:She left without a word.} - U bir so'z demasdan ketdi.

text: {r:Sweater}[ˈswetər] - sviter.
examples: {r:What color is your sweater?} - Sviteringiz qanday rangda?
{r:Which sweater do you like more, blue or red?} - Qaysi sviter sizga ko'proq yoqadi, ko'kmi yoki qizilmi?
{r:How warm is this sweater?} - Bu sviter qanchalik iliq?
{r:I wore this sweater once.} - Men bu sviterni bir marta kiyganman.

text: {r:Most}[moʊst] – eng, eng ko'p, ko'pchilik. Oxirgi hisob-kitoblar shuni ko’rsatyaptiki, {h:eng ko'p} sement {p:most} qurishga ketyapti.
examples: {r:What is the most important thing?} - Eng muhim narsa nima?
{r:Which house is the most beautiful?} - Eng chiroyli uy qaysi?
{r:Most of my money is being spent on children.} - Pullarimning eng ko'p qismi bolalarga sarflanyapti.
{r:Most people like music.} - Ko'pchilik musiqani yaxshi ko'radi.

text: {r:High}[haɪ] – baland. Toshkentdagi Amir Temur {p:hay}kali nafaqat chiroyli, balki juda {h:baland}.
examples: {r:What is behind this high mountain?} - Bu baland tog'ning orqasida nima bor?
{r:Which building is higher, this one or that one?} - Qaysi bino balandroq, bu biri yoki u biri?
{r:How high is the wall?} - Devor qanchalik baland?
{r:The bird is high in the sky.} - Qush osmonda balandda.

text: {r:Drawing}[ˈdrɔːɪŋ] - chizma, kartinka, rasm. Draw(chizmoq) so'zidan yasalgan.
examples: {r:What kind of drawing is this?} - Bu qanday turdagi rasm?
{r:Did your father pay attention to your drawings?} - Dadangiz chizmalaringizga e'tibor berganmi?
{r:How good is your drawing?} - Rasmingiz qanchalik yaxshi?
{r:This is a drawing of a tasty potato.} - Bu shirin kartoshka kartinasi.

text: {r:Attentive}[əˈtentɪv] - e'tiborli. Attention(e'tibor) so'zidan yasalgan.
examples: {r:What made him attentive?} - Uni nima e'tiborli qildi?
{r:Who was more attentive, he or she?} - Kim ko'proq e'tiborli edi, umi yoki bumi?
{r:How attentive were the students?} - Talabalar qanchalik e'tiborli edilar?
{r:Be attentive to your teacher.} - O'qituvchingizga e'tiborli bo'ling.

text: {r:Architecture}[ˈɑːrkɪtektʃər] - arxitektura.
examples: {r:What kind of architecture is common here?} - Bu yerda qanday turdagi arxitektura keng tarqalgan?
{r:Which architecture is older, this or that?} - Qaysi arxitektura eskiroq, bu yoki u?
{r:How old is this architecture?} - Bu arxitektura qancha yoshda?
{r:I think the architecture of this city is boring.} - Mening o'ylashimcha bu shahar arxitekturasi zerikarli.

text: {r:Opponent}[əˈpoʊnənt] – raqib, muxolif. Bilayn kompaniyasi yozgi aksiyasiga OPPO telefoni bermoqchi. Aksiyaning final soniga ikki kishi yetib keldi va g’olibni aniqlash qiyin bo’lmoqda. Bu ikki raqib OPPO telefonini yutish uchun mushtlashib ham ketishdi. Oxirida telefon bu ikki {p:ABONENT} {h:raqib}ning hech biriga berilmadi.
examples: {r:Who is your strongest opponent?} - Sizning eng kuchli raqibingiz kim?
{r:What did the opponent do?} - Raqib nima qildi?
{r:Which opponent did you play against?} - Qaysi raqibga qarshi o'ynadingiz?
{r:How strong is your opponent?} - Raqibingiz qanchalik kuchli?

text: {r:Complain}[kəmˈpleɪn] – shikoyat qilmoq. Tasavvur qiling, siz kompot sotasiz va bir kuni Eynshteyn kelib kompotingizdan xarid qildi. Ertasi kuni {p:KOMP}otdan {p:EYN}shteyn do’koningizga kelib {h:shikoyat} qildi. Uning aytishicha, kompotdan pashsha chiqqanmish.
examples: {r:What did they complain about?} - Ular nima haqida shikoyat qilishdi?
{r:Normally our waiters don't complain.} - Odatda bizning ofitsiantlarimiz shikoyat qilishmaydi
{r:How often do you complain?} - Siz qanchalik tez-tez shikoyat qilasiz?
{r:Please do not complain!} - Iltimos, shikoyat qilmang!

text:
{r:Argue}[ˈɑːrɡjuː] – bahslashmoq.
Men: Aroq gunoh
Alkash amaki: Yo’q unday emas
