text: {r:Possession}[pəˈzɛʃən] – egalik qilish; narsalar, buyumlar. Possess(egalik qilmoq) so'zidan yasalgan.
examples: {r:Do you have possession of the keys? Yes, I do.} - Kalitlar sizning egaligingizdami? Ha, menda.
{r:He can't have possession of the car anymore. Neither can we.} - U mashinaga endi egalik qilmaydi. Biz ham.
{r:Do you think he has possession of the documents? I hope so.} - U hujjatlarga egalik qiladi deb o'ylaysizmi? Umid qilamanki.
{r:The documents are not in his possession, are they?} - Hujjatlar unda emas, shunday emasmi?

text: {r:Mom}[mɒm] – ona, oyi (so'zlashuv tilida).
examples: {r:My mom always makes delicious food.} - Oyim har doim mazali taomlar tayyorlaydi.
{r:She called her mom to say hello.} - U onasiga salomlashish uchun qo‘ng‘iroq qildi.
{r:His mom helped him with homework.} - Uning onasi uy vazifasida yordam berdi.
{r:I gave my mom a hug before school.} - Maktabga ketishdan oldin onamni quchoqladim.

text: {r:Dad}[dæd] – dada, ota  (so'zlashuv tilida).
examples: {r:My dad taught me how to ride a bike.} - Dadam menga velosiped haydashni o‘rgatgan.
{r:She gave her dad a handmade gift.} - U dadasiga qo‘lbola sovg‘a berdi.
{r:His dad works at a hospital.} - Uning otasi kasalxonada ishlaydi.
{r:I went fishing with my dad last weekend.} - O‘tgan dam olish kunlari dadam bilan baliq oviga bordim.

text: {r:Simultaneously}[ˌsaɪməlˈteɪniəsli] – bir vaqtning o'zida, bir paytda. Simultaneous(bir vaqtning o'zida) so'zining ravish shakli.
examples: {r:They can work simultaneously} - Ular bir vaqtning o'zida ishlay olishadi.
{r:Do you handle multiple tasks simultaneously?} - Bir nechta vazifalarni bir vaqtda bajara olasizmi?
{r:The events have occurred simultaneously} - Voqealar bir vaqtda sodir bo'ldi.
{r:We are managing multiple projects simultaneously} - Biz bir nechta loyihalarni bir vaqtda boshqarmoqdamiz.
{r:It's impossible to negotiate simultaneously with multiple parties without confusion.} - Bir vaqtning o'zida bir nechta tomonlar bilan chalkashliklarsiz muzokara qilish ilojsiz.

text: {r:Grateful}[ˈɡreɪtfəl] – minnatdor.
examples: {r:She is grateful for your help} - U sizning yordamingiz uchun minnatdor.
{r:I'm grateful that you expressed your objection before it was too late to change the plan.} - Rejani o'zgartirishga kechikmasdan oldin o'z e'tirozingizni bildirganingiz uchun minnatdorman.
{r:They have expressed their gratitude} - Ular minnatdorchiliklarini bildirishdi.
{r:We are grateful for the opportunity} - Biz imkoniyat uchun minnatdormiz.

text: {r:Genuine}[ˈdʒɛnjuɪn] – asl, toza; haqqoniy, sofdil. Jentrangizni chang bosib ketibdiku. {p:JEN}trani {p:YUVIN}tiring {h:asl} suv Nestlega shunda salondan chiqqan yangi Jentradek bo'lib qoladi.
examples: {r:His smile is genuine} - Uning tabassumi chin edi.
{r:Does the product seem genuine?} - Mahsulot asl ko'rinadimi?
{r:The apology has been genuine} - Uzr so'rash chin edi.
{r:The company faced a genuine challenge due to the new trade restrictions.} - Kompaniya yangi savdo cheklovlari tufayli chinakam qiyinchiliklarga duch keldi.
{r:Her paintings have a genuine and distinct style that is easily recognizable.} - Uning rasmlari osonlik bilan tanib olinadigan haqiqiy va o'ziga xos uslubga ega.

text: {r:Silence}[ˈsaɪləns] – jimlik, sukunat. Tasavvur qiling siz jinoyatga va mafialarga to’la davlatning saylovida qatnashyapsiz. Saylovdagi shioringiz “{p:SAYLANS}am hamma yerda {h:sukunat} bo’ladi, mafiyalarni yo’q qilaman” bo’lyapti.
examples: {r:The room was completely silent, filled with a deep silence.} - Xona butunlay jim edi, chuqur sukunat bilan to'la.
{r:The library demands complete silence} - Kutubxona to'liq sukunat talab qiladi.
{r:We sat in comfortable silence watching the sunset} - Biz qulay sukunatda quyosh botishini tomosha qildik.
{r:His sudden silence made me suspicious} - Uning to'satdan jim bo‘lishi meni shubhalantirdi.
{r:The true leader must possess the wisdom to know when to speak and when to remain in silence.} - Haqiqiy lider qachon gapirishni va qachon sukut saqlashni biladigan donolikka ega bo'lishi kerak.

text: {r:Pretend}[prɪˈtɛnd] – mug’ombirlik qilmoq, o’zini biror kuyga solmoq. “Vir va Zara” filmidagi roli bilan shuhrat qozongan Priti Zinta 2025 yil yanvarida 50 yoshni qarshilaydi. Raqamlar kichik bo’lmasa ham {p:PRITI END}i dieta orqali qomatini saqlab o’zini {h:yosh ko’rsatishga harakat qilmoqda}.
examples: {r:Kids love to pretend they’re superheroes} - Bolalar o‘zlarini superqahramondek ko'rsatishni yaxshi ko‘radi.
{r:He pretended not to see me at the party} - U bazmda meni ko‘rmagandek bo‘ldi.
{r:Don’t pretend that you forgot – I reminded you twice} - Unutdim deb mug'ombirlik qilma – men sizga ikki marta eslatdim!
{r:She tried to pretend she wasn't upset when they had to postpone their vacation plans.} - U ta'til rejalarini qoldirishga majbur bo'lishganida, xafa emasligini ko'rsatishga harakat qildi.
{r:She would pretend to swallow the medicine, but then secretly spit it out.} - U dori ichganini ko'rsatar edi, ammo keyin yashirincha tupurib tashlardi.

text: {r:Dare}[dɛər] – jurat qilmoq, botinmoq; da'vat qilmoq, chaqirmoq. Yoshligimdan zo’r doyrachi bo’lganman. Lekin bitta barmog’imdan ayrilganimdan so’ng {p:DOYR}a chalishga {h:botinmay} qoldim. Lekin do’stlarim doyrachilik faoliyatimni tiklashga da'vat qilishadi.
examples: {r:She dared to ask for a raise – and got it} - U maosh oshirishni so‘rashga jur'at qildi – va uni oldi.
{r:Few climbers dare to attempt that dangerous peak} - Juda kam alpinistlar o‘sha xavfli cho‘qqiga chiqishga jur'at qiladilar.
{r:He dared his brother to eat the spicy pepper} - U akasini achchiq qalampir yeyishga undadi.
{r:How dare you say that about my kids?} - Bolalarim haqida bunday deyishga qanday hadding sig'di?
{r:How dare he shout at me?} - Uni menga baqirishga qanday haddi sig'di?

text: {r:Mad}[mæd] – tentak, jinni;jahli chiqish. 2016 – yilgi Olimpiada O’yinlari erkin kurash bo’yicha bronza bahslarida O’zbekistonlik Ixtiyor Navrozov va mana bu mongol kurashishdi. Oxirgi sekundda jarima bali evaziga yutqazib qo’ygan mongol kurashchisi {p:MED}alni yutqazib qo’yganiga {h:jinni} bo’lib qolay dedi.
examples: {r:My mom was mad because I came home so late} - Onam juda kech uyga kelganimdan jahli chiqdi.
{r:Eventually you will be mad at me} - Oxir-oqibat mendan jahlingiz chiqishi muqarrar.
{r:My boss is a mad guy} - Mening boshlig'im tentak yigit.
{r:The mad man has tried to steal my luggage} - Tentak kishi mening yukimni o'g'irlashga harakat qildi.

text: {r:Effort}[ˈɛfərt] – harakat, urinish. Bobomning 50 yildan beri hech kim yashamayotgan uyiga bordik. Derazalari kir bo’lib ketibdi, ayniqsa bir fortchkasi juda isqirt bo'lib ketibdi. {p:If}los {p:fort}chkani olib tashlash uchun {h:harakat} qilishimiz kerak, lekin hech kim urinib ko'rmayapti.
examples: {r:With some effort, actually I lifted the heavy box} - Biroz harakat bilan men aslida og‘ir qutini ko‘tardim.
{r:She put real effort into making the gift special} - U sovg‘ani o‘ziga xos qilish uchun chinakam harakat qildi.
{r:The project required a team effort to finish on time} - Loyiha o‘z vaqtida tugashi uchun jamoaviy harakat talab qilindi.
{r:I made every possible effort to reach here on time} - Men bu yerga o'z vaqtida yetib kelish uchun barcha harakatni qildim.
{r:The success of the mission depends solely on your effort} - Missiyaning muvaffaqiyati faqat sizning sa'y-harakatingizga bog'liq.

text: {r:Press}[prɛs] – presslamoq, g'ijimlamoq, ezmoq, bosmoq.
examples: {r:Press the button to start the machine} - Mashinani ishga tushirish uchun tugmani bosing.
{r:My dad pressed his hand against the window} - Dadam qo‘lini derazaga bosdi.
{r:Seeds are pressed to produce oil} - Yog' ishlab chiqarish uchun urug'lar eziladi.
{r:Either press your clothes or leave some of them here} - Kiyimlaringni yoki press qilib sol yoki ba'zilarini shu yerda qoldir.

text: {r:Tighten}[ˈtaɪtən] – siqmoq, qismoq, mustahkamlamoq. Tight(zich, tarrang) so'zidan yasalgan.
examples: {r:Tighten the lid so the juice doesn’t spill} - Sharbat to‘kilmasligi uchun qopqog‘ini mahkamlang.
{r:The coach told us to tighten our defense} - Murabbiy bizga himoyani kuchaytirishni aytdi.
{r:Rules are being tightened because of some weird people.} - Ba'zi bir g'alati odamlar tufayli qoidalar qattiqlashtirilyapti.
{r:New laws will tighten security at airports} - Yangi qonunlar aeroportlardagi xavfsizlikni kuchaytiradi.

text: {r:Mean}[miːn] – yomon, qo'pol; xasis, qizg'anchiq. Mean(ma'no bildirmoq) so'zining omonimi.
examples: {r:He was mean to his classmates for no reason} - U sinfdoshlariga hech qanday sababga ko'ra yomon munosabatda bo'ldi.
{r:She made a mean comment about his work} - U uning ishi haqida yomon fikr bildirdi.
{r:They always act mean when they lose a game} - Ular o'yinni yutqazganlarida har doim qo'pol munosabatda bo'lishadi.
{r:The boss seemed mean when he rejected our proposal} - Rahbar bizning taklifimizni rad etganida juda qattiqqo'l ko'rindi.

text: {r:Loose}[luːs] – bo’sh, shalviragan. Mana bu juda ajoyib lupa. Bu lupa bilan lyuboy narsani ko’rsangiz o’sha predmet shalvirab qoladi. Masalan bu {p:LU}pada {p:UZ}ukni kattalashtirib tomosha qildim va uzuk yumshoq bo’lib {h:shalvirab} qoldi.
examples: {r:My tooth feels loose – it might fall out soon} - Mening tishim bo'sh tuyulmoqda – tez orada tushib ketishi mumkin.
{r:Wear loose clothing for yoga class} - Yoga mashg‘ulotlari uchun keng kiyim kiying.
{r:He indicated a loose shelf in the library that needed fixing.} – U kutubxonadagi ta’mirlash kerak bo‘lgan shalviragan javonni ko‘rsatdi.
{r:She sat in the shade, wearing loose clothes, preferably light ones.} – U soya ostida, keng kiyimlarda, iloji boricha yengil kiyimlarda o‘tirdi.

text: {r:Dustbin}[ˈdʌstbɪn] – axlat qutisi. Dust(chang) va bin(quti) so'zlaridan yasalgan.
examples: {r:Throw the empty box in the dustbin} - Bo'sh qutini axlat qutisiga tashlang.
{r:The dustbin needs to be emptied – it’s full} - Axlat qutisini bo'shatish kerak – u to'lgan.
{r:His assumption was correct when he found the dustbin missing in the workplace.} – Ish joyida axlat qutisi yo‘qligini ko‘rganida, uning taxmini to‘g‘ri bo‘lib chiqdi.
{r:The green dustbin contains harmful chemicals} - Yashil axlat qutisida zararli ximikatlar saqlanadi.

text: {r:Endurance}[ɪnˈdjʊərəns] – chidam, toqat, bardosh. Endure(chidamoq) so'zidan yasalgan.
examples: {r:Marathon runners need incredible endurance} - Marafon yuguruvchilari aql bovar qilmas sabr-toqatga ega bo'lishlari kerak.
{r:The hike tested our physical endurance} - Sayr bizning jismoniy chidamliligimizni sinovdan o'tkazdi.
{r:His speech showed remarkable mental endurance} - Uning nutqi ajoyib aqliy bardoshlilikni ko'rsatdi.
{r:This battery has a long endurance – it lasts 48 hours} - Ushbu batareya uzoq chidamlilikka ega – 48 soat xizmat qiladi.

text: {r:Decline}[dɪˈklaɪn] – pasaymoq, tushmoq. Decline(rad etmoq) ning boshqa ma'nosini 104 - darsda o'rgangan edik. Bu so'zning omonimini quyidagi misollar orqali o'rganing.
examples: {r:The company’s profits declined last quarter} - Kompaniyaning daromadi o'tgan chorakda pasaydi.
{r:Apparently his health declined due to poor nutrition} - Ko'rinishidan uning salomatligi noto'g'ri ovqatlanish sababli yomonlashdi.
{r:They noticed a decline in customer demand} - Ular mijoz talabining pasayishini payqashdi.
{r:The population of the species has declined over the years} - Ushbu turning populyatsiyasi yillar davomida kamaydi.
{r:Although the economy declines, the small businesses somehow managed to stay profitable.} - Iqtisodiy pasayishga qaramay, kichik bizneslar qandaydir tarzda daromadliligini yo'qotmadi.

text: {r:Distant}[ˈdɪstənt] – olis, uzoq. Maktabda bugun diktant yozdik erkin mavzuda. Men {h:olis} Rossiyada ishlab yurgan dadam haqida {p:DIKTANT} yozdim.
examples: {r:The mountains appeared considerably distant in the fog} - Tog'lar tuman ichida anchagina olis ko'rinar edi.
{r:She kept a distant relationship with her cousins} - U amakivachchalari bilan uzoq munosabatda bo'ldi.
{r:We heard distant thunder before the storm} - Bo'ron oldidan uzoqdan momaqaldiroq eshitildi.
{r:His voice sounded distant on the phone} - Uning ovozi telefonda uzoqdan eshitilgandek edi.

text: {r:Conduct}[ˈkɒndʌkt] – o'tkazmoq. Bugun biz Toshkentdagi barcha {p:KONDUKT}orlar o'rtasida yig'ilish {h:o'tkazyapmiz}!
examples: {r:The professor will conduct an experiment tomorrow} - Professor ertaga tajriba o'tkazadi.
{r:Police conducted a search of the building} - Politsiya binoni tintuv qildi.
{r:We need to conduct an internal investigation to determine the source of this harmful rumor.} - Bu zararli mish-mishning manbasini aniqlash uchun ichki tekshiruv o'tkazishimiz kerak.
{r:We are not going to conduct a meeting tomorrow} - Ertaga majlis o'tkazmoqchi emasmiz.

text: {r:Leak}[liːk] – sizib chiqmoq, suvi oqmoq, tommoq. Asosan ikki xil kontekstda ishlatiladi. Birinchisi quvur, tom yoki nimadirda yoriqlar paydo bo'lishi natijasida suv oqishida. Ikkinchisi maxfiy ma'lumotlar omma uchun sizdirilganda. Tasavvur qiling katta {p:LIK}opchadan {h:suv oqyapti.} Hech qayeri sinmagan va oxirida sezdingizki likopchaning o'rtasida kichkina teshigi bor ekan.
examples: {r:The roof leaks when it rains} - Yomg'ir yog'ganda tomdan suv o'tadi.
{r:Someone leaked confidential documents eventually} - Kimdir maxfiy hujjatlarni oxir-oqibat sizdirib yuborgan.
{r:News of the scandal leaked to the press eventually} - Skandal haqidagi xabarlar oxir-oqibat matbuotga sizib chiqdi.
{r:The water pipe has been leaking for days} - Suv quvuri bir necha kundan beri sizib turibdi.

text: {r:Bark}[bɑːrk] – akillamoq, hurmoq, vovullamoq. Mening itim chinor {p:BARK}larini yeb qo'yganidan beri {h:akillash} qobiliyatini yo'qotdi.
examples: {r:The dog would like to bark at the stranger, but it's trained not to.} - It begona odamga vovullashni xohlardi, lekin u bunga o'rgatilmagan.
{r:She wouldn't mind hearing a dog barking loudly at night if it meant safety.} - Agar bu xavfsizlikni anglatsa, u kechqurun itning baland ovozda vovullashini eshitishga qarshi emas edi.
{r:The puppy would love to bark properly one day.} - Kuchuk bir kun kelib to'g'ri vovullashni juda xohlardi.
{r:Why are you barking at me?} - Nega menga akillayapsan?

text: {r:Fork}[fɔːrk] – sanchqi, vilka. Tasavvur qiling {h:vilka} shaklidagi {p:FORD} mashinasi chiqibdi.
examples: {r:He would like to use a fork for the first time.} - U birinchi marta sanchqidan foydalanishni xohlardi.
{r:I would love to buy the most expensive fork.} - Men eng qimmat sanchqini sotib olishni xohlardim.
{r:She would prefer to buy new forks for the party.} - U ziyofat uchun yangi sanchqilar sotib olishni afzal ko'rardi.
{r:Would you mind showing me how to hold a fork correctly?} - Sanchqini to'g'ri ushlashni ko'rsatib bera olmaysizmi?
{r:He has weird possession of forks, golden and wooden forks, for example.} - Uning egaligida g'alati sanchqilar bor, masalan tilladan va yog'ochdan qilinganlari.

text: {r:Suspend}[səˈspɛnd] – bir muncha vaqtga to’xtatib qo’ymoq, to’xtatib turmoq. Bugun maktabga kecha olgan chiroyli penalimni olib bordim. Lekin penalim qandaydir kimyoviy yelimdan qilingan ekan hammayoq sasib ketdi. {p:SAS}iq {p:PEN}al tufayli darsimiz biroz vaqtga {h:to’xtatildi}.
examples: {r:Shahnoza suspended her studies.} - Shahnoza o'qishini to'xtatdi.
{r:They would prefer to suspend the project temporarily rather than cancel it.} - Ular loyihani bekor qilishdan ko'ra vaqtincha to'xtatishni afzal ko'rishadi.
{r:The company wouldn't mind suspending the employee if there was proof.} - Agar dalil bo'lsa, kompaniya ishchini to'xtatishga(bo'shatishga) qarshi emas edi.
{r:A technical issue might disturb the broadcast and suspend the program.} - Texnik muammo eshittirishni buzishi va dasturni to'xtatib qo'yishi mumkin.

text: {r:Rebel}[ˈrɛbəl] – isyonchi, qo'zg'olonchi; isyon qilmoq. Konstaning aytishicha uning {p:REPL}ari jamiyatdagi mavjud muammolarga {h:isyon} ekan.(Namuna uchun yozildi. Amalda Konsta bu gaplarni aytmagan.)
examples: {r:The soldiers would hate to rebel against their leader.} - Askarlar o'z lideriga qarshi isyon qilishni yomon ko'rar edi.
{r:Teenagers would sometimes prefer to rebel against strict rules.} - O'smirlar ba'zan qattiq qoidalarga qarshi chiqishni afzal ko'rishadi.
{r:He wouldn't like to rebel again after the last time.} - U oxirgi martadan keyin yana isyon qilishni xohlamasdi.
{r:The workers would certainly rebel if their wages were reduced.} - Ishchilar ish haqi qisqartirilsa, albatta isyon qilishar edi.

text: {r:Frozen}[ˈfroʊzən] – muzlagan, muzlatilgan. Freeze(muzlamoq) so'zidan yasalgan.
examples: {r:I purchase specifically frozen meat because they are affordable.} - Men aynan muzlagan go'sht sotib olaman chunki ular arzonroq.
{r:She wouldn't mind taking the frozen meat out if someone reminded her.} - Agar kimdir eslatganida, u muzlagan go'shtni olib qo'yishga qarshi emas edi.
{r:The child would hate to eat the frozen yogurt because it's too cold.} - Bola muzlagan yogurtni yeyishni yomon ko'rardi, chunki u juda sovuq.
{r:We would prefer not to walk on the frozen river as it might be dangerous.} - Biz muzlagan daryo ustida yurmaslikni afzal ko'ramiz, chunki bu xavfli bo'lishi mumkin.

text: {r:Delicate}[ˈdɛlɪkət] – nozik, mo’rt; nafis, go’zal. Agar {p:DELIKAT}es yesangiz birdaniga {h:nozik}, ozg’in odamga aylanib qolasiz.
examples: {r:You would prefer to handle the delicate glass with care.} - Siz nozik stakanni ehtiyotkorlik bilan ushlashni afzal ko'rardingiz.
{r:Handling the delicate situation was his primary duty, requiring great care.} - Nozik vaziyatni boshqarish uning asosiy vazifasi bo'lib, katta e'tibor talab qilardi.
{r:The situation was deemed too delicate to discuss publicly.} - Vaziyat ommaviy muhokama qilish uchun juda nozik deb topildi.
{r:The artist wouldn't mind painting delicate details all day.} - Rassom butun kun nozik tafsilotlarni chizishga qarshi emas edi.

{r:Handling cases of financial fraud requires a delicate balance of legal and investigative skills.} - Moliyaviy firibgarlik holatlarini ko'rib chiqish huquqiy va tergov ko'nikmalarining nozik muvozanatini talab qiladi.

text: {r:Spouse}[spaʊs] – turmush o’rtoq, er yoki xotin. Onaxonlarning aytishicha qizlar o’zlarini {p:SIPO QIZ} dek tutsalar tezda erga tegib baxti ochilib ketar ekan. Yomon onalar esa “Bolam {r:SIPO QIZ} bo'lib turmushga chiqib ol keyin boshiga chiqib olasan {h:turmush o'rtog'ingni}” der ekan.
examples: {r:He would like to support his spouse in all her efforts.} - U turmush o'rtog'ini barcha ishlarida qo'llab-quvvatlashni xohlardi.
{r:They would love to invite their spouses to the party if they are free.} - Ular bo'sh bo'lishsa, turmush o'rtoqlarini ziyofatga taklif qilishni juda xohlardi.
{r:She would hate to argue with her spouse in public.} - U turmush o'rtog'i bilan omma oldida bahslashishni yomon ko'rardi.
{r:The company would prefer to relocate employees and their spouses together.} - Kompaniya xodimlar va ularning turmush o'rtoqlarini birga ko'chirishni afzal ko'radi.
{r:My spouse possesses leadership qualities indeed.} - Mening turmush o'rtog'im chindan liderlik sifatlariga ega.

text: {r:Forehead}[ˈfɒrɪd] – peshona. Bu vaziyatda {p:Farhod} ismli {h:peshonasi} katta odamni tasavvur qilishingiz mumkin.
examples: {r:We are unable to see our forehead.} - Biz peshonamizni ko'rolmaymiz.
{r:She would like to apply cream on her forehead before bed.} - U yotishdan oldin peshanasiga krem surtishni xohlardi.
{r:Sweat dripped from his forehead as he continued to chase the runaway dog.} - U qochgan itni quvishda davom etar ekan, peshonasidan ter tomchilardi.
{r:His forehead showed the border of his cap’s shadow.} – Uning peshonasida kepkasining soyasi chegarasi ko‘rindi.

text: {r:Hook}[hʊk] – ilmoq, ilgak; ilib qo’ymoq, ilinib qolmoq. {p:Huk}mdor Usmon jang payti chap qo’l panjasidan ayrilgan va uning o’rniga {h:ilmoq} taqib olgan. Agar hukmdor Usmon seriali sizga tanish bo’lmasa Piter Pen multfilmidagi kapitan HUKni eslasangiz kerak. Kapitan {p:HUK} bekorga bu ismga ega emas chunki uning chap qo’lida {h:ilmog’i} bor.
examples: {r:My dad would like to hang the coat on the hook.} - Dadam paltoni ilmoqqa osishni xohlardi.
{r:The fisherman would hate to forget his hooks for the trip.} - Baliqchi sayohat uchun ilmoqlarini unutishni yomon ko'rardi.
{r:She would prefer to buy new hooks for the kitchen if they match the decor.} - Agar ular dekorga mos kelsa, u oshxona uchun yangi ilmoqlar sotib olishni afzal ko'rardi.
{r:Would you mind showing me how to tie the hook properly?} - Ilmoqni to'g'ri bog'lashni ko'rsatib bera olmaysizmi?
{r:He used a long hook to retrieve the keys that had accidentally fallen into the rubbish dump.} - U tasodifan axlatxona joyiga tushib ketgan kalitlarni qaytarish uchun uzun ilgakdan foydalangan.

text: {r:Click}[klɪk] – qaysidir tugmani bosmoq, telefon yoki kompyuter ekranida qaysidir predmetni bosish orqali tanlash. Agar sizga katta keshbeklar kerak bo’lsa shunchaki {p:KLIK} ilovasini {h:bosing} va katta keshbeklarga ega bo’ling.
examples: {r:She would love to click the mouse quickly to finish the task.} - U vazifani tugatish uchun sichqonchani tez bosishni juda xohlardi.
{r:The camera would click repeatedly if it had a full battery.} - Agar batareyasi to'la bo'lsa, kamera qayta-qayta rasmga olardi.
{r:She clicked her pen while waiting on the shaded sidewalk.} – U soyali trotuarda kutayotib, ruchkasini bosib turdi.
{r:The child wouldn't mind clicking the button all day if he was allowed.} - Agar ruxsat berilsa, bola butun kun tugmachani bosishga qarshi emas edi.

text: {r:Charge}[tʃɑːrdʒ] – ma'suliyat. to be in charge - nimagadir ma'sul bo'lmoq
examples: {r:She would like to be in charge of organizing the event.} - U tadbirni tashkil etish uchun javobgar bo'lishni xohlardi.
{r:He would love to be put in charge of the new project.} - U yangi loyiha uchun javobgar qilib tayinlanishni juda xohlardi.
{r:They would prefer to be in charge of managing the budget themselves.} - Ular byudjetni o'zlari boshqarishni afzal ko'rishadi.
{r:The teacher would hate not to be in charge of the classroom's discipline.} - O'qituvchi sinf intizomiga javobgar bo'lmaslikni yomon ko'rardi.

text: {r:Dedicate}[ˈdɛdɪkeɪt] – bag‘ishlamoq, atamoq. Titanik filmi bilan dunyoga mashhur bo’lgan Keyt Uinsli ortiq kino sanoatini yoqtirmasligini aytdi. “Men 30 yil kinolarda rol o’ynab qadr topmadim. Kinodan ketaman va parklarda shar ishirib sotmoqchiman. Qolgan faoliyatimni sharchilikka {h:bag’ishlamoqchiman}” {p:DEDI KEYT}.
examples: {r:She would like to dedicate her life to helping others.} - U o'z hayotini boshqalarga yordam berishga bag'ishlashni xohlardi.
{r:He would love to dedicate a song to his girlfriend.} - U qiz do'stiga qo'shiq bag'ishlashni juda xohlardi.
{r:They would hate to dedicate all their time to one project.} - Ular butun vaqtlarini bitta loyihaga bag'ishlashni yomon ko'rishardi.
{r:Would you mind dedicating a few hours to the charity event?} - Hayriya tadbiriga bir necha soatingizni bag'ishlashga qarshi emasmisiz?

text: {r:Charm}[tʃɑːrm] – joziba, maftunkorlik, tarovat; maftun etmoq. Agar siz {p:charm} palto kiysangiz umuman boshqa insonga aylanasiz va yanada {h:maftunkor} ko’rinasiz.
examples: {r:He would love to charm the entire audience with his speech.} - U o'z nutqi bilan butun auditoriyani maftun etishni juda xohlardi.
{r:I would hate to use my charm to lie to people.} - Men odamlarni aldash uchun o'z jozibamdan foydalanishni yomon ko'raman.
{r:His natural charm brought significant positive feedback at the job interview.} – Uning tabiiy jozibasi ish suhbatida sezilarli ijobiy fikr-mulohazalarni keltirdi.
{r:Julia used her charm and intelligence, but Jack remained doubtful.} – Julia o‘zining jozibasi va aqlidan foydalandi, lekin Jekda baribir shubha bor edi.

text: {r:Chop}[tʃɒp] – to'g'ramoq, chopmoq. Ha tasodif! Ingliz tilida ham 'chop' so'zi 'chopmoq', 'to'g'ramoq' degani.
examples: {r:Would you mind chopping some firewood for the fire?} - Olov uchun bir oz o'tin chopib bera olmaysizmi?
{r:He would prefer to chop vegetables himself for the salad.} - U salat uchun sabzavotlarni o'zi to'g'rashni afzal ko'radi.
{r:She would like to chop some onions for the soup.} - U sho'rva uchun bir oz piyoz to'g'rashni xohlardi.
{r:The chef would hate to chop the ingredients too small.} - Oshpaz masalliqlarni juda mayda to'g'rashni yomon ko'radi.

text: {r:Excellent}[ˈeksələnt] – a'lo, ajoyib, zo'r. Excel dasturini yaxshi koraman. Bu dasturda hisob-kitob qilish, jadval tuzish, diagrammalar chizish va eng {h:ajoyib}i {p:EXCEL}da {p:NOT}alar yozib musiqa bastalash mumkin. Xullas bu juda {h:zo’r} dastur.
examples: {r:We would love to achieve an excellent result in the project.} - Biz loyihada a'lo natijaga erishishni juda xohlardik.
{r:The teacher gave him an excellent mark for his sincere effort on the task.} - O‘qituvchi vazifadagi samimiy mehnati uchun unga a’lo baho berdi.
{r:He felt dumb after forgetting such an excellent idea.} – U shunday a’lo fikrni unutgach, o‘zini ahmoqdek his qildi.
{r:I would like to write an excellent essay for my class.} - Men sinfimiz uchun a'lo insho yozishni xohlardim.

text: {r:Hill}[hɪl] – tepalik, adir. Bu vaziyatda {p:HIL}ola ismli qizni {h:tepalik} ustida tasavvur qilishingiz mumkin.
examples: {r:I would like to climb the hill before sunset.} - Men quyosh botishidan oldin tepalikka chiqishni xohlardim.
{r:They would prefer to build their house on that small hill.} - Ular o'z uylarini o'sha kichik tepalikda qurishni afzal ko'rishadi.
{r:Would you mind walking up the hill to get a better view?} - Yaxshiroq ko'rish uchun tepalikka ko'tarilishga qarshi emasmisiz?
{r:After climbing the hill, we were both thirsty and hungry.} – Tepaga chiqqanimizdan keyin ikkalamiz ham chanqadik va och qoldik.

text:
{r:Exclude}[ɪkˈskluːd] – hisobga olmaslik, chiqarib tashlamoq, o’chirmoq. Include(o'z ichiga olmoq) ning teskarisi. 
Biz ekskavatorchilar jamiyati ishni vaqtida bajarmagani, mushtlashgani uchun jamiyatimizdan {p:EKS}kavatorchi {p:KLUD} Van Dammni {h:chiqarib tashlaymiz}.
examples: {r:We would hate to exclude anyone from our team activities.} - Biz jamoamiz faoliyatidan birortani chetlatishni yomon ko'ramiz.
{r:Would you mind not excluding the new member from the group?} - Yangi a'zoni guruhdan chetlatmaslikka qarshimasmisiz?
{r:My intention for the future is not to exclude anyone from our plans.} – Mening kelajak uchun niyatim – hech kimni rejalarimizdan chetda qoldirmaslik.
{r:I would love to exclude all negative thoughts from my mind.} - Men barcha salbiy fikrlarni miyamdan chiqarib tashlashni juda xohlardim.

text: {r:Gender}[ˈdʒendər] – jins, gender.
examples: {r:We would like to understand more about gender diversity in the workplace.} - Biz ish joyidagi gender xilma-xilligi haqida ko'proq bilishni xohlardik.
{r:She finally put her signature on the paper, showing her support for gender equalit.y} – U nihoyat qog‘ozga imzo qo‘ydi va jinslar tengligini qo‘llab-quvvatlashini ko‘rsatdi.
{r:The scientist’s comparison showed that opportunities were not always given freely to each gender.} - Olimning taqqoslashiga ko‘ra imkoniyatlar har doim har bir jinsga erkin berilmagan.
{r:The survey would like to collect data on gender and age.} - So'rovnoma jins va yosh bo'yicha ma'lumotlarni yig'ishni xohlardi.

text: {r:Guard}[ɡɑːrd] – qo'riqlamoq, himoya qilmoq; qo'riqchi, qorovul. Mening bobom uzoq yillar Angliya qirolichasi Yelizavetta ning {p:gard}erobini {h:qo’riqlagan.}
examples: {r:Would you mind guarding the entrance for a few minutes while I get my keys?} - Kalitlarimni olib kelgunimcha, kirish joyini bir necha daqiqa qo'riqlab tura olasizmi?
{r:I would prefer to guard my belongings myself.} - Men o'z narsalarimni o'zim qo'riqlashni afzal ko'raman.
{r:The guard wore a brown uniform and stood under the bright lights.} – Qo‘riqchi jigarrang forma kiyib yorqin chiroqlar ostida turardi.
{r:The guard spoke in a low voice, but he was eager to help.} – Qo‘riqchi past ovozda gapirdi, ammo yordam berishga shay edi.
{r:They would love to guard the city from all threats.} - Ular shaharni barcha tahdidlardan himoya qilishni juda xohlardilar.

text: {r:Altogether}[ˌɔːltəˈɡɛðər] – butunlay.
examples: {r:My neighbors prefer to avoid this situation altogether.} - Mening qo'shnilarim bu vaziyatdan butunlay tiyilishni afzal ko'rishadi.
{r:We prefer leaving altogether to staying and arguing.} - Biz qolib bahslashishdan ko'ra butunlay ketishni afzal ko‘ramiz.
{r:My aunt prefers a complete solution altogether to a partial one.} - Mening xolam qisman yechimdan ko'ra butunlay to'liq yechimni afzal ko'radi.
{r:My uncle prefers to stop altogether rather than continue with errors.} - Mening tog'am xatolar bilan davom etishdan ko'ra butunlay to'xtatishni afzal ko'radi.
{r:We'd rather forget about the problem altogether.} - Biz bu muammo haqida butunlay unutishni afzal ko‘ramiz.
{r:We cannot exclude anyone altogether from the group because of gender.} - Biz hech kimni jinsi tufayli guruhdan chiqarib tashlay olmaymiz.

text: {r:Carve}[kɑːrv] – o'yib yozmoq, naqsh solmoq. Siz mana bu taxtaga {p:KARV}on so'zini {h:o'yib yozyapsiz}. Mevalarni o'yib gul soluvchi san'at turki Karving ham inglizcha carve so'zidan olingan!
examples: {r:My niece prefers carving the statue from a single piece of wood.} - Mening jiyanim haykalni bir parcha yog'ochdan o'yib yasashni afzal ko'radi.
{r:He carved a bird out of wood.} - U yog‘ochdan qush rasmini o‘ydi.
{r:She carved her name into the tree.} - U daraxtga o‘z ismini o‘yib yozdi.
{r:Artists carve statues from stone.} - San’atkorlar toshdan haykallar o‘yib yasashadi.

text: {r:Needle}[ˈniːdl] – igna. Tasavvur qiling siz {p:NIDERL}andiyaga futbol ko'rgani bordingiz va borishingiz bilan orqangizga {h:igna} kirib ketdi.
examples: {r:My nephew prefers to use a needle for delicate work.} - Mening jiyanim nozik ishlar uchun ignadan foydalanishni afzal ko'radi.
{r:My spouse prefers using a needle to using a sewing machine.} - Mening turmush o'rtog'im tikuv mashinasidan ko'ra ignadan foydalanishni afzal ko'radi.
{r:We prefer a sewing needle to a knitting needle.} - Biz to'qish ignasidan ko'ra tikuv ignasini afzal ko'ramiz.
{r:My aunt prefers to sew by hand rather than use a machine.} - Mening xolam mashinadan foydalanishdan ko'ra qo'lda tikishni afzal ko'radi.
{r:My husband would rather not look for a needle in a haystack.} - Mening turmush o'rtog'im pichan uyumidan igna qidirishni afzal ko'rmaydi.
{r:We'd rather you didn't use a blunt needle.} - Biz sizning o'tmas igna ishlatmasligingizni afzal ko'rardik.

text: {r:Belly}[ˈbɛli] – qorin. Tasavvur qiling mashhur futbolchi {p:BELLI}ngem qorin {h:qo'yib} yuboribdi. Agar uni tanimasangiz o'zbekchadagi belli degan so'z ham mavjud.
examples: {r:The small kid prefers rubbing her belly after a big meal.} - Yosh bolacha ovqatdan keyin qornini ishqalashni afzal ko'radi.
{r:My neighbors prefer rubbing their bellies to exercising.} - Mening qo'shnilarim mashq qilishdan ko'ra qorinlarini ishqalashni afzal ko'rishadi.
{r:My husband prefers a full belly to an empty one.} - Mening turmush o'rtog'im bo'sh qorindan ko'ra to'q qorinni afzal ko'radi.
{r:My niece prefers to lie on her back rather than on her belly.} - Mening jiyanim qorni bilan yotishdan ko'ra orqasi bilan yotishni afzal ko'radi.
{r:They'd rather not talk about their bellies.} - Ular qorinlari haqida gapirishni afzal ko'rmaydi.
{r:She'd rather her child didn't eat too much, as his belly is full.} - U bolasining qorni to'q bo'lgani uchun, juda ko'p yemasligini xohlardi.

text: {r:Ankle}[ˈæŋkl] – to'piq. Tasavvur qiling siz {h:to'pig'ingizni} baquvvatlashtirib ishonchliroq qilish uchun {p:EN KAL}oriyali narsa bananni to'pig'ingizga yopishtirib oldingiz.
examples: {r:My uncle prefers to wrap his ankle when it is sore.} - Mening tog'amning to'pig'i og'riganda uni bog'lab qo'yishni afzal ko'radi.
{r:My neighbors prefer jogging to walking to strengthen their ankles.} - Mening qo'shnilarim to'piqlarini mustahkamlash uchun yurishdan ko'ra yugurishni afzal ko'rishadi.
{r:My aunt prefers an ankle brace to a simple bandage.} - Mening xolam oddiy bog'lamdan ko'ra to'piq bog'ichini afzal ko'radi.
{r:My husband prefers to rest his ankle rather than walk on it.} - Mening turmush o'rtog'im to'pig'ini ishlatib yurishdan ko'ra uni dam oldirishni afzal ko'radi.
{r:We'd rather wear comfortable shoes to protect our ankles.} - Biz to'piqlarimizni himoya qilish uchun qulay poyabzal kiyishni afzal ko'ramiz.
{r:Your mom rather you didn't run on your swollen ankle.} - Onangiz sizning shishgan to'pig'ingiz bilan yugurmasligingizni afzal ko'rardi.

text: {r:Mild}[maɪld] – yumshoq, mayin. Ovozingizni {h:yumshoq} qilmoqchimisiz unda "{p:MAYLID}a kimgadir yoqsa yoqmasa" she'rini yumshoq o'qing, qayta-qayta shunda do'rillagan ovozingiz yumshab ketadi.
examples: {r:My neighbors prefer eating mild food.} - Mening qo'shnilarim yumshoq taom yeyishni afzal ko'rishadi.
{r:My aunt prefers eating mild food to spicy dishes.} - Mening xolam achchiq taomlardan ko'ra yumshoq taomlarni yeyishni afzal ko'radi.
{r:My uncle prefers a mild cheese to a strong one.} - Mening tog'am achchiq pishloqdan ko'ra yumshoq pishloqni afzal ko'radi.
{r:They prefer to have mild weather rather than harsh cold.} - Ular qattiq sovuqdan ko'ra yumshoq ob-havoni afzal ko'rishadi.
{r:We'd rather have a mild winter this year.} - Biz bu yil yumshoq qish bo'lishini afzal ko'ramiz.
{r:He'd rather the weather stayed mild.} - U ob-havoning yumshoq bo'lib qolishini afzal ko'rardi.

text: {r:Cautious}[ˈkɔːʃəs] – ehtiyotkor. {p:KOVISHIZ} teshilib qolmasligi uchun {h:ehtiyotkor} bo'ling. Orasidan suv kirib shamollab qolishingiz mumkin.
examples: {r:My husband prefers to be cautious when driving in the rain.} - Mening turmush o'rtog'im yomg'irda mashina haydashda ehtiyotkor bo'lishni afzal ko'radi.
{r:My aunt prefers being cautious to taking unnecessary risks.} - Mening xolam keraksiz tavakkal qilishdan ko'ra ehtiyotkor bo'lishni afzal ko'radi.
{r:My neighbors prefer a cautious approach to a reckless one.} - Mening qo'shnilarim beparvo yondashuvdan ko'ra ehtiyotkor yondashuvni afzal ko'rishadi.
{r:My nephew prefers to walk cautiously rather than run.} - Mening jiyanim yugurishdan ko'ra ehtiyotkorlik bilan yurishni afzal ko'radi.
{r:She'd rather be cautious and safe than sorry.} - U afsuslanishdan ko'ra ehtiyotkor va xavfsiz bo'lishni afzal ko'radi.
{r:We'd rather he took a cautious approach to the problem.} - Biz uning muammoga ehtiyotkor yondashishini afzal ko'rardik.

text: {r:Doll}[dɒl] – qo'g'irchoq. Kecha bizning mahallamizda qattiq {p:DO'L} yog'ib tashqarida qolib ketgan {h:qo'g'irchog'}imni ezib tashlabdi.
examples: {r:My niece and nephew prefer playing with a doll.} - Mening jiyanlarim qo'g'irchoq bilan o'ynashni afzal ko'rishadi.
{r:My nephew prefers playing with dolls to playing with toy cars.} - Mening jiyanim o'yinchoq mashinalar bilan o'ynashdan ko'ra qo'g'irchoqlar bilan o'ynashni afzal ko'radi.
{r:My niece prefers a doll to soft toys.} - Mening jiyanim yumshoq o'yinchoqdan ko'ra qo'g'irchoqni afzal ko'radi.
{r:My husband prefers to buy a doll rather than a toy robot.} - Mening turmush o'rtog'im o'yinchoq robot sotib olishdan ko'ra qo'g'irchoq sotib olishni afzal ko'radi.
{r:She'd rather have a new doll for her birthday.} - U tug'ilgan kuniga yangi qo'g'irchoq olishni afzal ko'radi.
{r:We'd rather you didn't play with the old doll.} - Biz seni eski qo'g'irchoq bilan o'ynamasligingni afzal ko'rardik.

text: {r:Noon}[nuːn] – peshin, obed. Tasavvur qiling har kuni {h:obed} payti juda mam{p:NUN} bo'lib ketasiz va o'zingizdan-o'zingiz tirjayaverasiz.
examples: {r:My neighbors prefer having lunch at noon to having it later.} - Mening qo'shnilarim kechroq ovqatlanishdan ko'ra peshinda ovqatlanishni afzal ko'rishadi.
{r:My husband prefers noon to midnight.} - Mening turmush o'rtog'im yarim tundan ko'ra peshinni afzal ko'radi.
{r:They prefer to finish work by noon rather than in the evening.} - Ular ishni kechqurun tugatishdan ko'ra peshinga qadar tugatishni afzal ko'rishadi.
{r:We'd rather not work past noon.} - Biz peshindan keyin ishlamaslikni afzal ko'ramiz.
{r:She'd rather Jack arrived at noon.} - U Jekning peshinda yetib kelishini afzal ko'rardi.

text: {r:Precise}[prɪˈsaɪs] – aniq, tushunarli, tayin. Islom Karimov 1994 - yilgi intervyuda SSSRni qayta tiklamoqchi bo'lgan kuchlar haqida keskin gapirgan edi. {p:PRE}zident "{p:SAYUZ} qayta tiklanmaydi. Biz bunga yo'l qo'ymaymiz" deya {h:aniq-tiniq} aytgan.
examples: {r:My neighbors prefer being precise when giving instructions.} - Mening qo'shnilarim ko'rsatmalar berayotganda aniq bo'lishni afzal ko'rishadi.
{r:My uncle prefers being precise to being vague.} - Mening tog'am noaniq bo'lishdan ko'ra aniq bo'lishni afzal ko'radi.
{r:My aunt prefers precise measurements to approximate ones.} - Mening xolam taxminiy o'lchovlardan ko'ra aniq o'lchovlarni afzal ko'radi.
{r:They prefer to work with precise data rather than general information.} - Ular umumiy ma'lumotdan ko'ra aniq ma'lumotlar bilan ishlashni afzal ko'rishadi.
{r:We'd rather you gave a precise answer.} - Sizning aniq javob berishingizni xohlardik.
{r:She'd rather her husband worked with precise attention to detail.} - U erining tafsilotlarga aniq e'tibor berib ishlashini afzal ko'rardi.

text: {r:Anxiety}[æŋˈzaɪəti] – tashvish, xavotir, asabiylik. Bizning enagamiz sho'x bolalarimizga qarayverib asabiy bo'lib qolibdi. Unga yordam berish va stressini bartaraf etish uchun biz {p:EN}agaga {p:ZAYTU}n berishimiz kerak. {h:Asabiylik}da eng yaxshi foyda beradi.
examples: {r:My aunt prefers to manage her anxiety with meditation.} - Mening xolam tashvishini meditatsiya bilan boshqarishni afzal ko'radi.
{r:My neighbors prefer peace of mind to constant anxiety.} - Mening qo'shnilarim doimiy tashvishdan ko'ra ichki tinchlikni afzal ko'rishadi.
{r:My niece prefers to face her anxiety rather than avoid it.} - Mening jiyanim tashvishlaridan qochishdan ko'ra unga qarshi turishni afzal ko'radi.
{r:My husband would rather not experience so much anxiety.} - Mening turmush o'rtog'im shunchalik ko'p tashvishni boshdan kechirmaslikni afzal ko'radi.
{r:We'd rather she didn't experience such high levels of anxiety.} - Biz uning bunday yuqori darajadagi xavotirni boshdan kechirmasligini afzal ko'rardik.

text: {r:Crawl}[krɔːl] – sudralmoq, o'rmalamoq, emaklamoq. {p:QIROL} Artur saroy do'konidan kreshki va chipslar o'g'irlash uchun do'konga {h:emaklab} kirayotgan ekan.
examples: {r:My niece and nephew prefer crawling under the fence.} - Mening jiyanlarim panjara ostidan emaklab o'tishni afzal ko'rishadi.
{r:My husband prefers crawling to walking when playing with his baby.} - Mening turmush o'rtog'im chaqalog'i bilan o'ynayotganda yurishdan ko'ra emaklashni afzal ko'radi.
{r:My spouse prefers a baby crawl to a walk.} - Mening turmush o'rtog'im yurishdan ko'ra chaqaloq emaklashini afzal ko'radi.
{r:My niece and nephew prefer to crawl through the tunnel rather than walk.} - Mening jiyanlarim tunnel orqali yurib o'tishdan ko'ra emaklab o'tishni afzal ko'rishadi.
{r:He'd rather not crawl in the mud.} - U loyda emaklamaslikni afzal ko'radi.
{r:She'd rather you didn't crawl on the dirty floor.} - U sizning iflos polda emaklamasligingizni afzal ko'rardi.

text: {r:Elevator}[ˈɛləveɪtər] – lift. {p:ELF AYTAR} 'Agar odam bo'lsang va bizning davlatga kelsang {h:lift}ga chiqma chunki bizning lift bo'yi past elflar uchun.'
examples: {r:My uncle prefers to take the elevator to the 10th floor.} - Mening tog'am 10-qavatga liftda chiqishni afzal ko'radi.
{r:My neighbors prefer taking the elevator to climbing the stairs.} - Mening qo'shnilarim zinadan ko'ra liftga chiqishni afzal ko'rishadi.
{r:My aunt prefers the elevator to the escalator.} - Mening xolam eskalatordan ko'ra liftni afzal ko'radi.
{r:My husband prefers to wait for the elevator rather than take the stairs.} - Mening turmush o'rtog'im zinadan chiqishdan ko'ra liftni kutishni afzal ko'radi.
{r:We'd rather take the elevator than the stairs.} - Biz zinadan ko'ra liftga chiqishni afzal ko'ramiz.
{r:They'd rather he fixed the elevator quickly.} - Ular uning liftni tezda tuzatishini afzal ko'rishardi.

text: {r:Endorse}[ɪnˈdɔːrs] – ma'qullamoq, tasdiqlamoq, qo'llamoq. Men mamlakatimizda odamlar dangasa va tartibsiz bo'lib ketyotgani uchun {p:IN}tizom {p:DORIS}ini har bir fuqaroga majburiy berilishini parlamentga taklif qildim. Parlament deputatlari esa mening taklifimni {h:ma'qullashdi}.
examples: {r:My spouse prefers endorsing products she believes in.} - Mening turmush o'rtog'im chinakam ishongan mahsulotlarni ma'qullashni afzal ko'radi.
{r:My uncle prefers endorsing a product to staying neutral about it.} - Mening tog'am mahsulot haqida betaraf turishdan ko'ra uni ma'qullashni afzal ko'radi.
{r:My neighbors prefer an endorsement from a friend to a celebrity.} - Mening qo'shnilarim mashhur shaxsdan ko'ra do'stining ma'qullashini afzal ko'rishadi.
{r:My aunt prefers to endorse a candidate rather than remain neutral.} - Mening xolam neytral bo'lib qolishdan ko'ra o'sha nomzodni qo'llashni afzal ko'radi.
{r:He'd rather endorse a charity that helps children.} - U bolalarga yordam beradigan xayriya tashkilotini qo'llashni afzal ko'radi.
{r:We'd rather the company didn't endorse controversial figures.} - Biz kompaniyaning munozarali shaxslarni qo'llamasligini afzal ko'rardik.

text: {r:Fist}[fɪst] – musht. Agar yosh yigit bo'lsangiz va {h:musht}ingiz qattiq bo'lishini xohlasangiz {p:FIST}ashka yeb yuring.
examples: {r:My husband prefers to shake hands rather than make a fist.} - Mening turmush o'rtog'im musht qilishdan ko'ra qo'l siqishni afzal ko'radi.
{r:He hit the sidewalk with his fist in anger.} – U g‘azab bilan mushtini trotuarga urdi.
{r:This fighter has an iron fist.} - Bu jangchining temir mushti bor.
{r:My father would rather I didn't use my fist in an argument.} - Dadam tortishuvlarda mushtdan foydalanmasligimni afzal ko'radi.

text: {r:Bold}[boʊld] – jasur, qo'rqmas. Siz shunchalik {h:qo'rqmas va jasursiz}ki {p:BOLT}larni qo'lingiz bilan qoqib tashlaysiz.
examples: {r:My aunt prefers making bold decisions.} - Mening xolam jasur qarorlar qabul qilishni afzal ko'radi.
{r:My uncle prefers being bold to being shy.} - Mening tog'am uyatchan bo'lishdan ko'ra jasur bo'lishni afzal ko'radi.
{r:My neighbors prefer bold colors to muted ones.} - Mening qo'shnilarim so'ngan ranglardan ko'ra yorqin ranglarni afzal ko'rishadi.
{r:My spouse prefers to speak boldly rather than stay silent.} - Mening turmush o'rtog'im jim turishdan ko'ra jasorat bilan gapirishni afzal ko'radi.
{r:He'd rather be bold and speak his mind.} - U jasur bo'lishni va o'z fikrini aytishni afzal ko'radi.
{r:We'd rather you were bold and spoke your mind.} - Biz sizning jasur bo'lishingizni va o'z fikringizni aytishingizni afzal ko'rardik.

text: {r:Hint}[hɪnt] – ishora, kinoya; ishora qilmoq, kinoya qilmoq. Agar xotinim 'Namaste', 'Rojam', 'Pyari he hogaye' so'zlarini ishlatishni boshlasa bu uning {p:HIND} kinosi ko'rgisi kelayotganligiga {h:ishora} bo'ladi.
examples: {r:What are you hinting at?} - Nimaga ishora qilyapsiz?
{r:My aunt prefers giving hints to giving direct answers.} - Mening xolam to'g'ridan-to'g'ri javob berishdan ko'ra ishora berishni afzal ko'radi.
{r:My nephew prefers to give a hint rather than tell them the answer.} - Mening jiyanim ularga javobni aytishdan ko'ra ishora berishni afzal ko'radi.
{r:She'd rather not give any hints.} - U hech qanday ishora bermaslikni afzal ko'radi.

text: {r:Madness}[ˈmædnəs] – jinnilik, ahmoqlik; jahl, g'azab. Mad(jinni; jahli chiqmoq) so'zidan yasalgan.
examples: {r:My aunt prefers order to madness.} - Mening xolam jinnilikdan ko'ra tartibni afzal ko'radi.
{r:They prefer to leave rather than stay and face the madness.} - Ular qolib jinnilikka duch kelishdan ko'ra ketishni afzal ko'rishadi.
{r:My uncle would rather not experience the madness of Black Friday shopping.} - Mening tog'am Black Friday xaridining ahmoqliklarini boshdan kechirmaslikni afzal ko'radi.
{r:To begin a war would be sheer madness.} - Urush boshlash haqiqiy jinnilik bo'lardi.

text: {r:Dedication}[ˌdɛdɪˈkeɪʃən] – bag'ishlov, sadoqat. Dedicate(bag'ishlamoq) so'zidan yasalgan.
examples: {r:My niece prefers to show dedication to her studies.} - Mening jiyanim o'qishiga sadoqat ko'rsatishni afzal ko'radi.
{r:My nephew prefers showing dedication to just having talent.} - Mening jiyanim faqat iste'dodga ega bo'lishdan ko'ra sadoqat ko'rsatishni afzal ko'radi.
{r:My neighbors prefer dedication to simple talent.} - Mening qo'shnilarim oddiy iste'doddan ko'ra sadoqatni afzal ko'rishadi.
{r:My spouse prefers to work with dedication rather than just for money.} - Mening turmush o'rtog'im faqat pul uchun ishlashdan ko'ra sadoqat bilan ishlashni afzal ko'radi.
{r:We'd rather you showed more dedication to your work.} - Biz sizning ishingizga ko'proq sadoqat ko'rsatishingizni afzal ko'ramiz.
{r:I'd rather he showed more dedication to his studies.} - Uning o'qishiga ko'proq sadoqat ko'rsatishini afzal ko'rardim.

text: {r:Enroll}[ɪnˈroʊl] – qabul qilinmoq, yozilmoq(kollej, kurs yoki darsga), ro'yxatdan o'tmoq.
examples: {r:My nephew prefers enrolling in online courses.} - Mening jiyanim onlayn kurslarga yozilishni afzal ko'radi.
{r:My niece prefers enrolling in a class to reading a book about it.} - Mening jiyanim biror narsa haqida kitob o'qishdan ko'ra darsga yozilishni afzal ko'radi.
{r:My neighbors prefer a language course to a computer science course.} - Mening qo'shnilarim kompyuter fanlari kursidan ko'ra til kursini afzal ko'rishadi.
{r:My uncle prefers to enroll in the program rather than just audit it.} - Mening tog'am dasturga shunchaki tinglovchi sifatida qatnashishdan ko'ra unga yozilishni afzal ko'radi.
{r:My niece would rather enroll in the university than a college.} - Mening jiyanim kollejdan ko'ra universitetga o'qishga kirishni afzal ko'radi.
{r:We'd rather you enrolled in the program as soon as possible.} - Biz sizning dasturga iloji boricha tezroq yozilishingizni afzal ko'rardik.

text: {r:Liberty}[ˈlɪbərti] – ozodlik, erkinlik. O'zbek tilida ham ishlatiladigan 'Liberal' so'zining ot so'z turkumiga xos shakli.
examples: {r:She is used to having the liberty to make her own decisions.} - U o'z qarorlarini o'zi qabul qilish erkinligiga odatlangan.
{r:Did you get used to the liberty of working from home?} - Uydan ishlash erkinligiga odatladingizmi?
{r:The liberty of speech is a fundamental right.} - So'z erkinligi asosiy huquqdir.
{r:They fought for liberty and the possibility of a better life.} - Ular erkinlik va yaxshi hayot imkoniyati uchun kurashdilar.

text: {r:Reluctant}[rɪˈlʌktənt] – xohlamay, istar-istamas, zo'rg'a, ikkalangan, istaksiz.
examples: {r:She was reluctant to speak, but her brain was full of ideas.} – U gapirishga istaksiz edi, lekin miyasi g‘oyalarga to‘la edi.
{r:The reluctant witness finally agreed to testify in court.} - Ikkilangan guvoh nihoyat sudda guvohlik berishga rozi bo'ldi.
{r:She felt reluctant to chop the old tree in her garden} – U bog‘idagi eski daraxtni chopishga ko‘ngli yo‘q edi.
{r:The child was reluctant to share his last piece of candy with his sister.} - Bola singlisi bilan oxirgi konfetini baham ko'rishni istamadi.

text: {r:Blend}[blɛnd] – aralashtirmoq; aralashma. {p:BLEND}er so'zi aynan 'blend' so'zidan kelib chiqqan va mahsulotlarni {h:aralashtirib} qandaydir yemish tayyorlab berish uchun ishlatiladigan asbobni bildiradi.
examples: {r:I am used to blending different flavors in my cooking.} - Men ovqat pishirishda turli xil ta'mlarni aralashtirishga odatlanganman.
{r:Did you get used to the blend of cultures in the city?} - Shahardagi madaniyatlar aralashuviga odatladingizmi?
{r:The blend of colors was stunning.} - Ranglar aralashmasi ajoyib edi.
{r:She was reluctant to blend in with the crowd, preferring to stand out.} - U olomon bilan aralashishni xohlamasdi, aksincha ajralib turishni afzal ko'rardi.

text: {r:Peel}[piːl] – archilamoq, archimoq; po'stloq. {p:PIL}la qurti boqishning eng arzon usulini bilasizmi? Shunchaki meva va sabzavotlarni {h:archilab} po'stlog'ini pillaga bering. Shuni o'zi yetadi.
examples: {r:She is used to peeling fruits quickly.} - U mevalarni tez archilashga odatlangan.
{r:Did he get used to the peel of a new fruit?} - U yangi mevaning po'stlog'iga odatlandimi?
{r:The peel of the orange was thick.} - Apelsin po'stlog'i qalin edi.
{r:We are used to using the peel to make zest for baking.} - Biz po'stloqdan pishiriqlar uchun zest tayyorlashga odatlanganmiz.

text: {r:Cancel}[ˈkænsəl] – bekor qilmoq, yo'q qilmoq. Akamning tug'ilgan kuniga Uzum Marketdan {p:KAMZUL} olgan edim. Lekin onam akamga kamzul yoqmasligini aytganidan so'ng buyurtmani {h:bekor qildim}.
examples: {r:Your dad cancelled the plan altogether two days ago.} - Dadangiz ikki kun oldin rejalarni butunlay bekor qildi.
{r:Did you get used to the cancellations due to bad weather?} - Yomon ob-havo tufayli bekor qilinishlarga odatladingizmi?
{r:I already got used to cancelling the appointments.} - Men allaqachon uchrashuvlarni bekor qilishga ko'nikkanman.
{r:The doctor gave excellent advice to cancel the spread of the disease.} – Shifokor kasallik tarqalishini to‘xtatish uchun ajoyib maslahat berdi.

text:
{r:Negotiation}[nɪˌɡoʊʃiˈeɪʃən] – muzokara. 
 Faraz qilaylik sigirga sig'inuvchi Hindiston kelajakda AQSH va Xitoydan keyingi qudratli davlatga aylanadi. Hozirda Hindistonda yashovchi 15% aholi musulmonlar va ularga sigir go'shtini iste'mol qilishi taqiqlangan. Kundan-kunga rivojlanayotgan Hindiston chet davlatlarni ham vegeteryan bo'lishga majburlamoqchi. O'zbekiston tashqi ishlari vazirligi bilan {h:muzokaralar} o'tkazgan hindlar bu siyosatning boshlanishi sifatida Ozbekistonga 1 million dona '{p:NE GOSH YEYSAN}' kitobini berishmoqda. Bu kitoblar aholiga tekinga tarqatiladi va vegeterianizm(go'sht iste'mol qilmaslik) targ'ib qilinadi bu kitob orqali.(Namuna uchun yozildi)
examples: {r:Did they get used to the negotiation process?} - Ular muzokara jarayoniga odatlandilarmi?
{r:The negotiation lasted for hours.} - Muzokara soatlab davom etdi.
{r:We will be used to succeeding in the negotiation phase.} - Biz muzokara bosqichida muvaffaqiyat qozonishga ko'nikib ketamiz hali.
{r:The success of the negotiation depended on effective persuasion.} - Muzokaraning muvaffaqiyati samarali ishontirishga bog'liq edi.

text: {r:Bias}[ˈbaɪəs] – xolislikning yo'qligi, bir tomonga o'gish, mayllik, tarafkashlik.
examples: {r:He is used to dealing with bias in the workplace.} - U ish joyidagi tarafkashlik bilan ishlashga odatlangan.
{r:Did you get used to the bias in the media?} - Ommaviy axborot vositalaridagi tarafkashlikka odatladingizmi?
{r:The bias was evident in the report.} - Hisobotda tarafkashlik aniq ko'rinardi.
{r:We are used to noticing the bias in the selection process.} - Biz tanlov jarayonidagi tarafkashlikni payqashga odatlanganmiz.

text: {r:Vanish}[ˈvænɪʃ] – g'oyib bo'lmoq, yo'qolmoq. Men supur-sudur ishlari bilan shug'ullanaman. Hozir obshiy{p: VAN}nada {p:ISH}layman. Vannani yig'ishtirish paytida odamlarning juda ko'p {h:g'oyib bo'lgan} narsalarini topib olaman va qaytaraman.
examples: {r:She got used to seeing things vanish in the magic show.} - U sehrli shoularda narsalar g'oyib bo'lishini ko'rishga odatlangan.
{r:You will get used to seeing public funds vanish.} - Jamiyatning umumiy budjeti g'oyib bo'lib qolishiga hali ko'nikib ketasan.
{r:The magician used to vanishing on the right and appearing from the left.} - Fokuschi o'ng tarafda yo'q bo'lib qolib chapdan chiqib kelardi.
{r:Brutality will vanish and humanity will thrive eventually.} - Oxir-oqibat shafqatsizlik yo'q bo'ladi va insoniylik rivojlanadi.

text: {r:Necessity}[nəˈsɛsəti] – zarurat, ehtiyoj. Men 1 oy oldin zo'r nasos oldim, {p:NASOS}niyam {p:ITI}, daxshati. Narxi 11 000$ ekan. Agar u bilan balonni damlasangiz velosipedni baloni ham teshilmaydi. Namuncha qimmat deysizmi? Chunki {h:zaruratim} bor edi shunaqa zo'r nasosga. Men fura haydayman. Bizning bitta balonimiz 500$ turadi. Yaxshi nasoslansa uncha-munchaga teshilmaydida.
examples: {r:He is used to the necessity of waking up early.} - U erta turish zaruratiga odatlangan.
{r:Did you get used to the necessity of wearing a uniform?} - Forma kiyish zaruratiga odatladingizmi?
{r:Taking charge in an emergency is not just a choice, but a necessity.} - Favqulodda vaziyatda mas'uliyatni o'z zimmaga olish nafaqat tanlov, balki zaruratdir.
{r:Raising an objection might seem like a formality, but it's often a legal necessity.} - E'tiroz bildirish rasmiyatchilik kabi tuyulishi mumkin, ammo bu ko'pincha qonuniy zaruratdir.

text: {r:Teenager}[ˈtiːnˌeɪdʒər] – o'smir. Bizning Toshkent zooparkida {p:DINAY} ichadigan {p:JIR}afa paydo bo'libdi. U yerda ishlaydigan do'stimning aytishicha bu aslida jirafa libosini kiyib olgan {h:o'smir} bola ekan.
examples: {r:My mom is used to working with teenagers.} - Oyim o'smirlar bilan ishlashga odatlangan.
{r:Did he get used to the behavior of teenagers?} - U o'smirlarning xulqiga odatlandimi?
{r:My niece is a weird teenager.} - Mening jiyanim g'alati o'smir.
{r:We are used to working with teenagers in the camp every summer.} - Biz har yozda lagerda o'smirlar bilan ishlashga odatlanganmiz.
{r:It's often hard to notice a distinct difference in behavior between a child and a young teenager.} - Bolalar va yosh o'smirlar o'rtasidagi xulq-atvordagi aniq farqni payqash ko'pincha qiyin.

text: {r:Decent}[ˈdiːsənt] – odobli, tarbiyali; normal, qoniqarli, maqbul. Rossiyada 2023 – yili Nastya Ivleeva boshliq qo’shiqchi va aktyorlar “Golaya Vecherinka” ya’ni kiyimsiz bayram tadbiri o’tkazishdi va bu katta shov-shuvga sabab bo’ldi. Agar yana shunday qilishadigan bo’lsa tadbir bo’layotgan hududga odobli soldatlar ishtirokida {p:DESANT} tashlaymiz va o’sha buzuqilarni ham bayramini to’xtatib o’zlarini {h:tarbiyali} qilib qo’yamiz.(Namuna uchun yozildi)
examples: {r:She is used to living in a decent neighborhood.} - U munosib mahallada yashashga odatlangan.
{r:These criminals are getting used to having decent conversations with decent people.} - Bu jinoyatchilar tarbiyali odamlar bilan normal suhbat qilishga ko'nikishyapti.
{r:It was a decent meal, nothing fancy.} - Bu yaxshi ovqat edi, hech qanday dabdabali emas.
{r:We got used to expecting decent service from that restaurant.} - Biz bu restorandan munosib xizmat kutishga odatlandik.

text: {r:Destination}[ˌdɛstɪˈneɪʃən] – manzil, joy, makon.
examples: {r:She is used to reaching her destination quickly.} - U o'z manziliga tez yetib borishga odatlangan.
{r:The old map, though familiar, showed a new destination for their journey.} - Eski xarita, garchi tanish bo'lsa ham, ularning sayohati uchun yangi manzilni ko'rsatdi.
{r:Our final destination was Paris.} - Bizning yakuniy manzilimiz Parij edi.
{r:We are used to planning our destination in advance.} - Biz manzilimizni oldindan rejalashtirishga odatlanganmiz.
{r:They possess enough land in their new destination.} - Ular yangi joylarida yetarlicha yerga egalik qilishadi.

text: {r:Diminish}[dɪˈmɪnɪʃ] – kamaytirmoq, pasaytirmoq. Hozirgi kunda ko’cha-ko’yda odamni obro’sini {h:pasaytiradigan} eng katta ish menimcha bu {p:TI}ko {p:MINISH.}
examples: {r:He is used to seeing his enthusiasm diminish over time.} - U vaqt o'tishi bilan o'z ishtiyoqining kamayishiga odatlangan.
{r:The light began to diminish as the sun set.} - Quyosh botgach, yorug'lik kamaya boshladi.
{r:We are used to the noise diminishing after midnight.} - Biz yarim tundan keyin shovqinning kamayishiga odatlanganmiz.
{r:The manager seemed reluctant to diminish his control over the project.} - Menejer loyiha ustidan nazoratini kamaytirishni istamayotgandek tuyuldi.

text: {r:Silk}[sɪlk] – ipak. silk – ipak. Mana bu youtube SSILKa(ya’ni havola) qanday qilib {h:ipakdan} 100$ kupyura yasashni o’rgatadi.
examples: {r:Your mom is used to wearing silk clothes because of their softness.} - Sening oying yumshoqligi sababli ipak kiyimlar kiyishga odatlangan.
{r:They believe that a special cure can be made by boiling silk and a stick together} – Ular ipak va tayoqni birga qaynatib maxsus dori tayyorlash mumkin deb ishonishadi.
{r:The dress was made of pure silk.} - Ko'ylak sof ipakdan qilingan edi.
{r:We are used to seeing silk being used in luxury items.} - Biz ipakning hashamatli buyumlarda ishlatilishini ko'rishga odatlanganmiz.

text: {r:Magnitude}[ˈmæɡnɪtjuːd] – ko’lam, hajm, ahamiyat. G’alati qiliqlar qanday ko’lamdagi zararlarga olib kelishini bilmoqchi bo’lsang. Ularni amalga oshirib ko’r. Masalan {p:MAGNIT YUT}  va ahmoqliging qay {h:ko’lamdagi} zararga olib kelganini bilasan(yozilganlarni amalda sinab ko’rmang).
examples: {r:He is used to dealing with problems of great magnitude.} - U katta miqdordagi muammolar bilan ishlashga odatlangan.
{r:Did they get used to the magnitude of the project?} - Ular loyihaning kattaligiga odatlandilarmi?
{r:The scientists studied the magnitude of the earthquake to gain more understanding about it} – Olimlar zilzilaning hajmini o‘rganib, u haqida ko‘proq tushuncha olishdi.
{r:The politician tried to handle the shame, but the magnitude of the scandal was too great} – Siyosatchi uyatni yenga olishga harakat qildi, ammo mojaroni ko'lami juda ulkan edi.

text: {r:Rebellion}[rɪˈbɛljən] – isyon, qo'zg'olon. Rebel(isyonchi) so'zidan yasalgan.
examples: {r:She is used to studying historical rebellions.} - U tarixiy isyonlarni o'rganishga odatlangan.
{r:Did the government get used to the constant threat of rebellion?} - Hukumat doimiy isyon tahdidiga odatlandimi?
{r:The rebellion was quickly suppressed.} - Isyon tezda bostirildi.
{r:We got used to hearing stories about past rebellions in our town.} - Biz shahrimizdagi o'tmishdagi isyonlar haqidagi hikoyalarni eshitishga odatlandik.

text: {r:Precisely}[prɪˈsaɪsli] – aniq, aynan. Precise(aniq) so'zidan yasalgan.
examples: {r:He is used to arriving precisely on time for meetings.} - U uchrashuvlarga aynan o'z vaqtida kelishga odatlangan.
{r:Did you get used to following instructions precisely?} - Ko'rsatmalarni aniq bajarishga odatlandingizmi?
{r:The chef chopped the onions precisely for the new dish} – Oshpaz yangi taom uchun piyozni aniq qilib chopdi.
{r:We are/got used to him speaking precisely and clearly during presentations.} - Biz uning taqdimotlar paytida aniq va ravshan gapirishiga odatlanganmiz.

text: {r:Caution}[ˈkɔːʃən] – ehtiyotkorlik, ogohlik. Cautious(ehtiyotkor) so'zidan yasalgan.
examples: {r:She is used to exercising caution when driving in bad weather.} - U yomon ob-havoda mashina haydashda ehtiyotkorlik ko'rsatishga odatlangan.
{r:Did he get used to the caution advised by the safety regulations?} - U xavfsizlik qoidalari tomonidan tavsiya etilgan ehtiyotkorlikka odatlandimi?
{r:It became obvious from previous experiences that caution leads to better results} – Oldingi tajribalardan ayon bo‘ldiki, ehtiyotkorlik yaxshiroq natijalarga olib keladi.
{r:The guard showed caution and did not exclude anyone without reason.} - Qo‘riqchi ehtiyotkorlik ko‘rsatdi va hech kimni sababsiz chiqarib tashlamadi.

text: {r:Alien}[ˈeɪliən] – begona, yot; o'zga sayyoralik. Tasavvur qiling {p:ALI YON}iga borsangiz ko’rinishingiz keskin o’zgarib {h:o’zga sayyoralik}ka o’xshab qolasiz.
examples: {r:I am used to encountering alien concepts in philosophy classes.} - Men falsafa darslarida begona tushunchalarga duch kelishga odatlanganman.
{r:Did you get used to feeling like an alien in a new country?} - Yangi mamlakatda o'zingizni begonadek his qilishga odatladingizmi?
{r:The idea was alien to his way of thinking.} - Bu g'oya uning fikrlash tarziga begona edi.
{r:We are used to seeing alien species portrayed in science fiction films.} - Biz ilmiy-fantastik filmlarda o'zga sayyoraliklarning tasvirlanganini ko'rishga odatlanganmiz.
{r:We don't know if aliens exist.} - Biz hali o'zga sayyoraliklar bor-yo'qligini bilmaymiz.

text: {r:Scare}[skɛər] – qo'rqitmoq, cho’chitmoq. Tasavvur qiling yangi skaner ishlab chiqarilyapti. Bu {p:SKANER} barmoqlaringizni tekshirib siz qachondir jinoyat qilganmisiz yo’qmi aniqlab berar ekan. Bu skanerlarni davlat organ xodimlari tomonidan aholi orasida yoppasiga qo’llanilishi haqidagi xabarlar ko’pchilikni {h:qo’rqityapti} va ayniqsa ko’plab mayda jinoyatlarga aralashganingiz uchun sizni ham.
examples: {r:I am used to watching horror movies, so they don't scare me anymore.} - Men qo'rqinchli filmlar ko'rishga odatlanganman, shuning uchun ular meni endi qo'rqitmaydi.
{r:Did you get used to the sudden scare tactics in the haunted house?} - Siz arvoh uyidagi to'satdan qo'rqitish taktikalariga odatladingizmi?
{r:We observed a wild animal in the forest, but its sudden roar scared us} – Biz o‘rmonda yovvoyi hayvonni kuzatdik, ammo uning to‘satdan o'kirishi bizni qo‘rqitdi.
{r:They got used to being scared by their prank-loving friends.} - Ular hazilkash do‘stlari tomonidan qo‘rqitilishiga odatlandilar.

text: {r:Biased}[ˈbaɪəst] – xolislikning yo'qligi, bir tomonga o'gish, mayllik. Bias(tarafkashlik) so'zining sifat so'z turkumiga xos shakli.
examples: {r:She succeeded in avoiding biased opinions} - U noxolis fikrlardan qochishga muvaffaq bo'ldi.
{r:They accused him of showing biased behavior} - Ular uni tarafkash munosabatda aybladilar.
{r:I don't approve of publishing biased articles} - Men xolis bo'lmagan maqolalarni nashr etishni ma'qullamayman.
{r:His biased reporting led to a decline in the newspaper's credibility.} - Uning tarafkash reportaji gazeta ishonchliligining pasayishiga olib keldi.

text: {r:Swear}[swɛər] – qasam ichmoq; so'kinmoq. Chilim chekadigan yomon odatim bor. Ota-onam va oilam uchun chilimni tashlashga {h:qasam ichdim} va chilimimni sandiqqa solib {p:SVAR}kalab tashladim.
examples: {r:He was suspected of swearing at the referee} - U hakamga so'kinganlikda gumon qilindi.
{r:She confessed to swearing during the argument} - U bahs paytida so'kinganligini tan oldi.
{r:I swear I will help you.} - Men sizga yordam berishga qasam ichaman.
{r:She swore to keep the secret.} - U sirni saqlashga qasam ichdi.
{r:He swore never to lie again.} - U qaytib hech qachon yolg‘on gapirmaslikka qasam ichdi.
{r:Do you swear to tell the truth?} - Siz rost gapirishga qasam ichasizmi?

text: {r:False}[fɔːls] – falshiviy, yolg'on.
examples: {r:They were accused of spreading false information} - Ular yolg'on ma'lumot tarqatganlikda ayblangan.
{r:He is strongly opposing any false claims} - U har qanday yolg'on iddaolarga kuchli qarshilik qilyapti.
{r:She dreams of correcting false impressions} - U noto'g'ri taassurotlarni tuzatishni orzu qiladi.
{r:I don't feel like tolerating false promises} - Men yolg'on va'dalarga chidashni xohlamayman.

text: {r:Lawn}[lɔːn] – gazon, maysazor. Tasavvur qiling siz gazoningiz ichiga {p:QOVUN} ekdingiz va bir tarafdan {h:gazon}ning go'zalligidan bahra olyapsiz boshqa tomondan esa qovunning hididan.
examples: {r:Get off my lawn! Understandable?} - Maysamdan qoch. Tushunarlimi?
{r:They insisted on watering the cute lawn daily} - Ular har kuni yoqimtoy maysani sug'oramiz deb turib oldi.
{r:She apologized for neglecting the lawn} - U maysaga e'tibor bermagani uchun uzr so'radi.
{r:He's thinking of reseeding the lawn} - U maysani qayta urug'lantirishni o'ylayapti.

text: {r:Angel}[ˈeɪndʒəl] – angel, farishta.
examples: {r:She was thanked for acting like an angel} - U farishta kabi harakat qilgani uchun minnatdorchilik bildirishdi.
{r:They dreamed of seeing real angels} - Ular haqiqiy farishtalarni ko'rishni orzu qilishdi.
{r:We don't approve of painting angels} - Biz farishtalarni chizishni ma'qullamaymiz.
{r:He was accused of pretending to be an angel} - U farishtalikka da'vo qilganlikda ayblangan.

text: {r:Prohibit}[prəˈhɪbɪt] – taqiqlamoq, man etmoq. Mana bu {p:ROHIB ITI} ayollarning cherkovga ro'molda kirishini tekshiradi. Agar ro'molsiz kimdir kirmoqchi bo'lsa akillab cherkovga kirishini {h:taqiqlaydi}.
examples: {r:The law succeeded in prohibiting smoking here altogether.} - Qonun bu yerda chekishni butunlay taqiqlashga muvaffaq bo'ldi.
{r:They're thinking of prohibiting loud noises} - Ular baland ovozlarni taqiqlashni o'ylayaptilar.
{r:We don't feel like prohibiting all celebrations} - Biz barcha bayramlarni taqiqlashni xohlamaymiz.
{r:We strongly object to any rule that will specifically prohibit free speech.} - Biz aynan so'z erkinligini taqiqlovchi har qanday qoidaga qat'iyan e'tiroz bildiramiz.

text: {r:Precious}[ˈprɛʃəs] – qimmatbaho, qimmat; qadrli, aziz. Tasavvur qiling siz stolovoyda yegan {p:PERASHKIZ} bu stolovoy tomonidan sotilgan 1 000 000 chi perashki ekan. Shuning uchun stolovoy egasi sizga {h:qimmatbaho} sovg'a beribdi.
examples: {r:My dad was congratulated for finding precious stones} - Qimmatbaho toshlarni topgani uchun dadamni tabriklashdi.
{r:They're looking forward to selling precious art} - Ular qimmatbaho san'at asarlarini sotishni kutmoqda.
{r:We suspect him of hiding precious documents} - Biz uni qimmatbaho hujjatlarni yashirganlikda gumon qilamiz.
{r:I don't approve of wasting precious time} - Men qimmatli vaqtni isrof qilishni ma'qullamayman.

text: {r:Outstanding}[aʊtˈstændɪŋ] – qoyilmaqom, zo'r, ajralib turuvchi. Og'lim Obid sen bugun 5 ga kirding. Xullas Obid sen zo'r, boshqalardan ajralib turuvchi, {h:qoyilmaqom} bolasan. Boshqa bolalar 2 yoshidan sutdan chiqsa sen {p:OBID SUT EMDING} 5 yoshingda ham. Sutdan chiqmagansan 5 yoshingda ham.
examples: {r:She was thanked for completing outstanding work} - U ajoyib ishni bajargani uchun minnatdorchilik bildirildi.
{r:We're thinking of recognizing outstanding students} - Biz ajoyib talabalarni tan olishni o'ylayapmiz.
{r:He dreams of receiving outstanding awards} - U ajoyib mukofotlar olishni orzu qiladi.
{r:My uncle was an outstanding seller who survived in such a competition} - Mening amakim mana shunday raqobatda omon qolgan qoyilmaqom sotuvchi edi.

text: {r:Permission}[pərˈmɪʃən] – ruxsat. Permit(ruxsat bermoq) so'zidan yasalgan.
examples: {r:They insisted on getting permission first} - Ular avval ruxsat olishni talab qilishdi.
{r:We need special permission for this occasion.} - Bu holat uchun bizga maxsus ruxsat kerak.
{r:She asked for her parents’ permission and slightly smiled with charm} – U ota-onasidan ruxsat so‘radi va biroz jozibali tabassum qildi.
{r:He apologized for not asking permission} - U ruxsat so'ramagani uchun uzr so'radi.

text: {r:Applaud}[əˈplɔːd] – qarsak chalmoq, olqishlamoq. Yozuvchi Mahmud Ravshanovning '{p:EPLAD}i' nomli kitobini o'qib shunchalik maza qildimki oxirida {h:qarsak} chalib yubordim.
examples: {r:We can only applaud the courage it takes to travel to such a distant and unknown land.} - Biz bunday uzoq va noma'lum yurtga sayohat qilish uchun kerak bo'ladigan jasoratni faqat olqishlashimiz mumkin.
{r:We don't feel like applauding bad behavior} - Biz yomon xatti-harakatlarga qarsak chalishni xohlamaymiz.
{r:They thanked for applauding at the right time} - Ular to'g'ri vaqtda qarsak chalganliklari uchun minnatdorchilik bildirdi.
{r:She dreams of being applauded on stage} - U sahnada unga qarsak chalishlarini orzu qiladi.
{r:He was reluctant to applaud a performance that he found average.} - U o'rtacha deb topgan chiqishni olqishlashni istamadi.

text: {r:Artificial}[ˌɑːrtɪˈfɪʃəl] – sun'iy.
examples: {r:He was suspected of using artificial ingredients} - U sun'iy masalliqlardan foydalanganlikda gumon qilindi.
{r:They're thinking of banning artificial colors} - Ular sun'iy ranglarni taqiqlashni o'ylayaptilar.
{r:We don't approve of creating artificial shortages} - Biz sun'iy tanqislik yaratishni ma'qullamaymiz.
{r:She apologized for preferring artificial flowers} - U sun'iy gullarni afzal ko'rgani uchun uzr so'radi.
{r:We thought that artificial intelligence would be possible in the distant future.} - Biz sun'iy intellektni faqatgina olis kelajakda imkoni bo'ladi deb o'ylardik.

text: {r:Tide}[taɪd] – to'lqin. Agar ummonda to'lqinlar hujumiga duch kelsangiz {p:TAYD} sodasini oching va {h:to'lqin}lar tomonga soching. Shunda to'lqinlar chekinishi mumkin.
examples: {r:They succeeded in predicting the tide changes} - Ular to'lqin o'zgarishlarini oldindan aytishga muvaffaq bo'lishdi.
{r:We're looking forward to watching the tide come in} - Biz to'lqin kelishini kuzatishni kutmoqdamiz.
{r:He was stopped from swimming against the tide} - U to'lqinga qarshi suzishdan to'xtatildi.
{r:She dreams of surfing during high tide} - U baland to'lqinda syorfing qilishni orzu qiladi.

text: {r:Boyfriend}[ˈbɔɪ.frɛnd] – yigit do‘st, yigiti. Bu so‘z to'ydan oldingi romantik munosabatda bo‘lgan erkak kishini bildiradi.
examples: {r:Her boyfriend is very kind and funny.} – Uning yigiti juda mehribon va hazilkash.
{r:They have been boyfriend and girlfriend for two years.} – Ular ikki yildan beri yigit-qiz munosabatida.
{r:She called her boyfriend to share the news.} – U yangilikni aytish uchun yigit do‘stiga qo‘ng‘iroq qildi.
{r:They said Julia's boyfriend was cute, but Julia loved him for his deep thoughts.} – Ular Julianing yigitini yoqimli deyishdi, lekin Julia uni chuqur fikrlari uchun sevardi.

text: {r:Awesome}[ˈɔː.səm] – ajoyib, hayratlanarli. Bu so‘z juda yaxshi, ta’sirli yoki ilhomlantiruvchi narsani ifodalaydi.
examples: {r:The view from the mountain was awesome.} – Tog‘dan manzara ajoyib edi.
{r:She did an awesome job on the project.} – U loyiha ustida ajoyib ish qildi.
{r:That movie was totally awesome.} – O‘sha film mutlaqo ajoyib edi.
{r:You’re doing awesome, keep going.} – Sen ajoyib ish qilyapsan, davom et!

text: {r:Cool}[kuːl] – ajoyib, yoqimli. Bu so‘z biror narsa jozibador, yoqimli yoki zamonaviy ekanini bildiradi. Cool(salqin) so'zining omonimi.
examples: {r:He wore a cool jacket to the concert.} – U konsertga ajoyib kurtka kiyib bordi.
{r:That’s a cool idea!} – Bu ajoyib g‘oya!
{r:They have a cool new app.} – Ularning yangi ilovasi juda ajoyib.
{r:The cool view from the hill filled me with a desire to stay longer.} – Tepalikdan ko‘ringan ajoyib manzara menda uzoqroq qolish istagini uyg‘otdi.

text: {r:Adore}[əˈdɔːr] – juda yaxshi ko‘rmoq, mehr bilan sevmoq. Bizning xalq top klubda futbol o'ynagan birinchi o'zbek {p:Eldor} Shomurodovni juda {h:yaxshi ko'radi}.
examples: {r:I absolutely adore this song.} – Men bu qo‘shiqni juda yaxshi ko‘raman.
{r:She adores her little brother.} – U kichik ukasini mehr bilan sevadi.
{r:They adore spending time together.} – Ular birga vaqt o‘tkazishni juda yaxshi ko‘rishadi.
{r:He adores animals and volunteers at the shelter.} – U hayvonlarni yaxshi ko‘radi va boshpanada ko‘ngilli bo‘lib ishlaydi.

text: {r:Conversation}[ˌkɒn.vəˈseɪ.ʃən] – suhbat, muloqot.
examples: {r:We had a long conversation about our future.} – Biz kelajagimiz haqida uzoq suhbatlashdik.
{r:She joined the conversation with a smile.} – U suhbatga tabassum bilan qo‘shildi.
{r:The conversation was interesting and fun.} – Suhbat qiziqarli va zavqli bo‘ldi.
{r:He started a conversation with the new student.} – U yangi o‘quvchi bilan suhbat boshladi.

text: {r:Burglar}[ˈbɜː.ɡlər] – qulfbuzar o‘g‘ri, uyga buzib kiruvchi. Qishloqdagi uyimga qulfbuzar o'g'ri kiribdi. Darhol militsiyaga yozib berdim. Ko'chamizdagi kameralar orqali o'g'rini aniqladik. Hayratlanarlisi {h:o'g'rilar} {p:BO'RILAR} to'dasi ekan. Qanday qulfni buzganiga hayronman.
examples: {r:The burglar broke into the house at night.} – O‘g‘ri kechasi uyga buzib kirdi.
{r:They caught the burglar with the stolen items.} – Ular o‘g‘rini o‘g‘irlangan buyumlar bilan ushlashdi.
{r:The alarm scared away the burglar.} – Signal o‘g‘rini qo‘rqitib yubordi.
{r:He was caught with burglary.} – U o'g'irlik bilan qo'lga tushdi.

text: {r:adjust}[əˈdʒʌst] – moslashtirmoq, sozlamoq. Bu so‘z biror narsani to‘g‘rilash, o‘zgartirish yoki sharoitga moslashtirishni bildiradi.
examples: {r:He adjusted the chair to make it more comfortable.} - U stulni qulayroq bo‘lishi uchun moslashtirdi.
{r:She quickly adjusted to the new environment.} - U tezda yangi muhitga moslashdi.
{r:Adjust the volume if it’s too loud.} - Agar ovoz baland bo‘lsa, uni sozlang.
{r:They had to adjust their plans because of the weather.} - Ular ob-havo sababli rejalarini o‘zgartirishga majbur bo‘lishdi.

text: {r:assist}[əˈsɪst] – yordam bermoq, ko‘maklashmoq. Mana bu o’yinda tomoshabin stadionga tushib ketib futbolchiga assist berdi va gol urilishiga sababchi bo’ldi. Muxlisning {p:assist}i {h:yordam}ida jamoa keyingi bosqichga chiqdi.
examples: {r:The nurse assisted the doctor during the operation.} - Hamshira operatsiya vaqtida doktorga yordam berdi.
{r:He assisted his friend with the homework.} - U do‘stiga uy vazifasida yordam berdi.
{r:They assist people to find affordable doctors who can prescribe treatment.} - Ular odamlarga muolaja yozib beradigan arzon shifokorlarni topishda yordam beradi.
{r:She formerly was a viewer but now she assists the team.} - U ilgari tomoshabin edi, lekin hozir jamoaga yordam beradi.

text: {r:Lately}[ˈleɪtli] – oxirgi paytlarda. {h:Oxirgi paytlarda}, mana shu oxirgi 7 kun ichida mana bu {p:LEYT}enant {p:LI}mon bilan janglyor qilishni o’rgandi.
examples: {r:It's no use worrying about what's been happening lately} - So'nggi paytlarda bo'layotgan narsalar haqida xavotirlanishning foydasi yo'q.
{r:Lately, there's been a shortage of fresh vegetables} - So'nggi paytlarda yangi sabzavotlar yetishmayapti.
{r:She has been feeling tired lately} - U so'nggi paytlarda charchagan his qilyapti.
{r:It's worth paying attention to the changes happening lately} - So'nggi paytlarda bo'layotgan o'zgarishlar e'tibor berishga arziydi.

text: {r:Shortage}[ˈʃɔːrtɪdʒ] – yetishmovchilik, tanqislik, taqchillik. Mamlakatimizda bu yili yoz payti {p:SHORTIK} {h:yetishmovchiligi} bo'lyapti. Bozor aylanib birorta SHORTIK topolmadim. Agar bu taqchillik davom etsa odamlar yozda ichki kiyimda yurishni boshlaydi.
examples: {r:There's no point in complaining about the shortage; let's find a solution} - Yetishmovchilik haqida shikoyat qilishning ma'nosi yo'q; buning uchun yechim topaylik.
{r:The shortage of water is becoming a serious problem} - Suv yetishmovchiligi jiddiy muammoga aylanmoqda.
{r:It's no use ignoring the shortage; we need to act now} - Yetishmovchilikni e'tiborsiz qoldirishning foydasi yo'q; hozir harakat qilishimiz kerak.
{r:We had difficulty coping with the shortage} - Taqchillikni qondirishda bizda qiyinchiliklar bo'ldi.

text: {r:Tribe}[traɪb] – qabila. Bizning ota bobolarimiz ya’ni turkiy {h:qabilalar} o’tovlarni yerga {p:tirab} qo’yishgan va o’sha atrofda chorvasini boqqan. Laylov o’tloqlari qisqargandan so’ng boshqa yaylovga ko’chishgan.
examples: {r:The tribe had difficulty adapting to the new rules consistently} - Qabila yangi qoidalarga izchillik bilan moslashishda qiyinchilik ko'rdi.
{r:It's worth learning about the traditions of this tribe} - Bu qabilaning an'analarini o'rganishga arziydi.
{r:Who is in charge of this tribe lately?} - Bu qabilaga oxirgi paytlarda kim javobgar?
{r:The neighboring tribe is busy celebrating the festival.} - Qo'shni qabila festivalni nishonlash bilan band.

text: {r:Ridiculous}[rɪˈdɪkjələs] – kulgili, bema’ni, ahmoqona. Rediskani yashil bo’yoqqa botirib olgandim {p:RED}iskani {p:KALLAS}i shunaqangi {h:kulgili} bo’lib qoldi. Bir soat mazza qilib kulibman.
examples: {r:It's no use getting upset over such a ridiculous mistake} - Bunday bema'ni xato uchun xafa bo'lishning foydasi yo'q.
{r:The idea sounded ridiculous at first, but it worked} - G'oya dastlab bema'ni tuyuldi, lekin u ishladi.
{r:She said, 'It's a waste of time arguing about something so ridiculous'.} - U aytdi: 'Bunday bema'ni narsa haqida bahslashish vaqtni isrof qilishdir.'
{r:She had trouble understanding these ridiculous opinions.} - U bu ahmoqona fikrlarni tushunishda qiynaldi.

text: {r:Credible}[ˈkrɛdəbəl] – ishonchli. Milliy bank bilimdonlar o'rtasida teleshou o'tkazib yutganlarga foizsiz kredit beryapti. Yaxshi tashabbus foizsiz {p:KREDI}t {p:BIL}ag'onlarga. Chunki ular {h:ishonchli} odamlar.
examples: {r:It's worth listening to his advice; he's a credible source} - Uning maslahati tinglashga arziydi; u ishonchli manba.
{r:The story seemed credible at first, but later we found out it was false} - Hikoya dastlab ishonchli tuyuldi, lekin keyin u yolg'on ekanligini bildik.
{r:There's no point in trusting someone who isn't credible} - Ishonchsiz odamga ishonishning ma'nosi yo'q.
{r:It's difficult for a teenager to earn credible praise from their older siblings.} - O'smir uchun o'zining akalaridan ishonchli maqtov olish qiyin.

text: {r:Oversee}[ˌoʊvərˈsiː] – nazorat qilmoq, ko'rib chiqmoq. Faraz qiling hojatxonada ishlaysiz. Sizning ishingiz bu joy {p:IVIRSI}b ketmaganmi {h:nazorat qilib turish}.
examples: {r:The safety team needs to oversee maintenance to prevent the system from a sudden crash.} - Xavfsizlik guruhi tizimning to'satdan ishdan chiqishining oldini olish uchun texnik xizmat ko'rsatishni nazorat qilishi kerak.
{r:She had difficulty overseeing the project because of the shortage of staff} - Xodimlar yetishmovchiligi tufayli loyihani nazorat qilishda qiyinchilik ko'rdi.
{r:A manager will oversee all operations at the new facility.} - Yangi inshootdagi barcha operatsiyalarni menejer nazorat qiladi.
{r:He spent hours overseeing the construction of the new building} - U yangi binoning qurilishini nazorat qilishga soatlar sarfladi.

text: {r:Inspire}[ɪnˈspaɪər] – ilhomlantirmoq. Mana bu {p:INSOF AYR}oni. Bu ayrondan ichsangiz sizga insof kirishni boshlaydi va o'zingizning chiroyli xulqingiz bilan ko'pchilikni {h:ilhomlantira} boshlaysiz.
examples: {r:It's no good trying to inspire others if you're not motivated yourself} - Agar o'zingiz motivatsiyaga ega bo'lmasangiz, boshqalarni ilhomlantirishga urinishning foydasi yo'q.
{r:The teacher inspired her students to work harder} - O'qituvchi o'quvchilarini ko'proq ishlashga ilhomlantirdi.
{r:There's no point in giving up; let this story inspire you} - Chekinishdan foyda yo'q; bu hikoya sizni ilhomlantirsin.
{r:His speech was so inspiring that everyone applauded} - Uning nutqi shunchalik ilhomli ediki, hamma olqishladi.

text: {r:Mate}[meɪt] – do’st, og’ayni; juft; juftlashmoq. O’zbekiston sharoitida qishda eng yaqin {h:do’st} bu {p:MET}an gazini muammosiz bergan zapravka.
examples: {r:It's no use arguing with your mate; just talk it out} - Do'stingiz bilan bahslashishning foydasi yo'q; shunchaki gaplashib oling.
{r:He had trouble finding a mate who shared his interests} - U o'z qiziqishlarini baham ko'radigan do'st topishda qiyinchilik ko'rdi.
{r:It's worth spending time with a loyal mate} - Sodiq do'st bilan vaqt o'tkazishga arziydi.
{r:She said, 'There's no point in being friends with someone who isn't a good mate.'} - U aytdi: 'Yaxshi do'st bo'lmagan odam bilan do'st bo'lishning ma'nosi yo'q.'
{r:Even a minor argument can diminish the trust between close mates.} - Hatto kichik janjal ham yaqin do'stlar orasidagi ishonchni kamaytirishi mumkin.

text: {r:Genius}[ˈdʒiːniəs] – geniy, daho.
examples: {r:It's no good pretending to be a genius; just be yourself} - Geniy bo'lib ko'rinishga urinishning foydasi yo'q; shunchaki o'zingiz bo'ling.
{r:The young genius had no difficulty solving the complex problem} - Yosh daho murakkab muammoni hal qilishda qiyinchilik ko'rmadi.
{r:It's worth listening to the ideas of a true genius} - Haqiqiy dahoning g'oyalarini tinglashga arziydi.
{r:The explorer had a clear destination in mind, a place of historical genius.} - Tadqiqotchi o'z oldiga aniq maqsad qo'ydi, bu tarixiy daholik joyi edi.

text: {r:Sacrifice}[ˈsækɹɪfaɪs] – qurbonlik qilmoq; qurbonlik qilish, voz kechish. Oldin mening qo’limda mana bu yigit sekretar bo’lib ishlagan. Qo’limda 5 yil ishlagandan so’ng {p:SEKR}etar {p:FAYZ}iyev yaxshigina ishini {h:qurbon qilib} qo’shiq aytishni boshladi, Ozod akaga shogird bo’lib ko’tarilib ketdi.
